articles.title: 少年宫延长开放后的晚间安排
articles.summary: 东湖少年宫将开放时间延长到晚上八点，并通过作业区、兴趣课程、晚饭服务和安全登记解决学生与家长的实际需要。
articles.topic: 少年宫延长开放后的晚间安排
paragraphs: 下周一开始，东湖少年宫的关门时间将从下午五点改到晚上八点。以前，不少学生放学后刚到这里，活动就快结束了；有些家长六点才下班，也来不及接孩子。为了让学生有更充分的活动时间，少年宫决定延长开放时间，不过周末的安排暂时不变。
新安排不是简单地把所有课程推迟。五点到六点，一楼阅览室会变成安静的作业区，两位老师负责回答学习问题。六点十分以后，音乐室、美术室和篮球馆才开始兴趣活动。学生可以先完成作业，再参加一个小时的课程，这样回家后不会太晚。
安全和吃饭问题也被考虑进去了。服务台会登记每名学生离开的时间，低年级学生必须由家长来接。需要留下吃晚饭的学生，可以提前一天报名，食堂会准备简单的热饭和水果。少年宫还提醒家长，如果接孩子的时间有变化，要及时打电话告诉值班老师。
少年宫在公布安排前，邀请十二名学生和八位家长参加了一次讨论。有人担心晚上活动会影响休息，因此每名学生一周最多只能选择两个晚间课程。新安排先实行一个月，工作人员会记录报名情况，也会听取家长和学生的意见。大家最欢迎的不是更多课程，而是可以安静写作业、按时吃饭和安全回家的完整服务。
pinyin: xià zhōu yī kāi shǐ ， dōng hú shào nián gōng de guān mén shí jiān jiāng cóng xià wǔ wǔ diǎn gǎi dào wǎn shàng bā diǎn 。 yǐ qián ， bù shǎo xué shēng fàng xué hòu gāng dào zhè lǐ ， huó dòng jiù kuài jié shù le ； yǒu xiē jiā zhǎng liù diǎn cái xià bān ， yě lái bù jí jiē hái zi 。 wèi le ràng xué shēng yǒu gèng chōng fèn de huó dòng shí jiān ， shào nián gōng jué dìng yán cháng kāi fàng shí jiān ， bù guò zhōu mò de ān pái zàn shí bù biàn 。

xīn ān pái bú shì jiǎn dān dì bǎ suǒ yǒu kè chéng tuī chí 。 wǔ diǎn dào liù diǎn ， yī lóu yuè lǎn shì huì biàn chéng ān jìng de zuò yè qū ， liǎng wèi lǎo shī fù zé huí dá xué xí wèn tí 。 liù diǎn shí fēn yǐ hòu ， yīn yuè shì 、 měi shù shì hé lán qiú guǎn cái kāi shǐ xìng qù huó dòng 。 xué shēng kě yǐ xiān wán chéng zuò yè ， zài cān jiā yí gè xiǎo shí de kè chéng ， zhè yàng huí jiā hòu bú huì tài wǎn 。

ān quán hé chī fàn wèn tí yě bèi kǎo lǜ jìn qù le 。 fú wù tái huì dēng jì měi míng xué shēng lí kāi de shí jiān ， dī nián jí xué shēng bì xū yóu jiā zhǎng lái jiē 。 xū yào liú xià chī wǎn fàn de xué shēng ， kě yǐ tí qián yī tiān bào míng ， shí táng huì zhǔn bèi jiǎn dān de rè fàn hé shuǐ guǒ 。 shào nián gōng hái tí xǐng jiā zhǎng ， rú guǒ jiē hái zi de shí jiān yǒu biàn huà ， yào jí shí dǎ diàn huà gào sù zhí bān lǎo shī 。

shào nián gōng zài gōng bù ān pái qián ， yāo qǐng shí èr míng xué shēng hé bā wèi jiā zhǎng cān jiā le yī cì tǎo lùn 。 yǒu rén dān xīn wǎn shàng huó dòng huì yǐng xiǎng xiū xī ， yīn cǐ měi míng xué shēng yī zhōu zuì duō zhǐ néng xuǎn zé liǎng gè wǎn jiān kè chéng 。 xīn ān pái xiān shí xíng yí gè yuè ， gōng zuò rén yuán huì jì lù bào míng qíng kuàng ， yě huì tīng qǔ jiā zhǎng hé xué shēng de yì jiàn 。 dà jiā zuì huān yíng de bú shì gèng duō kè chéng ， ér shì kě yǐ ān jìng xiě zuò yè 、 àn shí chī fàn hé ān quán huí jiā de wán zhěng fú wù 。
translation: Starting next Monday, Donghu Youth Center will change its closing time from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. In the past, many students had only just arrived after school when the activities were almost over. Some parents did not finish work until six and could not pick up their children in time. To give students more time for activities, the center decided to extend its opening hours, although the weekend schedule will remain unchanged for now.

The new arrangement does not simply move all classes to a later time. From five to six, the reading room on the first floor will become a quiet homework area, where two teachers will be responsible for answering study-related questions. After 6:10, interest activities will begin in the music room, art room, and basketball hall. Students can finish their homework first and then attend a one-hour class, so they will not return home too late.

Safety and meal needs have also been taken into consideration. The service desk will record the time each student leaves, and younger students must be picked up by a parent. Students who need to stay for dinner can register one day in advance, and the cafeteria will prepare a simple hot meal and fruit. The center also reminds parents that if their pickup time changes, they should call the teacher on duty promptly.

Before announcing the arrangement, the center invited twelve students and eight parents to take part in a discussion. Some people worried that evening activities might affect rest, so each student may choose no more than two evening classes per week. The new arrangement will be carried out for one month at first. Staff members will record enrollment and listen to the opinions of parents and students. What people welcome most is not a greater number of classes, but a complete service that allows students to do homework quietly, eat on time, and return home safely.

articles.title: 晚两小时的校史馆
articles.summary: 大学校史馆延长开放时间后，李然终于找到了课程作业需要的旧照片，并通过留言帮助校史馆改进了晚间服务。
articles.topic: 晚两小时的校史馆
paragraphs: 周一中午，大学生李然去校史馆归还一本纪念册，在门口看见了新的服务通知。从下周起，校史馆的闭馆时间将从下午四点改到晚上六点，周一到周五都一样。通知还提醒，五点以后只有一楼展厅和资料室开放，参观团需要提前预约。
李然正在准备一份关于校园建筑变化的课程作业。她每天下午都要在实验室上课，四点才能离开。以前她几次想去资料室查看旧地图，可是赶到门口时，校史馆已经关门了。看到通知后，她马上约了两位同学，决定下周三下课后一起去找材料。
周三下午四点二十分，三个人来到资料室。值班的志愿者先问清他们需要哪个年代的材料，再带他们找到一张三十年前的校园照片。照片上的图书馆还是一座两层小楼，旁边却有一棵现在仍能看到的大树。志愿者还教他们使用扫描设备，并提醒他们不能把原件带出资料室。
离开前，李然在意见本上写道，希望晚上也能提供电脑查询服务。两天后，校史馆在通知旁增加了说明：五点半以前可以申请使用查询电脑。新的安排不但让李然按时完成了作业，还方便了白天有课的学生。她认为，延长时间很重要，及时了解学生真正需要什么也同样重要。
pinyin: zhōu yī zhōng wǔ ， dà xué shēng lǐ rán qù xiào shǐ guǎn guī huán yī běn jì niàn cè ， zài mén kǒu kàn jiàn le xīn de fú wù tōng zhī 。 cóng xià zhōu qǐ ， xiào shǐ guǎn de bì guǎn shí jiān jiāng cóng xià wǔ sì diǎn gǎi dào wǎn shàng liù diǎn ， zhōu yī dào zhōu wǔ dōu yī yàng 。 tōng zhī hái tí xǐng ， wǔ diǎn yǐ hòu zhǐ yǒu yī lóu zhǎn tīng hé zī liào shì kāi fàng ， cān guān tuán xū yào tí qián yù yuē 。

lǐ rán zhèng zài zhǔn bèi yī fèn guān yú xiào yuán jiàn zhù biàn huà de kè chéng zuò yè 。 tā měi tiān xià wǔ dōu yào zài shí yàn shì shàng kè ， sì diǎn cái néng lí kāi 。 yǐ qián tā jǐ cì xiǎng qù zī liào shì chá kàn jiù dì tú ， kě shì gǎn dào mén kǒu shí ， xiào shǐ guǎn yǐ jīng guān mén le 。 kàn dào tōng zhī hòu ， tā mǎ shàng yuē le liǎng wèi tóng xué ， jué dìng xià zhōu sān xià kè hòu yì qǐ qù zhǎo cái liào 。

zhōu sān xià wǔ sì diǎn èr shí fēn ， sān gè rén lái dào zī liào shì 。 zhí bān de zhì yuàn zhě xiān wèn qīng tā men xū yào nǎ ge nián dài de cái liào ， zài dài tā men zhǎo dào yī zhāng sān shí nián qián de xiào yuán zhào piān 。 zhào piān shàng de tú shū guǎn hái shì yī zuò liǎng céng xiǎo lóu ， páng biān què yǒu yī kē xiàn zài réng néng kàn dào de dà shù 。 zhì yuàn zhě hái jiào tā men shǐ yòng sǎo miáo shè bèi ， bìng tí xǐng tā men bù néng bǎ yuán jiàn dài chū zī liào shì 。

lí kāi qián ， lǐ rán zài yì jiàn běn shàng xiě dào ， xī wàng wǎn shàng yě néng tí gōng diàn nǎo chá xún fú wù 。 liǎng tiān hòu ， xiào shǐ guǎn zài tōng zhī páng zēng jiā le shuō míng ： wǔ diǎn bàn yǐ qián kě yǐ shēn qǐng shǐ yòng chá xún diàn nǎo 。 xīn de ān pái bù dàn ràng lǐ rán àn shí wán chéng le zuò yè ， hái fāng biàn le bái tiān yǒu kè de xué shēng 。 tā rèn wéi ， yán cháng shí jiān hěn zhòng yào ， jí shí liǎo jiě xué shēng zhēn zhèng xū yào shén me yě tóng yàng zhòng yào 。
translation: At noon on Monday, university student Li Ran went to the university history museum to return a commemorative album and saw a new service notice at the entrance. Starting the following week, the museum's closing time would change from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., from Monday through Friday. The notice also stated that after 5 p.m. only the first-floor exhibition hall and the reference room would remain open, and visiting groups would need to make reservations in advance.

Li Ran was preparing a course assignment about changes in campus buildings. She had classes in the laboratory every afternoon and could not leave until four. In the past, she had tried several times to visit the reference room to look at old maps, but the museum was already closed when she reached the entrance. After seeing the notice, she immediately contacted two classmates and decided to look for materials together after class the following Wednesday.

At 4:20 on Wednesday afternoon, the three students arrived at the reference room. The volunteer on duty first asked which period they needed materials from and then helped them find a photograph of the campus taken thirty years earlier. In the photograph, the library was still a two-story building, but beside it stood a large tree that can still be seen today. The volunteer also taught them how to use the scanning equipment and reminded them that original materials could not be taken out of the reference room.

Before leaving, Li Ran wrote in the suggestion book that she hoped computer search services could also be provided in the evening. Two days later, the museum added an explanation beside the notice: visitors could apply to use a search computer before 5:30. The new arrangement not only allowed Li Ran to finish her assignment on time, but also made things more convenient for students who had classes during the day. She believed that extending the opening hours was important, and that promptly understanding what students truly needed was equally important.

articles.title: 夜里十点的健身房
articles.summary: 城南市民健身房根据晚班职工和员工的需要，试行新的开放时间，并通过轮流值班保证服务质量。
articles.topic: 夜里十点的健身房
paragraphs: 过去，城南市民健身房每天晚上八点关门。附近医院的护士、饭店服务员和商场工作人员下班较晚，常常来不及锻炼。有些人虽然办了卡，一个月却只能来两三次。前台收到不少意见，希望健身房晚上多开一会儿。
负责人周海没有马上改变时间。他先用一个星期走访附近单位，又请会员写下最方便的锻炼时间。大家最需要的不是增加新课程，而是把关门时间推迟。教练们也提出，如果每天都晚下班，身体会太累，服务质量可能下降。
经过讨论，健身房决定从九月起试行新的安排：周二到周五延长到晚上十点，周一仍在八点关门，方便检查器材。周末时间不变。晚间课程减少为两节，每节课需要提前预约；没有预约的会员仍可使用跑步机和其他器材。
为了不让工作人员过度劳累，前台和教练分成两组，轮流上晚班。健身房还增加了一名安全员，并在九点半提醒会员整理物品。第一次来晚间锻炼的人，可以请教练免费介绍器材的正确用法，但不能要求单独上课。
新安排实行两周后，晚间来锻炼的会员明显多了，白天的正常开放却没有受到影响。周海没有立刻把时间固定下来，而是继续收集意见。他说，只有会员方便、员工也能休息好，新服务才算真正合适。
pinyin: guò qù ， chéng nán shì mín jiàn shēn fáng měi tiān wǎn shàng bā diǎn guān mén 。 fù jìn yī yuàn de hù shì 、 fàn diàn fú wù yuán hé shāng chǎng gōng zuò rén yuán xià bān jiào wǎn ， cháng cháng lái bù jí duàn liàn 。 yǒu xiē rén suī rán bàn le kǎ ， yí gè yuè què zhǐ néng lái liǎng sān cì 。 qián tái shōu dào bù shǎo yì jiàn ， xī wàng jiàn shēn fáng wǎn shàng duō kāi yī huì er 。

fù zé rén zhōu hǎi méi yǒu mǎ shàng gǎi biàn shí jiān 。 tā xiān yòng yí gè xīng qī zǒu fǎng fù jìn dān wèi ， yòu qǐng huì yuán xiě xià zuì fāng biàn de duàn liàn shí jiān 。 dà jiā zuì xū yào de bú shì zēng jiā xīn kè chéng ， ér shì bǎ guān mén shí jiān tuī chí 。 jiào liàn men yě tí chū ， rú guǒ měi tiān dōu wǎn xià bān ， shēn tǐ huì tài lèi ， fú wù zhì liàng kě néng xià jiàng 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， jiàn shēn fáng jué dìng cóng jiǔ yuè qǐ shì xíng xīn de ān pái ： zhōu èr dào zhōu wǔ yán cháng dào wǎn shàng shí diǎn ， zhōu yī réng zài bā diǎn guān mén ， fāng biàn jiǎn chá qì cái 。 zhōu mò shí jiān bù biàn 。 wǎn jiān kè chéng jiǎn shǎo wèi liǎng jié ， měi jié kè xū yào tí qián yù yuē ； méi yǒu yù yuē de huì yuán réng kě shǐ yòng pǎo bù jī hé qí tā qì cái 。

wèi le bù ràng gōng zuò rén yuán guò dù láo lèi ， qián tái hé jiào liàn fēn chéng liǎng zǔ ， lún liú shàng wǎn bān 。 jiàn shēn fáng hái zēng jiā le yī míng ān quán yuán ， bìng zài jiǔ diǎn bàn tí xǐng huì yuán zhěng lǐ wù pǐn 。 dì yī cì lái wǎn jiān duàn liàn de rén ， kě yǐ qǐng jiào liàn miǎn fèi jiè shào qì cái de zhèng què yòng fǎ ， dàn bù néng yāo qiú dān dú shàng kè 。

xīn ān pái shí xíng liǎng zhōu hòu ， wǎn jiān lái duàn liàn de huì yuán míng xiǎn duō le ， bái tiān de zhèng cháng kāi fàng què méi yǒu shòu dào yǐng xiǎng 。 zhōu hǎi méi yǒu lì kè bǎ shí jiān gù dìng xià lái ， ér shì jì xù shōu jí yì jiàn 。 tā shuō ， zhǐ yǒu huì yuán fāng biàn 、 yuán gōng yě néng xiū xī hǎo ， xīn fú wù cái suàn zhēn zhèng hé shì 。
translation: In the past, Chengnan Municipal Gym closed at eight o'clock every evening. Nurses from a nearby hospital, restaurant servers, and shopping mall employees finished work late and often could not get there in time to exercise. Although some people had bought membership cards, they could only visit two or three times a month. The front desk received many comments asking the gym to stay open a little longer at night.

The manager, Zhou Hai, did not change the schedule immediately. He first spent a week visiting nearby workplaces and also asked members to write down the most convenient times for them to exercise. What people needed most was not additional classes, but a later closing time. The coaches also pointed out that if they finished work late every day, they would become too tired and the quality of service might decline.

After discussion, the gym decided to test a new schedule starting in September: from Tuesday through Friday, the opening hours would be extended until ten at night, while on Monday the gym would still close at eight so that the equipment could be inspected. Weekend hours would remain unchanged. Evening classes would be reduced to two, and each class would require an advance reservation; members without reservations could still use the treadmills and other equipment.

To prevent the staff from becoming overworked, the front desk employees and coaches were divided into two groups that would take turns working the evening shift. The gym also added a safety officer and reminded members at nine thirty to gather their belongings. People exercising there in the evening for the first time could ask a coach to explain the correct use of the equipment free of charge, but they could not request an individual lesson.

After the new schedule had been in place for two weeks, noticeably more members came to exercise in the evening, while daytime operations were not affected. Zhou Hai did not make the schedule permanent immediately, but continued to collect comments. He said that the new service could only be considered truly suitable if it was convenient for members and also allowed employees to get enough rest.

articles.title: 两晚亮着的灯
articles.summary: 社区阅览室根据来访者的实际需要调整开放时间，并通过短期试行找到了合适的服务安排。
articles.topic: 两晚亮着的灯
paragraphs: 周三晚上，林阿姨忙完家里的事，带着一本快到期的书来到社区阅览室，却发现门已经关了。她白天要照顾父亲，只有晚饭后才有空，于是在门口的意见本上写下建议，希望阅览室每周能晚关几次。
第二天，管理员赵宁读到了这条留言。他发现，最近还有几位上班族提出过同样的要求。不过，他没有立刻改变时间，而是连续一周记录大家到访的时间，并当面询问他们晚上来阅览室主要想做什么。
记录显示，六点以后来的人大多需要还书、查资料或安静地学习。赵宁和工作人员讨论后，决定把这次调整当作一次阶段试行：周二、周四开放到晚上九点，其他日期保持原来的时间。两名社区志愿者主动参加晚间值班。
试行后的第一个周二下起了大雨。赵宁本以为不会有人来，没想到八点二十分，林阿姨推门走进来。她还了书，又坐在窗边读完一篇健康文章。离开前，她笑着说，晚间服务让她不用再急着安排白天的事情。
三周后，阅览室根据每天的记录进行了总结。周二和周四的晚间来访人数比较稳定，而其他日期很少有人提出延长时间的要求。因此，阅览室保留了两晚开放的安排，还增加了网上续借服务。林阿姨看到新通知后，报名成为周四的志愿者。

jì lù xiǎn shì ， liù diǎn yǐ hòu lái de rén dà duō xū yào huán shū 、 chá zī liào huò ān jìng dì xué xí 。 zhào níng hé gōng zuò rén yuán tǎo lùn hòu ， jué dìng bǎ zhè cì tiáo zhěng dàng zuò yī cì jiē duàn shì xíng ： zhōu èr 、 zhōu sì kāi fàng dào wǎn shàng jiǔ diǎn ， qí tā rì qī bǎo chí yuán lái de shí jiān 。 liǎng míng shè qū zhì yuàn zhě zhǔ dòng cān jiā wǎn jiān zhí bān 。

shì xíng hòu de dì yí gè zhōu èr xià qǐ le dà yǔ 。 zhào níng běn yǐ wéi bú huì yǒu rén lái ， méi xiǎng dào bā diǎn èr shí fēn ， lín ā yí tuī mén zǒu jìn lái 。 tā hái le shū ， yòu zuò zài chuāng biān dú wán yī piān jiàn kāng wén zhāng 。 lí kāi qián ， tā xiào zhe shuō ， wǎn jiān fú wù ràng tā bù yòng zài jí zhe ān pái bái tiān de shì qíng 。

sān zhōu hòu ， yuè lǎn shì gēn jù měi tiān de jì lù jìn xíng le zǒng jié 。 zhōu èr hé zhōu sì de wǎn jiān lái fǎng rén shù bǐ jiào wěn dìng ， ér qí tā rì qī hěn shǎo yǒu rén tí chū yán cháng shí jiān de yāo qiú 。 yīn cǐ ， yuè lǎn shì bǎo liú le liǎng wǎn kāi fàng de ān pái ， hái zēng jiā le wǎng shàng xù jiè fú wù 。 lín ā yí kàn dào xīn tōng zhī hòu ， bào míng chéng wéi zhōu sì de zhì yuàn zhě 。
translation: On Wednesday evening, Aunt Lin finished her household tasks and came to the community reading room with a book that was nearly due, only to find that the door was already closed. She had to care for her father during the day and was free only after dinner, so she wrote a suggestion in the comment book by the entrance, hoping the reading room could close later a few times each week.

The next day, the administrator, Zhao Ning, read the message. He discovered that several office workers had recently made the same request. However, he did not change the hours immediately. Instead, for a full week he recorded when people visited and asked them in person what they mainly wanted to do in the reading room at night.

The records showed that most people arriving after six needed to return books, look up information, or study quietly. After discussing the matter with the staff, Zhao Ning decided to treat the change as a trial in stages: the reading room would stay open until nine on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while keeping its original hours on other days. Two community volunteers offered to take the evening shifts.

It rained heavily on the first Tuesday of the trial. Zhao Ning thought no one would come, but at eight twenty, Aunt Lin opened the door and walked in. She returned her book and then sat by the window to finish reading a health article. Before leaving, she said with a smile that the evening service meant she no longer had to rush to arrange her daytime activities.

Three weeks later, the reading room reviewed its daily records. The number of evening visitors on Tuesdays and Thursdays was fairly steady, while few people requested longer hours on the other days. Therefore, the reading room kept the two evening openings and also added an online renewal service. After seeing the new notice, Aunt Lin signed up to become a Thursday volunteer.

articles.title: 下班后也能看展览
articles.summary: 艺术展览中心延长晚间开放时间，并根据居民的体验意见增加服务，让上班族更方便地参观展览。
articles.topic: 下班后也能看展览
paragraphs: 市民林悦喜欢看展览，但她在一家旅行公司上班，平日下班时，艺术展览中心已经快关门了。她虽然办了年卡，却只能周末去，遇到热门展览时常常要排很久的队。上周，她收到中心的邮件，得知开放时间将从下周起由下午五点半延长到晚上八点半。
延长时间并不是简单地晚点关门。中心重新安排了工作人员，每晚六点和七点各有一场免费讲解，还把一楼休息区改成了安静的阅读角。观众可以在那里查看作品介绍，也可以给手机充电。为了方便带孩子的家庭，服务台还准备了儿童画纸和铅笔。
正式开始前，中心请附近居民参加了一次晚间体验。林悦下班后直接坐地铁过去，七点前就到了。她先把电脑包存在入口旁的柜子里，然后跟着讲解员参观。以前她常因时间紧张而走得很快，那天却能停下来认真观察，还和另一位观众讨论了一幅海边的画。
体验结束时，工作人员请大家填写意见卡。林悦建议晚上增加简单的饮水服务，并在网站上说明最后入场时间。她认为，延长开放时间以后，上班的人有了更多选择；不过，如果信息写得不清楚，有人可能八点以后才到，结果无法完整参观。
两天后，中心采用了这两条建议：阅读角旁增加了饮水机，网站首页也写明八点停止入场。林悦决定下周三再去一次，这次她想带一位刚搬来本市的同事。对她来说，新安排不只是多了三个小时，也让看展览成为工作日里容易实现的计划。
pinyin: shì mín lín yuè xǐ huān kàn zhǎn lǎn ， dàn tā zài yī jiā lǚ xíng gōng sī shàng bān ， píng rì xià bān shí ， yì shù zhǎn lǎn zhōng xīn yǐ jīng kuài guān mén le 。 tā suī rán bàn le nián kǎ ， què zhǐ néng zhōu mò qù ， yù dào rè mén zhǎn lǎn shí cháng cháng yào pái hěn jiǔ de duì 。 shàng zhōu ， tā shōu dào zhōng xīn de yóu jiàn ， dé zhī kāi fàng shí jiān jiāng cóng xià zhōu qǐ yóu xià wǔ wǔ diǎn bàn yán cháng dào wǎn shàng bā diǎn bàn 。

yán cháng shí jiān bìng bú shì jiǎn dān dì wǎn diǎn guān mén 。 zhōng xīn zhòng xīn ān pái le gōng zuò rén yuán ， měi wǎn liù diǎn hé qī diǎn gè yǒu yī cháng miǎn fèi jiǎng jiě ， hái bǎ yī lóu xiū xī qū gǎi chéng le ān jìng de yuè dú jiǎo 。 guān zhòng kě yǐ zài nà lǐ chá kàn zuò pǐn jiè shào ， yě kě yǐ gěi shǒu jī chōng diàn 。 wèi le fāng biàn dài hái zi de jiā tíng ， fú wù tái hái zhǔn bèi le ér tóng huà zhǐ hé qiān bǐ 。

zhèng shì kāi shǐ qián ， zhōng xīn qǐng fù jìn jū mín cān jiā le yī cì wǎn jiān tǐ yàn 。 lín yuè xià bān hòu zhí jiē zuò dì tiě guò qù ， qī diǎn qián jiù dào le 。 tā xiān bǎ diàn nǎo bāo cún zài rù kǒu páng de guì zi lǐ ， rán hòu gēn zhe jiǎng jiě yuán cān guān 。 yǐ qián tā cháng yīn shí jiān jǐn zhāng ér zǒu dé hěn kuài ， nà tiān què néng tíng xià lái rèn zhēn guān chá ， hái hé lìng yī wèi guān zhòng tǎo lùn le yī fú hǎi biān de huà 。

tǐ yàn jié shù shí ， gōng zuò rén yuán qǐng dà jiā tián xiě yì jiàn kǎ 。 lín yuè jiàn yì wǎn shàng zēng jiā jiǎn dān de yǐn shuǐ fú wù ， bìng zài wǎng zhàn shàng shuō míng zuì hòu rù chǎng shí jiān 。 tā rèn wéi ， yán cháng kāi fàng shí jiān yǐ hòu ， shàng bān de rén yǒu le gèng duō xuǎn zé ； bù guò ， rú guǒ xìn xī xiě dé bù qīng chǔ ， yǒu rén kě néng bā diǎn yǐ hòu cái dào ， jié guǒ wú fǎ wán zhěng cān guān 。

liǎng tiān hòu ， zhōng xīn cǎi yòng le zhè liǎng tiáo jiàn yì ： yuè dú jiǎo páng zēng jiā le yǐn shuǐ jī ， wǎng zhàn shǒu yè yě xiě míng bā diǎn tíng zhǐ rù chǎng 。 lín yuè jué dìng xià zhōu sān zài qù yī cì ， zhè cì tā xiǎng dài yī wèi gāng bān lái běn shì de tóng shì 。 duì tā lái shuō ， xīn ān pái bù zhǐ shì duō le sān gè xiǎo shí ， yě ràng kàn zhǎn lǎn chéng wéi gōng zuò rì lǐ róng yì shí xiàn de jì huà 。
translation: Lin Yue, a city resident, enjoys visiting exhibitions, but she works at a travel company. By the time she gets off work on weekdays, the art exhibition center is almost closed. Although she has an annual pass, she can only visit on weekends and often has to wait in a long line when an exhibition is popular. Last week, she received an email from the center and learned that, starting next week, its opening hours would be extended from 5:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.

Extending the hours does not simply mean closing later. The center has rearranged its staff schedule and will offer a free guided tour at both six and seven each evening. It has also turned the first-floor rest area into a quiet reading corner. Visitors can read information about the artworks there and charge their phones as well. To help families with children, the service desk has also prepared drawing paper and pencils for children.

Before the new schedule officially began, the center invited nearby residents to take part in an evening trial visit. Lin Yue took the subway there directly after work and arrived before seven. She first stored her laptop bag in a locker beside the entrance and then joined a guide for the visit. In the past, she often walked quickly because she had little time, but that evening she was able to stop and observe carefully. She even discussed a painting of the seaside with another visitor.

At the end of the trial visit, the staff asked everyone to fill out a comment card. Lin Yue suggested providing basic drinking water in the evening and stating the final admission time on the website. She believed that longer opening hours would give working people more choices. However, if the information was unclear, some people might arrive after eight and be unable to complete their visit.

Two days later, the center adopted both suggestions: it added a water dispenser beside the reading corner, and the website homepage stated that admission would stop at eight. Lin Yue decided to return the following Wednesday, and this time she wanted to bring a colleague who had recently moved to the city. For her, the new schedule not only added three hours but also made visiting exhibitions an achievable weekday plan.

articles.title: 下班后也能办事了
articles.summary: 春河社区的便民服务站根据居民的需要延长工作时间，并通过轮流值班、分设窗口和电话预约改善晚间服务。
articles.topic: 下班后也能办事了
paragraphs: 周一早上，住在春河社区的林阿姨去便民服务站交水费，看见门口贴了一张新通知。通知说，从下周开始，服务站的工作时间将由下午四点延长到晚上六点半，周一到周五都这样安排。
以前，服务站下午四点就关门，不少上班的居民来不及办理事情，只能请假，或者请家里的老人帮忙。工作人员也常接到电话，大家希望下班后还能交生活费用、领取信件、询问社区活动。服务站听取了这些意见，决定先把新时间试行一个月。
新安排不是简单地晚关门。白天的工作人员仍按原来的时间上班，傍晚则由两名同事轮流值班。为了减少等待，服务站设置了三个办理常见业务的窗口，还开通了电话预约。需要准备材料的居民，可以先打电话问清楚，免得来回跑。
新安排实行后的第一个星期三，林阿姨下班后去领取一封重要信件。她到站时是五点四十分，前面只有两个人。不到十分钟，她就办完了事情。工作人员提醒她，晚上只能办理通知中写明的服务，办理居住证明等比较复杂的事情仍要在白天进行。
回家的路上，林阿姨遇到邻居小赵，便把新安排告诉了他。小赵说自己正担心没时间交电费，听后马上放下心来。一个月后，服务站会根据居民的意见决定是否继续延长时间。林阿姨觉得，改变不一定要很大，只要真正解决大家的困难，就值得支持。
pinyin: zhōu yī zǎo shàng ， zhù zài chūn hé shè qū de lín ā yí qù biàn mín fú wù zhàn jiāo shuǐ fèi ， kàn jiàn mén kǒu tiē le yī zhāng xīn tōng zhī 。 tōng zhī shuō ， cóng xià zhōu kāi shǐ ， fú wù zhàn de gōng zuò shí jiān jiāng yóu xià wǔ sì diǎn yán cháng dào wǎn shàng liù diǎn bàn ， zhōu yī dào zhōu wǔ dōu zhè yàng ān pái 。

yǐ qián ， fú wù zhàn xià wǔ sì diǎn jiù guān mén ， bù shǎo shàng bān de jū mín lái bù jí bàn lǐ shì qíng ， zhǐ néng qǐng jià ， huò zhě qǐng jiā lǐ de lǎo rén bāng máng 。 gōng zuò rén yuán yě cháng jiē dào diàn huà ， dà jiā xī wàng xià bān hòu hái néng jiāo shēng huó fèi yòng 、 lǐng qǔ xìn jiàn 、 xún wèn shè qū huó dòng 。 fú wù zhàn tīng qǔ le zhè xiē yì jiàn ， jué dìng xiān bǎ xīn shí jiān shì xíng yí gè yuè 。

xīn ān pái bú shì jiǎn dān dì wǎn guān mén 。 bái tiān de gōng zuò rén yuán réng àn yuán lái de shí jiān shàng bān ， bàng wǎn zé yóu liǎng míng tóng shì lún liú zhí bān 。 wèi le jiǎn shǎo děng dài ， fú wù zhàn shè zhì le sān gè bàn lǐ cháng jiàn yè wù de chuāng kǒu ， hái kāi tōng le diàn huà yù yuē 。 xū yào zhǔn bèi cái liào de jū mín ， kě yǐ xiān dǎ diàn huà wèn qīng chǔ ， miǎn de lái huí pǎo 。

xīn ān pái shí xíng hòu de dì yí gè xīng qī sān ， lín ā yí xià bān hòu qù lǐng qǔ yī fēng zhòng yào xìn jiàn 。 tā dào zhàn shí shì wǔ diǎn sì shí fēn ， qián miàn zhǐ yǒu liǎng gè rén 。 bú dào shí fēn zhōng ， tā jiù bàn wán le shì qíng 。 gōng zuò rén yuán tí xǐng tā ， wǎn shàng zhǐ néng bàn lǐ tōng zhī zhōng xiě míng de fú wù ， bàn lǐ jū zhù zhèng míng děng bǐ jiào fù zá de shì qíng réng yào zài bái tiān jìn xíng 。

huí jiā de lù shàng ， lín ā yí yù dào lín jū xiǎo zhào ， biàn bǎ xīn ān pái gào sù le tā 。 xiǎo zhào shuō zì jǐ zhèng dān xīn méi shí jiān jiāo diàn fèi ， tīng hòu mǎ shàng fàng xià xīn lái 。 yí gè yuè hòu ， fú wù zhàn huì gēn jù jū mín de yì jiàn jué dìng shì fǒu jì xù yán cháng shí jiān 。 lín ā yí jué de ， gǎi biàn bù yí dìng yào hěn dà ， zhǐ yào zhēn zhèng jiě jué dà jiā de kùn nán ， jiù zhí de zhī chí 。
translation: On Monday morning, Aunt Lin, who lives in Chunhe Community, went to the convenience service station to pay her water bill and saw a new notice posted at the entrance. The notice said that starting the following week, the station's working hours would be extended from 4:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. from Monday to Friday.

Previously, the station closed at 4:00 p.m., so many residents who worked during the day could not get there in time to handle their affairs. They had to take time off or ask older family members for help. The staff also often received calls from people hoping to pay household bills, collect mail, or ask about community activities after work. After listening to these requests, the station decided to try the new schedule for one month.

The new arrangement did not simply mean closing later. The daytime staff continued to work their original hours, while two colleagues took turns working the evening shift. To reduce waiting times, the station set up three counters for handling common services and also introduced telephone appointments. Residents who needed to prepare documents could call first to get clear information and avoid making unnecessary trips.

On the first Wednesday after the new schedule began, Aunt Lin went to collect an important letter after work. It was 5:40 p.m. when she arrived, and only two people were ahead of her. She finished in less than ten minutes. A staff member reminded her that only the services listed in the notice were available in the evening, while more complicated matters, such as obtaining proof of residence, still had to be handled during the day.

On her way home, Aunt Lin met her neighbor Xiao Zhao and told him about the new schedule. Xiao Zhao said he had been worried that he would not have time to pay his electricity bill, so he immediately felt relieved after hearing the news. After one month, the station would use residents' feedback to decide whether to keep the extended hours. Aunt Lin believed that a change did not have to be major to deserve support, as long as it truly helped solve people's difficulties.

articles.title: 毕业季打印不再只能排长队
articles.summary: 一名学生志愿者发现打印中心排队时间过长的原因，并帮助学校设计了预约、检查文件和保留时间的新安排。
articles.topic: 毕业季打印不再只能排长队
paragraphs: 五月下旬，海城大学打印中心门口每天都排着长队。大四学生林悦来打印毕业论文时，发现不少同学到了窗口才修改文件名、纸张大小和页码。后面的人虽然着急，却只能继续等。林悦是学生志愿者，她决定先了解问题，再提出办法。
她连续三个下午在门口帮助同学，并把大家常问的问题记在本子上。她发现，机器数量并不是唯一原因：有人忘了带校园卡，有人的文件打不开，还有人不清楚彩色打印的价格。工作人员需要一遍遍解释，处理每份材料的时间自然变长了。
林悦向中心提出一项新安排：学生可以提前在学校系统里选择时间，上传文件并检查格式；没有预约的人也能现场排队。中心接受了建议，还在入口放了一块说明牌，写清服务时间、收费标准和文件要求。毕业材料可以从早上七点半开始打印，比原来提前一小时。
新安排实行的第一天，陈宇因为公交车晚点，错过了预约时间。他担心必须重新排队，工作人员却告诉他，预约会保留十分钟；超过时间后，只要当天还有空位，就可以重新选择。陈宇很快完成了打印，也没有影响下一位同学。
新安排实行一周后，中心发现，大家等待时更安静了，窗口前反复询问的情况也少了。林悦认为，延长服务时间只能解决一部分问题，让使用者提前准备、同时给意外情况留下选择，才是这项安排真正方便的地方。
pinyin: wǔ yuè xià xún ， hǎi chéng dà xué dǎ yìn zhōng xīn mén kǒu měi tiān dōu pái zhe cháng duì 。 dà sì xué shēng lín yuè lái dǎ yìn bì yè lùn wén shí ， fā xiàn bù shǎo tóng xué dào le chuāng kǒu cái xiū gǎi wén jiàn míng 、 zhǐ zhāng dà xiǎo hé yè mǎ 。 hòu miàn de rén suī rán zháo jí ， què zhǐ néng jì xù děng 。 lín yuè shì xué shēng zhì yuàn zhě ， tā jué dìng xiān liǎo jiě wèn tí ， zài tí chū bàn fǎ 。

tā lián xù sān gè xià wǔ zài mén kǒu bāng zhù tóng xué ， bìng bǎ dà jiā cháng wèn de wèn tí jì zài běn zi shàng 。 tā fā xiàn ， jī qì shù liàng bìng bú shì wéi yī yuán yīn ： yǒu rén wàng le dài xiào yuán kǎ ， yǒu rén de wén jiàn dǎ bù kāi ， hái yǒu rén bù qīng chǔ cǎi sè dǎ yìn de jià gé 。 gōng zuò rén yuán xū yào yī biàn biàn jiě shì ， chǔ lǐ měi fèn cái liào de shí jiān zì rán biàn zhǎng le 。

lín yuè xiàng zhōng xīn tí chū yī xiàng xīn ān pái ： xué shēng kě yǐ tí qián zài xué xiào xì tǒng lǐ xuǎn zé shí jiān ， shàng chuán wén jiàn bìng jiǎn chá gé shì ； méi yǒu yù yuē de rén yě néng xiàn chǎng pái duì 。 zhōng xīn jiē shòu le jiàn yì ， hái zài rù kǒu fàng le yī kuài shuō míng pái ， xiě qīng fú wù shí jiān 、 shōu fèi biāo zhǔn hé wén jiàn yāo qiú 。 bì yè cái liào kě yǐ cóng zǎo shàng qī diǎn bàn kāi shǐ dǎ yìn ， bǐ yuán lái tí qián yī xiǎo shí 。

xīn ān pái shí xíng de dì yī tiān ， chén yǔ yīn wèi gōng jiāo chē wǎn diǎn ， cuò guò le yù yuē shí jiān 。 tā dān xīn bì xū chóng xīn pái duì ， gōng zuò rén yuán què gào sù tā ， yù yuē huì bǎo liú shí fēn zhōng ； chāo guò shí jiān hòu ， zhǐ yào dàng tiān hái yǒu kòng wèi ， jiù kě yǐ chóng xīn xuǎn zé 。 chén yǔ hěn kuài wán chéng le dǎ yìn ， yě méi yǒu yǐng xiǎng xià yī wèi tóng xué 。

xīn ān pái shí xíng yī zhōu hòu ， zhōng xīn fā xiàn ， dà jiā děng dài shí gèng ān jìng le ， chuāng kǒu qián fǎn fù xún wèn de qíng kuàng yě shǎo le 。 lín yuè rèn wéi ， yán cháng fú wù shí jiān zhǐ néng jiě jué yī bù fèn wèn tí ， ràng shǐ yòng zhě tí qián zhǔn bèi 、 tóng shí gěi yì wài qíng kuàng liú xià xuǎn zé ， cái shì zhè xiàng ān pái zhēn zhèng fāng biàn de dì fāng 。
translation: In late May, long lines formed every day outside the printing center at Haicheng University. When senior student Lin Yue came to print her graduation thesis, she noticed that many students did not change their file names, paper sizes, or page numbers until they reached the service window. Although the people behind them were anxious, they could only keep waiting. Lin Yue was a student volunteer, and she decided to understand the problem before suggesting a solution.

For three afternoons in a row, she helped students at the entrance and wrote down their frequently asked questions in a notebook. She discovered that the number of machines was not the only cause: some people had forgotten their campus cards, some had files that would not open, and others did not know the price of color printing. Staff members had to explain the same things repeatedly, so dealing with each document naturally took longer.

Lin Yue suggested a new arrangement to the center: students could choose a time in advance through the university system, upload their files, and check the formatting, while those without appointments could still wait in line on site. The center accepted her suggestion and placed an information board at the entrance listing the service hours, pricing standards, and file requirements. Graduation materials could now be printed from 7:30 in the morning, one hour earlier than before.

On the first day of the new arrangement, Chen Yu missed his appointment because his bus was late. He was worried that he would have to line up again, but a staff member told him that an appointment would be kept for ten minutes. After that period, as long as a space was still available that day, he could select another time. Chen Yu quickly finished his printing without delaying the next student.

One week after the new arrangement was introduced, the center found that people were quieter while waiting and that repeated questions at the service window had become less common. Lin Yue believed that extending service hours could solve only part of the problem. The real convenience of the arrangement came from helping users prepare in advance while still giving them options when something unexpected happened.

articles.title: 药房用灯牌提示营业状态
articles.summary: 一家社区药房根据来访者的实际需要调整晚间服务，并通过记录问题、提前联系和清楚提醒，让新安排更加方便可靠。
articles.topic: 药房把关门时间写在灯牌上
paragraphs: 周一晚上，张阿姨下班后去社区药房买药。她八点十分赶到门口，却发现药房已经关门。第二天早上，她把自己的经历告诉林经理，并建议药房每周选择几天晚一点关门。她说，附近不少人白天上班，很难在原来的服务时间内过来。
林经理没有马上延长每天的服务时间，而是先记录来访者的需要，再考虑怎样安排。他请工作人员连续一周询问顾客，希望了解大家最需要哪些晚间服务。多数人希望星期二和星期四开到晚上九点，也有人担心晚上买不到自己需要的药。
药房决定先实行两周的新安排。两名药师轮流负责晚班，其他工作人员每天傍晚检查常用药的数量。如果某种药快没有了，他们会提前补上。药房还在门口放了一块灯牌，用绿色表示正在营业，用红色提醒顾客第二天再来。
第一个星期四晚上，一位年轻父亲拿着医生开的药单赶来。他出门前先给药房打电话，确认药品已经准备好，然后才带孩子过来。药师检查药单后，把使用方法写得更清楚，还提醒他如果孩子继续发烧，应该及时联系医生。
两周结束后，药房发现晚间顾客主要需要取药和询问使用方法，很少有人来买其他东西。这是药房内部的阶段观察，不是正式统计。林经理最后保留了每周两个晚班，并增加了电话确认服务。张阿姨看到新的时间表后说，这样的改变既方便，也让人更放心。

yào fáng jué dìng xiān shí xíng liǎng zhōu de xīn ān pái 。 liǎng míng yào shī lún liú fù zé wǎn bān ， qí tā gōng zuò rén yuán měi tiān bàng wǎn jiǎn chá cháng yòng yào de shù liàng 。 rú guǒ mǒu zhǒng yào kuài méi yǒu le ， tā men huì tí qián bǔ shàng 。 yào fáng hái zài mén kǒu fàng le yī kuài dēng pái ， yòng lǜ sè biǎo shì zhèng zài yíng yè ， yòng hóng sè tí xǐng gù kè dì èr tiān zài lái 。

dì yí gè xīng qī sì wǎn shàng ， yī wèi nián qīng fù qīn ná zhe yī shēng kāi de yào dān gǎn lái 。 tā chū mén qián xiān gěi yào fáng dǎ diàn huà ， què rèn yào pǐn yǐ jīng zhǔn bèi hǎo ， rán hòu cái dài hái zi guò lái 。 yào shī jiǎn chá yào dān hòu ， bǎ shǐ yòng fāng fǎ xiě dé gèng qīng chǔ ， hái tí xǐng tā rú guǒ hái zi jì xù fā shāo ， yīng gāi jí shí lián xì yī shēng 。

liǎng zhōu jié shù hòu ， yào fáng fā xiàn wǎn jiān gù kè zhǔ yào xū yào qǔ yào hé xún wèn shǐ yòng fāng fǎ ， hěn shǎo yǒu rén lái mǎi qí tā dōng xī 。 zhè shì yào fáng nèi bù de jiē duàn guān chá ， bú shì zhèng shì tǒng jì 。 lín jīng lǐ zuì hòu bǎo liú le měi zhōu liǎng gè wǎn bān ， bìng zēng jiā le diàn huà què rèn fú wù 。 zhāng ā yí kàn dào xīn de shí jiān biǎo hòu shuō ， zhè yàng de gǎi biàn jì fāng biàn ， yě ràng rén gèng fàng xīn 。
translation: On Monday evening, Aunt Zhang went to the community pharmacy to buy medicine after work. She arrived at 8:10, only to find that the pharmacy had already closed. The next morning, she told Manager Lin about her experience and suggested that the pharmacy close later on selected days each week. She said that many nearby residents worked during the day and found it difficult to visit during the original service hours.

Manager Lin did not immediately extend the service hours every day. Instead, he first recorded visitors' needs and then considered how to arrange the schedule. He asked the staff to question customers for one week so they could understand which evening services were most needed. Most people wanted the pharmacy to stay open until nine on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while some were worried that the medicine they needed might not be available at night.

The pharmacy decided to follow the new arrangement for two weeks first. Two pharmacists took turns working the evening shift, and other staff members checked the supply of commonly used medicine every evening. If a certain medicine was running low, they restocked it in advance. The pharmacy also placed an illuminated sign at the entrance, using green to show that it was open and red to remind customers to return the next day.

On the first Thursday evening, a young father arrived with a prescription from a doctor. Before leaving home, he called the pharmacy to confirm that the medicine was ready, and only then did he bring his child over. After checking the prescription, the pharmacist wrote the instructions more clearly and reminded him to contact a doctor promptly if the child's fever continued.

At the end of the two weeks, the pharmacy found that evening customers mainly needed to collect medicine and ask how to use it, while few came to buy other things. This was an interim observation made within the pharmacy, not an official statistic. Manager Lin ultimately kept two evening shifts each week and added a telephone confirmation service. After seeing the new timetable, Aunt Zhang said that the change was both convenient and reassuring.

articles.title: 实行弹性到岗并调整会议规则后，临时会议更少了
articles.summary: 一家科技公司通过为期六周的试行，发现弹性到岗不仅改变了员工的作息，也暴露出会议安排和团队合作中的问题。公司随后调整规则，在个人选择与集体合作之间找到了更合适的平衡。
articles.topic: 十点到岗以后，会议反而更少了
paragraphs: 杭州一家科技公司准备试行新的到岗制度。过去，所有员工都必须在早上九点前进入办公室，迟到需要向主管解释。产品经理林悦发现，有些同事住得远，为了避开交通高峰，不得不提前一个多小时出门；也有人习惯早起，到了公司却要等其他部门上班以后才能讨论工作。于是，公司决定用六周时间试行新的到岗制度。
按照新规则，员工可以在早上七点到十点之间自由选择到岗时间，但每天必须工作够规定的时间。下午两点到四点被定为共同工作时间，需要合作的会议尽量安排在这段时间。为了避免影响客户，公司还要求每个小组保证从九点开始就有人值班。林悦负责记录试行过程中出现的问题，而不是只比较谁来得早、谁走得晚。
第一周，不少员工以为时间自由以后，工作会变得更轻松，实际情况却没有这么简单。有人七点半就到了，却连续收到十点以后才上班的同事发来的会议邀请；有人选择晚到，晚上准备离开时又找不到能够及时确认方案的人。最明显的问题不是工作时间减少了，而是大家仍然按照原来的习惯随时开会，结果一天被切成许多短时间，注意力很难集中。
林悦没有建议取消新制度，而是和各组主管重新整理合作方式。公司规定，除非客户遇到紧急情况，上午十点前不安排需要全员参加的会议；需要别人当天回复的任务，必须在下午三点前发出。同时，员工要在日历上公开自己的工作时间。根据林悦记录的阶段性情况，规则调整两周后，临时会议减少了，员工等待回复的情况也有所改善。
六周结束时，公司没有把某一种作息当成标准答案。喜欢安静工作的程序员可以早点来，需要送孩子上学的员工也可以晚些到，只要提前说明并履行职责。林悦在总结中写道，弹性制度真正考验的不是员工能否管理时间，而是团队能否尊重彼此的安排。最后，公司保留了弹性到岗，同时决定每个月收集一次意见，并根据项目变化继续调整。
pinyin: háng zhōu yī jiā kē jì gōng sī zhǔn bèi shì xíng xīn de dào gǎng zhì dù 。 guò qù ， suǒ yǒu yuán gōng dōu bì xū zài zǎo shàng jiǔ diǎn qián jìn rù bàn gōng shì ， chí dào xū yào xiàng zhǔ guǎn jiě shì 。 chǎn pǐn jīng lǐ lín yuè fā xiàn ， yǒu xiē tóng shì zhù dé yuǎn ， wèi le bì kāi jiāo tōng gāo fēng ， bù dé bù tí qián yí gè duō xiǎo shí chū mén ； yě yǒu rén xí guàn zǎo qǐ ， dào le gōng sī què yào děng qí tā bù mén shàng bān yǐ hòu cái néng tǎo lùn gōng zuò 。 yú shì ， gōng sī jué dìng yòng liù zhōu shí jiān shì xíng xīn de dào gǎng zhì dù 。

àn zhào xīn guī zé ， yuán gōng kě yǐ zài zǎo shàng qī diǎn dào shí diǎn zhī jiān zì yóu xuǎn zé dào gǎng shí jiān ， dàn měi tiān bì xū gōng zuò gòu guī dìng de shí jiān 。 xià wǔ liǎng diǎn dào sì diǎn bèi dìng wèi gòng tóng gōng zuò shí jiān ， xū yào hé zuò de huì yì jǐn liàng ān pái zài zhè duàn shí jiān 。 wèi le bì miǎn yǐng xiǎng kè hù ， gōng sī hái yāo qiú měi gè xiǎo zǔ bǎo zhèng cóng jiǔ diǎn kāi shǐ jiù yǒu rén zhí bān 。 lín yuè fù zé jì lù shì xíng guò chéng zhōng chū xiàn de wèn tí ， ér bú shì zhǐ bǐ jiào shuí lái de zǎo 、 shuí zǒu dé wǎn 。

dì yī zhōu ， bù shǎo yuán gōng yǐ wéi shí jiān zì yóu yǐ hòu ， gōng zuò huì biàn dé gèng qīng sōng ， shí jì qíng kuàng què méi yǒu zhè me jiǎn dān 。 yǒu rén qī diǎn bàn jiù dào le ， què lián xù shōu dào shí diǎn yǐ hòu cái shàng bān de tóng shì fā lái de huì yì yāo qǐng ； yǒu rén xuǎn zé wǎn dào ， wǎn shàng zhǔn bèi lí kāi shí yòu zhǎo bú dào néng gòu jí shí què rèn fāng àn de rén 。 zuì míng xiǎn de wèn tí bú shì gōng zuò shí jiān jiǎn shǎo le ， ér shì dà jiā réng rán àn zhào yuán lái de xí guàn suí shí kāi huì ， jié guǒ yī tiān bèi qiè chéng xǔ duō duǎn shí jiān ， zhù yì lì hěn nán jí zhōng 。

lín yuè méi yǒu jiàn yì qǔ xiāo xīn zhì dù ， ér shì hé gè zǔ zhǔ guǎn chóng xīn zhěng lǐ hé zuò fāng shì 。 gōng sī guī dìng ， chú fēi kè hù yù dào jǐn jí qíng kuàng ， shàng wǔ shí diǎn qián bù ān pái xū yào quán yuán cān jiā de huì yì ； xū yào bié rén dàng tiān huí fù de rèn wù ， bì xū zài xià wǔ sān diǎn qián fā chū 。 tóng shí ， yuán gōng yào zài rì lì shàng gōng kāi zì jǐ de gōng zuò shí jiān 。 gēn jù lín yuè jì lù de jiē duàn xìng qíng kuàng ， guī zé tiáo zhěng liǎng zhōu hòu ， lín shí huì yì jiǎn shǎo le ， yuán gōng děng dài huí fù de qíng kuàng yě yǒu suǒ gǎi shàn 。

liù zhōu jié shù shí ， gōng sī méi yǒu bǎ mǒu yī zhǒng zuò xī dàng chéng biāo zhǔn dá àn 。 xǐ huān ān jìng gōng zuò de chéng xù yuán kě yǐ zǎo diǎn lái ， xū yào sòng hái zi shàng xué de yuán gōng yě kě yǐ wǎn xiē dào ， zhǐ yào tí qián shuō míng bìng lǚ xíng zhí zé 。 lín yuè zài zǒng jié zhōng xiě dào ， tán xìng zhì dù zhēn zhèng kǎo yàn de bú shì yuán gōng néng fǒu guǎn lǐ shí jiān ， ér shì tuán duì néng fǒu zūn zhòng bǐ cǐ de ān pái 。 zuì hòu ， gōng sī bǎo liú le tán xìng dào gǎng ， tóng shí jué dìng měi gè yuè shōu jí yī cì yì jiàn ， bìng gēn jù xiàng mù biàn huà jì xù tiáo zhěng 。
translation: A technology company in Hangzhou planned to test a new arrival-time policy. In the past, all employees had to enter the office before 9 a.m., and anyone arriving late had to explain it to a supervisor. Product manager Lin Yue noticed that some colleagues lived far away and had to leave home more than an hour earlier to avoid rush hour. Others preferred getting up early but still had to wait until other departments began work before they could discuss tasks. The company therefore decided to conduct a six-week trial of the new arrival-time policy.

Under the new rule, employees could freely choose to arrive between 7 and 10 a.m., but they still had to work the required number of hours each day. The period from 2 to 4 p.m. was designated as shared working time, and meetings requiring cooperation were to be scheduled during that period whenever possible. To avoid affecting clients, the company also required each team to have someone on duty from 9 a.m. Lin Yue was responsible for recording problems that arose during the trial rather than merely comparing who arrived early and who left late.

During the first week, many employees thought that greater freedom over time would make work easier, but the reality was not so simple. Some arrived at 7:30 yet kept receiving meeting invitations from colleagues who did not begin work until after 10. Others chose to arrive late but could not find anyone available to confirm the plan promptly when they were ready to leave in the evening. The clearest problem was not a reduction in working hours, but that people still followed their old habit of holding meetings at any time. As a result, the day was divided into many short periods, making it difficult to concentrate.

Lin Yue did not suggest canceling the new system. Instead, she worked with team supervisors to reorganize how people collaborated. The company stipulated that, unless a client faced an emergency, meetings requiring all staff would not be scheduled before 10 a.m. Tasks needing a reply that same day had to be sent before 3 p.m. Employees also had to make their working hours visible on their calendars. According to Lin Yue's interim observations, two weeks after the rules were adjusted, last-minute meetings decreased, and employees also spent less time waiting for replies.

At the end of the six weeks, the company did not treat any single schedule as the standard answer. Programmers who preferred quiet working conditions could arrive early, while employees who needed to take their children to school could arrive later, as long as they explained in advance and fulfilled their responsibilities. Lin Yue wrote in her summary that what a flexible system truly tests is not whether employees can manage time, but whether a team can respect one another's arrangements. In the end, the company kept flexible arrival times and decided that it would collect feedback once a month and continue to make adjustments as projects changed.

articles.title: 青禾工作室的两天居家办公试验
articles.summary: 一家设计工作室试行每周两天居家办公，并通过调整沟通规则，在灵活工作与团队协作之间找到平衡。
articles.topic: 青禾工作室的两天居家办公试验
paragraphs: 三个月前，青禾设计工作室遇到一个难题：不少设计师每天要花很长时间坐车，到了办公室已经很累；可是负责人林岚又担心，在家办公会影响讨论效率。她没有立刻改变全部制度，而是宣布试行一项新规则：员工每周可以选择两天在家办公，其余时间必须到工作室。
新规则开始后，多数员工都觉得时间安排更灵活了，但问题也很快出现。有一次，负责图片的周宁上午修改了方案，却没有及时通知负责文字的同事。下午开会时，大家才发现图片和文字表达的意思完全不同，只好重新调整。还有人因为没有看清任务的最后期限，差点造成交付延误。林岚发现，真正影响进度的并不是工作地点，而是信息没有及时交流。
为了减少误会，工作室在第二周补充了三条要求。第一，无论在哪里办公，每天上午十点到十一点都必须在线，方便团队集中讨论；第二，任何方案经过修改，都要在项目记录中说明原因；第三，如果当天无法完成任务，必须提前告诉合作同事。林岚还安排每周三全员到工作室见面，因为她认为，有些意见通过屏幕很难解释清楚，面对面交流仍然有必要。
一个月后，团队接到一家书店的设计项目。客户在交付前一天突然要求更换主要颜色，当天正好有两名设计师在家办公。按照新要求，项目负责人立刻更新了记录，并在共同在线的时间组织讨论。两名设计师分别处理图片和版面，办公室里的同事负责检查文字。虽然任务来得突然，大家却没有像以前那样反复确认，最后按时完成了修改。
试行满三个月后，林岚没有简单地宣布成功或失败，而是请员工写下最方便和最困难的地方。多数人希望保留居家办公，同时建议重要项目开始时必须当面讨论。林岚接受了这个建议，并决定继续试行。她认识到，灵活并不等于随便，管理也不只是要求员工坐在办公室，而是建立清楚的责任和可靠的信任。
pinyin: sān gè yuè qián ， qīng hé shè jì gōng zuò shì yù dào yí gè nán tí ： bù shǎo shè jì shī měi tiān yào huā hěn zhǎng shí jiān zuò chē ， dào le bàn gōng shì yǐ jīng hěn lèi ； kě shì fù zé rén lín lán yòu dān xīn ， zài jiā bàn gōng huì yǐng xiǎng tǎo lùn xiào lǜ 。 tā méi yǒu lì kè gǎi biàn quán bù zhì dù ， ér shì xuān bù shì xíng yī xiàng xīn guī zé ： yuán gōng měi zhōu kě yǐ xuǎn zé liǎng tiān zài jiā bàn gōng ， qí yú shí jiān bì xū dào gōng zuò shì 。

xīn guī zé kāi shǐ hòu ， duō shù yuán gōng dōu jué de shí jiān ān pái gèng líng huó le ， dàn wèn tí yě hěn kuài chū xiàn 。 yǒu yī cì ， fù zé tú piàn de zhōu níng shàng wǔ xiū gǎi le fāng àn ， què méi yǒu jí shí tōng zhī fù zé wén zì de tóng shì 。 xià wǔ kāi huì shí ， dà jiā cái fā xiàn tú piàn hé wén zì biǎo dá de yì si wán quán bù tóng ， zhǐ hǎo chóng xīn tiáo zhěng 。 hái yǒu rén yīn wèi méi yǒu kàn qīng rèn wù de zuì hòu qī xiàn ， chà diǎn zào chéng jiāo fù yán wù 。 lín lán fā xiàn ， zhēn zhèng yǐng xiǎng jìn dù de bìng bú shì gōng zuò dì diǎn ， ér shì xìn xī méi yǒu jí shí jiāo liú 。

wèi le jiǎn shǎo wù huì ， gōng zuò shì zài dì èr zhōu bǔ chōng le sān tiáo yāo qiú 。 dì yī ， wú lùn zài nǎ lǐ bàn gōng ， měi tiān shàng wǔ shí diǎn dào shí yì diǎn dōu bì xū zài xiàn ， fāng biàn tuán duì jí zhōng tǎo lùn ； dì èr ， rèn hé fāng àn jīng guò xiū gǎi ， dōu yào zài xiàng mù jì lù zhōng shuō míng yuán yīn ； dì sān ， rú guǒ dàng tiān wú fǎ wán chéng rèn wù ， bì xū tí qián gào sù hé zuò tóng shì 。 lín lán hái ān pái měi zhōu sān quán yuán dào gōng zuò shì jiàn miàn ， yīn wèi tā rèn wéi ， yǒu xiē yì jiàn tōng guò píng mù hěn nán jiě shì qīng chǔ ， miàn duì miàn jiāo liú réng rán yǒu bì yào 。

yí gè yuè hòu ， tuán duì jiē dào yī jiā shū diàn de shè jì xiàng mù 。 kè hù zài jiāo fù qián yī tiān tū rán yāo qiú gēng huàn zhǔ yào yán sè ， dàng tiān zhèng hǎo yǒu liǎng míng shè jì shī zài jiā bàn gōng 。 àn zhào xīn yāo qiú ， xiàng mù fù zé rén lì kè gēng xīn le jì lù ， bìng zài gòng tóng zài xiàn de shí jiān zǔ zhī tǎo lùn 。 liǎng míng shè jì shī fēn bié chǔ lǐ tú piàn hé bǎn miàn ， bàn gōng shì lǐ de tóng shì fù zé jiǎn chá wén zì 。 suī rán rèn wù lái de tū rán ， dà jiā què méi yǒu xiàng yǐ qián nà yàng fǎn fù què rèn ， zuì hòu àn shí wán chéng le xiū gǎi 。

shì xíng mǎn sān gè yuè hòu ， lín lán méi yǒu jiǎn dān dì xuān bù chéng gōng huò shī bài ， ér shì qǐng yuán gōng xiě xià zuì fāng biàn hé zuì kùn nán de dì fāng 。 duō shù rén xī wàng bǎo liú jū jiā bàn gōng ， tóng shí jiàn yì zhòng yào xiàng mù kāi shǐ shí bì xū dāng miàn tǎo lùn 。 lín lán jiē shòu le zhè ge jiàn yì ， bìng jué dìng jì xù shì xíng 。 tā rèn shí dào ， líng huó bìng bù děng yú suí biàn ， guǎn lǐ yě bù zhǐ shì yāo qiú yuán gōng zuò zài bàn gōng shì ， ér shì jiàn lì qīng chǔ de zé rèn hé kě kào de xìn rèn 。
translation: Three months ago, Qinghe Design Studio faced a difficult problem. Many designers spent a long time commuting each day and were already tired when they reached the office, but the manager, Lin Lan, worried that working from home would reduce the efficiency of discussions. Instead of changing the entire system immediately, she announced a trial rule: employees could choose to work from home two days a week but had to come to the studio on the other days.

After the new rule began, most employees felt that their schedules had become more flexible, but problems soon appeared. On one occasion, Zhou Ning, who was responsible for the images, revised the proposal in the morning but did not promptly inform the colleague responsible for the text. Only during the afternoon meeting did everyone discover that the images and text expressed completely different ideas, so they had to make adjustments again. Someone else almost caused a delivery delay because they had not clearly noticed the task deadline. Lin Lan realized that what truly affected progress was not the workplace but the failure to communicate information promptly.

To reduce misunderstandings, the studio added three requirements in the second week. First, regardless of where employees worked, they had to be online from ten to eleven every morning so that the team could hold focused discussions. Second, whenever a proposal was revised, the reason had to be explained in the project record. Third, anyone unable to finish a task that day had to inform their colleagues in advance. Lin Lan also arranged for everyone to meet at the studio every Wednesday because she believed that some opinions were difficult to explain clearly through a screen and that face-to-face communication was still necessary.

One month later, the team received a design project from a bookstore. The day before delivery, the client suddenly requested a change to the main color, and two designers happened to be working from home that day. Following the new requirements, the project manager immediately updated the record and organized a discussion during the shared online period. The two designers handled the images and page layout separately, while colleagues in the office checked the text. Although the request was sudden, the team did not repeatedly seek confirmation as they had before, and they completed the revisions on time.

After the three-month trial, Lin Lan did not simply declare it a success or failure. Instead, she asked the employees to write down what they found most convenient and most difficult. Most wanted to retain the option of working from home while suggesting that important projects should begin with an in-person discussion. Lin Lan accepted this suggestion and decided to continue the trial. She realized that flexibility does not mean acting without rules, and that management is not merely about requiring employees to sit in an office, but about establishing clear responsibilities and dependable trust.

articles.title: 溪桥社区学校的教室预约实验
articles.summary: 溪桥社区学校通过短期试行，分别改进教师预约教室和居民报名课程的流程，并在听取不同使用者的意见后保留了必要的灵活安排。
articles.topic: 溪桥社区学校的教室预约实验
paragraphs: 溪桥社区学校白天为孩子提供课后活动，晚上则向居民开放书法、舞蹈和手工课程。过去，教师只要在办公室登记，就可以使用空教室。随着课程增加，同一间教室有时会被两位教师同时安排。有些课程临时取消，负责人却没有及时通知，想参加活动的居民到了学校才发现白跑一趟。学校因此决定试行新的预约规则。
这是一则用于分级阅读的教学案例，其中的安排和结果不代表真实政策或正式统计。校长没有立刻限制课程数量，而是邀请教师、居民代表和管理人员组成小组。小组先查看一个月内的登记记录，又分别询问老人、家长和年轻学员。大家最关心的不是谁有优先权，而是怎样减少冲突，同时保留临时开展活动的可能。
新规则试行三个星期。教师预约教室时，需要提前两天提交申请，写明课程时间、参加人数和所需设备。如果无法上课，最迟应在当天中午取消。空出的教室会优先提供给候补名单中的教师，其他教师也可以申请使用。居民则可以通过手机页面报名参加课程。为了应对突然增加的公益讲座，学校还保留了一间活动室，由值班人员根据实际情况安排。这样既建立了基本秩序，也没有把所有选择都固定下来。
试行第一周就出现了意外。几位老人不会使用手机上的课程报名页面，误以为自己不能再参加课程。学校发现问题后，没有要求他们必须学习手机操作，而是在门口增加纸质报名表，并请学生志愿者提供帮助。另一位陶艺教师因为送材料的车辆迟到，无法按时布置教室。值班人员了解情况后，把他的课程推迟半小时，而没有直接取消。虽然新的管理方式提高了效率，但现场判断仍然十分重要。
试行三个星期后，小组整理了这一阶段的观察结果。教室冲突比以前少，取消消息也能更快传给居民；不过，纸质报名和网络报名之间偶尔还会出现重复记录。居民代表建议继续试行，同时安排一名工作人员每天核对两种报名记录。校长接受了这个建议，把试行期延长一个月，并决定暂时保留人工服务。这次实验的结果不是制定一套永远不变的规定，而是让学校明白：规则只有照顾不同人的实际困难，才可能得到长期支持。
pinyin: xī qiáo shè qū xué xiào bái tiān wèi hái zi tí gōng kè hòu huó dòng ， wǎn shàng zé xiàng jū mín kāi fàng shū fǎ 、 wǔ dǎo hé shǒu gōng kè chéng 。 guò qù ， jiào shī zhǐ yào zài bàn gōng shì dēng jì ， jiù kě yǐ shǐ yòng kōng jiào shì 。 suí zhe kè chéng zēng jiā ， tóng yī jiān jiào shì yǒu shí huì bèi liǎng wèi jiào shī tóng shí ān pái 。 yǒu xiē kè chéng lín shí qǔ xiāo ， fù zé rén què méi yǒu jí shí tōng zhī ， xiǎng cān jiā huó dòng de jū mín dào le xué xiào cái fā xiàn bái pǎo yī tàng 。 xué xiào yīn cǐ jué dìng shì xíng xīn de yù yuē guī zé 。

zhè shì yī zé yòng yú fēn jí yuè dú de jiào xué àn lì ， qí zhōng de ān pái hé jié guǒ bù dài biǎo zhēn shí zhèng cè huò zhèng shì tǒng jì 。 xiào zhǎng méi yǒu lì kè xiàn zhì kè chéng shù liàng ， ér shì yāo qǐng jiào shī 、 jū mín dài biǎo hé guǎn lǐ rén yuán zǔ chéng xiǎo zǔ 。 xiǎo zǔ xiān chá kàn yí gè yuè nèi de dēng jì jì lù ， yòu fēn bié xún wèn lǎo rén 、 jiā zhǎng hé nián qīng xué yuán 。 dà jiā zuì guān xīn de bú shì shuí yǒu yōu xiān quán ， ér shì zěn yàng jiǎn shǎo chōng tū ， tóng shí bǎo liú lín shí kāi zhǎn huó dòng de kě néng 。

xīn guī zé shì xíng sān gè xīng qī 。 jiào shī yù yuē jiào shì shí ， xū yào tí qián liǎng tiān tí jiāo shēn qǐng ， xiě míng kè chéng shí jiān 、 cān jiā rén shù hé suǒ xū shè bèi 。 rú guǒ wú fǎ shàng kè ， zuì chí yīng zài dàng tiān zhōng wǔ qǔ xiāo 。 kòng chū de jiào shì huì yōu xiān tí gōng gěi hòu bǔ míng dān zhōng de jiào shī ， qí tā jiào shī yě kě yǐ shēn qǐng shǐ yòng 。 jū mín zé kě yǐ tōng guò shǒu jī yè miàn bào míng cān jiā kè chéng 。 wèi le yìng duì tū rán zēng jiā de gōng yì jiǎng zuò ， xué xiào hái bǎo liú le yī jiān huó dòng shì ， yóu zhí bān rén yuán gēn jù shí jì qíng kuàng ān pái 。 zhè yàng jì jiàn lì le jī běn zhì xù ， yě méi yǒu bǎ suǒ yǒu xuǎn zé dōu gù dìng xià lái 。

shì xíng dì yī zhōu jiù chū xiàn le yì wài 。 jǐ wèi lǎo rén bú huì shǐ yòng shǒu jī shàng de kè chéng bào míng yè miàn ， wù yǐ wéi zì jǐ bù néng zài cān jiā kè chéng 。 xué xiào fā xiàn wèn tí hòu ， méi yǒu yāo qiú tā men bì xū xué xí shǒu jī cāo zuò ， ér shì zài mén kǒu zēng jiā zhǐ zhì bào míng biǎo ， bìng qǐng xué shēng zhì yuàn zhě tí gōng bāng zhù 。 lìng yī wèi táo yì jiào shī yīn wèi sòng cái liào de chē liàng chí dào ， wú fǎ àn shí bù zhì jiào shì 。 zhí bān rén yuán liǎo jiě qíng kuàng hòu ， bǎ tā de kè chéng tuī chí bàn xiǎo shí ， ér méi yǒu zhí jiē qǔ xiāo 。 suī rán xīn de guǎn lǐ fāng shì tí gāo le xiào lǜ ， dàn xiàn chǎng pàn duàn réng rán shí fēn zhòng yào 。

shì xíng sān gè xīng qī hòu ， xiǎo zǔ zhěng lǐ le zhè yī jiē duàn de guān chá jié guǒ 。 jiào shì chōng tū bǐ yǐ qián shǎo ， qǔ xiāo xiāo xī yě néng gèng kuài chuán gěi jū mín ； bù guò ， zhǐ zhì bào míng hé wǎng luò bào míng zhī jiān ǒu ěr hái huì chū xiàn chóng fù jì lù 。 jū mín dài biǎo jiàn yì jì xù shì xíng ， tóng shí ān pái yī míng gōng zuò rén yuán měi tiān hé duì liǎng zhǒng bào míng jì lù 。 xiào zhǎng jiē shòu le zhè ge jiàn yì ， bǎ shì xíng qī yán cháng yí gè yuè ， bìng jué dìng zàn shí bǎo liú rén gōng fú wù 。 zhè cì shí yàn de jié guǒ bú shì zhì dìng yī tào yǒng yuǎn bù biàn de guī dìng ， ér shì ràng xué xiào míng bái ： guī zé zhǐ yǒu zhào gù bù tóng rén de shí jì kùn nán ， cái kě néng dé dào cháng qī zhī chí 。
translation: Xiqiao Community School provides after-school activities for children during the day and opens calligraphy, dance, and handicraft classes to residents in the evening. In the past, teachers could use an empty classroom simply by registering at the office. As the number of classes grew, the same classroom was sometimes assigned to two teachers. Some classes were canceled at short notice, but the person in charge failed to inform people in time, so residents arrived at the school only to find that they had made the trip for nothing. The school therefore decided to test new reservation rules.

This is a teaching case created for graded reading, and its arrangements and results do not represent real policies or official statistics. Instead of immediately limiting the number of classes, the principal invited teachers, resident representatives, and administrators to form a group. The group first reviewed registration records from one month and then spoke separately with older residents, parents, and younger learners. Their greatest concern was not who should have priority, but how to reduce conflicts while preserving the possibility of organizing activities at short notice.

The new rules were tested for three weeks. When reserving classrooms, teachers had to submit applications two days in advance and state the class time, number of participants, and required equipment. If a class could not take place, it had to be canceled by noon that day at the latest. Vacated classrooms would first be offered to teachers on the waiting list, and other teachers could also apply to use them. Residents, meanwhile, could sign up for classes through a mobile webpage. To accommodate public-interest lectures added at short notice, the school also kept one activity room available for the staff member on duty to assign according to actual circumstances. In this way, the school established basic order without fixing every choice in advance.

An unexpected problem appeared during the first week of the trial. Several older residents did not know how to use the class registration page on their phones and mistakenly thought they could no longer attend classes. After discovering the problem, the school did not require them to learn how to operate a phone. Instead, it added a paper registration form at the entrance and asked student volunteers to provide assistance. A pottery teacher was unable to prepare his classroom on time because the vehicle delivering his materials was late. After learning what had happened, the staff member on duty postponed his class by half an hour instead of canceling it. Although the new management system improved efficiency, judgment at the scene remained very important.

At the end of the three-week trial, the group compiled its findings. Classroom conflicts occurred less often than before, and cancellation notices reached residents more quickly. However, duplicate entries still occasionally occurred across the paper and online registration systems. The resident representatives suggested continuing the trial and assigning a staff member to check the two sets of registration records every day. The principal accepted the suggestion, extended the trial for another month, and decided to retain in-person assistance for the time being. The result of the experiment was not a set of rules that would never change, but a lesson for the school: rules can gain long-term support only when they take different people's practical difficulties into account.

articles.title: 一张暂离卡带来的改变
articles.summary: 市图书馆针对读者长时间占座的问题，在部分区域试行暂离卡制度，并根据现场意见调整规则。
articles.topic: 一张暂离卡带来的改变
paragraphs: 去年秋天，市图书馆收到不少关于占座的意见。有些读者把书包放在桌上，离开一两个小时，其他人虽然找不到座位，却不敢移动别人的物品。工作人员过去只能口头提醒，但判断读者是暂时离开还是已经回家并不容易。有人建议直接清理所有无人使用的座位，也有人担心这样会拿错私人物品。
图书馆没有立刻把新规定用于全部楼层，而是先选择二楼阅览区进行为期三周的试行。工作人员在入口处发放暂离卡，并向读者解释使用方法：需要短时间离开时，应在卡片上写下离开时间，放在桌面明显的位置。超过四十分钟仍未返回，工作人员才会把物品移到服务台保管。
试行的第一周并不顺利。有位老人不会填写卡片，以为只要把卡压在书下就可以；一名学生去食堂排队，回来时已经超过规定时间，发现自己的电脑被送到了服务台。这名学生非常生气，认为四十分钟太短。值班人员没有急着争论，而是请这名学生说明当天的情况，同时记录了午餐时间排队较长的问题。
几天后，图书馆邀请不同年龄的读者参加讨论。大家认为，规则既不能因为个别人的不满就取消，也不能忽视读者实际遇到的困难。工作人员因此作出调整：午餐时段的暂离时间增加到一小时，其他时间仍保持四十分钟；不会写字或看不清卡片的读者，可以请服务台代为填写。
在这份教学案例的阶段观察中，试行后无人使用却放着物品的座位明显减少，因占座引起的争吵也比以前少。不过，工作人员发现，靠近窗户的热门座位仍有人故意写错离开时间。为了解决这个问题，他们开始每隔一段时间在卡片上盖章，而不是完全依靠读者自己填写的信息。这里提到的变化只用于说明试行过程，并不代表真实城市的统计结果。
三周结束后，图书馆没有宣布这项规定将长期不变。负责人把读者意见、现场记录和工作人员的建议整理成报告，决定先修改卡片设计，再把试行范围扩大到另一个楼层。对图书馆来说，试行的意义不只是判断一条规则是否有效，更重要的是在正式采用之前发现问题，并给受到影响的人留下表达意见的机会。
pinyin: qù nián qiū tiān ， shì tú shū guǎn shōu dào bù shǎo guān yú zhàn zuò de yì jiàn 。 yǒu xiē dú zhě bǎ shū bāo fàng zài zhuō shàng ， lí kāi yī liǎng gè xiǎo shí ， qí tā rén suī rán zhǎo bú dào zuò wèi ， què bù gǎn yí dòng bié rén de wù pǐn 。 gōng zuò rén yuán guò qù zhǐ néng kǒu tóu tí xǐng ， dàn pàn duàn dú zhě shì zàn shí lí kāi hái shì yǐ jīng huí jiā bìng bù róng yì 。 yǒu rén jiàn yì zhí jiē qīng lǐ suǒ yǒu wú rén shǐ yòng de zuò wèi ， yě yǒu rén dān xīn zhè yàng huì ná cuò sī rén wù pǐn 。

tú shū guǎn méi yǒu lì kè bǎ xīn guī dìng yòng yú quán bù lóu céng ， ér shì xiān xuǎn zé èr lóu yuè lǎn qū jìn xíng wéi qī sān zhōu de shì xíng 。 gōng zuò rén yuán zài rù kǒu chù fā fàng zàn lí kǎ ， bìng xiàng dú zhě jiě shì shǐ yòng fāng fǎ ： xū yào duǎn shí jiān lí kāi shí ， yīng zài kǎ piàn shàng xiě xià lí kāi shí jiān ， fàng zài zhuō miàn míng xiǎn de wèi zhì 。 chāo guò sì shí fēn zhōng réng wèi fǎn huí ， gōng zuò rén yuán cái huì bǎ wù pǐn yí dào fú wù tái bǎo guǎn 。

shì xíng de dì yī zhōu bìng bù shùn lì 。 yǒu wèi lǎo rén bú huì tián xiě kǎ piàn ， yǐ wéi zhǐ yào bǎ kǎ yā zài shū xià jiù kě yǐ ； yī míng xué shēng qù shí táng pái duì ， huí lái shí yǐ jīng chāo guò guī dìng shí jiān ， fā xiàn zì jǐ de diàn nǎo bèi sòng dào le fú wù tái 。 zhè míng xué shēng fēi cháng shēng qì ， rèn wéi sì shí fēn zhōng tài duǎn 。 zhí bān rén yuán méi yǒu jí zhe zhēng lùn ， ér shì qǐng zhè míng xué shēng shuō míng dàng tiān de qíng kuàng ， tóng shí jì lù le wǔ cān shí jiān pái duì jiào zhǎng de wèn tí 。

jǐ tiān hòu ， tú shū guǎn yāo qǐng bù tóng nián líng de dú zhě cān jiā tǎo lùn 。 dà jiā rèn wéi ， guī zé jì bù néng yīn wèi gè bié rén de bù mǎn jiù qǔ xiāo ， yě bù néng hū shì dú zhě shí jì yù dào de kùn nán 。 gōng zuò rén yuán yīn cǐ zuò chū tiáo zhěng ： wǔ cān shí duàn de zàn lí shí jiān zēng jiā dào yī xiǎo shí ， qí tā shí jiān réng bǎo chí sì shí fēn zhōng ； bú huì xiě zì huò kàn bù qīng kǎ piàn de dú zhě ， kě yǐ qǐng fú wù tái dài wéi tián xiě 。

zài zhè fèn jiào xué àn lì de jiē duàn guān chá zhōng ， shì xíng hòu wú rén shǐ yòng què fàng zhe wù pǐn de zuò wèi míng xiǎn jiǎn shǎo ， yīn zhàn zuò yǐn qǐ de zhēng chǎo yě bǐ yǐ qián shǎo 。 bù guò ， gōng zuò rén yuán fā xiàn ， kào jìn chuāng hù de rè mén zuò wèi réng yǒu rén gù yì xiě cuò lí kāi shí jiān 。 wèi le jiě jué zhè ge wèn tí ， tā men kāi shǐ měi gé yī duàn shí jiān zài kǎ piàn shàng gài zhāng ， ér bú shì wán quán yī kào dú zhě zì jǐ tián xiě de xìn xī 。 zhè lǐ tí dào de biàn huà zhǐ yòng yú shuō míng shì xíng guò chéng ， bìng bù dài biǎo zhēn shí chéng shì de tǒng jì jié guǒ 。

sān zhōu jié shù hòu ， tú shū guǎn méi yǒu xuān bù zhè xiàng guī dìng jiāng cháng qī bù biàn 。 fù zé rén bǎ dú zhě yì jiàn 、 xiàn chǎng jì lù hé gōng zuò rén yuán de jiàn yì zhěng lǐ chéng bào gào ， jué dìng xiān xiū gǎi kǎ piàn shè jì ， zài bǎ shì xíng fàn wéi kuò dà dào lìng yí gè lóu céng 。 duì tú shū guǎn lái shuō ， shì xíng de yì yì bù zhǐ shì pàn duàn yī tiáo guī zé shì fǒu yǒu xiào ， gèng zhòng yào de shì zài zhèng shì cǎi yòng zhī qián fā xiàn wèn tí ， bìng gěi shòu dào yǐng xiǎng de rén liú xià biǎo dá yì jiàn de jī huì 。
translation: Last autumn, the city library received many comments about people occupying seats. Some readers left their bags on desks and went away for one or two hours. Although others could not find a seat, they did not dare move someone else's belongings. In the past, staff could only give verbal reminders, but it was not easy to determine whether a reader had stepped away briefly or had already gone home. Some people suggested clearing every unattended seat immediately, while others worried that personal belongings might be taken by mistake.

The library did not immediately apply the new rule to every floor. Instead, it selected the second-floor reading area for a three-week trial. Staff handed out temporary-leave cards at the entrance and explained how to use them: readers who needed to leave briefly should write down their departure time and place the card where it could easily be seen on the desk. Only when a reader had been away for more than forty minutes would staff move the belongings to the service desk for safekeeping.

The first week of the trial did not go smoothly. An elderly reader did not know how to fill out the card and thought it was enough to place it under a book. A student went to line up at the cafeteria and returned after the permitted time, only to discover that their computer had been taken to the service desk. The student was very angry and believed that forty minutes was too short. The staff member on duty did not rush into an argument, but asked the student to explain what had happened that day and recorded the problem of long lunchtime lines.

A few days later, the library invited readers of different ages to join a discussion. Everyone agreed that the rule should not be canceled simply because a few people were dissatisfied, nor should the practical difficulties readers faced be ignored. The staff therefore made an adjustment: during lunchtime, the permitted leave time was extended to one hour, while at other times it remained forty minutes. Readers who could not write or see the card clearly could ask the service desk to fill it out for them.

According to the interim observations in this educational case, after the trial began, the number of seats left unused while still holding belongings clearly decreased, and arguments caused by seat occupation also became less frequent. However, staff discovered that some people still deliberately wrote incorrect departure times for the popular seats near the windows. To address this problem, staff began stamping the cards at intervals instead of relying entirely on information filled in by readers. The changes mentioned here are used only to illustrate the trial process and do not represent statistical results from any real city.

When the three weeks ended, the library did not announce that the rule would remain unchanged in the long term. The person in charge organized reader comments, on-site records, and staff suggestions into a report, and decided to revise the card design before expanding the trial to another floor. For the library, the purpose of a trial was not merely to judge whether a rule was effective. More importantly, it allowed problems to be discovered before formal adoption and gave affected people an opportunity to express their views.

articles.title: 三个人怎样调整周末班次
articles.summary: 一则管理教学案例：物流中心试行周末换班规则，并在实际安排中发现休息时间与班次公平问题。
articles.topic: 三个人怎样换成了周末班
paragraphs: 东河物流中心周末的包裹通常比平日多，可是一些员工也常在周末遇到照顾孩子、参加考试等安排。过去，谁临时不能上班，就得先找主管说明，再由主管逐个打电话找人替班。这个过程既慢，又容易让同一批员工总被叫来加班。下面的内容是一则用于语言学习的管理教学案例，并非真实企业的调查报告。
为减少临时请假带来的混乱，中心在四月试行了“周末换班”规则。员工可以在内部系统里公开自己想换出的班次，并写清愿意接受的时间。只要双方工作岗位相同、休息时间符合要求，就可以提出交换申请。不过，申请必须在上班前一天中午以前交给主管确认，员工不能私下换完就算了。
第一周，负责检查包裹的林晓准备参加职业考试，想把星期六上午的班换到星期日。她在系统中发出申请后，夜班员工周海主动联系了她。周海星期日要陪父亲去医院，正好需要星期六的班。两人很快谈妥，但主管检查时发现，周海刚上完星期五夜班，如果第二天一早继续工作，休息时间就不够。
主管没有直接拒绝，而是建议他们把交换范围扩大。后来，另一名员工陈杰接下林晓的星期六班，林晓替周海上星期日的班，周海则在下周替陈杰值一次班。三个人重新提交申请，系统也分别提醒了新的工作时间。这次安排没有违反休息时间规定，林晓和周海原来的周末计划也都保住了，陈杰的调班也在下周得到补偿。
试行期间还出现了一个问题：热门班次很快有人接受，较累的深夜班却常常无人愿意交换。有人建议给接深夜班的人额外奖金，主管没有马上同意，因为换班的目的不是鼓励大家长期多工作。他在公告中补充说明，每人每月最多交换两次；如果一个班次始终找不到人，仍由主管按照原来的办法协调。
一个月后，中心根据排班记录开了总结会。材料中的阶段观察显示，临时打电话找人的情况减少了，员工也能更早安排个人事情。不过，大家认为新规则能否继续，不能只看申请数量，还要看包裹检查是否准时、员工是否得到足够休息。中心因此决定再试行一个月，并邀请员工提出更简单的操作建议。
pinyin: dōng hé wù liú zhōng xīn zhōu mò de bāo guǒ tōng cháng bǐ píng rì duō ， kě shì yī xiē yuán gōng yě cháng zài zhōu mò yù dào zhào gù hái zi 、 cān jiā kǎo shì děng ān pái 。 guò qù ， shuí lín shí bù néng shàng bān ， jiù dé xiān zhǎo zhǔ guǎn shuō míng ， zài yóu zhǔ guǎn zhú gè dǎ diàn huà zhǎo rén tì bān 。 zhè ge guò chéng jì màn ， yòu róng yì ràng tóng yī pī yuán gōng zǒng bèi jiào lái jiā bān 。 xià miàn de nèi róng shì yī zé yòng yú yǔ yán xué xí de guǎn lǐ jiào xué àn lì ， bìng fēi zhēn shí qǐ yè de diào chá bào gào 。

wèi jiǎn shǎo lín shí qǐng jià dài lái de hùn luàn ， zhōng xīn zài sì yuè shì xíng le “ zhōu mò huàn bān ” guī zé 。 yuán gōng kě yǐ zài nèi bù xì tǒng lǐ gōng kāi zì jǐ xiǎng huàn chū de bān cì ， bìng xiě qīng yuàn yì jiē shòu de shí jiān 。 zhǐ yào shuāng fāng gōng zuò gǎng wèi xiāng tóng 、 xiū xī shí jiān fú hé yāo qiú ， jiù kě yǐ tí chū jiāo huàn shēn qǐng 。 bù guò ， shēn qǐng bì xū zài shàng bān qián yī tiān zhōng wǔ yǐ qián jiāo gěi zhǔ guǎn què rèn ， yuán gōng bù néng sī xià huàn wán jiù suàn le 。

dì yī zhōu ， fù zé jiǎn chá bāo guǒ de lín xiǎo zhǔn bèi cān jiā zhí yè kǎo shì ， xiǎng bǎ xīng qī liù shàng wǔ de bān huàn dào xīng qī rì 。 tā zài xì tǒng zhōng fā chū shēn qǐng hòu ， yè bān yuán gōng zhōu hǎi zhǔ dòng lián xì le tā 。 zhōu hǎi xīng qī rì yào péi fù qīn qù yī yuàn ， zhèng hǎo xū yào xīng qī liù de bān 。 liǎng rén hěn kuài tán tuǒ ， dàn zhǔ guǎn jiǎn chá shí fā xiàn ， zhōu hǎi gāng shàng wán xīng qī wǔ yè bān ， rú guǒ dì èr tiān yī zǎo jì xù gōng zuò ， xiū xī shí jiān jiù bù gòu 。

zhǔ guǎn méi yǒu zhí jiē jù jué ， ér shì jiàn yì tā men bǎ jiāo huàn fàn wéi kuò dà 。 hòu lái ， lìng yī míng yuán gōng chén jié jiē xià lín xiǎo de xīng qī liù bān ， lín xiǎo tì zhōu hǎi shàng xīng qī rì de bān ， zhōu hǎi zé zài xià zhōu tì chén jié zhí yī cì bān 。 sān gè rén chóng xīn tí jiāo shēn qǐng ， xì tǒng yě fēn bié tí xǐng le xīn de gōng zuò shí jiān 。 zhè cì ān pái méi yǒu wéi fǎn xiū xī shí jiān guī dìng ， lín xiǎo hé zhōu hǎi yuán lái de zhōu mò jì huà yě dōu bǎo zhù le ， chén jié de diào bān yě zài xià zhōu dé dào bǔ cháng 。

shì xíng qī jiān hái chū xiàn le yí gè wèn tí ： rè mén bān cì hěn kuài yǒu rén jiē shòu ， jiào lèi de shēn yè bān què cháng cháng wú rén yuàn yì jiāo huàn 。 yǒu rén jiàn yì gěi jiē shēn yè bān de rén é wài jiǎng jīn ， zhǔ guǎn méi yǒu mǎ shàng tóng yì ， yīn wèi huàn bān de mù dì bú shì gǔ lì dà jiā cháng qī duō gōng zuò 。 tā zài gōng gào zhōng bǔ chōng shuō míng ， měi rén měi yuè zuì duō jiāo huàn liǎng cì ； rú guǒ yí gè bān cì shǐ zhōng zhǎo bú dào rén ， réng yóu zhǔ guǎn àn zhào yuán lái de bàn fǎ xié tiáo 。

yí gè yuè hòu ， zhōng xīn gēn jù pái bān jì lù kāi le zǒng jié huì 。 cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， lín shí dǎ diàn huà zhǎo rén de qíng kuàng jiǎn shǎo le ， yuán gōng yě néng gèng zǎo ān pái gè rén shì qíng 。 bù guò ， dà jiā rèn wéi xīn guī zé néng fǒu jì xù ， bù néng zhǐ kàn shēn qǐng shù liàng ， hái yào kàn bāo guǒ jiǎn chá shì fǒu zhǔn shí 、 yuán gōng shì fǒu dé dào zú gòu xiū xī 。 zhōng xīn yīn cǐ jué dìng zài shì xíng yí gè yuè ， bìng yāo qǐng yuán gōng tí chū gèng jiǎn dān de cāo zuò jiàn yì 。
translation: Weekend parcel volume at Donghe Logistics Center is usually higher than on weekdays, but some employees also need to care for children, take exams, or handle other plans on weekends. In the past, anyone who could not work at short notice had to explain the situation to a supervisor, who would then call employees one by one to find a replacement. This process was slow and often resulted in the same group of employees repeatedly being asked to work overtime. The following is a management case created for language learning, not a research report about a real company.

To reduce the confusion caused by last-minute leave, the center began testing a weekend shift-exchange rule in April. Employees could post the shift they wanted to give up in an internal system and specify the times they were willing to accept. As long as both employees held the same type of position and the arrangement met rest-time requirements, they could submit an exchange request. However, the request had to be sent to a supervisor for approval before noon on the day before work; employees could not simply make a private exchange and consider the matter settled.

During the first week, Lin Xiao, who inspected parcels, was preparing to take a professional exam and wanted to exchange her Saturday morning shift for a Sunday shift. After she posted the request in the system, night-shift employee Zhou Hai contacted her. Zhou Hai needed to accompany his father to the hospital on Sunday, so he happened to need the Saturday shift. They quickly reached an agreement, but when the supervisor reviewed it, he discovered that Zhou Hai would have just finished a Friday night shift, and working again early the next morning would not leave him enough rest time.

The supervisor did not reject the request immediately but suggested that they widen the exchange arrangement. Later, another employee, Chen Jie, took Lin Xiao's Saturday shift, Lin Xiao took Zhou Hai's Sunday shift, and Zhou Hai agreed to cover one of Chen Jie's shifts the following week. The three employees submitted a new request, and the system separately reminded each of them about the revised work times. This arrangement did not violate the rest-time regulations, and Lin Xiao and Zhou Hai were able to keep their original weekend plans, while Chen Jie's shift change was offset the following week.

Another problem appeared during the trial: popular shifts were accepted quickly, while tiring late-night shifts often had no willing takers. Someone suggested giving an additional bonus to employees who accepted late-night shifts, but the supervisor did not agree immediately because the purpose of exchanging shifts was not to encourage people to work extra hours for long periods. He added a notice stating that each employee could make no more than two exchanges per month; if no one could ultimately be found to take a shift, the supervisor would still coordinate it using the previous method.

After one month, the center held a review meeting based on the scheduling records. The interim observations in the case materials showed that fewer last-minute calls were needed to find replacement workers and that employees could plan personal matters earlier. However, everyone believed that the future of the new rule should not be judged only by the number of requests; they also needed to consider whether parcel inspections were completed on time and whether employees received enough rest. The center therefore decided to continue the trial for another month and invited employees to suggest ways to simplify the process.

articles.title: 屏幕另一边的复诊
articles.summary: 一家医院在教学案例中试行视频复诊，并通过一位患者的经历发现新规则带来的便利、限制与改进方向。
articles.topic: 屏幕另一边的复诊
paragraphs: 在这篇教学案例中，三个月前，青河医院门诊部开始试行一项新规则：病情稳定、已经在本院看过病的部分患者，可以通过视频完成复诊。过去，这些患者即使只想让医生查看检查结果，也必须到医院重新排队。新办法希望减少不必要的往返，同时把现场的时间留给更需要检查和治疗的人。
新规则并不是让所有病人都在网上看病。患者提出申请后，护士会先查看病历，判断他是否适合视频复诊。第一次就诊、突然出现严重症状或者需要医生动手检查的患者，仍然必须到医院。申请通过的人要提前上传检查报告，并在约定时间进入视频诊室。医生如果发现情况不适合继续远程判断，也会立即要求患者来院检查。
周女士经营一家面包店，需要长期服药控制血压。以前每次复诊，她都得请店员替班，再乘一个多小时的公共汽车去医院。第一次使用视频复诊时，她提前拍下最近一周的血压记录，却忘了上传药盒照片。医生无法确认药品的具体规格，只能请她去找药盒。周女士在家里找了十分钟，视频时间因此被延长，后面的患者也受到了一点影响。
这次经历让门诊部发现，流程虽然方便，准备说明却不够清楚。第二周，护士把原来的一页文字通知改成了简单的步骤表，提醒患者准备身份证、检查报告、用药记录和药盒。系统还会在复诊前一天自动发送消息，让患者测试网络和声音。只要材料齐全，医生就能把更多时间用来了解病情变化，而不是反复询问信息。
根据案例材料中的阶段观察，多数符合条件的患者愿意继续使用这种方式，但年纪较大或不熟悉手机的人仍可能需要家人帮助。医院因此保留了现场复诊，也安排工作人员提供操作指导。负责人认为，视频复诊的价值不在于完全代替面对面看病，而在于给患者增加一种合适的选择。规则是否真正有效，还要根据医疗安全、患者体验和实际问题不断调整。
pinyin: zài zhè piān jiào xué àn lì zhōng ， sān gè yuè qián ， qīng hé yī yuàn mén zhěn bù kāi shǐ shì xíng yī xiàng xīn guī zé ： bìng qíng wěn dìng 、 yǐ jīng zài běn yuàn kàn guò bìng de bù fèn huàn zhě ， kě yǐ tōng guò shì pín wán chéng fù zhěn 。 guò qù ， zhè xiē huàn zhě jí shǐ zhǐ xiǎng ràng yī shēng chá kàn jiǎn chá jié guǒ ， yě bì xū dào yī yuàn chóng xīn pái duì 。 xīn bàn fǎ xī wàng jiǎn shǎo bù bì yào de wǎng fǎn ， tóng shí bǎ xiàn chǎng de shí jiān liú gěi gèng xū yào jiǎn chá hé zhì liáo de rén 。

xīn guī zé bìng bú shì ràng suǒ yǒu bìng rén dōu zài wǎng shàng kàn bìng 。 huàn zhě tí chū shēn qǐng hòu ， hù shì huì xiān chá kàn bìng lì ， pàn duàn tā shì fǒu shì hé shì pín fù zhěn 。 dì yī cì jiù zhěn 、 tū rán chū xiàn yán zhòng zhèng zhuàng huò zhě xū yào yī shēng dòng shǒu jiǎn chá de huàn zhě ， réng rán bì xū dào yī yuàn 。 shēn qǐng tōng guò de rén yào tí qián shàng chuán jiǎn chá bào gào ， bìng zài yuē dìng shí jiān jìn rù shì pín zhěn shì 。 yī shēng rú guǒ fā xiàn qíng kuàng bú shì hé jì xù yuǎn chéng pàn duàn ， yě huì lì jí yāo qiú huàn zhě lái yuàn jiǎn chá 。

zhōu nǚ shì jīng yíng yī jiā miàn bāo diàn ， xū yào cháng qī fú yào kòng zhì xuè yā 。 yǐ qián měi cì fù zhěn ， tā dōu dé qǐng diàn yuán tì bān ， zài chéng yí gè duō xiǎo shí de gōng gòng qì chē qù yī yuàn 。 dì yī cì shǐ yòng shì pín fù zhěn shí ， tā tí qián pāi xià zuì jìn yī zhōu de xuè yā jì lù ， què wàng le shàng chuán yào hé zhào piān 。 yī shēng wú fǎ què rèn yào pǐn de jù tǐ guī gé ， zhǐ néng qǐng tā qù zhǎo yào hé 。 zhōu nǚ shì zài jiā lǐ zhǎo le shí fēn zhōng ， shì pín shí jiān yīn cǐ bèi yán cháng ， hòu miàn de huàn zhě yě shòu dào le yì diǎn yǐng xiǎng 。

zhè cì jīng lì ràng mén zhěn bù fā xiàn ， liú chéng suī rán fāng biàn ， zhǔn bèi shuō míng què bù gòu qīng chǔ 。 dì èr zhōu ， hù shì bǎ yuán lái de yī yè wén zì tōng zhī gǎi chéng le jiǎn dān de bù zhòu biǎo ， tí xǐng huàn zhě zhǔn bèi shēn fèn zhèng 、 jiǎn chá bào gào 、 yòng yào jì lù huò yào hé 。 xì tǒng hái huì zài fù zhěn qián yī tiān zì dòng fā sòng xiāo xī ， ràng huàn zhě cè shì wǎng luò hé shēng yīn 。 zhǐ yào cái liào qí quán ， yī shēng jiù néng bǎ gèng duō shí jiān yòng lái liǎo jiě bìng qíng biàn huà ， ér bú shì fǎn fù xún wèn xìn xī 。

gēn jù àn lì cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá ， duō shù fú hé tiáo jiàn de huàn zhě yuàn yì jì xù shǐ yòng zhè zhǒng fāng shì ， dàn nián jì jiào dà huò bù shú xī shǒu jī de rén réng kě néng xū yào jiā rén bāng zhù 。 yī yuàn yīn cǐ bǎo liú le xiàn chǎng fù zhěn ， yě ān pái gōng zuò rén yuán tí gōng cāo zuò zhǐ dǎo 。 fù zé rén rèn wéi ， shì pín fù zhěn de jià zhí bù zài yú wán quán dài tì miàn duì miàn kàn bìng ， ér zài yú gěi huàn zhě zēng jiā yī zhǒng hé shì de xuǎn zé 。 guī zé shì fǒu zhēn zhèng yǒu xiào ， hái yào gēn jù yī liáo ān quán 、 huàn zhě tǐ yàn hé shí jì wèn tí bù duàn tiáo zhěng 。
translation: In this teaching case, the outpatient department of Qinghe Hospital began testing a new rule three months ago: some patients whose conditions were stable and who had previously visited the hospital could complete follow-up consultations by video. In the past, even if these patients only wanted a doctor to review their test results, they still had to return to the hospital and wait in line. The new approach was intended to reduce unnecessary travel while reserving in-person appointment time for people who needed examinations and treatment more urgently.

The new rule did not mean that every patient could see a doctor online. After a patient submitted a request, a nurse first reviewed the medical record and decided whether the person was suitable for a video follow-up. Patients making their first visit, experiencing sudden serious symptoms, or requiring a physical examination still had to come to the hospital. Approved patients needed to upload their test reports in advance and enter the video consultation room at the scheduled time. If a doctor found that the situation was unsuitable for further remote assessment, the patient would immediately be asked to visit the hospital for an examination.

Ms. Zhou ran a bakery and needed long-term medication to control her blood pressure. In the past, she had to ask an employee to cover her shift and then take a bus for more than an hour whenever she had a follow-up appointment. During her first video follow-up, she photographed her blood pressure readings from the previous week in advance but forgot to upload a picture of the medicine package. The doctor could not confirm the exact specifications of the medicine and had to ask her to find the package. Ms. Zhou searched her home for ten minutes, which extended the video appointment and slightly affected the patients scheduled after her.

This experience helped the outpatient department realize that although the process was convenient, the preparation instructions were not clear enough. In the second week, the nurses replaced the original one-page written notice with a simple checklist, reminding patients to prepare their identification, test reports, medication records, and medicine packages. The system also automatically sent a message one day before the follow-up, asking patients to test their internet connection and sound. As long as the materials were complete, doctors could spend more time learning about changes in the patient's condition instead of repeatedly asking for information.

According to the interim observations described in the case materials, most eligible patients were willing to continue using this method, but older people or those unfamiliar with smartphones might still need help from family members. The hospital therefore kept in-person follow-up appointments and also assigned staff to provide technical guidance. The person in charge believed that the value of video follow-ups was not in completely replacing face-to-face medical visits, but in giving patients another suitable option. Whether the rule was truly effective would still require continuous adjustment based on medical safety, patient experience, and practical problems.
