articles.title: 积分柜台前的争论
articles.summary: 一个教学案例通过社区垃圾分类积分制度的调整，讨论物质奖励、公共责任与居民参与之间的关系。
articles.topic: 积分柜台前的争论
paragraphs: 以下故事是为分级阅读设计的教学案例。青岚社区曾在垃圾分类点旁设置积分柜台：居民把厨余、塑料和废纸正确投入不同容器后，可以登记积分，月底兑换肥皂、垃圾袋等生活用品。居委会原以为奖励能迅速培养习惯，起初参与人数确实增加，分类点前甚至排起了队。然而，热闹持续一段时间后，工作人员发现，有些居民只在礼品充足时出现，兑换结束便不再主动分类。
负责积分登记的周岚认为，问题不在奖励本身，而在执行方式。过去，居民无论处理多少垃圾，只要来一次就能得分，这让少数人把一袋废纸拆成几次投放。更麻烦的是，有人为了多得积分，从办公室带回大量包装盒，却没有清除盒内的胶带和污渍。表面上看，投放量上升了，后续分拣的负担却更重。周岚建议暂时降低礼品价值，并把分类准确程度列为主要标准。
这个建议遭到志愿者老魏反对。他担心奖励减少以后，刚刚建立的参与热情会迅速消失。在他看来，居民愿意改变原有习惯已经不容易，制度应当先鼓励行动，再逐步提高要求。如果一开始就检查得过于严格，人们可能会觉得分类既麻烦又容易出错。老魏还指出，不能因为少数人钻空子，就否定多数居民付出的时间。
双方争论不下，居委会没有急着作出选择，而是邀请不同年龄的居民参加讨论。一位年轻父亲说，孩子每次兑换礼品都很兴奋，但更值得肯定的是，孩子开始主动研究各种包装属于哪类垃圾。一位独居老人则坦率地表示，复杂的积分规则令她紧张，她宁愿得到清楚的图示，也不想在众人面前反复确认。居民的意见让工作人员意识到，奖励效果不仅取决于礼品，还取决于规则是否公平、说明是否容易理解。
经过讨论，社区取消了按投放次数计分的办法，改为每周一次的分类记录。志愿者不再站在桶边判断谁对谁错，而是对常见错误进行示范。积分仍然保留，但可兑换的内容增加了旧物修理、植物照料课程和公共空间预约。与其用礼品吸引居民短暂参与，不如让他们从分类过程中获得便利、知识和社区联系。对于行动不便的居民，社区还安排预约回收，避免统一规则造成新的不公平。
几个月后的阶段观察显示，前来兑换实物的人少了，分类错误却没有随之增加，居民提出的改进建议反而更加具体。周岚承认，奖励可以成为改变习惯的起点，却不该成为唯一理由；老魏也发现，降低物质奖励并不等于取消鼓励。社区最后把积分称为“参与记录”，不再公开排名。这个调整没有彻底解决所有问题，但它提醒管理者：判断一项制度是否有效，不能只看现场是否热闹，还要看人们在奖励减弱以后，是否仍愿意承担公共责任。
pinyin: yǐ xià gù shì shì wèi fēn jí yuè dú shè jì de jiào xué àn lì 。 qīng lán shè qū céng zài lā jī fēn lèi diǎn páng shè zhì jī fēn guì tái ： jū mín bǎ chú yú 、 sù liào hé fèi zhǐ zhèng què tóu rù bù tóng róng qì hòu ， kě yǐ dēng jì jī fēn ， yuè dǐ duì huàn féi zào 、 lā jī dài děng shēng huó yòng pǐn 。 jū wěi huì yuán yǐ wéi jiǎng lì néng xùn sù péi yǎng xí guàn ， qǐ chū cān yù rén shù què shí zēng jiā ， fēn lèi diǎn qián shèn zhì pái qǐ le duì 。 rán ér ， rè nào chí xù yī duàn shí jiān hòu ， gōng zuò rén yuán fā xiàn ， yǒu xiē jū mín zhǐ zài lǐ pǐn chōng zú shí chū xiàn ， duì huàn jié shù biàn bù zài zhǔ dòng fēn lèi 。

fù zé jī fēn dēng jì de zhōu lán rèn wéi ， wèn tí bù zài jiǎng lì běn shēn ， ér zài zhí xíng fāng shì 。 guò qù ， jū mín wú lùn chǔ lǐ duō shǎo lā jī ， zhǐ yào lái yī cì jiù néng dé fēn ， zhè ràng shǎo shù rén bǎ yī dài fèi zhǐ chāi chéng jǐ cì tóu fàng 。 gèng má fán de shì ， yǒu rén wèi le duō dé jī fēn ， cóng bàn gōng shì dài huí dà liàng bāo zhuāng hé ， què méi yǒu qīng chú hé nèi de jiāo dài hé wū zì 。 biǎo miàn shàng kàn ， tóu fàng liàng shàng shēng le ， hòu xù fēn jiǎn de fù dān què gèng zhòng 。 zhōu lán jiàn yì zàn shí jiàng dī lǐ pǐn jià zhí ， bìng bǎ fēn lèi zhǔn què chéng dù liè wéi zhǔ yào biāo zhǔn 。

zhè ge jiàn yì zāo dào zhì yuàn zhě lǎo wèi fǎn duì 。 tā dān xīn jiǎng lì jiǎn shǎo yǐ hòu ， gāng gāng jiàn lì de cān yù rè qíng huì xùn sù xiāo shī 。 zài tā kàn lái ， jū mín yuàn yì gǎi biàn yuán yǒu xí guàn yǐ jīng bù róng yì ， zhì dù yīng dāng xiān gǔ lì xíng dòng ， zài zhú bù tí gāo yāo qiú 。 rú guǒ yī kāi shǐ jiù jiǎn chá dé guò yú yán gé ， rén men kě néng huì jué de fēn lèi jì má fán yòu róng yì chū cuò 。 lǎo wèi hái zhǐ chū ， bù néng yīn wèi shǎo shù rén zuān kòng zi ， jiù fǒu dìng duō shù jū mín fù chū de shí jiān 。

shuāng fāng zhēng lùn bù xià ， jū wěi huì méi yǒu jí zhe zuò chū xuǎn zé ， ér shì yāo qǐng bù tóng nián líng de jū mín cān jiā tǎo lùn 。 yī wèi nián qīng fù qīn shuō ， hái zi měi cì duì huàn lǐ pǐn dōu hěn xīng fèn ， dàn gèng zhí de kěn dìng de shì ， hái zi kāi shǐ zhǔ dòng yán jiū gè zhǒng bāo zhuāng shǔ yú nǎ lèi lā jī 。 yī wèi dú jū lǎo rén zé tǎn shuài dì biǎo shì ， fù zá de jī fēn guī zé lìng tā jǐn zhāng ， tā nìng yuàn dé dào qīng chǔ de tú shì ， yě bù xiǎng zài zhòng rén miàn qián fǎn fù què rèn 。 jū mín de yì jiàn ràng gōng zuò rén yuán yì shí dào ， jiǎng lì xiào guǒ bù jǐn qǔ jué yú lǐ pǐn ， hái qǔ jué yú guī zé shì fǒu gōng píng 、 shuō míng shì fǒu róng yì lǐ jiě 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， shè qū qǔ xiāo le àn tóu fàng cì shù jì fēn de bàn fǎ ， gǎi wéi měi zhōu yī cì de fēn lèi jì lù 。 zhì yuàn zhě bù zài zhàn zài tǒng biān pàn duàn shuí duì shuí cuò ， ér shì duì cháng jiàn cuò wù jìn xíng shì fàn 。 jī fēn réng rán bǎo liú ， dàn kě duì huàn de nèi róng zēng jiā le jiù wù xiū lǐ 、 zhí wù zhào liào kè chéng hé gōng gòng kōng jiān yù yuē 。 yǔ qí yòng lǐ pǐn xī yǐn jū mín duǎn zàn cān yù ， bù rú ràng tā men cóng fēn lèi guò chéng zhōng huò dé biàn lì 、 zhī shí hé shè qū lián xì 。 duì yú xíng dòng bù biàn de jū mín ， shè qū hái ān pái yù yuē huí shōu ， bì miǎn tǒng yī guī zé zào chéng xīn de bù gōng píng 。

jǐ gè yuè hòu de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， qián lái duì huàn shí wù de rén shǎo le ， fēn lèi cuò wù què méi yǒu suí zhī zēng jiā ， jū mín tí chū de gǎi jìn jiàn yì fǎn ér gèng jiā jù tǐ 。 zhōu lán chéng rèn ， jiǎng lì kě yǐ chéng wéi gǎi biàn xí guàn de qǐ diǎn ， què bù gāi chéng wéi wéi yī lǐ yóu ； lǎo wèi yě fā xiàn ， jiàng dī wù zhì jiǎng lì bìng bù děng yú qǔ xiāo gǔ lì 。 shè qū zuì hòu bǎ jī fēn chēng wéi “ cān yù jì lù ”， bù zài gōng kāi pái míng 。 zhè ge tiáo zhěng méi yǒu chè dǐ jiě jué suǒ yǒu wèn tí ， dàn tā tí xǐng guǎn lǐ zhě ： pàn duàn yī xiàng zhì dù shì fǒu yǒu xiào ， bù néng zhǐ kàn xiàn chǎng shì fǒu rè nào ， hái yào kàn rén men zài jiǎng lì jiǎn ruò yǐ hòu ， shì fǒu réng yuàn yì chéng dān gōng gòng zé rèn 。
translation: The following story is a teaching case designed for graded reading. Qinglan Community once set up a points counter beside its waste-sorting station. After residents correctly placed food waste, plastic, and waste paper into separate containers, they could register points and exchange them at the end of the month for daily necessities such as soap and garbage bags. The residents' committee expected the rewards to build habits quickly, and participation did increase at first, with lines even forming in front of the station. After the excitement had continued for a while, however, staff members noticed that some residents came only when gifts were available and stopped sorting voluntarily once the exchange period ended.

Zhou Lan, who was responsible for registering points, believed that the problem lay not in the rewards themselves but in the way the program was carried out. Previously, residents earned points for every visit regardless of how much waste they handled, leading a few people to split one bag of waste paper into several deliveries. More troublingly, some brought large numbers of packaging boxes home from their offices to earn extra points without removing the tape and stains inside. Although the amount delivered appeared to rise, the burden of later sorting became heavier. Zhou Lan suggested temporarily reducing the value of the gifts and making sorting accuracy the main standard.

This proposal was opposed by Lao Wei, a volunteer. He worried that the enthusiasm which had only recently been established would quickly disappear if the rewards were reduced. In his view, residents had already found it difficult to change their old habits, so the program should encourage action first and gradually raise its requirements. If inspections were too strict from the beginning, people might feel that sorting was troublesome and that mistakes were too easy to make. Lao Wei also pointed out that the time contributed by most residents should not be dismissed merely because a few people exploited loopholes.

Unable to settle the dispute, the residents' committee did not rush to choose a side but invited residents of different ages to join a discussion. A young father said that his child became excited whenever exchanging points for gifts, but what deserved greater recognition was that the child had begun actively researching which category different types of packaging belonged to. An elderly person living alone admitted frankly that the complicated points rules made her nervous. She would rather receive clear diagrams than repeatedly seek confirmation in front of others. The residents' views made the staff realize that the effectiveness of rewards depended not only on the gifts but also on whether the rules were fair and the explanations easy to understand.

After the discussion, the community abolished the practice of awarding points according to the number of deliveries and replaced it with a weekly sorting record. Volunteers no longer stood beside the bins judging who was right or wrong, but instead demonstrated how to correct common mistakes. The points remained, but residents could now exchange them for services such as used-item repairs, plant-care classes, and reservations for shared spaces. Rather than using gifts to attract brief participation, it was better to let residents gain convenience, knowledge, and community connections through sorting. The community also arranged collection by appointment for residents with limited mobility so that a uniform rule would not create new unfairness.

A progress review several months later showed that fewer people came to exchange points for physical goods, yet sorting errors did not increase, while residents' suggestions for improvement became more specific. Zhou Lan acknowledged that rewards could serve as the starting point for changing habits but should not become the only reason. Lao Wei also discovered that reducing material rewards was not the same as removing encouragement. The community eventually renamed the points a participation record and stopped publishing rankings. This adjustment did not solve every problem completely, but it reminded administrators that the effectiveness of a system should not be judged merely by how lively the scene appears. They must also consider whether people remain willing to assume public responsibility after the rewards become less attractive.

articles.title: 号码之前，先看需要
articles.summary: 一所医院尝试根据病情紧急程度安排预约时段，并在争议中逐步完善解释、复核和隐私保护机制。
articles.topic: 号码之前，先看需要
paragraphs: 星期一清晨，城南医院门诊部还没开门，入口处已经排起长队。有人只是想复查药量，有人却捂着胸口，脸色发白。过去，医院主要按照患者抢到的号码安排就诊，先预约的人往往先看。门诊主任罗岚发现，这种看似公平的顺序忽略了病情变化：慢性病患者可能占着最早的时段，而突然恶化的人只能去急诊或继续等待。本文所述改革及数据均为分级阅读教学案例中的阶段观察，并非真实医院的统计结论。
罗岚提出“先判断需要，再安排时间”。患者仍可通过手机、电话或窗口预约，但必须回答几项与症状有关的问题。系统不直接诊断，只把申请分成紧急、近期和常规三类，再由护士审核。若答案前后矛盾，护士会打电话确认；一旦出现胸痛、呼吸困难等危险信号，就建议患者立即前往急诊。为了避免老人因不会使用手机而吃亏，窗口还保留了人工登记和解释服务。
改革启动后的第一周，争议很快出现。六十八岁的秦师傅每月复查高血压，原来总能约到周一上午，这次却被安排到周三。他认为自己受到了冷落，在大厅里要求恢复旧规则。护士没有只说“系统决定了”，而是向他展示同一天的预约情况：两个患者的药物反应突然加重，一个孩子持续高烧。她同时为秦师傅检查了剩余药量，确认足够服用到周三，并替他保留了交通较方便的时段。
这场冲突让罗岚意识到，排序标准如果不透明，再合理的改革也会被理解为插队。医院随后在预约页面和候诊区公布原则，却没有公开患者的具体病情；通知只说明“该时段优先提供给需要更快处理的人”。此外，每次调整都留下审核记录，患者可以申请复核。工作人员也被要求说明替代方案，例如改约其他医生、先做必要检查，或者在病情稳定时接受远程咨询。
一个月后，这份教学案例记录了几项阶段变化：危险症状被更早识别，普通复查的平均等待时间略有增加，因不理解规则而投诉的人先升后降。不过，团队没有把“投诉减少”直接当成成功，因为部分患者可能只是不愿表达不满。罗岚邀请患者代表查看匿名记录，并发现电话预约者更容易遗漏症状描述。于是，医院简化了提问方式，让接线员逐项复述答案，还允许患者补充照护者的联系方式。
改革并没有取消排队，也无法保证每个人都得到最理想的时间。它改变的是预约的含义：号码不再只是时间顺序，而是医疗需要与服务能力之间的一次协调。秦师傅后来参加了患者座谈会，他建议通知中同时写明延期理由和药物不足时的求助渠道。罗岚采纳了前半项，却拒绝使用容易泄露隐私的详细理由。她说，制度既要识别真正的紧急情况，也要给被延后的人留下选择、解释和申诉的空间；否则，效率越高，误解可能越深。
pinyin: xīng qī yī qīng chén ， chéng nán yī yuàn mén zhěn bù hái méi kāi mén ， rù kǒu chù yǐ jīng pái qǐ cháng duì 。 yǒu rén zhǐ shì xiǎng fù chá yào liàng ， yǒu rén què wǔ zhe xiōng kǒu ， liǎn sè fā bái 。 guò qù ， yī yuàn zhǔ yào àn zhào huàn zhě qiǎng dào de hào mǎ ān pái jiù zhěn ， xiān yù yuē de rén wǎng wǎng xiān kàn 。 mén zhěn zhǔ rèn luó lán fā xiàn ， zhè zhǒng kàn shì gōng píng de shùn xù hū lüè le bìng qíng biàn huà ： màn xìng bìng huàn zhě kě néng zhàn zhe zuì zǎo de shí duàn ， ér tū rán è huà de rén zhǐ néng qù jí zhěn huò jì xù děng dài 。 běn wén suǒ shù gǎi gé jí shù jù jūn wèi fēn jí yuè dú jiào xué àn lì zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá ， bìng fēi zhēn shí yī yuàn de tǒng jì jié lùn 。

luó lán tí chū “ xiān pàn duàn xū yào ， zài ān pái shí jiān ”。 huàn zhě réng kě tōng guò shǒu jī 、 diàn huà huò chuāng kǒu yù yuē ， dàn bì xū huí dá jǐ xiàng yǔ zhèng zhuàng yǒu guān de wèn tí 。 xì tǒng bù zhí jiē zhěn duàn ， zhǐ bǎ shēn qǐng fēn chéng jǐn jí 、 jìn qī hé cháng guī sān lèi ， zài yóu hù shì shěn hé 。 ruò dá àn qián hòu máo dùn ， hù shì huì dǎ diàn huà què rèn ； yí dàn chū xiàn xiōng tòng 、 hū xī kùn nán děng wēi xiǎn xìn hào ， jiù jiàn yì huàn zhě lì jí qián wǎng jí zhěn 。 wèi le bì miǎn lǎo rén yīn bú huì shǐ yòng shǒu jī ér chī kuī ， chuāng kǒu hái bǎo liú le rén gōng dēng jì hé jiě shì fú wù 。

gǎi gé qǐ dòng hòu de dì yī zhōu ， zhēng yì hěn kuài chū xiàn 。 liù shí bā suì de qín shī fù měi yuè fù chá gāo xuè yā ， yuán lái zǒng néng yuē dào zhōu yī shàng wǔ ， zhè cì què bèi ān pái dào zhōu sān 。 tā rèn wéi zì jǐ shòu dào le lěng luò ， zài dà tīng lǐ yāo qiú huī fù jiù guī zé 。 hù shì méi yǒu zhǐ shuō “ xì tǒng jué dìng le ”， ér shì xiàng tā zhǎn shì tóng yī tiān de yù yuē qíng kuàng ： liǎng gè huàn zhě de yào wù fǎn yìng tū rán jiā zhòng ， yí gè hái zi chí xù gāo shāo 。 tā tóng shí wèi qín shī fù jiǎn chá le shèng yú yào liàng ， què rèn zú gòu fú yòng dào zhōu sān ， bìng tì tā bǎo liú le jiāo tōng jiào fāng biàn de shí duàn 。

zhè chǎng chōng tū ràng luó lán yì shí dào ， pái xù biāo zhǔn rú guǒ bú tòu míng ， zài hé lǐ de gǎi gé yě huì bèi lǐ jiě wèi chā duì 。 yī yuàn suí hòu zài yù yuē yè miàn hé hòu zhěn qū gōng bù yuán zé ， què méi yǒu gōng kāi huàn zhě de jù tǐ bìng qíng ； tōng zhī zhǐ shuō míng “ gāi shí duàn yōu xiān tí gōng gěi xū yào gèng kuài chǔ lǐ de rén ”。 cǐ wài ， měi cì tiáo zhěng dōu liú xià shěn hé jì lù ， huàn zhě kě yǐ shēn qǐng fù hé 。 gōng zuò rén yuán yě bèi yāo qiú shuō míng tì dài fāng àn ， lì rú gǎi yuē qí tā yī shēng 、 xiān zuò bì yào jiǎn chá ， huò zhě zài bìng qíng wěn dìng shí jiē shòu yuǎn chéng zī xún 。

yí gè yuè hòu ， zhè fèn jiào xué àn lì jì lù le jǐ xiàng jiē duàn biàn huà ： wēi xiǎn zhèng zhuàng bèi gèng zǎo shí bié ， pǔ tōng fù chá de píng jūn děng dài shí jiān lüè yǒu zēng jiā ， yīn bù lǐ jiě guī zé ér tóu sù de rén xiān shēng hòu jiàng 。 bù guò ， tuán duì méi yǒu bǎ “ tóu sù jiǎn shǎo ” zhí jiē dàng chéng chéng gōng ， yīn wèi bù fèn huàn zhě kě néng zhǐ shì bù yuàn biǎo dá bù mǎn 。 luó lán yāo qǐng huàn zhě dài biǎo chá kàn nì míng jì lù ， bìng fā xiàn diàn huà yù yuē zhě gèng róng yì yí lòu zhèng zhuàng miáo shù 。 yú shì ， yī yuàn jiǎn huà le tí wèn fāng shì ， ràng jiē xiàn yuán zhú xiàng fù shù dá àn ， hái yǔn xǔ huàn zhě bǔ chōng zhào hù zhě de lián xì fāng shì 。

gǎi gé bìng méi yǒu qǔ xiāo pái duì ， yě wú fǎ bǎo zhèng měi gè rén dōu dé dào zuì lǐ xiǎng de shí jiān 。 tā gǎi biàn de shì yù yuē de hán yì ： hào mǎ bù zài zhǐ shì shí jiān shùn xù ， ér shì yī liáo xū yào yǔ fú wù néng lì zhī jiān de yī cì xié tiáo 。 qín shī fù hòu lái cān jiā le huàn zhě zuò tán huì ， tā jiàn yì tōng zhī zhōng tóng shí xiě míng yán qī lǐ yóu huò yào wù bù zú shí de qiú zhù qú dào 。 luó lán cǎi nà le qián bàn xiàng ， què jù jué shǐ yòng róng yì xiè lòu yǐn sī de xiáng xì lǐ yóu 。 tā shuō ， zhì dù jì yào shí bié zhēn zhèng de jǐn jí qíng kuàng ， yě yào gěi bèi yán hòu de rén liú xià xuǎn zé 、 jiě shì hé shēn sù de kōng jiān ； fǒu zé ， xiào lǜ yuè gāo ， wù jiě kě néng yuè shēn 。
translation: Early on Monday morning, before the outpatient department of Chengnan Hospital had opened, a long line had already formed at the entrance. Some people merely wanted to review their medication dosage, while others were clutching their chests with pale faces. In the past, the hospital mainly arranged consultations according to the numbers patients managed to obtain, so those who booked first were usually seen first. Luo Lan, the director of the outpatient department, realized that this seemingly fair order ignored changes in medical conditions: patients with chronic illnesses might occupy the earliest time slots, while those whose conditions suddenly worsened could only go to the emergency department or continue waiting. The reform and data described here are interim observations from a graded-reading teaching case, not statistical conclusions from a real hospital.

Luo Lan proposed assessing needs before assigning times. Patients could still make appointments by mobile phone, telephone, or at the service window, but they had to answer several questions about their symptoms. The system did not make diagnoses. It only classified requests as urgent, near-term, or routine before nurses reviewed them. If the answers contradicted one another, a nurse would call to confirm them; once warning signs such as chest pain or difficulty breathing appeared, the patient would be advised to go to the emergency department immediately. To prevent older people from being disadvantaged because they could not use mobile phones, the service window continued to offer manual registration and explanations.

Disputes quickly arose during the first week of the reform. Sixty-eight-year-old Mr. Qin had his high blood pressure reviewed every month and had previously always obtained a Monday morning appointment, but this time he was assigned to Wednesday. Feeling neglected, he demanded in the lobby that the old rules be restored. Rather than merely telling him that the system had made the decision, the nurse showed him the appointments scheduled for that day: two patients had experienced sudden worsening of medication reactions, and a child had a persistent high fever. She also checked Mr. Qin's remaining medication, confirmed that it would last until Wednesday, and reserved a time slot that was convenient for transportation.

The conflict made Luo Lan realize that if the ranking criteria were not transparent, even a reasonable reform would be interpreted as allowing people to jump the line. The hospital then published its principles on the booking page and in the waiting area without revealing patients' specific conditions; notices only stated that a time slot had been given priority for someone requiring faster attention. In addition, a review record was retained for every adjustment, and patients could request reconsideration. Staff members were also required to explain alternatives, such as making an appointment with another doctor, completing necessary tests first, or using a remote consultation when the patient's condition was stable.

One month later, the teaching case recorded several interim changes: dangerous symptoms were identified earlier, the average waiting time for routine reviews rose slightly, and complaints caused by misunderstanding the rules first increased and then declined. However, the team did not directly regard fewer complaints as proof of success, because some patients might simply have been unwilling to express dissatisfaction. Luo Lan invited patient representatives to examine anonymized records and discovered that people booking by telephone were more likely to omit descriptions of their symptoms. The hospital therefore simplified its questions, asked telephone operators to repeat each answer, and allowed patients to add a caregiver's contact information.

The reform did not eliminate waiting, nor could it guarantee an ideal appointment time for everyone. What it changed was the meaning of an appointment: a number no longer represented only chronological order, but a coordination between medical needs and service capacity. Mr. Qin later attended a patient discussion meeting and suggested that notices should state both the reason for a delay and a channel for seeking help when medication was running out. Luo Lan accepted the first part of his suggestion but rejected detailed explanations that could easily reveal private information. She said that a system must both identify genuinely urgent situations and leave postponed patients room for choice, explanation, and appeal; otherwise, the more efficient it becomes, the deeper the misunderstandings may grow.

articles.title: 被一场暴雨检验的数据平台
articles.summary: 教学案例中的临江市尝试开放交通与环境数据，却在暴雨期间暴露出更新延迟、标准不统一和责任不清等问题。市政府随后调整计划，让公共数据从“可以下载”走向“能够使用”。
articles.topic: 被一场暴雨检验的数据平台
paragraphs: 以下内容是为语言学习设计的城市治理案例，其中的城市、人物和阶段观察均为虚构。临江市准备建设公共数据平台时，项目负责人周岚提出，首批开放公交到站、道路施工、空气质量和河流水位等信息。她认为，政府部门长期积累的数据如果只保存在各自的系统里，不但难以发挥价值，还会增加重复调查的成本。然而，在第一次协调会上，部分部门担心数据被误解，另一些部门则认为整理资料会占用本来就有限的人力。
为了减少阻力，周岚没有要求各部门一次性公开全部资料，而是选择两个街区进行教学案例中的试点。平台上线后，地图开发者利用道路施工数据设计绕行提醒，几所学校根据空气质量调整户外活动时间。材料中的阶段观察显示，访问量虽然不断增加，真正能够直接使用数据的人却不多。许多文件只有专业人员看得懂，有些表格缺少单位和更新时间，还有两个部门对“道路封闭”采用了不同的判断标准。
问题在一场暴雨中集中暴露出来。当天傍晚，城西河流水位迅速上升，平台显示的数据却停留在三个小时前。一家社区服务机构据此安排志愿者运送物资，车辆到达低洼路段后才发现道路已经封闭，只能临时返回。虽然没有造成人员受伤，但这次经历使周岚意识到，公开数据并不等于简单地上传文件；如果信息缺乏时效性和明确解释，使用者反而可能作出错误判断。
周岚随后邀请数据提供部门、记者、程序员和社区代表共同检查平台。大家没有把注意力放在页面是否美观上，而是追问每项数据由谁采集、多久更新一次、出现错误后由谁负责。经过讨论，团队决定为数据增加统一说明，标明来源、单位、更新时间和适用范围；对于水位、封路等紧急信息，则设置自动提醒和人工复核两道程序。平台还保留历史版本，使公众能够判断某项记录后来是否被修改。
新的安排也引起了争议。有人主张，只要数据来自政府，就应该毫无保留地开放；社区代表却指出，过细的出行记录可能暴露个人生活规律。周岚同意，开放不应以牺牲隐私为代价。团队因此删除能够识别个人身份的内容，并把部分资料按区域和时间段汇总。对于暂时不能公开的数据，平台必须说明限制理由、负责部门和重新评估的日期，而不能仅仅显示“无权访问”。
三个月后的课堂复盘并没有把下载次数当作唯一成绩。评审者更关心的是，普通居民能否理解说明，开发者能否稳定调用数据，部门能否及时纠正错误。周岚在总结中写道，公共数据的价值不在于文件数量，而在于它是否帮助人们作出更可靠的决定。经历暴雨的检验后，临江市没有停止开放计划，而是把准确性、可理解性和责任机制放在发布速度之前，也为公众留下了提出质疑和获得答复的渠道。
pinyin: yǐ xià nèi róng shì wèi yǔ yán xué xí shè jì de chéng shì zhì lǐ àn lì ， qí zhōng de chéng shì 、 rén wù hé jiē duàn guān chá jūn wèi xū gòu 。 lín jiāng shì zhǔn bèi jiàn shè gōng gòng shù jù píng tái shí ， xiàng mù fù zé rén zhōu lán tí chū ， shǒu pī kāi fàng gōng jiāo dào zhàn 、 dào lù shī gōng 、 kōng qì zhì liàng hé hé liú shuǐ wèi děng xìn xī 。 tā rèn wéi ， zhèng fǔ bù mén cháng qī jī lěi de shù jù rú guǒ zhǐ bǎo cún zài gè zì de xì tǒng lǐ ， bù dàn nán yǐ fā huī jià zhí ， hái huì zēng jiā zhòng fù diào chá de chéng běn 。 rán ér ， zài dì yī cì xié tiáo huì shàng ， bù fèn bù mén dān xīn shù jù bèi wù jiě ， lìng yī xiē bù mén zé rèn wéi zhěng lǐ zī liào huì zhàn yòng běn lái jiù yǒu xiàn de rén lì 。

wèi le jiǎn shǎo zǔ lì ， zhōu lán méi yǒu yāo qiú gè bù mén yí cì xìng gōng kāi quán bù zī liào ， ér shì xuǎn zé liǎng gè jiē qū jìn xíng jiào xué àn lì zhōng de shì diǎn 。 píng tái shàng xiàn hòu ， dì tú kāi fā zhě lì yòng dào lù shī gōng shù jù shè jì rào xíng tí xǐng ， jǐ suǒ xué xiào gēn jù kōng qì zhì liàng tiáo zhěng hù wài huó dòng shí jiān 。 cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， fǎng wèn liàng suī rán bù duàn zēng jiā ， zhēn zhèng néng gòu zhí jiē shǐ yòng shù jù de rén què bù duō 。 xǔ duō wén jiàn zhǐ yǒu zhuān yè rén yuán kàn de dǒng ， yǒu xiē biǎo gé quē shǎo dān wèi hé gēng xīn shí jiān ， hái yǒu liǎng gè bù mén duì “ dào lù fēng bì ” cǎi yòng le bù tóng de pàn duàn biāo zhǔn 。

wèn tí zài yī cháng bào yǔ zhōng jí zhōng bào lù chū lái 。 dàng tiān bàng wǎn ， chéng xī hé liú shuǐ wèi xùn sù shàng shēng ， píng tái xiǎn shì de shù jù què tíng liú zài sān gè xiǎo shí qián 。 yī jiā shè qū fú wù jī gòu jù cǐ ān pái zhì yuàn zhě yùn sòng wù zī ， chē liàng dào dá dī wā lù duàn hòu cái fā xiàn dào lù yǐ jīng fēng bì ， zhǐ néng lín shí fǎn huí 。 suī rán méi yǒu zào chéng rén yuán shòu shāng ， dàn zhè cì jīng lì shǐ zhōu lán yì shí dào ， gōng kāi shù jù bìng bù děng yú jiǎn dān dì shàng chuán wén jiàn ； rú guǒ xìn xī quē fá shí xiào xìng hé míng què jiě shì ， shǐ yòng zhě fǎn ér kě néng zuò chū cuò wù pàn duàn 。

zhōu lán suí hòu yāo qǐng shù jù tí gōng bù mén 、 jì zhě 、 chéng xù yuán hé shè qū dài biǎo gòng tóng jiǎn chá píng tái 。 dà jiā méi yǒu bǎ zhù yì lì fàng zài yè miàn shì fǒu měi guān shàng ， ér shì zhuī wèn měi xiàng shù jù yóu shuí cǎi jí 、 duō jiǔ gēng xīn yī cì 、 chū xiàn cuò wù hòu yóu shuí fù zé 。 jīng guò tǎo lùn ， tuán duì jué dìng wéi shù jù zēng jiā tǒng yī shuō míng ， biāo míng lái yuán 、 dān wèi 、 gēng xīn shí jiān hé shì yòng fàn wéi ； duì yú shuǐ wèi 、 fēng lù děng jǐn jí xìn xī ， zé shè zhì zì dòng tí xǐng hé rén gōng fù hé liǎng dào chéng xù 。 píng tái hái bǎo liú lì shǐ bǎn běn ， shǐ gōng zhòng néng gòu pàn duàn mǒu xiàng jì lù hòu lái shì fǒu bèi xiū gǎi 。

xīn de ān pái yě yǐn qǐ le zhēng yì 。 yǒu rén zhǔ zhāng ， zhǐ yào shù jù lái zì zhèng fǔ ， jiù yīng gāi háo wú bǎo liú dì kāi fàng ； shè qū dài biǎo què zhǐ chū ， guò xì de chū xíng jì lù kě néng bào lù gè rén shēng huó guī lǜ 。 zhōu lán tóng yì ， kāi fàng bù yīng yǐ xī shēng yǐn sī wèi dài jià 。 tuán duì yīn cǐ shān chú néng gòu shí bié gè rén shēn fèn de nèi róng ， bìng bǎ bù fèn zī liào àn qū yù hé shí jiān duàn huì zǒng 。 duì yú zàn shí bù néng gōng kāi de shù jù ， píng tái bì xū shuō míng xiàn zhì lǐ yóu 、 fù zé bù mén hé chóng xīn píng gū de rì qī ， ér bù néng jǐn jǐn xiǎn shì “ wú quán fǎng wèn ”。

sān gè yuè hòu de kè táng fù pán bìng méi yǒu bǎ xià zài cì shù dàng zuò wéi yì chéng jì 。 píng shěn zhě gèng guān xīn de shì ， pǔ tōng jū mín néng fǒu lǐ jiě shuō míng ， kāi fā zhě néng fǒu wěn dìng diào yòng shù jù ， bù mén néng fǒu jí shí jiū zhèng cuò wù 。 zhōu lán zài zǒng jié zhōng xiě dào ， gōng gòng shù jù de jià zhí bù zài yú wén jiàn shù liàng ， ér zài yú tā shì fǒu bāng zhù rén men zuò chū gèng kě kào de jué dìng 。 jīng lì bào yǔ de jiǎn yàn hòu ， lín jiāng shì méi yǒu tíng zhǐ kāi fàng jì huà ， ér shì bǎ zhǔn què xìng 、 kě lǐ jiě xìng hé zé rèn jī zhì fàng zài fā bù sù dù zhī qián ， yě wèi gōng zhòng liú xià le tí chū zhì yí hé huò dé dá fù de qú dào 。
translation: The following is an urban governance case designed for language learning; its city, characters, and interim observations are all fictional. When Linjiang City prepared to build a public data platform, project leader Zhou Lan proposed that the first release include information such as bus arrivals, road construction, air quality, and river levels. She believed that if data accumulated by government departments remained confined to separate systems, it would not only be difficult to realize its value but would also increase the cost of repeated investigations. However, at the first coordination meeting, some departments worried that the data might be misunderstood, while others argued that organizing the material would consume their already limited staff resources.

To reduce resistance, Zhou Lan did not ask every department to disclose all its materials at once. Instead, she selected two neighborhoods for a pilot within the teaching case. After the platform went online, map developers used road construction data to create detour alerts, and several schools adjusted outdoor activities according to air quality. Interim observations in the learning material showed that although visits continued to rise, few people could actually use the data directly. Many files could be understood only by specialists, some tables lacked units and update times, and two departments used different standards to determine what counted as a road closure.

The problems were exposed all at once during a rainstorm. That evening, the river level in the west of the city rose rapidly, but the data displayed on the platform was still from three hours earlier. A community service organization used that information to arrange for volunteers to deliver supplies, only to discover upon reaching a low-lying section that the road had already been closed, forcing them to turn back. Although no one was injured, the experience made Zhou Lan realize that releasing data was not the same as simply uploading files; if information lacked timeliness and clear explanations, users might instead make incorrect judgments.

Zhou Lan then invited data-providing departments, journalists, programmers, and community representatives to examine the platform together. Rather than focusing on whether the pages looked attractive, they asked who collected each dataset, how often it was updated, and who would be responsible when errors appeared. After discussion, the team decided to add standardized descriptions indicating the source, unit, update time, and scope of application. For urgent information such as river levels and road closures, it established both automated alerts and manual review. The platform also retained historical versions so that the public could determine whether a record had later been changed.

The new arrangements also caused debate. Some people argued that as long as data came from the government, it should be disclosed without reservation. Community representatives, however, pointed out that overly detailed travel records could reveal patterns in an individual's daily life. Zhou Lan agreed that openness should not come at the cost of privacy. The team therefore removed content that could identify individuals and aggregated some material by area and time period. For data that could not yet be released, the platform had to state the reason for the restriction, the department responsible, and the date of reassessment, rather than merely displaying the message “Access denied.”

The classroom review three months later did not treat download counts as the only measure of success. The reviewers cared more about whether ordinary residents could understand the descriptions, whether developers could access the data reliably, and whether departments could correct errors promptly. In her summary, Zhou Lan wrote that the value of public data lay not in the number of files but in whether it helped people make more reliable decisions. After being tested by the rainstorm, Linjiang City did not abandon its open-data plan. Instead, it placed accuracy, comprehensibility, and accountability ahead of release speed, while also leaving the public channels through which to raise questions and receive answers.

articles.title: 一份被暂缓表决的课程改革方案
articles.summary: 一所大学计划减少必修课并开设跨专业项目课，但课程委员会没有立即表决，而是要求改革团队先通过小规模试行解决公平、师资和评价方面的问题。
articles.topic: 一份被暂缓表决的课程改革方案
paragraphs: 在一份用于课堂讨论的教学案例中，东临大学准备调整本科课程。改革小组发现，不少学生虽然修满了学分，却很少有机会处理真实而复杂的问题。因此，他们建议减少部分重复的必修课，把节省出来的时间用于跨专业项目。学生可以与不同院系的同伴合作，为社区交通、老年服务或文化保护提出方案。改革小组原以为，这项强调实践能力的计划会顺利获得支持。
方案提交课程委员会后，会议气氛却比预想中谨慎。委员们并不反对跨专业学习，但他们担心改革会产生新的不公平。资源充足的院系能够邀请校外专家，也有专门的实验场地；规模较小的院系则可能连指导教师都不够。如果项目课迅速成为毕业要求，一些学生获得的是丰富的实践经历，另一些学生得到的却可能只是形式上的小组作业。
学生代表林遥还指出，方案虽然允许学生自由选择项目，却没有解释时间冲突如何解决。医学专业的实习安排十分固定，艺术专业的创作周期又常常集中在学期末，仅仅把不同专业的学生编入同一组，并不意味着他们真的能够合作。她认为，改革不能只设计理想的学习过程，还要考虑学生是否承担得起交通、材料和额外时间等成本。
面对质疑，改革小组负责人周教授没有急于为原方案辩护。他承认，团队此前把注意力主要放在课程内容上，低估了执行条件的重要性。不过，他也提醒委员会，如果因为方案不完善就彻底放弃改革，旧课程中重复教学、知识分割等问题仍会继续存在。与其在“立即通过”和“完全否定”之间选择，不如先缩小范围，检验哪些设想真正可行。
经过讨论，委员会决定暂缓表决，并要求改革小组设计一个为期一学期的校内试行。试行只邀请三个自愿参加的院系，每个项目都必须配备两名不同专业的教师，同时为经济困难的学生提供材料补助。评价方式也不再只看最终成果，而是包括个人记录、合作过程和公开答辩。这些安排属于教学案例中的阶段设计，并不代表任何现实大学已经实施的政策。
一学期后，委员会将根据学生访谈、教师记录和项目作品重新审查方案。周教授起初对延期感到失望，后来却发现，暂缓并不等于拒绝，它迫使改革者回答那些容易被热情掩盖的问题。课程改革的价值不仅取决于目标是否先进，也取决于机会是否公平、条件是否具备。委员会没有立即通过方案，反而为改革建立了更清楚的责任边界，也让参与者明白：谨慎有时不是阻力，而是使改变能够持续的条件。
pinyin: zài yī fèn yòng yú kè táng tǎo lùn de jiào xué àn lì zhōng ， dōng lín dà xué zhǔn bèi tiáo zhěng běn kē kè chéng 。 gǎi gé xiǎo zǔ fā xiàn ， bù shǎo xué shēng suī rán xiū mǎn le xué fēn ， què hěn shǎo yǒu jī huì chǔ lǐ zhēn shí ér fù zá de wèn tí 。 yīn cǐ ， tā men jiàn yì jiǎn shǎo bù fèn chóng fù de bì xiū kè ， bǎ jié shěng chū lái de shí jiān yòng yú kuà zhuān yè xiàng mù 。 xué shēng kě yǐ yǔ bù tóng yuàn xì de tóng bàn hé zuò ， wèi shè qū jiāo tōng 、 lǎo nián fú wù huò wén huà bǎo hù tí chū fāng àn 。 gǎi gé xiǎo zǔ yuán yǐ wéi ， zhè xiàng qiáng diào shí jiàn néng lì de jì huà huì shùn lì huò dé zhī chí 。

fāng àn tí jiāo kè chéng wěi yuán huì hòu ， huì yì qì fēn què bǐ yù xiǎng zhōng jǐn shèn 。 wěi yuán men bìng bù fǎn duì kuà zhuān yè xué xí ， dàn tā men dān xīn gǎi gé huì chǎn shēng xīn de bù gōng píng 。 zī yuán chōng zú de yuàn xì néng gòu yāo qǐng xiào wài zhuān jiā ， yě yǒu zhuān mén de shí yàn chǎng dì ； guī mó jiào xiǎo de yuàn xì zé kě néng lián zhǐ dǎo jiào shī dōu bù gòu 。 rú guǒ xiàng mù kè xùn sù chéng wéi bì yè yāo qiú ， yī xiē xué shēng huò dé de shì fēng fù de shí jiàn jīng lì ， lìng yī xiē xué shēng dé dào de què kě néng zhǐ shì xíng shì shàng de xiǎo zǔ zuò yè 。

xué shēng dài biǎo lín yáo hái zhǐ chū ， fāng àn suī rán yǔn xǔ xué shēng zì yóu xuǎn zé xiàng mù ， què méi yǒu jiě shì shí jiān chōng tū rú hé jiě jué 。 yī xué zhuān yè de shí xí ān pái shí fēn gù dìng ， yì shù zhuān yè de chuàng zuò zhōu qī yòu cháng cháng jí zhōng zài xué qī mò ， jǐn jǐn bǎ bù tóng zhuān yè de xué shēng biān rù tóng yī zǔ ， bìng bù yì wèi zhe tā men zhēn de néng gòu hé zuò 。 tā rèn wéi ， gǎi gé bù néng zhǐ shè jì lǐ xiǎng de xué xí guò chéng ， hái yào kǎo lǜ xué shēng shì fǒu chéng dān dé qǐ jiāo tōng 、 cái liào hé é wài shí jiān děng chéng běn 。

miàn duì zhì yí ， gǎi gé xiǎo zǔ fù zé rén zhōu jiào shòu méi yǒu jí yú wèi yuán fāng àn biàn hù 。 tā chéng rèn ， tuán duì cǐ qián bǎ zhù yì lì zhǔ yào fàng zài kè chéng nèi róng shàng ， dī gū le zhí xíng tiáo jiàn de zhòng yào xìng 。 bù guò ， tā yě tí xǐng wěi yuán huì ， rú guǒ yīn wèi fāng àn bù wán shàn jiù chè dǐ fàng qì gǎi gé ， jiù kè chéng zhōng chóng fù jiào xué 、 zhī shí fēn gē děng wèn tí réng huì jì xù cún zài 。 yǔ qí zài “ lì jí tōng guò ” hé “ wán quán fǒu dìng ” zhī jiān xuǎn zé ， bù rú xiān suō xiǎo fàn wéi ， jiǎn yàn nǎ xiē shè xiǎng zhēn zhèng kě xíng 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， wěi yuán huì jué dìng zàn huǎn biǎo jué ， bìng yāo qiú gǎi gé xiǎo zǔ shè jì yí gè wéi qī yī xué qī de xiào nèi shì xíng 。 shì xíng zhǐ yāo qǐng sān gè zì yuàn cān jiā de yuàn xì ， měi gè xiàng mù dōu bì xū pèi bèi liǎng míng bù tóng zhuān yè de jiào shī ， tóng shí wèi jīng jì kùn nán de xué shēng tí gōng cái liào bǔ zhù 。 píng jià fāng shì yě bù zài zhǐ kàn zuì zhōng chéng guǒ ， ér shì bāo kuò gè rén jì lù 、 hé zuò guò chéng hé gōng kāi dá biàn 。 zhè xiē ān pái shǔ yú jiào xué àn lì zhōng de jiē duàn shè jì ， bìng bù dài biǎo rèn hé xiàn shí dà xué yǐ jīng shí shī de zhèng cè 。

yī xué qī hòu ， wěi yuán huì jiāng gēn jù xué shēng fǎng tán 、 jiào shī jì lù hé xiàng mù zuò pǐn chóng xīn shěn chá fāng àn 。 zhōu jiào shòu qǐ chū duì yán qī gǎn dào shī wàng ， hòu lái què fā xiàn ， zàn huǎn bìng bù děng yú jù jué ， tā pò shǐ gǎi gé zhě huí dá nà xiē róng yì bèi rè qíng yǎn gài de wèn tí 。 kè chéng gǎi gé de jià zhí bù jǐn qǔ jué yú mù biāo shì fǒu xiān jìn ， yě qǔ jué yú jī huì shì fǒu gōng píng 、 tiáo jiàn shì fǒu jù bèi 。 wěi yuán huì méi yǒu lì jí tōng guò fāng àn ， fǎn ér wèi gǎi gé jiàn lì le gèng qīng chǔ de zé rèn biān jiè ， yě ràng cān yù zhě míng bái ： jǐn shèn yǒu shí bú shì zǔ lì ， ér shì shǐ gǎi biàn néng gòu chí xù de tiáo jiàn 。
translation: In a teaching case prepared for classroom discussion, Donglin University was planning to revise its undergraduate curriculum. The reform team had found that many students completed all their credits but rarely had opportunities to deal with real and complex problems. It therefore proposed reducing some repetitive required courses and using the time saved for interdisciplinary projects. Students could work with peers from different departments to develop proposals on community transportation, services for older adults, or cultural preservation. The team originally expected this plan, with its emphasis on practical competence, to gain support smoothly.

After the proposal was submitted to the curriculum committee, however, the atmosphere at the meeting was more cautious than expected. The committee members did not oppose interdisciplinary learning, but they worried that the reform might create new inequalities. Well-resourced departments could invite outside experts and had dedicated experimental facilities, while smaller departments might not even have enough instructors. If project courses quickly became a graduation requirement, some students would gain rich practical experience, whereas others might receive nothing more than a group assignment that existed in name only.

The student representative, Lin Yao, also pointed out that although the proposal allowed students to choose projects freely, it did not explain how scheduling conflicts would be resolved. Internship schedules in medical programs were highly fixed, while the creative work of art students was often concentrated near the end of the semester. Simply placing students from different majors in the same group did not mean that they could genuinely cooperate. In her view, reform should not merely design an ideal learning process; it should also consider whether students could afford the costs of transportation, materials, and additional time.

Faced with these doubts, Professor Zhou, the head of the reform team, did not rush to defend the original proposal. He admitted that the team had previously focused mainly on course content and underestimated the importance of implementation conditions. Nevertheless, he reminded the committee that if the reform were abandoned entirely because the proposal was imperfect, problems such as repetitive teaching and fragmented knowledge in the old curriculum would continue. Rather than choosing between immediate approval and complete rejection, it would be better to narrow the scope first and test which ideas were genuinely feasible.

After discussion, the committee decided to postpone the vote and asked the reform team to design a one-semester internal trial. Only three departments that volunteered would participate, and every project would be required to have two instructors from different disciplines. Students with financial difficulties would also receive subsidies for materials. Assessment would no longer focus solely on the final product but would include individual records, the collaboration process, and a public presentation. These arrangements are interim designs within a teaching case and do not represent policies already implemented by any real university.

One semester later, the committee would review the proposal again on the basis of student interviews, faculty records, and project work. Professor Zhou was disappointed by the delay at first, but later realized that postponement did not equal rejection; it forced reformers to answer questions that enthusiasm could easily conceal. The value of curriculum reform depends not only on whether its goals are progressive, but also on whether opportunities are fair and necessary conditions are in place. By not approving the proposal immediately, the committee instead established clearer boundaries of responsibility for the reform and helped participants understand that caution is sometimes not an obstacle, but a condition that enables change to last.

articles.title: 屋顶之上，责任之下
articles.summary: 一项教学案例中的屋顶花园计划在安全、收益与公共使用之间寻找平衡，并通过阶段观察调整扩建决定。
articles.topic: 屋顶之上，责任之下
paragraphs: 在一门城市治理课程中，教师设计了一个名为“云梯花园”的教学案例。案例地点是南方城市临川区一片建于二十年前的商业街。那里店铺密集，地面缺少公共绿地，十二栋楼的屋顶却长期闲置。区里提出屋顶花园计划，希望改善夏季高温，也给附近居民增加休息空间。消息公布后，支持者称它能让灰色街区恢复生机，反对者则担心这只是昂贵的城市装饰。
项目负责人林岚没有急着施工，而是先邀请结构工程师逐栋检查。结果显示，部分屋顶能够承受花池和人群，另外几栋只能铺设轻型植物，还有两栋必须放弃。她据此把原方案缩小，并要求所有参与建筑保留排水通道。商户起初不满，认为检查拖慢进度；林岚却解释，如果忽略承重、防水和消防，再漂亮的设计也可能给楼下经营者带来长期风险。
真正的争论出现在使用方式上。餐馆老板希望屋顶成为消费区，以便收回维护成本；居民代表周叔则主张免费开放，尤其要给老人和孩子留出安静角落。林岚没有在两者之间简单选边，而是把空间分成公共花园、小型经营区和雨水种植区。经营收入的一部分进入共同账户，用于购买土壤、修理护栏，并公开每月支出。
计划运行三个月后，课程材料记录了阶段观察：傍晚来散步的人逐渐增加，顶层几家店的室内温度在部分晴天有所下降，但效果并不稳定。一场暴雨还暴露出问题，一处排水口被落叶堵住，积水渗进仓库。虽然损失不大，这次事故仍改变了团队的态度。他们不再把“种上植物”等同于完成项目，而是建立巡查表，明确谁在雨前清理、谁在发现裂缝后联系维修。
随后，林岚把是否继续扩建交给居民、商户和物业共同讨论。会上有人拿出漂亮照片，证明花园深受欢迎；也有人指出，志愿者热情正在减退，仅靠周末劳动难以维持。周叔提出轮班制度，餐馆老板愿意承担专业养护费用，条件是经营区可以保留。经过协商，各方决定暂不增加新屋顶，先观察半年，并把安全记录、开放时段和账户余额定期公布。
这个案例没有把屋顶花园写成成功或失败的简单故事。它提醒学生，城市空间的价值不仅取决于绿色面积，还取决于责任是否清楚、成本由谁承担，以及不同人能否公平使用。反对意见并非故意阻碍变化，支持态度也不能代替细致管理。真正可靠的计划，往往愿意根据证据缩小规模，也允许参与者在发现问题后修改最初的承诺。
pinyin: zài yī mén chéng shì zhì lǐ kè chéng zhōng ， jiào shī shè jì le yí gè míng wèi “ yún tī huā yuán ” de jiào xué àn lì 。 àn lì dì diǎn shì nán fāng chéng shì lín chuān qū yī piàn jiàn yú èr shí nián qián de shāng yè jiē 。 nà lǐ diàn pù mì jí ， dì miàn quē shǎo gōng gòng lǜ dì ， shí èr dòng lóu de wū dǐng què cháng qī xián zhì 。 qū lǐ tí chū wū dǐng huā yuán jì huà ， xī wàng gǎi shàn xià jì gāo wēn ， yě gěi fù jìn jū mín zēng jiā xiū xī kōng jiān 。 xiāo xī gōng bù hòu ， zhī chí zhě chēng tā néng ràng huī sè jiē qū huī fù shēng jī ， fǎn duì zhě zé dān xīn zhè zhǐ shì áng guì de chéng shì zhuāng shì 。

xiàng mù fù zé rén lín lán méi yǒu jí zhe shī gōng ， ér shì xiān yāo qǐng jié gòu gōng chéng shī zhú dòng jiǎn chá 。 jié guǒ xiǎn shì ， bù fèn wū dǐng néng gòu chéng shòu huā chí hé rén qún ， lìng wài jǐ dòng zhǐ néng pū shè qīng xíng zhí wù ， hái yǒu liǎng dòng bì xū fàng qì 。 tā jù cǐ bǎ yuán fāng àn suō xiǎo ， bìng yāo qiú suǒ yǒu cān yù jiàn zhù bǎo liú pái shuǐ tōng dào 。 shāng hù qǐ chū bù mǎn ， rèn wéi jiǎn chá tuō màn jìn dù ； lín lán què jiě shì ， rú guǒ hū lüè chéng zhòng 、 fáng shuǐ hé xiāo fáng ， zài piào liàng de shè jì yě kě néng gěi lóu xià jīng yíng zhě dài lái cháng qī fēng xiǎn 。

zhēn zhèng de zhēng lùn chū xiàn zài shǐ yòng fāng shì shàng 。 cān guǎn lǎo bǎn xī wàng wū dǐng chéng wéi xiāo fèi qū ， yǐ biàn shōu huí wéi hù chéng běn ； jū mín dài biǎo zhōu shū zé zhǔ zhāng miǎn fèi kāi fàng ， yóu qí yào gěi lǎo rén hé hái zi liú chū ān jìng jiǎo luò 。 lín lán méi yǒu zài liǎng zhě zhī jiān jiǎn dān xuǎn biān ， ér shì bǎ kōng jiān fēn chéng gōng gòng huā yuán 、 xiǎo xíng jīng yíng qū hé yǔ shuǐ zhòng zhí qū 。 jīng yíng shōu rù de yī bù fèn jìn rù gòng tóng zhàng hù ， yòng yú gòu mǎi tǔ rǎng 、 xiū lǐ hù lán ， bìng gōng kāi měi yuè zhī chū 。

jì huà yùn xíng sān gè yuè hòu ， kè chéng cái liào jì lù le jiē duàn guān chá ： bàng wǎn lái sàn bù de rén zhú jiàn zēng jiā ， dǐng céng jǐ jiā diàn de shì nèi wēn dù zài bù fèn qíng tiān yǒu suǒ xià jiàng ， dàn xiào guǒ bìng bù wěn dìng 。 yī cháng bào yǔ hái bào lù chū wèn tí ， yī chù pái shuǐ kǒu bèi luò yè dǔ zhù ， jī shuǐ shèn jìn cāng kù 。 suī rán sǔn shī bù dà ， zhè cì shì gù réng gǎi biàn le tuán duì de tài dù 。 tā men bù zài bǎ “ zhǒng shàng zhí wù ” děng tóng yú wán chéng xiàng mù ， ér shì jiàn lì xún chá biǎo ， míng què shuí zài yǔ qián qīng lǐ 、 shuí zài fā xiàn liè fèng hòu lián xì wéi xiū 。

suí hòu ， lín lán bǎ shì fǒu jì xù kuò jiàn jiāo gěi jū mín 、 shāng hù hé wù yè gòng tóng tǎo lùn 。 huì shàng yǒu rén ná chū piào liàng zhào piān ， zhèng míng huā yuán shēn shòu huān yíng ； yě yǒu rén zhǐ chū ， zhì yuàn zhě rè qíng zhèng zài jiǎn tuì ， jǐn kào zhōu mò láo dòng nán yǐ wéi chí 。 zhōu shū tí chū lún bān zhì dù ， cān guǎn lǎo bǎn yuàn yì chéng dān zhuān yè yǎng hù fèi yòng ， tiáo jiàn shì jīng yíng qū kě yǐ bǎo liú 。 jīng guò xié shāng ， gè fāng jué dìng zàn bù zēng jiā xīn wū dǐng ， xiān guān chá bàn nián ， bìng bǎ ān quán jì lù 、 kāi fàng shí duàn hé zhàng hù yú é dìng qī gōng bù 。

zhè ge àn lì méi yǒu bǎ wū dǐng huā yuán xiě chéng chéng gōng huò shī bài de jiǎn dān gù shì 。 tā tí xǐng xué shēng ， chéng shì kōng jiān de jià zhí bù jǐn qǔ jué yú lǜ sè miàn jī ， hái qǔ jué yú zé rèn shì fǒu qīng chǔ 、 chéng běn yóu shuí chéng dān ， yǐ jí bù tóng rén néng fǒu gōng píng shǐ yòng 。 fǎn duì yì jiàn bìng fēi gù yì zǔ ài biàn huà ， zhī chí tài dù yě bù néng dài tì xì zhì guǎn lǐ 。 zhēn zhèng kě kào de jì huà ， wǎng wǎng yuàn yì gēn jù zhèng jù suō xiǎo guī mó ， yě yǔn xǔ cān yù zhě zài fā xiàn wèn tí hòu xiū gǎi zuì chū de chéng nuò 。
translation: In an urban governance course, the instructor created a teaching case called Cloud Ladder Garden. The case was set on a commercial street built twenty years earlier in Linchuan District of a southern city. Shops were densely packed there, public green space at ground level was scarce, yet the rooftops of twelve buildings had long remained unused. The district proposed a rooftop garden plan in the hope of easing summer heat and providing nearby residents with additional places to rest. After the announcement, supporters said it could bring life back to the gray neighborhood, while opponents worried that it was merely an expensive urban decoration.

Lin Lan, the project manager, did not rush into construction. Instead, she first invited structural engineers to inspect the buildings one by one. The results showed that some rooftops could support planting beds and crowds, several others could hold only lightweight plants, and two had to be abandoned. On this basis, she reduced the original plan and required every participating building to keep its drainage channels clear. The merchants were dissatisfied at first, believing the inspections were delaying progress. Lin Lan explained, however, that if load-bearing capacity, waterproofing, and fire safety were ignored, even the most attractive design could create long-term risks for the businesses downstairs.

The real dispute concerned how the space would be used. The restaurant owner wanted the rooftops to become commercial areas so that they could recover maintenance costs, while Uncle Zhou, a residents' representative, argued that access should be free, with quiet corners reserved especially for older people and children. Lin Lan did not simply take one side. Instead, she divided the space into a public garden, a small commercial zone, and a rainwater planting area. Part of the business revenue was placed in a shared account to purchase soil and repair railings, and the monthly expenses were made public.

After the plan had operated for three months, the course materials recorded several interim observations: the number of people taking evening walks gradually increased, and indoor temperatures at several top-floor shops fell on some sunny days, although the effect was inconsistent. A heavy rainstorm also exposed a problem when leaves blocked a drain and standing water leaked into a warehouse. Although the loss was limited, the incident still changed the team's attitude. They no longer treated putting in plants as equivalent to completing the project. Instead, they created an inspection checklist specifying who would clean before rain and who would contact maintenance workers after cracks were discovered.

Lin Lan then asked residents, merchants, and the property management company to discuss together whether the project should continue expanding. At the meeting, some people presented attractive photographs as proof that the garden was popular. Others pointed out that the volunteers' enthusiasm was fading and that weekend labor alone would be difficult to sustain. Uncle Zhou proposed a rotating duty system, while the restaurant owner agreed to cover the cost of professional care on the condition that the commercial zone could remain. After negotiation, all parties decided not to add new rooftops for the time being, but to observe the project for another six months and regularly publish safety records, opening hours, and the account balance.

This case does not present the rooftop garden as a simple story of success or failure. It reminds students that the value of urban space depends not only on the amount of greenery, but also on whether responsibilities are clear, who bears the costs, and whether different people can use the space fairly. Opposition does not necessarily obstruct change on purpose, and support cannot replace careful management. A truly reliable plan is often willing to reduce its scale in response to evidence and allows participants to revise their original commitments after problems are discovered.

articles.title: 把两个夜晚还给学生
articles.summary: 柳溪中学以教学案例的形式试行晚自习调整，允许学生每周两晚在家学习，并通过任务设计、过程记录和个别支持，在自主安排与学校管理之间寻找平衡。
articles.topic: 把两个夜晚还给学生
paragraphs: 本文是一则用于讨论学校管理的教学案例。临江市柳溪中学过去要求全体住校生从周一到周四参加晚自习，走读生也被鼓励留下。晚上十点以后，校门口常挤着接孩子的车辆；有些学生回家还要洗衣、整理书包，睡眠因此受到影响。校长并没有立刻取消晚自习，而是请学生、家长和教师分别说明困难。意见很快出现分歧：一部分家长担心孩子在家缺乏约束，另一部分家长则认为，统一安排忽视了通勤距离和个人节奏。
经过两轮讨论，学校提出一项为期六周的教学试行方案，而不是宣布长期政策。按照方案，学生每周二、周四可以选择在家自习，其余两个晚上仍在学校学习。选择回家的学生需要在离校前提交当晚计划，内容可以包括复习、阅读、运动或整理错题，但教师不得把在家自习变成额外作业。遇到考试临近、家庭环境不适合学习等情况，学生也可以临时申请留校。学校希望保留选择，而不是用另一种统一要求代替原来的安排。
试行开始后，变化并没有像支持者想象的那样整齐。有的学生回家后效率更高，因为他们可以按照自己的薄弱环节分配时间；也有人被手机和娱乐吸引，直到睡前才匆忙完成计划。教师根据学习记录进行阶段观察，发现问题不完全在于学习地点，而在于学生是否具备安排任务、估计时间和抵抗干扰的能力。于是，班主任不再只检查学生完成了多少页练习，而是指导他们把模糊的目标改成能够执行的小任务。
最大的争议来自一次家长会。一位母亲展示了儿子连续两周没有完成计划的记录，要求学校恢复统一晚自习。她的儿子却解释说，自己过去坐在教室里看似安静，实际上经常发呆，只是问题没有被看见。班主任没有替任何一方下结论，而是请他尝试新的安排：先把手机交给家人保管，完成两项任务后再休息，并在第二天说明计划落空的原因。与其把一次失败理解为学生不自觉，不如把它当作学习自我管理的机会。
六周结束时，学校没有用一次考试成绩判断试行是否成功，也没有宣称这一做法适合所有学校。案例材料中的阶段观察显示，多数学生逐渐形成了较具体的晚间计划，但仍有少数学生需要固定教室和教师提醒。学校最终决定保留每周两个可选择的夜晚，同时为缺乏安静空间或暂时无法独立安排时间的学生开放自习室。调整后的制度承认学生之间存在差异，也提醒家长：真正的自主并不是想做什么就做什么，而是在获得选择之后承担相应的责任。
pinyin: běn wén shì yī zé yòng yú tǎo lùn xué xiào guǎn lǐ de jiào xué àn lì 。 lín jiāng shì liǔ xī zhōng xué guò qù yāo qiú quán tǐ zhù xiào shēng cóng zhōu yī dào zhōu sì cān jiā wǎn zì xí ， zǒu dú shēng yě bèi gǔ lì liú xià 。 wǎn shàng shí diǎn yǐ hòu ， xiào mén kǒu cháng jǐ zhe jiē hái zi de chē liàng ； yǒu xiē xué shēng huí jiā hái yào xǐ yī 、 zhěng lǐ shū bāo ， shuì mián yīn cǐ shòu dào yǐng xiǎng 。 xiào zhǎng bìng méi yǒu lì kè qǔ xiāo wǎn zì xí ， ér shì qǐng xué shēng 、 jiā zhǎng hé jiào shī fēn bié shuō míng kùn nán 。 yì jiàn hěn kuài chū xiàn fēn qí ： yī bù fèn jiā zhǎng dān xīn hái zi zài jiā quē fá yuē shù ， lìng yī bù fèn jiā zhǎng zé rèn wéi ， tǒng yī ān pái hū shì le tōng qín jù lí hé gè rén jié zòu 。

jīng guò liǎng lún tǎo lùn ， xué xiào tí chū yī xiàng wéi qī liù zhōu de jiào xué shì xíng fāng àn ， ér bú shì xuān bù cháng qī zhèng cè 。 àn zhào fāng àn ， xué shēng měi zhōu èr 、 zhōu sì kě yǐ xuǎn zé zài jiā zì xí ， qí yú liǎng gè wǎn shàng réng zài xué xiào xué xí 。 xuǎn zé huí jiā de xué shēng xū yào zài lí xiào qián tí jiāo dàng wǎn jì huà ， nèi róng kě yǐ bāo kuò fù xí 、 yuè dú 、 yùn dòng huò zhěng lǐ cuò tí ， dàn jiào shī bù dé bǎ zài jiā zì xí biàn chéng é wài zuò yè 。 yù dào kǎo shì lín jìn 、 jiā tíng huán jìng bú shì hé xué xí děng qíng kuàng ， xué shēng yě kě yǐ lín shí shēn qǐng liú xiào 。 xué xiào xī wàng bǎo liú xuǎn zé ， ér bú shì yòng lìng yī zhǒng tǒng yī yāo qiú dài tì yuán lái de ān pái 。

shì xíng kāi shǐ hòu ， biàn huà bìng méi yǒu xiàng zhī chí zhě xiǎng xiàng de nà yàng zhěng qí 。 yǒu de xué shēng huí jiā hòu xiào lǜ gèng gāo ， yīn wèi tā men kě yǐ àn zhào zì jǐ de bó ruò huán jié fēn pèi shí jiān ； yě yǒu rén bèi shǒu jī hé yú lè xī yǐn ， zhí dào shuì qián cái cōng máng wán chéng jì huà 。 jiào shī gēn jù xué xí jì lù jìn xíng jiē duàn guān chá ， fā xiàn wèn tí bù wán quán zài yú xué xí dì diǎn ， ér zài yú xué shēng shì fǒu jù bèi ān pái rèn wù 、 gū jì shí jiān hé dǐ kàng gān rǎo de néng lì 。 yú shì ， bān zhǔ rèn bù zài zhǐ jiǎn chá xué shēng wán chéng le duō shǎo yè liàn xí ， ér shì zhǐ dǎo tā men bǎ mó hú de mù biāo gǎi chéng néng gòu zhí xíng de xiǎo rèn wù 。

zuì dà de zhēng yì lái zì yī cì jiā zhǎng huì 。 yī wèi mǔ qīn zhǎn shì le ér zi lián xù liǎng zhōu méi yǒu wán chéng jì huà de jì lù ， yāo qiú xué xiào huī fù tǒng yī wǎn zì xí 。 tā de ér zi què jiě shì shuō ， zì jǐ guò qù zuò zài jiào shì lǐ kàn shì ān jìng ， shí jì shàng jīng cháng fā dāi ， zhǐ shì wèn tí méi yǒu bèi kàn jiàn 。 bān zhǔ rèn méi yǒu tì rèn hé yī fāng xià jié lùn ， ér shì qǐng tā cháng shì xīn de ān pái ： xiān bǎ shǒu jī jiāo gěi jiā rén bǎo guǎn ， wán chéng liǎng xiàng rèn wù hòu zài xiū xī ， bìng zài dì èr tiān shuō míng jì huà luò kōng de yuán yīn 。 yǔ qí bǎ yī cì shī bài lǐ jiě wèi xué shēng bù zì jué ， bù rú bǎ tā dàng zuò xué xí zì wǒ guǎn lǐ de jī huì 。

liù zhōu jié shù shí ， xué xiào méi yǒu yòng yī cì kǎo shì chéng jì pàn duàn shì xíng shì fǒu chéng gōng ， yě méi yǒu xuān chēng zhè yī zuò fǎ shì hé suǒ yǒu xué xiào 。 àn lì cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， duō shù xué shēng zhú jiàn xíng chéng le jiào jù tǐ de wǎn jiān jì huà ， dàn réng yǒu shǎo shù xué shēng xū yào gù dìng jiào shì hé jiào shī tí xǐng 。 xué xiào zuì zhōng jué dìng bǎo liú měi zhōu liǎng gè kě xuǎn zé de yè wǎn ， tóng shí wèi quē fá ān jìng kōng jiān huò zàn shí wú fǎ dú lì ān pái shí jiān de xué shēng kāi fàng zì xí shì 。 tiáo zhěng hòu de zhì dù chéng rèn xué shēng zhī jiān cún zài chā yì ， yě tí xǐng jiā zhǎng ： zhēn zhèng de zì zhǔ bìng bú shì xiǎng zuò shén me jiù zuò shén me ， ér shì zài huò dé xuǎn zé zhī hòu chéng dān xiāng yìng de zé rèn 。
translation: This is a teaching case designed for discussing school management. Willow Creek Middle School in Linjiang previously required all boarding students to attend evening study sessions from Monday through Thursday, while day students were also encouraged to stay. After ten o'clock at night, vehicles picking up children often crowded the school entrance. Some students still had to wash clothes and organize their schoolbags after returning home, which affected their sleep. Instead of immediately canceling evening study, the principal asked students, parents, and teachers to describe their difficulties separately. Disagreement soon emerged: some parents worried that their children would lack discipline at home, while others believed that a uniform arrangement ignored commuting distances and individual routines.

After two rounds of discussion, the school proposed a six-week instructional trial rather than announcing a long-term policy. Under the plan, students could choose to study at home on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while continuing to study at school on the other two evenings. Students choosing to go home had to submit an evening plan before leaving school. It could include reviewing, reading, exercising, or reviewing questions they had answered incorrectly, but teachers were not allowed to turn home study into additional homework. When examinations were approaching or the home environment was unsuitable for studying, students could also apply to remain at school temporarily. The school wanted to preserve choice rather than replace the original arrangement with another uniform requirement.

After the trial began, the changes were not as consistent as supporters had imagined. Some students became more efficient at home because they could allocate time according to their own weak areas. Others were distracted by phones and entertainment and did not hurriedly complete their plans until bedtime. Based on study logs, teachers conducted observations at different stages and found that the problem did not lie entirely in the place of study, but in whether students could organize tasks, estimate time, and resist distractions. As a result, homeroom teachers stopped checking only how many pages of exercises students had completed and instead taught them to turn vague goals into small, actionable tasks.

The greatest controversy arose at a parent meeting. One mother presented records showing that her son had failed to complete his plans for two consecutive weeks and demanded that uniform evening study be restored. Her son, however, explained that although he had appeared quiet while sitting in the classroom, he had often been lost in thought; the problem had simply remained unseen. The homeroom teacher did not reach a conclusion on behalf of either side. Instead, the teacher asked him to try a new arrangement: first hand his phone to a family member for safekeeping, rest only after completing two tasks, and explain the next day why the plan had failed. Rather than interpreting one failure as proof that a student lacks self-discipline, it is better to treat it as an opportunity to learn self-management.

At the end of the six weeks, the school did not judge the trial's success by a single examination result, nor did it claim that the approach was suitable for every school. The staged observations in the case materials indicated that most students gradually developed more specific evening plans, although a small number still needed a designated classroom and reminders from teachers. The school ultimately decided to retain two optional evenings each week while keeping study rooms open for students who lacked a quiet space or were temporarily unable to manage their time independently. The revised system acknowledged differences among students and also reminded parents that genuine autonomy does not mean doing whatever one wants; it means accepting the corresponding responsibility after being given a choice.

articles.title: 旧印刷厂里的共享厨房
articles.summary: 一座由旧印刷厂改造的共享厨房在运营中暴露出排期、责任和成本等问题，管理者通过调整制度，使项目逐渐成为餐饮创业者验证产品与相互协作的平台。
articles.topic: 旧印刷厂里的共享厨房
paragraphs: 林澄在南川市经营一家食品设备公司。一次拜访客户时，他发现河西旧印刷厂长期空置，而附近不少餐饮创业者正为场地发愁：有人想试做低糖点心，却承担不起整间店铺的租金；有人接到临时订单，却因设备不足只能放弃。林澄由此提出共享厨房计划，把厂房改造成六个操作间，配备烤箱、冷库和消毒设备，使用者可以按小时预约。这个项目并非真实统计研究，而是编辑设计的教学案例，其中的经营情况只代表材料所记录的阶段观察。
改造完成后，第一批申请者很快进场。做地方酱料的周岚原来在家生产，订单稍多就无法周转；搬进共享厨房后，她既能按照卫生要求分区操作，也能在销售旺季延长使用时间。然而，按小时出租看似灵活，执行起来却不轻松。有人提前结束却忘记关闭设备，有人为了赶工占用公共清洗区，还有人迟到半小时，导致后面的预约全部推迟。管理人员起初只在群里提醒，结果同类问题反复出现，使用者之间也开始互相抱怨。

最棘手的一次冲突发生在端午节前。三支团队同时接到粽子订单，却只有一台大型蒸箱可用。系统按照预约顺序分配设备，但其中一支团队临时增加产量，希望延长两个小时。周岚不同意让出时段，因为她若不能按时完成，合作商店就会取消第二天的促销。林澄没有简单地要求双方互相体谅，而是调出预约记录，计算各自已经投入的原料和延误成本，最后把空闲的小蒸箱组合起来，并安排工作人员协助调整流程。三支团队虽然都缩减了部分产量，但没有任何一方被迫停工。

这次冲突促使林澄重新设计规则。他把收费拆成基础场地费、设备使用费和清洁保证金，使使用者能够看清每项成本；同时规定，热门设备必须提前两天确认，临时延长只能进入候补名单。与其依赖口头提醒，不如把责任写进可执行的流程。新系统还记录设备故障和交接情况，如果上一位使用者没有完成清洁，下一位可以上传照片，由值班人员当场判断责任。规则变得严格后，起初有人担心失去自由，但一个月内，预约冲突明显减少，设备闲置时间也得到利用。

更出乎林澄意料的是，共享厨房后来不仅提供场地，还形成了合作网络。周岚把自己的酱料推荐给制作便当的团队，对方则帮她联系社区团购负责人；擅长拍摄短视频的创业者，用厨房时长交换其他人的产品作为拍摄素材。项目没有保证每个品牌都能成功，却降低了试错的代价。年底，林澄拒绝了快速扩建的建议，因为现有模式仍需检验。他认为，共享并不等于把空间切成许多时段，而是通过清楚的边界，让有限资源在不同需求之间保持秩序，并为真正有潜力的想法争取成长时间。
pinyin: lín chéng zài nán chuān shì jīng yíng yī jiā shí pǐn shè bèi gōng sī 。 yī cì bài fǎng kè hù shí ， tā fā xiàn hé xī jiù yìn shuā chǎng zhǎng qī kōng zhì ， ér fù jìn bù shǎo cān yǐn chuàng yè zhě zhèng wèi chǎng dì fā chóu ： yǒu rén xiǎng shì zuò dī táng diǎn xīn ， què chéng dān bù qǐ zhěng jiān diàn pù de zū jīn ； yǒu rén jiē dào lín shí dìng dān ， què yīn shè bèi bù zú zhǐ néng fàng qì 。 lín chéng yóu cǐ tí chū gòng xiǎng chú fáng jì huà ， bǎ chǎng fáng gǎi zào chéng liù gè cāo zuò jiān ， pèi bèi kǎo xiāng 、 lěng kù hé xiāo dú shè bèi ， shǐ yòng zhě kě yǐ àn xiǎo shí yù yuē 。 zhè ge xiàng mù bìng fēi zhēn shí tǒng jì yán jiū ， ér shì biān jí shè jì de jiào xué àn lì ， qí zhōng de jīng yíng qíng kuàng zhǐ dài biǎo cái liào suǒ jì lù de jiē duàn guān chá 。

gǎi zào wán chéng hòu ， dì yī pī shēn qǐng zhě hěn kuài jìn chǎng 。 zuò dì fāng jiàng liào de zhōu lán yuán lái zài jiā shēng chǎn ， dìng dān shāo duō jiù wú fǎ zhōu zhuǎn ； bān jìn gòng xiǎng chú fáng hòu ， tā jì néng àn zhào wèi shēng yāo qiú fēn qū cāo zuò ， yě néng zài xiāo shòu wàng jì yán cháng shǐ yòng shí jiān 。 rán ér ， àn xiǎo shí chū zū kàn shì líng huó ， zhí xíng qǐ lái què bù qīng sōng 。 yǒu rén tí qián jié shù què wàng jì guān bì shè bèi ， yǒu rén wèi le gǎn gōng zhàn yòng gōng gòng qīng xǐ qū ， hái yǒu rén chí dào bàn xiǎo shí ， dǎo zhì hòu miàn de yù yuē quán bù tuī chí 。 guǎn lǐ rén yuán qǐ chū zhǐ zài qún lǐ tí xǐng ， jié guǒ tóng lèi wèn tí fǎn fù chū xiàn ， shǐ yòng zhě zhī jiān yě kāi shǐ hù xiāng bào yuàn 。

zuì jí shǒu de yī cì chōng tū fā shēng zài duān wǔ jié qián 。 sān zhī tuán duì tóng shí jiē dào zòng zi dìng dān ， què zhǐ yǒu yī tái dà xíng zhēng xiāng kě yòng 。 xì tǒng àn zhào yù yuē shùn xù fēn pèi shè bèi ， dàn qí zhōng yī zhī tuán duì lín shí zēng jiā chǎn liàng ， xī wàng yán cháng liǎng gè xiǎo shí 。 zhōu lán bù tóng yì ràng chū shí duàn ， yīn wèi tā ruò bù néng àn shí wán chéng ， hé zuò shāng diàn jiù huì qǔ xiāo dì èr tiān de cù xiāo 。 lín chéng méi yǒu jiǎn dān dì yāo qiú shuāng fāng hù xiāng tǐ liàng ， ér shì diào chū yù yuē jì lù ， jì suàn gè zì yǐ jīng tóu rù de yuán liào hé yán wù chéng běn ， zuì hòu bǎ kòng xián de xiǎo zhēng xiāng zǔ hé qǐ lái ， bìng ān pái gōng zuò rén yuán xié zhù tiáo zhěng liú chéng 。 sān zhī tuán duì suī rán dōu suō jiǎn le bù fèn chǎn liàng ， dàn méi yǒu rèn hé yī fāng bèi pò tíng gōng 。

zhè cì chōng tū cù shǐ lín chéng chóng xīn shè jì guī zé 。 tā bǎ shōu fèi chāi chéng jī chǔ chǎng dì fèi 、 shè bèi shǐ yòng fèi hé qīng jié bǎo zhèng jīn ， shǐ shǐ yòng zhě néng gòu kàn qīng měi xiàng chéng běn ； tóng shí guī dìng ， rè mén shè bèi bì xū tí qián liǎng tiān què rèn ， lín shí yán cháng zhǐ néng jìn rù hòu bǔ míng dān 。 yǔ qí yī lài kǒu tóu tí xǐng ， bù rú bǎ zé rèn xiě jìn kě zhí xíng de liú chéng 。 xīn xì tǒng hái jì lù shè bèi gù zhàng hé jiāo jiē qíng kuàng ， rú guǒ shàng yī wèi shǐ yòng zhě méi yǒu wán chéng qīng jié ， xià yī wèi kě yǐ shàng chuán zhào piān ， yóu zhí bān rén yuán dāng chǎng pàn duàn zé rèn 。 guī zé biàn dé yán gé hòu ， qǐ chū yǒu rén dān xīn shī qù zì yóu ， dàn yí gè yuè nèi ， yù yuē chōng tū míng xiǎn jiǎn shǎo ， shè bèi xián zhì shí jiān yě dé dào lì yòng 。

gèng chū hū lín chéng yì liào de shì ， gòng xiǎng chú fáng hòu lái bù jǐn tí gōng chǎng dì ， hái xíng chéng le hé zuò wǎng luò 。 zhōu lán bǎ zì jǐ de jiàng liào tuī jiàn gěi zhì zuò biàn dāng de tuán duì ， duì fāng zé bāng tā lián xì shè qū tuán gòu fù zé rén ； shàn cháng pāi shè duǎn shì pín de chuàng yè zhě ， yòng chú fáng shí cháng jiāo huàn qí tā rén de chǎn pǐn zuò wéi pāi shè sù cái 。 xiàng mù méi yǒu bǎo zhèng měi gè pǐn pái dōu néng chéng gōng ， què jiàng dī le shì cuò de dài jià 。 nián dǐ ， lín chéng jù jué le kuài sù kuò jiàn de jiàn yì ， yīn wèi xiàn yǒu mó shì réng xū jiǎn yàn 。 tā rèn wéi ， gòng xiǎng bìng bù děng yú bǎ kōng jiān qiè chéng xǔ duō shí duàn ， ér shì tōng guò qīng chǔ de biān jiè ， ràng yǒu xiàn zī yuán zài bù tóng xū qiú zhī jiān bǎo chí zhì xù ， bìng wèi zhēn zhèng yǒu qián lì de xiǎng fǎ zhēng qǔ chéng zhǎng shí jiān 。
translation: Lin Cheng ran a food equipment company in Nanchuan. During a visit to a client, he discovered that an old printing plant west of the river had stood vacant for a long time, while many nearby food entrepreneurs were struggling to find suitable premises. Some wanted to test low-sugar pastries but could not afford the rent for an entire shop; others had to reject temporary orders because they lacked equipment. Lin therefore proposed a shared-kitchen plan. He converted the plant into six workrooms equipped with ovens, cold storage, and sanitizing facilities, which users could reserve by the hour. This project is not presented as real statistical research but as an educational case designed by the editors, and its operating conditions represent only the observations recorded at one stage in the material.

After the renovation was completed, the first group of applicants quickly moved in. Zhou Lan, who made regional sauces, had previously produced them at home and could not keep operations moving whenever orders increased. After entering the shared kitchen, she could separate her work areas in accordance with hygiene requirements and extend her hours during the peak sales season. Yet hourly rental, though seemingly flexible, was difficult to manage in practice. Some people finished early but forgot to switch off the equipment, some occupied the communal washing area to rush their work, and others arrived half an hour late, delaying every subsequent reservation. At first, the managers only posted reminders in the group chat. Similar problems kept recurring, however, and users began blaming one another.

The most difficult conflict occurred shortly before the Dragon Boat Festival. Three teams received rice-dumpling orders at the same time, but only one large steamer was available. The system allocated the equipment according to reservation order, yet one team unexpectedly increased its planned output and requested an additional two hours. Zhou Lan refused to give up her time slot because, if she failed to finish on schedule, a partner store would cancel the next day's promotion. Instead of simply asking both sides to be considerate, Lin retrieved the booking records and calculated the ingredients already committed and the costs of delay for each party. He then combined several idle smaller steamers and assigned staff to help reorganize the workflow. Although all three teams reduced part of their output, none was forced to stop working.

This conflict prompted Lin to redesign the rules. He divided the charges into a basic venue fee, an equipment fee, and a cleaning deposit so that users could see every cost clearly. He also required popular equipment to be confirmed two days in advance, while requests for last-minute extensions could only enter a waiting list. Rather than relying on verbal reminders, it was better to put responsibilities into enforceable procedures. The new system also recorded equipment failures and handover conditions. If the previous user failed to clean properly, the next user could upload photographs, allowing the staff member on duty to determine responsibility immediately. When the rules became stricter, some people initially worried that they would lose flexibility. Within a month, however, booking conflicts fell noticeably, and idle equipment time was put to use.

Even more unexpectedly for Lin, the shared kitchen eventually became not only a place to work but also a network for cooperation. Zhou Lan recommended her sauces to a team making boxed meals, while that team introduced her to the organizer of a neighborhood group-purchasing service. An entrepreneur skilled at filming short videos exchanged kitchen hours for other users' products to use as filming material. The project did not guarantee that every brand would succeed, but it reduced the cost of trial and error. At the end of the year, Lin rejected a proposal for rapid expansion because the existing model still needed to be tested. In his view, sharing did not mean merely dividing a space into many time slots. It meant establishing clear boundaries so that limited resources could remain orderly amid different demands and promising ideas could gain time to grow.

articles.title: 一场暴雨之后的第二份方案
articles.summary: 青禾社区提出雨水回收方案，却因维护责任、费用分配和实际需求尚不明确而未获立即通过。经过小规模试验和居民协商，委员会最终批准了更透明、更灵活的修改方案。
articles.topic: 一场暴雨之后的第二份方案
paragraphs: 青禾社区建成已有二十多年，每逢暴雨，北门附近的道路就容易积水；到了连续晴天，公共花园却又需要使用自来水浇灌。物业经理周岚因此建议，在三栋住宅楼旁安装雨水收集设备，把屋顶流下来的水储存起来，用于浇花、清洗地面和补充景观池。需要说明的是，这是一则用于课堂讨论的教学案例，文中的费用、降雨量和节水效果都是情境设定，并非真实研究或正式统计。
方案提交后，不少居民认为它既能缓解积水，也能减少浪费。按照最初设计，雨水会先经过过滤装置，再流入地下储水箱；水位超过安全范围时，多余的水仍会进入原有排水系统。周岚估计，如果设备运行稳定，公共区域的部分用水需求可以由雨水满足。然而，工程公司要求社区一次性支付安装费，并建议每户按面积承担费用，这立即引起了争议。住在低层的居民担心施工噪声，高层住户则质疑自己是否能从项目中直接受益。
在居民听证会上，退休工程师许伯提出，设备本身并不复杂，真正容易被忽略的是后期维护。过滤网如果长期不清理，不仅会降低效率，还可能产生气味；储水箱若缺乏定期检查，也会带来卫生风险。他还追问，设备损坏后由谁负责、维修支出是否设有上限、租户搬走时已经支付的费用如何处理。面对这些具体问题，委员会没有立即表决通过，而是要求物业补充维护计划、费用明细和紧急处理办法。

决定延期后，有人批评委员会过于谨慎，周岚却没有急着为原方案辩护。她邀请十二户居民组成观察小组，并借来两个容量较小的储水桶，在社区活动室旁进行六周试验。试验期间，志愿者记录每次降雨后的储水情况，也记录清理过滤网所花的时间。一次大风把树叶吹进排水槽，进水速度明显下降，这个意外让大家意识到，维护频率不能只按照固定日期安排，还要根据天气和周围环境及时调整。原本反对项目的几位居民也参加了清理，并提出可以把简单检查交给志愿者，把涉及安全的工作留给专业人员。

根据试验中暴露的问题，第二份方案取消了按住房面积收费的做法，改为从公共设施预算中分期支出，同时规定任何额外维修都必须提前公开报价。物业还承诺每月公布储水用途、设备状态和维护记录，居民则可以通过季度会议决定是否扩大规模。委员会最终批准先在一栋楼实施一年，而没有同时改造整个社区。这个结果既不是对环保目标的否定，也不是毫无条件的支持；它说明公共方案要获得信任，除了展示可能的好处，还必须回答谁承担责任、信息是否透明以及出现问题后能否及时调整。
pinyin: qīng hé shè qū jiàn chéng yǐ yǒu èr shí duō nián ， měi féng bào yǔ ， běi mén fù jìn de dào lù jiù róng yì jī shuǐ ； dào le lián xù qíng tiān ， gōng gòng huā yuán què yòu xū yào shǐ yòng zì lái shuǐ jiāo guàn 。 wù yè jīng lǐ zhōu lán yīn cǐ jiàn yì ， zài sān dòng zhù zhái lóu páng ān zhuāng yǔ shuǐ shōu jí shè bèi ， bǎ wū dǐng liú xià lái de shuǐ chǔ cún qǐ lái ， yòng yú jiāo huā 、 qīng xǐ dì miàn hé bǔ chōng jǐng guān chí 。 xū yào shuō míng de shì ， zhè shì yī zé yòng yú kè táng tǎo lùn de jiào xué àn lì ， wén zhōng de fèi yòng 、 jiàng yǔ liàng hé jié shuǐ xiào guǒ dōu shì qíng jìng shè dìng ， bìng fēi zhēn shí yán jiū huò zhèng shì tǒng jì 。

fāng àn tí jiāo hòu ， bù shǎo jū mín rèn wéi tā jì néng huǎn jiě jī shuǐ ， yě néng jiǎn shǎo làng fèi 。 àn zhào zuì chū shè jì ， yǔ shuǐ huì xiān jīng guò guò lǜ zhuāng zhì ， zài liú rù dì xià chǔ shuǐ xiāng ； shuǐ wèi chāo guò ān quán fàn wéi shí ， duō yú de shuǐ réng huì jìn rù yuán yǒu pái shuǐ xì tǒng 。 zhōu lán gū jì ， rú guǒ shè bèi yùn xíng wěn dìng ， gōng gòng qū yù de bù fèn yòng shuǐ xū qiú kě yǐ yóu yǔ shuǐ mǎn zú 。 rán ér ， gōng chéng gōng sī yāo qiú shè qū yí cì xìng zhī fù ān zhuāng fèi ， bìng jiàn yì měi hù àn miàn jī chéng dān fèi yòng ， zhè lì jí yǐn qǐ le zhēng yì 。 zhù zài dī céng de jū mín dān xīn shī gōng zào shēng ， gāo céng zhù hù zé zhì yí zì jǐ shì fǒu néng cóng xiàng mù zhōng zhí jiē shòu yì 。

zài jū mín tīng zhèng huì shàng ， tuì xiū gōng chéng shī xǔ bó tí chū ， shè bèi běn shēn bìng bù fù zá ， zhēn zhèng róng yì bèi hū lüè de shì hòu qī wéi hù 。 guò lǜ wǎng rú guǒ cháng qī bù qīng lǐ ， bù jǐn huì jiàng dī xiào lǜ ， hái kě néng chǎn shēng qì wèi ； chǔ shuǐ xiāng ruò quē fá dìng qī jiǎn chá ， yě huì dài lái wèi shēng fēng xiǎn 。 tā hái zhuī wèn ， shè bèi sǔn huài hòu yóu shuí fù zé 、 wéi xiū zhī chū shì fǒu shè yǒu shàng xiàn 、 zū hù bān zǒu shí yǐ jīng zhī fù de fèi yòng rú hé chǔ lǐ 。 miàn duì zhè xiē jù tǐ wèn tí ， wěi yuán huì méi yǒu lì jí biǎo jué tōng guò ， ér shì yāo qiú wù yè bǔ chōng wéi hù jì huà 、 fèi yòng míng xì hé jǐn jí chǔ lǐ bàn fǎ 。

jué dìng yán qī hòu ， yǒu rén pī píng wěi yuán huì guò yú jǐn shèn ， zhōu lán què méi yǒu jí zhe wèi yuán fāng àn biàn hù 。 tā yāo qǐng shí èr hù jū mín zǔ chéng guān chá xiǎo zǔ ， bìng jiè lái liǎng gè róng liàng jiào xiǎo de chǔ shuǐ tǒng ， zài shè qū huó dòng shì páng jìn xíng liù zhōu shì yàn 。 shì yàn qī jiān ， zhì yuàn zhě jì lù měi cì jiàng yǔ hòu de chǔ shuǐ qíng kuàng ， yě jì lù qīng lǐ guò lǜ wǎng suǒ huā de shí jiān 。 yī cì dà fēng bǎ shù yè chuī jìn pái shuǐ cáo ， jìn shuǐ sù dù míng xiǎn xià jiàng ， zhè ge yì wài ràng dà jiā yì shí dào ， wéi hù pín lǜ bù néng zhǐ àn zhào gù dìng rì qī ān pái ， hái yào gēn jù tiān qì hé zhōu wéi huán jìng jí shí diào zhěng 。 yuán běn fǎn duì xiàng mù dì jǐ wèi jū mín yě cān jiā le qīng lǐ ， bìng tí chū kě yǐ bǎ jiǎn dān jiǎn chá jiāo gěi zhì yuàn zhě ， bǎ shè jí ān quán de gōng zuò liú gěi zhuān yè rén yuán 。

gēn jù shì yàn zhōng bào lù de wèn tí ， dì èr fèn fāng àn qǔ xiāo le àn zhù fáng miàn jī shōu fèi de zuò fǎ ， gǎi wéi cóng gōng gòng shè shī yù suàn zhōng fēn qī zhī chū ， tóng shí guī dìng rèn hé é wài wéi xiū dōu bì xū tí qián gōng kāi bào jià 。 wù yè hái chéng nuò měi yuè gōng bù chǔ shuǐ yòng tú 、 shè bèi zhuàng tài hé wéi hù jì lù ， jū mín zé kě yǐ tōng guò jì dù huì yì jué dìng shì fǒu kuò dà guī mó 。 wěi yuán huì zuì zhōng pī zhǔn xiān zài yī dòng lóu shí shī yī nián ， ér méi yǒu tóng shí gǎi zào zhěng gè shè qū 。 zhè ge jié guǒ jì bú shì duì huán bǎo mù biāo de fǒu dìng ， yě bú shì háo wú tiáo jiàn de zhī chí ； tā shuō míng gōng gòng fāng àn yào huò dé xìn rèn ， chú le zhǎn shì kě néng de hǎo chù ， hái bì xū huí dá shuí chéng dān zé rèn 、 xìn xī shì fǒu tòu míng yǐ jí chū xiàn wèn tí hòu néng fǒu jí shí diào zhěng 。
translation: Qinghe Community was built more than twenty years ago. Whenever there is a heavy rainstorm, the road near the north gate is prone to flooding; yet during extended periods of clear weather, the public garden has to be watered with tap water. Property manager Zhou Lan therefore proposed installing rainwater collection equipment beside three residential buildings. Water flowing from the roofs would be stored and used to water plants, clean the grounds, and replenish the ornamental pond. It should be noted that this is a teaching case designed for classroom discussion. The costs, rainfall levels, and water-saving effects mentioned here are scenario assumptions rather than findings from actual research or official statistics.

After the proposal was submitted, many residents believed that it could both ease flooding and reduce waste. Under the initial design, rainwater would first pass through a filtration unit and then flow into an underground storage tank. When the water level exceeded the safe range, the excess would still enter the existing drainage system. Zhou Lan estimated that, if the equipment operated reliably, rainwater could meet part of the demand for water in public areas. However, the engineering company required the community to pay the installation cost in a single payment and recommended dividing the expense among households according to floor area. This immediately caused controversy. Residents on lower floors worried about construction noise, while those on higher floors questioned whether they would benefit directly from the project.

At the residents' hearing, a retired engineer named Mr. Xu pointed out that the equipment itself was not complicated; what was truly easy to overlook was its long-term maintenance. If the filter screens were not cleaned for a long period, their efficiency would decline and odors might develop. A storage tank without regular inspection could also create hygiene risks. He further asked who would be responsible if the equipment broke down, whether there would be a limit on repair expenses, and how payments already made by tenants would be handled if they moved away. Faced with these specific questions, the committee did not immediately vote to approve the proposal. Instead, it asked the property management company to provide a maintenance plan, an itemized budget, and emergency procedures.

After the decision was postponed, some people criticized the committee for being excessively cautious, but Zhou Lan did not rush to defend the original proposal. She invited residents from twelve households to form an observation group and borrowed two smaller storage barrels for a six-week trial beside the community activity room. During the trial, volunteers recorded the amount of water stored after each rainfall and the time needed to clean the filter screens. On one occasion, strong winds blew leaves into the drainage channel, clearly slowing the inflow. This unexpected event made everyone realize that maintenance frequency could not be arranged solely according to fixed dates and had to be adjusted promptly according to the weather and surrounding conditions. Several residents who had originally opposed the project also joined the cleaning work. They suggested assigning simple inspections to volunteers while leaving safety-related tasks to professionals.

In response to the problems revealed during the trial, the second proposal abandoned charges based on residential floor area and instead divided the expense into installments paid from the public facilities budget. It also required quotations for any additional repairs to be disclosed in advance. Property management promised to publish the uses of the stored water, the condition of the equipment, and maintenance records every month, while residents would be able to decide at quarterly meetings whether to expand the project. The committee ultimately approved a one-year implementation in a single building rather than renovating the entire community at once. This outcome was neither a rejection of environmental goals nor unconditional support. It showed that, to gain trust, a public proposal must do more than demonstrate possible benefits: it must also explain who will bear responsibility, whether information will be transparent, and whether adjustments can be made promptly when problems arise.
