articles.title: 开往山村的图书车
articles.summary: 一辆公共图书流动车进入山区后，工作人员通过调整路线、服务方式和选书机制，使有限的公共阅读资源真正融入当地居民的生活。
articles.topic: 开往山村的图书车
paragraphs: 以下内容是一则用于中文学习的教学案例，其中的地点、人物和数字均为虚构，相关数据只代表项目材料中的阶段观察。云岭县地处山区，村庄分散，居民去县城图书馆往往要换两次车。县图书馆因此把一辆旧客车改造成流动图书馆，车内安装书架、照明设备和无线网络，每两周前往六个偏远村庄。项目负责人周岚原以为，只要把书送到村民家门口，借阅量自然会增加。
图书车第一次抵达石桥村时，孩子们兴奋地围在车旁，成年人却很少靠近。有位老人甚至问，借书是否需要交押金。工作人员解释免费借阅的规则后，仍只有十几个人上车。周岚没有急着把冷清归因于村民缺乏阅读兴趣，而是留下来观察大家的日常安排。她发现，图书车到达的时间正好赶上村民下地劳动；车里的农业书籍虽然不少，内容却比较陈旧，无法解答果树病害、网络销售等实际问题。
周岚随后邀请村医、教师、果农和几名学生参加座谈，请他们提出具体需求。根据建议，图书馆更换了一部分藏书，增加儿童文学、健康常识、短视频制作和农产品经营等内容，还把停车时间从工作日上午改到周末傍晚。考虑到部分老人视力不佳，工作人员准备了大字读物，并在车外设置可以坐下来听书的区域。与其单方面猜测读者喜欢什么，不如让使用者参与选择，这一调整逐渐改变了图书车与村庄之间的关系。
不过，新的问题很快出现了：热门书经常被借走，偏远住户又无法及时归还。若严格执行逾期规定，他们可能因为担心受罚而不再借书；若完全取消期限，其他读者又很难获得同一本书。村民何叔提出，可以让往返县城的班车司机代收图书，再由图书车统一登记。图书馆起初担心书籍丢失，但经过协商，决定先在两个村试行，并用电话短信提醒借阅者。材料记录的三个月阶段观察显示，归还过程比以前顺畅，损坏和遗失也没有明显增加。
项目结束首次评估时，工作人员没有只看借阅总数。他们发现，有些人虽然不把书带回家，却会固定来听故事、查询资料或请人帮助使用网络。一位过去从不上车的果农，还根据新书中的方法改进了产品介绍，并主动给其他村民讲解经验。周岚由此意识到，公共文化服务的价值不只在于提供物品，更在于降低人们接触知识的门槛。图书车能否长期发挥作用，取决于它是否愿意倾听当地需求，并随着生活方式的变化不断调整。
pinyin: yǐ xià nèi róng shì yī zé yòng yú zhōng wén xué xí de jiào xué àn lì ， qí zhōng de dì diǎn 、 rén wù hé shù zì jūn wèi xū gòu ， xiāng guān shù jù zhǐ dài biǎo xiàng mù cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá 。 yún lǐng xiàn dì chǔ shān qū ， cūn zhuāng fēn sàn ， jū mín qù xiàn chéng tú shū guǎn wǎng wǎng yào huàn liǎng cì chē 。 xiàn tú shū guǎn yīn cǐ bǎ yī liàng jiù kè chē gǎi zào chéng liú dòng tú shū guǎn ， chē nèi ān zhuāng shū jià 、 zhào míng shè bèi hé wú xiàn wǎng luò ， měi liǎng zhōu qián wǎng liù gè piān yuǎn cūn zhuāng 。 xiàng mù fù zé rén zhōu lán yuán yǐ wéi ， zhǐ yào bǎ shū sòng dào cūn mín jiā mén kǒu ， jiè yuè liàng zì rán huì zēng jiā 。

tú shū chē dì yī cì dǐ dá shí qiáo cūn shí ， hái zi men xīng fèn dì wéi zài chē páng ， chéng nián rén què hěn shǎo kào jìn 。 yǒu wèi lǎo rén shèn zhì wèn ， jiè shū shì fǒu xū yào jiāo yā jīn 。 gōng zuò rén yuán jiě shì miǎn fèi jiè yuè de guī zé hòu ， réng zhǐ yǒu shí jǐ gè rén shàng chē 。 zhōu lán méi yǒu jí zhe bǎ lěng qīng guī yīn yú cūn mín quē fá yuè dú xìng qù ， ér shì liú xià lái guān chá dà jiā de rì cháng ān pái 。 tā fā xiàn ， tú shū chē dào dá de shí jiān zhèng hǎo gǎn shàng cūn mín xià dì láo dòng ； chē lǐ de nóng yè shū jí suī rán bù shǎo ， nèi róng què bǐ jiào chén jiù ， wú fǎ jiě dá guǒ shù bìng hài 、 wǎng luò xiāo shòu děng shí jì wèn tí 。

zhōu lán suí hòu yāo qǐng cūn yī 、 jiào shī 、 guǒ nóng hé jǐ míng xué shēng cān jiā zuò tán ， qǐng tā men tí chū jù tǐ xū qiú 。 gēn jù jiàn yì ， tú shū guǎn gēng huàn le yī bù fèn cáng shū ， zēng jiā ér tóng wén xué 、 jiàn kāng cháng shí 、 duǎn shì pín zhì zuò hé nóng chǎn pǐn jīng yíng děng nèi róng ， hái bǎ tíng chē shí jiān cóng gōng zuò rì shàng wǔ gǎi dào zhōu mò bàng wǎn 。 kǎo lǜ dào bù fèn lǎo rén shì lì bù jiā ， gōng zuò rén yuán zhǔn bèi le dà zì dú wù ， bìng zài chē wài shè zhì kě yǐ zuò xià lái tīng shū de qū yù 。 yǔ qí dān fāng miàn cāi cè dú zhě xǐ huān shén me ， bù rú ràng shǐ yòng zhě cān yù xuǎn zé ， zhè yī tiáo zhěng zhú jiàn gǎi biàn le tú shū chē yǔ cūn zhuāng zhī jiān de guān xì 。

bù guò ， xīn de wèn tí hěn kuài chū xiàn le ： rè mén shū jīng cháng bèi jiè zǒu ， piān yuǎn zhù hù yòu wú fǎ jí shí guī huán 。 ruò yán gé zhí xíng yú qī guī dìng ， tā men kě néng yīn wèi dān xīn shòu fá ér bù zài jiè shū ； ruò wán quán qǔ xiāo qī xiàn ， qí tā dú zhě yòu hěn nán huò dé tóng yī běn shū 。 cūn mín hé shū tí chū ， kě yǐ ràng wǎng fǎn xiàn chéng de bān chē sī jī dài shōu tú shū ， zài yóu tú shū chē tǒng yī dēng jì 。 tú shū guǎn qǐ chū dān xīn shū jí diū shī ， dàn jīng guò xié shāng ， jué dìng xiān zài liǎng gè cūn shì xíng ， bìng yòng diàn huà duǎn xìn tí xǐng jiè yuè zhě 。 cái liào jì lù de sān gè yuè jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， guī huán guò chéng bǐ yǐ qián shùn chàng ， sǔn huài hé yí shī yě méi yǒu míng xiǎn zēng jiā 。

xiàng mù jié shù shǒu cì píng gū shí ， gōng zuò rén yuán méi yǒu zhǐ kàn jiè yuè zǒng shù 。 tā men fā xiàn ， yǒu xiē rén suī rán bù bǎ shū dài huí jiā ， què huì gù dìng lái tīng gù shì 、 chá xún zī liào huò qǐng rén bāng zhù shǐ yòng wǎng luò 。 yī wèi guò qù cóng bù shàng chē de guǒ nóng ， hái gēn jù xīn shū zhōng de fāng fǎ gǎi jìn le chǎn pǐn jiè shào ， bìng zhǔ dòng gěi qí tā cūn mín jiǎng jiě jīng yàn 。 zhōu lán yóu cǐ yì shí dào ， gōng gòng wén huà fú wù de jià zhí bù zhǐ zài yú tí gōng wù pǐn ， gèng zài yú jiàng dī rén men jiē chù zhī shí de mén kǎn 。 tú shū chē néng fǒu cháng qī fā huī zuò yòng ， qǔ jué yú tā shì fǒu yuàn yì qīng tīng dāng dì xū qiú ， bìng suí zhe shēng huó fāng shì de biàn huà bù duàn tiáo zhěng 。
translation: The following is a teaching case designed for Chinese-language learning. Its locations, characters, and figures are fictional, and the data represent only interim observations recorded in the project materials. Yunling County lies in a mountainous region where villages are widely scattered, and residents often have to change buses twice to reach the county library. The library therefore converted an old coach into a mobile library, installing bookshelves, lighting, and wireless internet. Every two weeks, it traveled to six remote villages. The project director, Zhou Lan, initially assumed that borrowing would naturally increase as long as books were delivered to the villagers' doorsteps.

When the bookmobile first arrived in Shiqiao Village, children gathered around it excitedly, but few adults approached. One elderly resident even asked whether a deposit was required. After the staff explained the rules for free borrowing, only a little more than a dozen people boarded. Zhou Lan did not hastily attribute the poor turnout to a lack of interest in reading. Instead, she stayed to observe the residents' daily routines. She discovered that the bookmobile arrived just as villagers were leaving to work in the fields. Although it carried many agricultural books, their content was outdated and could not answer practical questions about fruit-tree diseases or online sales.

Zhou Lan then invited a village doctor, teachers, fruit growers, and several students to a discussion and asked them to identify specific needs. In response, the library replaced part of its collection and added children's literature, basic health information, short-video production guides, and books on agricultural product management. It also moved its visiting time from weekday mornings to weekend evenings. Because some elderly residents had poor eyesight, the staff prepared large-print books and created an outdoor area where people could sit and listen to readings. Rather than guessing unilaterally what readers preferred, it was better to involve users in making selections, and this adjustment gradually changed the relationship between the bookmobile and the village.

However, a new problem soon arose: popular books were often checked out, while residents in distant homes could not return them promptly. If overdue rules were strictly enforced, these readers might stop borrowing because they feared penalties; if deadlines were removed entirely, other readers would struggle to obtain the same books. A villager named Uncle He suggested asking bus drivers traveling to and from the county seat to collect books, which the bookmobile could later register together. The library initially worried about losses, but after discussion it decided to test the method in two villages and remind borrowers by text message. Interim observations recorded in the materials over three months showed that returns became smoother, with no noticeable increase in damage or loss.

During the project's first evaluation, the staff did not look only at the total number of loans. They found that some people, although they did not take books home, regularly came to listen to stories, search for information, or ask for help using the internet. A fruit grower who had previously never entered the vehicle used methods from a new book to improve his product descriptions and voluntarily explained his experience to other villagers. Zhou Lan consequently realized that the value of public cultural services lies not only in providing materials but also in lowering the barriers to accessing knowledge. Whether the bookmobile can remain effective in the long term depends on its willingness to listen to local needs and continually adapt to changes in people's ways of life.

articles.title: 当实验室在周末打开大门
articles.summary: 一所大学以教学案例的形式试行周末开放实验室，通过预约、培训和分层任务，让中学生安全地接触基础实验设备，也促使大学重新思考公共教育资源的使用方式。
articles.topic: 当实验室在周末打开大门
paragraphs: 在不少人的想象中，大学实验室的大门只对研究人员和大学生开放。本文教学案例中的北川大学却尝试改变这一惯例：每月选择一个周末，邀请附近中学的学生进入材料实验室，在教师和志愿者的指导下使用显微镜、电子秤等基础设备。学校没有把活动办成热闹的参观，而是要求每名学生亲手完成观察、记录和解释三个环节。
制度刚公布时，实验室负责人林教授并不赞成。他担心中学生缺乏经验，既可能损坏仪器，也可能因操作不当而受伤。更现实的问题是，研究团队平日已经承担繁重任务，周末值班会增加额外负担。负责项目的教务人员没有回避这些顾虑，而是把开放范围限制在风险较低的区域，并规定学生必须提前预约、完成安全课程，才能获得入场资格。
第一次活动中，学生要判断三种包装材料在潮湿环境中的变化。工作人员没有直接讲解结论，只提供样品、测量工具和记录表。一名学生发现自己的数据与同组伙伴差别很大，便认为仪器出了故障。志愿者没有替他重新测量，而是请他检查取样位置、操作顺序和记录单位。经过反复核对，他终于发现自己把克和毫克混在了一起，也因此理解了实验规范并非多余的形式。
活动结束后的讨论暴露出另一个问题：有些学生能够熟练操作，却无法说明数据意味着什么；还有些学生害怕犯错，始终等着教师给出标准答案。项目组随后调整任务，把问题分为基础观察、原因推测和方案设计三个层次，并允许学生保留没有得到验证的猜想。与其追求整齐一致的答案，教师更看重学生能否说明判断依据，以及能否承认证据暂时不足。
为了避免开放制度影响正常科研，学校建立了设备清单和责任记录。精密仪器仍由专业人员操作，中学生只能在旁观察；基础设备则按照使用频率安排维护。大学生志愿者也不再只是维持秩序，他们需要接受沟通训练，学习怎样用准确而不生硬的语言解释概念。林教授逐渐发现，回答初学者提出的简单问题，反而迫使研究人员重新审视那些早已习以为常的假设。
经过一个学期的阶段观察，项目组没有急于用参加人数证明制度成功。教学案例记录显示，真正值得关注的结果，是部分学生开始主动修改实验步骤，并能区分事实、推测与结论。学校最终决定继续试行，但没有盲目扩大规模，而是优先完善预约流程和志愿者培训。开放实验室的意义不在于让所有人接触昂贵设备，而在于把严谨求证的态度带到更广泛的学习生活中。
pinyin: zài bù shǎo rén de xiǎng xiàng zhōng ， dà xué shí yàn shì de dà mén zhǐ duì yán jiū rén yuán hé dà xué shēng kāi fàng 。 běn wén jiào xué àn lì zhōng de běi chuān dà xué què cháng shì gǎi biàn zhè yī guàn lì ： měi yuè xuǎn zé yí gè zhōu mò ， yāo qǐng fù jìn zhōng xué de xué shēng jìn rù cái liào shí yàn shì ， zài jiào shī hé zhì yuàn zhě de zhǐ dǎo xià shǐ yòng xiǎn wēi jìng 、 diàn zi chèng děng jī chǔ shè bèi 。 xué xiào méi yǒu bǎ huó dòng bàn chéng rè nào de cān guān ， ér shì yāo qiú měi míng xué shēng qīn shǒu wán chéng guān chá 、 jì lù hé jiě shì sān gè huán jié 。

zhì dù gāng gōng bù shí ， shí yàn shì fù zé rén lín jiào shòu bìng bù zàn chéng 。 tā dān xīn zhōng xué shēng quē fá jīng yàn ， jì kě néng sǔn huài yí qì ， yě kě néng yīn cāo zuò bù dàng ér shòu shāng 。 gèng xiàn shí de wèn tí shì ， yán jiū tuán duì píng rì yǐ jīng chéng dān fán zhòng rèn wù ， zhōu mò zhí bān huì zēng jiā é wài fù dān 。 fù zé xiàng mù dì jiào wù rén yuán méi yǒu huí bì zhè xiē gù lǜ ， ér shì bǎ kāi fàng fàn wéi xiàn zhì zài fēng xiǎn jiào dī de qū yù ， bìng guī dìng xué shēng bì xū tí qián yù yuē 、 wán chéng ān quán kè chéng ， cái néng huò dé rù chǎng zī gé 。

dì yī cì huó dòng zhōng ， xué shēng yào pàn duàn sān zhǒng bāo zhuāng cái liào zài cháo shī huán jìng zhōng de biàn huà 。 gōng zuò rén yuán méi yǒu zhí jiē jiǎng jiě jié lùn ， zhǐ tí gōng yàng pǐn 、 cè liáng gōng jù hé jì lù biǎo 。 yī míng xué shēng fà xiàn zì jǐ de shù jù yǔ tóng zǔ huǒ bàn chā bié hěn dà ， biàn rèn wéi yí qì chū le gù zhàng 。 zhì yuàn zhě méi yǒu tì tā chóng xīn cè liáng ， ér shì qǐng tā jiǎn chá qǔ yàng wèi zhì 、 cāo zuò shùn xù hé jì lù dān wèi 。 jīng guò fǎn fù hé duì ， tā zhōng yú fā xiàn zì jǐ bǎ kè hé háo kè hùn zài le yì qǐ ， yě yīn cǐ lǐ jiě le shí yàn guī fàn bìng fēi duō yú de xíng shì 。

huó dòng jié shù hòu de tǎo lùn bào lù chū lìng yí gè wèn tí ： yǒu xiē xué shēng néng gòu shú liàn cāo zuò ， què wú fǎ shuō míng shù jù yì wèi zhe shén me ； hái yǒu xiē xué shēng hài pà fàn cuò ， shǐ zhōng děng zhe jiào shī gěi chū biāo zhǔn dá àn 。 xiàng mù zǔ suí hòu tiáo zhěng rèn wù ， bǎ wèn tí fēn wéi jī chǔ guān chá 、 yuán yīn tuī cè hé fāng àn shè jì sān gè céng cì ， bìng yǔn xǔ xué shēng bǎo liú méi yǒu dé dào yàn zhèng de cāi xiǎng 。 yǔ qí zhuī qiú zhěng qí yí zhì de dá àn ， jiào shī gèng kàn zhòng xué shēng néng fǒu shuō míng pàn duàn yī jù ， yǐ jí néng fǒu chéng rèn zhèng jù zàn shí bù zú 。

wèi le bì miǎn kāi fàng zhì dù yǐng xiǎng zhèng cháng kē yán ， xué xiào jiàn lì le shè bèi qīng dān hé zé rèn jì lù 。 jīng mì yí qì réng yóu zhuān yè rén yuán cāo zuò ， zhōng xué shēng zhǐ néng zài páng guān chá ； jī chǔ shè bèi zé àn zhào shǐ yòng pín lǜ ān pái wéi hù 。 dà xué shēng zhì yuàn zhě yě bù zài zhǐ shì wéi chí zhì xù ， tā men xū yào jiē shòu gōu tōng xùn liàn ， xué xí zěn yàng yòng zhǔn què ér bù shēng yìng de yǔ yán jiě shì gài niàn 。 lín jiào shòu zhú jiàn fā xiàn ， huí dá chū xué zhě tí chū de jiǎn dān wèn tí ， fǎn ér pò shǐ yán jiū rén yuán chóng xīn shěn shì nà xiē zǎo yǐ xí yǐ wéi cháng de jiǎ shè 。

jīng guò yí gè xué qī de jiē duàn guān chá ， xiàng mù zǔ méi yǒu jí yú yòng cān jiā rén shù zhèng míng zhì dù chéng gōng 。 jiào xué àn lì jì lù xiǎn shì ， zhēn zhèng zhí de guān zhù de jié guǒ ， shì bù fèn xué shēng kāi shǐ zhǔ dòng xiū gǎi shí yàn bù zhòu ， bìng néng qū fēn shì shí 、 tuī cè yǔ jié lùn 。 xué xiào zuì zhōng jué dìng jì xù shì xíng ， dàn méi yǒu máng mù kuò dà guī mó ， ér shì yōu xiān wán shàn yù yuē liú chéng hé zhì yuàn zhě péi xùn 。 kāi fàng shí yàn shì de yì yì bù zài yú ràng suǒ yǒu rén jiē chù áng guì shè bèi ， ér zài yú bǎ yán jǐn qiú zhèng de tài dù dài dào gèng guǎng fàn de xué xí shēng huó zhōng 。
translation: In many people's imagination, university laboratories are open only to researchers and university students. In this teaching case, however, Beichuan University tried to change that convention. One weekend each month, it invited students from nearby secondary schools into its materials laboratory to use basic equipment such as microscopes and electronic scales under the guidance of teachers and volunteers. Instead of turning the activity into a lively tour, the university required every student to complete the three stages of observation, recording, and explanation personally.

When the program was first announced, Professor Lin, the head of the laboratory, did not support it. He worried that inexperienced secondary school students might damage instruments or injure themselves through improper operation. A more practical concern was that the research team already carried a heavy workload on weekdays, and weekend duty would create an additional burden. Rather than avoiding these concerns, the academic affairs staff limited access to lower-risk areas and required students to make reservations and complete a safety course before becoming eligible to enter.

During the first session, students were asked to determine how three kinds of packaging material changed in a humid environment. The staff did not explain the conclusion directly, but provided only samples, measuring tools, and record sheets. One student noticed that his data differed greatly from those of his group members and assumed that the instrument was faulty. Instead of repeating the measurement for him, a volunteer asked him to check the sampling location, operating sequence, and recorded units. After checking repeatedly, he finally discovered that he had confused grams with milligrams, and he came to understand that experimental rules were not pointless formalities.

The discussion after the session revealed another problem. Some students could operate the equipment skillfully but could not explain what the data meant, while others were so afraid of making mistakes that they kept waiting for the teacher to provide a standard answer. The project team then revised the tasks, dividing the questions into three levels: basic observation, inference about causes, and solution design. Students were also allowed to retain hypotheses that had not yet been verified. Rather than seeking perfectly uniform answers, the teachers cared more about whether students could explain the basis of their judgments and acknowledge when the evidence remained insufficient.

To prevent the access program from interfering with regular research, the university established an equipment list and a responsibility log. Precision instruments continued to be operated by professionals while secondary school students could only observe; basic equipment was maintained according to how frequently it was used. University volunteers were no longer there merely to keep order. They had to receive communication training and learn to explain concepts in language that was accurate without being stiff. Professor Lin gradually realized that answering simple questions from beginners actually forced researchers to reconsider assumptions they had long taken for granted.

After one semester of interim observation, the project team did not rush to prove the program successful by citing attendance. Records from the teaching case showed that the result truly worth noting was that some students began revising experimental procedures on their own and became able to distinguish facts, hypotheses, and conclusions. The university ultimately decided to continue the trial, but instead of expanding it blindly, it gave priority to improving the reservation process and volunteer training. The significance of an open laboratory does not lie in allowing everyone to handle expensive equipment, but in bringing an attitude of rigorous verification into a broader range of learning and everyday life.

articles.title: 旧衣换车票之后
articles.summary: 一项旧衣回收积分计划因信息不透明和兑换规则不公平而暂停，社区通过公开衣物去向、调整积分标准和提供替代奖励，使环保行动变得更可信、更方便。
articles.topic: 旧衣换车票之后
paragraphs: 以下内容是一则用于中文课堂讨论的教学案例，不对应任何城市已经公布的政策或统计。临江社区附近交通方便，却有不少居民习惯开车短途出行。社区工作人员陈岚提出一项试行计划：居民把不再穿的旧衣送到回收站，经过登记和称重后获得积分，积分可以兑换公交优惠券。她希望这项计划既能减少旧衣浪费，也能鼓励居民优先选择公共交通。
计划开始后的第一个星期，回收站门口常常排起长队。有人特意把衣服洗干净、叠整齐，也有人一次拖来几个塞满衣物的大袋子。工作人员需要检查衣物是否潮湿，再按照重量折算积分。起初，不少居民以为衣服越多，得到的优惠就越大，因此连破损严重、无法再次使用的衣物也送了过来，现场很快出现了堆放和分类的压力。
更大的问题来自居民对旧衣去向的质疑。宣传单上只写着“统一处理”，没有说明哪些衣服会被捐赠，哪些会被加工成再生材料。一位居民在网上留言说，自己原以为完好的外套会直接交给有需要的人，后来却听说部分衣物被送进工厂。虽然这种处理并不一定造成浪费，但含糊的说明使人产生了被欺骗的感觉。社区只好暂时停止接收旧衣，并邀请回收企业公开处理流程。
陈岚随后追踪了衣物从登记、运输到最终处理的各个环节。她发现，原来的积分规则只考虑重量，没有考虑衣物状态，也忽略了不会使用手机的老年居民。此外，有些人平时很少乘公交，优惠券对他们并没有吸引力。与其用同一种奖励吸引所有人参与，不如给居民提供符合实际需要的选择。
重新开放后，回收站把衣物分为可再次穿着、可加工利用和无法接收三类，并在现场说明每一类的去向。完好衣物不再单纯按重量计算，而是经过简单核实后获得额外积分；居民除了兑换公交优惠券，还可以选择社区食堂餐券或公共自行车使用时长。没有智能手机的人可以领取纸质积分卡，从而避免技术门槛影响参与。
一个月后的阶段观察显示，回收站收到的衣物总量有所下降，但潮湿、严重破损的衣物明显减少，工作人员也不必反复解释处理方式。这些变化只是教学案例中的阶段性结果，不能被当作普遍统计。陈岚认为，环保计划的价值不在于短时间收集了多少旧衣，而在于是否建立了透明、方便并且能够长期维持的机制。奖励可以吸引居民迈出第一步，清楚的规则和可靠的处理过程才能保留他们的信任。
pinyin: yǐ xià nèi róng shì yī zé yòng yú zhōng wén kè táng tǎo lùn de jiào xué àn lì ， bú duì yīng rèn hé chéng shì yǐ jīng gōng bù de zhèng cè huò tǒng jì 。 lín jiāng shè qū fù jìn jiāo tōng fāng biàn ， què yǒu bù shǎo jū mín xí guàn kāi chē duǎn tú chū xíng 。 shè qū gōng zuò rén yuán chén lán tí chū yī xiàng shì xíng jì huà ： jū mín bǎ bù zài chuān de jiù yī sòng dào huí shōu zhàn ， jīng guò dēng jì hé chēng zhòng hòu huò dé jī fēn ， jī fēn kě yǐ duì huàn gōng jiāo yōu huì quàn 。 tā xī wàng zhè xiàng jì huà jì néng jiǎn shǎo jiù yī làng fèi ， yě néng gǔ lì jū mín yōu xiān xuǎn zé gōng gòng jiāo tōng 。

jì huà kāi shǐ hòu de dì yí gè xīng qī ， huí shōu zhàn mén kǒu cháng cháng pái qǐ cháng duì 。 yǒu rén tè yì bǎ yī fú xǐ gān jìng 、 dié zhěng qí ， yě yǒu rén yī cì tuō lái jǐ gè sāi mǎn yī wù de dà dài zi 。 gōng zuò rén yuán xū yào jiǎn chá yī wù shì fǒu cháo shī ， zài àn zhào zhòng liàng zhé suàn jī fēn 。 qǐ chū ， bù shǎo jū mín yǐ wéi yī fú yuè duō ， dé dào de yōu huì jiù yuè dà ， yīn cǐ lián pò sǔn yán zhòng 、 wú fǎ zài cì shǐ yòng de yī wù yě sòng le guò lái ， xiàn chǎng hěn kuài chū xiàn le duī fàng hé fēn lèi de yā lì 。

gèng dà de wèn tí lái zì jū mín duì jiù yī qù xiàng de zhì yí 。 xuān chuán dān shàng zhǐ xiě zhe “ tǒng yī chǔ lǐ ”， méi yǒu shuō míng nǎ xiē yī fú huì bèi juān zèng ， nǎ xiē huì bèi jiā gōng chéng zài shēng cái liào 。 yī wèi jū mín zài wǎng shàng liú yán shuō ， zì jǐ yuán yǐ wéi wán hǎo de wài tào huì zhí jiē jiāo gěi yǒu xū yào de rén ， hòu lái què tīng shuō bù fèn yī wù bèi sòng jìn gōng chǎng 。 suī rán zhè zhǒng chǔ lǐ bìng bù yí dìng zào chéng làng fèi ， dàn hán hú de shuō míng shǐ rén chǎn shēng le bèi qī piàn de gǎn jué 。 shè qū zhǐ hǎo zàn shí tíng zhǐ jiē shōu jiù yī ， bìng yāo qǐng huí shōu qǐ yè gōng kāi chǔ lǐ liú chéng 。

chén lán suí hòu zhuī zōng le yī wù cóng dēng jì 、 yùn shū dào zuì zhōng chǔ lǐ de gè gè huán jié 。 tā fā xiàn ， yuán lái de jī fēn guī zé zhǐ kǎo lǜ zhòng liàng ， méi yǒu kǎo lǜ yī wù zhuàng tài ， yě hū lüè le bú huì shǐ yòng shǒu jī de lǎo nián jū mín 。 cǐ wài ， yǒu xiē rén píng shí hěn shǎo chéng gōng jiāo ， yōu huì quàn duì tā men bìng méi yǒu xī yǐn lì 。 yǔ qí yòng tóng yī zhǒng jiǎng lì xī yǐn suǒ yǒu rén shēn yǔ ， bù rú gěi jū mín tí gōng fú hé shí jì xū yào de xuǎn zé 。

chóng xīn kāi fàng hòu ， huí shōu zhàn bǎ yī wù fēn wéi kě zài cì chuān zhe 、 kě jiā gōng lì yòng hé wú fǎ jiē shōu sān lèi ， bìng zài xiàn chǎng shuō míng měi yī lèi de qù xiàng 。 wán hǎo yī wù bù zài dān chún àn zhòng liàng jì suàn ， ér shì jīng guò jiǎn dān hé shí hòu huò dé é wài jī fēn ； jū mín chú le duì huàn gōng jiāo yōu huì quàn ， hái kě yǐ xuǎn zé shè qū shí táng cān quàn huò gōng gòng zì xíng chē shǐ yòng shí cháng 。 méi yǒu zhì néng shǒu jī de rén kě yǐ lǐng qǔ zhǐ zhì jī fēn kǎ ， cóng ér bì miǎn jì shù mén kǎn yǐng xiǎng cān yù 。

yí gè yuè hòu de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， huí shōu zhàn shōu dào de yī wù zǒng liàng yǒu suǒ xià jiàng ， dàn cháo shī 、 yán zhòng pò sǔn de yī wù míng xiǎn jiǎn shǎo ， gōng zuò rén yuán yě bù bì fǎn fù jiě shì chǔ lǐ fāng shì 。 zhè xiē biàn huà zhǐ shì jiào xué àn lì zhōng de jiē duàn xìng jié guǒ ， bù néng bèi dàng zuò pǔ biàn tǒng jì 。 chén lán rèn wéi ， huán bǎo jì huà de jià zhí bù zài yú duǎn shí jiān shōu jí le duō shǎo jiù yī ， ér zài yú shì fǒu jiàn lì le tòu míng 、 fāng biàn bìng qiě néng gòu cháng qī wéi chí de jī zhì 。 jiǎng lì kě yǐ xī yǐn jū mín mài chū dì yī bù ， qīng chǔ de guī zé hé kě kào de chǔ lǐ guò chéng cái néng bǎo liú tā men de xìn rèn 。
translation: The following is a teaching case designed for discussion in a Chinese-language classroom and does not correspond to any policy or statistics published by an actual city. The Linjiang community had convenient transportation nearby, yet many residents were accustomed to driving for short trips. Chen Lan, a community employee, proposed a pilot program: residents could bring unwanted clothes to a collection station, have them registered and weighed, and receive points exchangeable for bus discount vouchers. She hoped the program would both reduce clothing waste and encourage residents to choose public transportation first.

During the first week of the program, long lines often formed outside the collection station. Some people washed and neatly folded their clothes, while others dragged in several large bags stuffed with garments. Staff members had to check whether the clothes were damp and then convert their weight into points. At first, many residents assumed that bringing more clothes would earn them greater discounts, so they even delivered badly damaged items that could not be reused. The station soon faced pressure from storage and sorting.

A more serious problem arose from residents' doubts about where the clothes would go. The leaflet merely said that they would be handled together, without explaining which clothes would be donated and which would be processed into recycled materials. One resident posted online that she had assumed her intact coat would be given directly to someone in need, but later heard that some garments had been sent to a factory. Although this kind of processing did not necessarily result in waste, the vague explanation made people feel deceived. The community therefore temporarily stopped accepting clothes and asked the recycling company to disclose its handling procedures.

Chen Lan then followed every stage of the clothes' journey, from registration and transportation to final processing. She discovered that the original point system considered only weight, not the condition of the clothes, and also overlooked older residents who did not use smartphones. In addition, some people rarely traveled by bus, so the discount vouchers did not appeal to them. Rather than trying to encourage everyone to participate with the same reward, it would be better to offer residents choices suited to their actual needs.

After reopening, the collection station divided clothes into three categories: wearable again, suitable for material recycling, and unacceptable. It also explained on site where each category would go. Intact clothing was no longer assessed solely by weight; after a basic inspection, it earned extra points. In addition to bus discount vouchers, residents could choose community cafeteria vouchers or time credits for public bicycles. Those without smartphones could receive paper point cards, preventing technical barriers from affecting participation.

A follow-up observation one month later showed that the total amount of clothing received by the station had declined, but damp and badly damaged items had decreased noticeably, and staff no longer had to explain the handling methods repeatedly. These changes are only interim results within a teaching case and must not be treated as general statistics. Chen Lan believed that the value of an environmental program lay not in how many clothes it collected within a short period, but in whether it established a transparent, convenient, and sustainable system. Rewards may persuade residents to take the first step, but clear rules and a reliable handling process are what preserve their trust.

articles.title: 一条没有立即降速的梧桐路
articles.summary: 梧桐路居民要求降低机动车限速，街区委员会却没有仓促表决，而是通过临时改造、现场观察和多方协商寻找更合适的方案。
articles.topic: 一条没有立即降速的梧桐路
paragraphs: 梧桐路位于一所小学和一座菜市场之间，每到早晚高峰，接送孩子的车辆、送货的货车和过马路的居民常常挤在一起。居民顾岚发现，路口虽然没有发生严重事故，急刹车和互相催促的情况却越来越多。她收集了邻居的意见，向街区委员会建议把机动车限速从每小时四十公里降到三十公里，并增设两处减速设施。本文所述过程及数据均为教学案例，不代表任何真实地区的政策或统计结果。
委员会开会时，不少人以为建议会顺利通过，结果会议持续了两个小时，表决却被暂时推迟。委员周启明并不反对降低风险，但他指出，单纯更换限速标志未必能改变驾驶习惯；如果减速设施的位置不合理，还可能导致车辆频繁鸣笛，甚至影响救护车通行。菜市场经营者也担心，货车装卸时间本来就集中，突然缩窄道路会造成拥堵。顾岚起初有些失望，不过她承认，这些顾虑不能被简单地理解为反对安全。
委员会没有否定提案，而是要求工作小组先进行为期三周的临时试验。工作人员用可移动花箱缩短行人过街距离，在校门附近画出醒目的路面标记，同时保留货车清晨装卸的空间。志愿者分别在上学、放学和市场进货时段记录车辆让行、排队以及急刹车的情况。按照案例材料中的阶段观察，车辆经过校门时普遍更加谨慎，但市场入口在雨天出现了短暂堵塞，部分骑车人还因花箱遮挡视线而突然转向。
这些现象改变了讨论的重点。居民不再争论“该不该降速”，而是开始研究“怎样降速才不会产生新的危险”。顾岚邀请校车司机、外卖骑手和市场管理员一起步行检查道路。大家发现，原计划设置减速带的位置正好靠近排水口，下雨后容易积水；相比之下，把花箱向后移动，并提前设置转弯提示，更有利于驾驶员和骑车人判断彼此的方向。周启明还建议保留三十公里的目标，但通过路面设计引导减速，而不是只依靠处罚。
第二次会议上，委员会仍没有批准最初的改造方案，却一致同意了修改后的试行计划：校门前采用弯曲车道和清晰标线，市场入口取消减速带，雨天安排人员疏导，六周后再根据记录决定是否长期保留。顾岚后来表示，第一次会议的推迟并不是对居民诉求的敷衍，反而迫使各方把模糊的愿望变成可以检验的措施。街区最终得到的也不只是一个更低的数字，而是一套能够根据实际反应继续调整的办法。
pinyin: wú tóng lù wèi yú yī suǒ xiǎo xué hé yī zuò cài shì chǎng zhī jiān ， měi dào zǎo wǎn gāo fēng ， jiē sòng hái zi de chē liàng 、 sòng huò de huò chē hé guò mǎ lù de jū mín cháng cháng jǐ zài yì qǐ 。 jū mín gù lán fā xiàn ， lù kǒu suī rán méi yǒu fā shēng yán zhòng shì gù ， jí shā chē hé hù xiāng cuī cù de qíng kuàng què yuè lái yuè duō 。 tā shōu jí le lín jū de yì jiàn ， xiàng jiē qū wěi yuán huì jiàn yì bǎ jī dòng chē xiàn sù cóng měi xiǎo shí sì shí gōng lǐ jiàng dào sān shí gōng lǐ ， bìng zēng shè liǎng chù jiǎn sù shè shī 。 běn wén suǒ shù guò chéng jí shù jù jūn wèi jiào xué àn lì ， bù dài biǎo rèn hé zhēn shí dì qū de zhèng cè huò tǒng jì jié guǒ 。

wěi yuán huì kāi huì shí ， bù shǎo rén yǐ wéi jiàn yì huì shùn lì tōng guò ， jié guǒ huì yì chí xù le liǎng gè xiǎo shí ， biǎo jué què bèi zàn shí tuī chí 。 wěi yuán zhōu qǐ míng bìng bù fǎn duì jiàng dī fēng xiǎn ， dàn tā zhǐ chū ， dān chún gēng huàn xiàn sù biāo zhì wèi bì néng gǎi biàn jià shǐ xí guàn ； rú guǒ jiǎn sù shè shī de wèi zhì bù hé lǐ ， hái kě néng dǎo zhì chē liàng pín fán míng dí ， shèn zhì yǐng xiǎng jiù hù chē tōng xíng 。 cài shì chǎng jīng yíng zhě yě dān xīn ， huò chē zhuāng xiè shí jiān běn lái jiù jí zhōng ， tū rán suō zhǎi dào lù huì zào chéng yōng dǔ 。 gù lán qǐ chū yǒu xiē shī wàng ， bù guò tā chéng rèn ， zhè xiē gù lǜ bù néng bèi jiǎn dān dì lǐ jiě wèi fǎn duì ān quán 。

wěi yuán huì méi yǒu fǒu dìng tí àn ， ér shì yāo qiú gōng zuò xiǎo zǔ xiān jìn xíng wéi qī sān zhōu de lín shí shì yàn 。 gōng zuò rén yuán yòng kě yí dòng huā xiāng suō duǎn xíng rén guò jiē jù lí ， zài xiào mén fù jìn huà chū xǐng mù dì lù miàn biāo jì ， tóng shí bǎo liú huò chē qīng chén zhuāng xiè de kōng jiān 。 zhì yuàn zhě fēn bié zài shàng xué 、 fàng xué hé shì chǎng jìn huò shí duàn jì lù chē liàng ràng xíng 、 pái duì yǐ jí jí shā chē de qíng kuàng 。 àn zhào àn lì cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn guān chá ， chē liàng jīng guò xiào mén shí pǔ biàn gèng jiā jǐn shèn ， dàn shì chǎng rù kǒu zài yǔ tiān chū xiàn le duǎn zàn dǔ sè ， bù fèn qí chē rén hái yīn huā xiāng zhē dǎng shì xiàn ér tū rán zhuǎn xiàng 。

zhè xiē xiàn xiàng gǎi biàn le tǎo lùn de zhòng diǎn 。 jū mín bù zài zhēng lùn “ gāi bù gāi jiàng sù ”， ér shì kāi shǐ yán jiū “ zěn yàng jiàng sù cái bú huì chǎn shēng xīn de wēi xiǎn ”。 gù lán yāo qǐng xiào chē sī jī 、 wài mài qí shǒu hé shì chǎng guǎn lǐ yuán yì qǐ bù xíng jiǎn chá dào lù 。 dà jiā fā xiàn ， yuán jì huà shè zhì jiǎn sù dài de wèi zhì zhèng hǎo kào jìn pái shuǐ kǒu ， xià yǔ hòu róng yì jī shuǐ ； xiāng bǐ zhī xià ， bǎ huā xiāng xiàng hòu yí dòng ， bìng tí qián shè zhì zhuǎn wān tí shì ， gèng yǒu lì yú jià shǐ yuán hé qí chē rén pàn duàn bǐ cǐ de fāng xiàng 。 zhōu qǐ míng hái jiàn yì bǎo liú sān shí gōng lǐ de mù biāo ， dàn tōng guò lù miàn shè jì yǐn dǎo jiǎn sù ， ér bú shì zhǐ yī kào chǔ fá 。

dì èr cì huì yì shàng ， wěi yuán huì réng méi yǒu pī zhǔn zuì chū de gǎi zào fāng àn ， què yí zhì tóng yì le xiū gǎi hòu de shì xíng jì huà ： xiào mén qián cǎi yòng wān qū chē dào hé qīng xī biāo xiàn ， shì chǎng rù kǒu qǔ xiāo jiǎn sù dài ， yǔ tiān ān pái rén yuán shū dǎo ， liù zhōu hòu zài gēn jù jì lù jué dìng shì fǒu cháng qī bǎo liú 。 gù lán hòu lái biǎo shì ， dì yī cì huì yì de tuī chí bìng bú shì duì jū mín sù qiú de fū yǎn ， fǎn ér pò shǐ gè fāng bǎ mó hú de yuàn wàng biàn chéng kě yǐ jiǎn yàn de cuò shī 。 jiē qū zuì zhōng dé dào de yě bù zhǐ shì yí gè gèng dī de shù zì ， ér shì yī tào néng gòu gēn jù shí jì fǎn yìng jì xù tiáo zhěng de bàn fǎ 。
translation: Wutong Road lies between a primary school and a food market. During the morning and evening rush hours, cars dropping off children, delivery trucks, and residents crossing the street often crowd together. A resident named Gu Lan noticed that although no serious accident had occurred at the intersection, sudden braking and impatient urging had become increasingly common. She gathered opinions from her neighbors and proposed to the neighborhood committee that the vehicle speed limit be reduced from forty to thirty kilometers per hour and that two traffic-calming devices be added. The process and data described here form a teaching case and do not represent the policies or statistics of any real area.

When the committee met, many people assumed that the proposal would pass smoothly. However, after a two-hour meeting, the vote was postponed. Committee member Zhou Qiming did not oppose reducing risk, but he pointed out that merely replacing speed-limit signs might not change driving habits. If traffic-calming devices were placed improperly, they might also cause frequent honking or even obstruct ambulances. Market operators were concerned as well, because truck unloading was already concentrated within a limited period, and a sudden narrowing of the road could create congestion. Gu Lan was disappointed at first, but she acknowledged that these concerns could not simply be interpreted as opposition to safety.

Instead of rejecting the proposal, the committee asked a working group to conduct a three-week temporary trial. Staff used movable planters to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance, painted noticeable road markings near the school gate, and preserved space for trucks to unload in the early morning. Volunteers recorded vehicle yielding, queues, and sudden braking during school arrival, school dismissal, and market delivery periods. According to the interim observations in the case materials, vehicles generally moved more cautiously past the school gate, but brief congestion appeared at the market entrance on rainy days, and some cyclists made sudden turns because the planters blocked their view.

These findings shifted the focus of the discussion. Residents stopped debating whether the speed limit should be reduced and began examining how to reduce speed without creating new dangers. Gu Lan invited school-bus drivers, delivery riders, and market administrators to inspect the road on foot. They discovered that the originally planned location of a speed bump was right beside a drain, where water could easily collect after rain. By comparison, moving the planters farther back and installing turning warnings in advance would help drivers and cyclists judge each other's direction. Zhou Qiming also suggested keeping the target of thirty kilometers per hour while using road design to guide drivers to slow down instead of relying solely on penalties.

At the second meeting, the committee still did not approve the original renovation plan, but it unanimously accepted a revised trial plan: curved lanes and clear markings would be introduced in front of the school, the planned speed bump at the market entrance would be dropped, staff would direct traffic on rainy days, and the records would be reviewed after six weeks to decide whether the measures should be retained permanently. Gu Lan later said that postponing the first meeting's decision was not a dismissal of residents' concerns. Instead, it compelled all parties to turn a vague wish into measures that could be tested. What the neighborhood ultimately gained was not merely a lower number, but an approach that could continue to be adjusted according to actual responses.

articles.title: 陪诊员没有替患者作决定
articles.summary: 一项教学案例中的医院陪诊志愿服务经历调整，从热情代办转向边界清晰的协助，说明真正有效的帮助既需要温度，也需要规则。
articles.topic: 陪诊员没有替患者作决定
paragraphs: 周一清晨，市立医院门诊大厅刚开放，志愿者林悦便在服务台前见到了独自前来的赵师傅。老人要去三个科室复查，手里攥着一叠检查单，却分不清先去哪里。林悦参加的是医院与社区共同设计的陪诊志愿项目。按照安排，她可以帮助患者识别路线、使用自助设备、整理就诊材料，也可以在患者同意后记录医生交代的注意事项，但不能替患者描述病情或作出医疗决定。
赵师傅听力不太好，面对自助挂号机又显得格外紧张。林悦没有直接拿走他的证件代为操作，而是放慢速度，把屏幕上的步骤逐项念给他听。排队时，老人几次说：“你替我选吧，我也不懂。”林悦却提醒他，检查时间和医生选择会影响后续安排，应由本人确认。她把不同选项解释清楚，等赵师傅点头后才协助提交。这种做法看似费时，却保留了患者的知情权。
进入诊室后，赵师傅一紧张，忘了说明最近服药后头晕。林悦根据事先整理的问题清单，小声提醒他还有一种不适没有提到，但并未抢着回答医生的询问。医生调整用药方案时，她只负责记录药名、用量和复诊日期。离开诊室后，她请赵师傅用自己的话复述一遍；发现他把“饭后服用”记成“饭前服用”，便陪他返回护士台核实，避免了可能发生的误解。
不过，项目刚开始时并非如此谨慎。在这则教学案例的早期阶段观察中，有些志愿者出于热心，曾替患者回答病情、保管银行卡，甚至主动联系并不知情的家属。这些行为提高了办事速度，却带来隐私泄露、责任不清等风险。项目负责人因此暂停了部分服务，并邀请医护人员、社会工作者和患者代表一起讨论：陪诊究竟应该替人解决问题，还是帮助患者恢复处理问题的能力？
讨论后，项目重新划定了服务边界。志愿者不得接触支付密码，不得保存患者病历照片，也不能承诺挂到某位专家的号；遇到患者突然不适时，应立即寻找医护人员，而不是凭经验判断。与此同时，医院也不再把志愿者当作临时跑腿人员，而是为他们提供沟通训练、情景演练和固定的求助渠道。与其要求志愿者无所不能，不如让他们清楚何时可以协助、何时必须退出。
复查结束时，赵师傅已经能独立找到取药窗口。他向林悦道谢，林悦却说，顺利就诊并不全是陪诊者的功劳，患者愿意表达疑问同样重要。这项服务后来没有把完成了多少次陪诊作为唯一标准，而是结合教学材料中的阶段记录，观察患者是否理解医嘱、志愿者是否遵守边界，以及遇到意外时能否及时求助。陪诊的价值不在于替患者包办一切，而在于减少陌生环境造成的障碍，使患者仍然掌握与自身健康有关的选择。
pinyin: zhōu yī qīng chén ， shì lì yī yuàn mén zhěn dà tīng gāng kāi fàng ， zhì yuàn zhě lín yuè biàn zài fú wù tái qián jiàn dào le dú zì qián lái de zhào shī fù 。 lǎo rén yào qù sān gè kē shì fù chá ， shǒu lǐ zuàn zhe yī dié jiǎn chá dān ， què fēn bù qīng xiān qù nǎ lǐ 。 lín yuè cān jiā de shì yī yuàn yǔ shè qū gòng tóng shè jì de péi zhěn zhì yuàn xiàng mù 。 àn zhào ān pái ， tā kě yǐ bāng zhù huàn zhě shí bié lù xiàn 、 shǐ yòng zì zhù shè bèi 、 zhěng lǐ jiù zhěn cái liào ， yě kě yǐ zài huàn zhě tóng yì hòu jì lù yī shēng jiāo dài de zhù yì shì xiàng ， dàn bù néng tì huàn zhě miáo shù bìng qíng huò zuò chū yī liáo jué dìng 。

zhào shī fù tīng lì bù tài hǎo ， miàn duì zì zhù guà hào jī yòu xiǎn de gé wài jǐn zhāng 。 lín yuè méi yǒu zhí jiē ná zǒu tā de zhèng jiàn dài wéi cāo zuò ， ér shì fàng màn sù dù ， bǎ píng mù shàng de bù zhòu zhú xiàng niàn gěi tā tīng 。 pái duì shí ， lǎo rén jǐ cì shuō ：“ nǐ tì wǒ xuǎn ba ， wǒ yě bù dǒng 。” lín yuè què tí xǐng tā ， jiǎn chá shí jiān hé yī shēng xuǎn zé huì yǐng xiǎng hòu xù ān pái ， yīng yóu běn rén què rèn 。 tā bǎ bù tóng xuǎn xiàng jiě shì qīng chǔ ， děng zhào shī fù diǎn tóu hòu cái xié zhù tí jiāo 。 zhè zhǒng zuò fǎ kàn shì fèi shí ， què bǎo liú le huàn zhě de zhī qíng quán 。

jìn rù zhěn shì hòu ， zhào shī fù yī jǐn zhāng ， wàng le shuō míng zuì jìn fú yào hòu tou yūn 。 lín yuè gēn jù shì xiān zhěng lǐ de wèn tí qīng dān ， xiǎo shēng tí xǐng tā hái yǒu yī zhǒng bù shì méi yǒu tí dào ， dàn bìng wèi qiǎng zhe huí dá yī shēng de xún wèn 。 yī shēng tiáo zhěng yòng yào fāng àn shí ， tā zhǐ fù zé jì lù yào míng 、 yòng liàng hé fù zhěn rì qī 。 lí kāi zhěn shì hòu ， tā qǐng zhào shī fù yòng zì jǐ de huà fù shù yī biàn ； fā xiàn tā bǎ “ fàn hòu fú yòng ” jì chéng “ fàn qián fú yòng ”， biàn péi tā fǎn huí hù shì tái hé shí ， bì miǎn le kě néng fā shēng de wù jiě 。

bù guò ， xiàng mù gāng kāi shǐ shí bìng fēi rú cǐ jǐn shèn 。 zài zhè zé jiào xué àn lì de zǎo qī jiē duàn guān chá zhōng ， yǒu xiē zhì yuàn zhě chū yú rè xīn ， céng tì huàn zhě huí dá bìng qíng 、 bǎo guǎn yín háng kǎ ， shèn zhì zhǔ dòng lián xì bìng bù zhī qíng de jiā shǔ 。 zhè xiē xíng wéi tí gāo le bàn shì sù dù ， què dài lái yǐn sī xiè lòu 、 zé rèn bù qīng děng fēng xiǎn 。 xiàng mù fù zé rén yīn cǐ zàn tíng le bù fèn fú wù ， bìng yāo qǐng yī hù rén yuán 、 shè huì gōng zuò zhě hé huàn zhě dài biǎo yì qǐ tǎo lùn ： péi zhěn jiū jìng yīng gāi tì rén jiě jué wèn tí ， hái shì bāng zhù huàn zhě huī fù chǔ lǐ wèn tí de néng lì ？

tǎo lùn hòu ， xiàng mù chóng xīn huà dìng le fú wù biān jiè 。 zhì yuàn zhě bù dé jiē chù zhī fù mì mǎ ， bù dé bǎo cún huàn zhě bìng lì zhào piān ， yě bù néng chéng nuò guà dào mǒu wèi zhuān jiā de hào ； yù dào huàn zhě tū rán bù shì shí ， yīng lì jí xún zhǎo yī hù rén yuán ， ér bú shì píng jīng yàn pàn duàn 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， yī yuàn yě bù zài bǎ zhì yuàn zhě dàng zuò lín shí pǎo tuǐ rén yuán ， ér shì wèi tā men tí gōng gōu tōng xùn liàn 、 qíng jǐng yǎn liàn hé gù dìng de qiú zhù qú dào 。 yǔ qí yāo qiú zhì yuàn zhě wú suǒ bù néng ， bù rú ràng tā men qīng chǔ hé shí kě yǐ xié zhù 、 hé shí bì xū tuì chū 。

fù chá jié shù shí ， zhào shī fù yǐ jīng néng dú lì zhǎo dào qǔ yào chuāng kǒu 。 tā xiàng lín yuè dào xiè ， lín yuè què shuō ， shùn lì jiù zhěn bìng bù quán shì péi zhěn zhě de gōng láo ， huàn zhě yuàn yì biǎo dá yí wèn tóng yàng zhòng yào 。 zhè xiàng fú wù hòu lái méi yǒu bǎ wán chéng le duō shǎo cì péi zhěn zuò wéi wéi yī biāo zhǔn ， ér shì jié hé jiào xué cái liào zhōng de jiē duàn jì lù ， guān chá huàn zhě shì fǒu lǐ jiě yī zhǔ 、 zhì yuàn zhě shì fǒu zūn shǒu biān jiè ， yǐ jí yù dào yì wài shí néng fǒu jí shí qiú zhù 。 péi zhěn de jià zhí bù zài yú tì huàn zhě bāo bàn yī qiè ， ér zài yú jiǎn shǎo mò shēng huán jìng zào chéng de zhàng ài ， shǐ huàn zhě réng rán zhǎng wò yǔ zì shēn jiàn kāng yǒu guān de xuǎn zé 。
translation: Early on Monday morning, just after the municipal hospital's outpatient hall opened, volunteer Lin Yue met Mr. Zhao at the service desk. The elderly man had come alone for follow-up examinations in three departments. He clutched a stack of test forms but could not tell where to go first. Lin Yue belonged to a volunteer patient-assistance program jointly designed by the hospital and the local community. Under its rules, she could help patients find their way, use self-service machines, organize medical documents, and, with their consent, record a doctor's instructions. However, she could not describe a patient's condition on the patient's behalf or make medical decisions for them.

Mr. Zhao had difficulty hearing and appeared especially anxious in front of the self-service registration machine. Instead of taking his identification and operating it for him, Lin Yue slowed down and read each step on the screen aloud. While they waited, he repeatedly asked her to choose for him because he did not understand. Lin Yue reminded him that the examination time and choice of doctor would affect later arrangements and therefore required his confirmation. She explained the alternatives and did not help submit the selection until he nodded. Although this approach seemed time-consuming, it preserved the patient's right to make an informed choice.

Once inside the consultation room, Mr. Zhao became nervous and forgot to mention that he had recently felt dizzy after taking his medicine. Referring to the list of questions they had prepared, Lin Yue quietly reminded him that one symptom had not yet been mentioned, but she did not rush to answer the doctor's questions herself. When the doctor adjusted the medication plan, she recorded only the medicine's name, dosage, and follow-up date. After they left, she asked Mr. Zhao to repeat the instructions in his own words. When she discovered that he had confused taking the medicine after meals with taking it before meals, she accompanied him back to the nurses' station for confirmation, preventing a possible misunderstanding.

The program had not always operated with such caution. In the early-stage observations presented in this teaching case, some volunteers, motivated by kindness, had answered questions about patients' conditions, held bank cards for them, and even contacted relatives who had not been informed. These actions made procedures faster but created risks such as privacy breaches and unclear responsibility. The program manager therefore suspended part of the service and invited medical staff, social workers, and patient representatives to discuss whether assistance should solve problems for patients or help them regain the ability to handle problems themselves.

After the discussion, the program redefined its service boundaries. Volunteers could not access payment passwords, retain photographs of medical records, or promise appointments with particular specialists. If a patient suddenly became unwell, they had to find medical staff immediately rather than rely on personal experience. At the same time, the hospital stopped treating volunteers as temporary errand runners and instead provided communication training, scenario-based practice, and established channels for seeking help. Rather than expecting volunteers to be capable of everything, it is better to ensure that they know when they may assist and when they must step aside.

By the end of the follow-up visit, Mr. Zhao could find the pharmacy window by himself. He thanked Lin Yue, but she said that a smooth medical visit was not entirely the assistant's achievement; the patient's willingness to voice questions was equally important. The service later stopped using the number of completed visits as its sole standard. Instead, drawing on staged records in the teaching materials, it examined whether patients understood medical instructions, whether volunteers respected boundaries, and whether they could seek help promptly in unexpected situations. The value of patient assistance does not lie in taking care of everything for patients, but in reducing barriers created by an unfamiliar environment while allowing patients to retain control over choices concerning their own health.

articles.title: 一把电钻引发的共享实验
articles.summary: 一名社区居民通过建立共享工具库，解决工具闲置、借用混乱和责任不清等问题，并促使邻里关系从物品交换走向技能互助。
articles.topic: 一把电钻引发的共享实验
paragraphs: 林岚搬进松桥社区后，发现一个颇为矛盾的现象：居民家中堆着不少很少使用的工具，可是谁家需要临时修理桌椅或在墙上安装书架时，仍会重新购买。她自己就为挂一面镜子买过电钻，用了不到十分钟，此后它便一直躺在柜子里。一次整理地下储藏室时，她想到，与其让这些工具各自在角落里积灰，不如建立一个供邻居借用的工具库。
林岚起初以为，只要腾出房间、摆好工具，再做一张借用登记表，事情就能顺利运转。居委会同意把活动室旁边的小仓库交给她试用，几位居民也捐出了梯子、扳手和修枝剪。然而，工具库开放后的第一个月并不理想。有人担心损坏工具后要赔偿，有人不知道该怎样安全操作，还有人觉得登记姓名和联系方式太麻烦，宁愿继续向熟人借。
真正的转折来自一把没有按时归还的电钻。借用者周师傅说自己还没用完，下一位预约者却急着修理漏水的厨房吊柜，双方在群里争论起来。林岚没有简单地批评其中任何一方，而是邀请他们当面说明各自的困难。她由此意识到，共享并不等于取消边界；相反，越是共同使用的物品，越需要明确预约期限、延期方式以及损坏后的处理原则。
随后，林岚和几名志愿者重新设计了借用流程。居民可以在线预约，也可以请值班人员代为登记；常用工具最长借三天，如果无人排队，可以申请延期。工具归还时，双方共同检查状态，不把正常磨损算作人为损坏。对于电钻、电锯等有一定危险性的设备，第一次借用前必须参加简短的操作演示。规则看起来比以前多了，却消除了许多模糊之处。
后来，工具库最受欢迎的并不是某件昂贵设备，而是每月一次的“修理下午”。懂木工的周师傅教年轻人固定松动的椅子，学过电路维修的退休职工帮助邻居判断故障，孩子们则在志愿者陪同下给旧工具分类。人们逐渐发现，自己贡献的不一定是物品，也可以是经验、时间和耐心。原先因电钻发生争执的两位居民，后来还合作修好了活动室的储物架。
半年后，林岚没有急着扩大工具库，而是先整理借用记录和居民建议。她发现，决定项目能否持续的并非工具数量，而是谁负责维护、规则是否公平，以及遇到矛盾时有没有沟通渠道。社区因此设立了轮流值班制度，并把维修费用的用途定期公开。工具库没有让每个人都停止购物，却使居民在购买之前多了一个选择，也让原本互不熟悉的邻居有了合作的理由。
pinyin: lín lán bān jìn sōng qiáo shè qū hòu ， fā xiàn yí gè pǒ wèi máo dùn de xiàn xiàng ： jū mín jiā zhōng duī zhe bù shǎo hěn shǎo shǐ yòng de gōng jù ， kě shì shuí jiā xū yào lín shí xiū lǐ zhuō yǐ huò zài qiáng shàng ān zhuāng shū jià shí ， réng huì chóng xīn gòu mǎi 。 tā zì jǐ jiù wèi guà yí miàn jìng zi mǎi guò diàn zuān ， yòng le bú dào shí fēn zhōng ， cǐ hòu tā biàn yì zhí tǎng zài guì zi lǐ 。 yī cì zhěng lǐ dì xià chǔ cáng shì shí ， tā xiǎng dào ， yǔ qí ràng zhè xiē gōng jù gè zì zài jiǎo luò lǐ jī huī ， bù rú jiàn lì yí gè gōng lín jū jiè yòng de gōng jù kù 。

lín lán qǐ chū yǐ wéi ， zhǐ yào téng chū fáng jiān 、 bǎi hǎo gōng jù ， zài zuò yī zhāng jiè yòng dēng jì biǎo ， shì qíng jiù néng shùn lì yùn zhuàn 。 jū wěi huì tóng yì bǎ huó dòng shì páng biān de xiǎo cāng kù jiāo gěi tā shì yòng ， jǐ wèi jū mín yě juān chū le tī zi 、 bān shǒu hé xiū zhī jiǎn 。 rán ér ， gōng jù kù kāi fàng hòu de dì yí gè yuè bìng bù lǐ xiǎng 。 yǒu rén dān xīn sǔn huài gōng jù hòu yào péi cháng ， yǒu rén bù zhī dào gāi zěn yàng ān quán cāo zuò ， hái yǒu rén jué de dēng jì xìng míng hé lián xì fāng shì tài má fán ， nìng yuàn jì xù xiàng shú rén jiè 。

zhēn zhèng de zhuǎn zhé lái zì yī bǎ méi yǒu àn shí guī huán de diàn zuàn 。 jiè yòng zhě zhōu shī fù shuō zì jǐ hái méi yòng wán ， xià yī wèi yù yuē zhě què jí zhe xiū lǐ lòu shuǐ de chú fáng diào guì ， shuāng fāng zài qún lǐ zhēng lùn qǐ lái 。 lín lán méi yǒu jiǎn dān dì pī píng qí zhōng rèn hé yī fāng ， ér shì yāo qǐng tā men dāng miàn shuō míng gè zì de kùn nán 。 tā yóu cǐ yì shí dào ， gòng xiǎng bìng bù děng yú qǔ xiāo biān jiè ； xiāng fǎn ， yuè shì gòng tóng shǐ yòng de wù pǐn ， yuè xū yào míng què yù yuē qī xiàn 、 yán qī fāng shì yǐ jí sǔn huài hòu de chǔ lǐ yuán zé 。

suí hòu ， lín lán hé jǐ míng zhì yuàn zhě chóng xīn shè jì le jiè yòng liú chéng 。 jū mín kě yǐ zài xiàn yù yuē ， yě kě yǐ qǐng zhí bān rén yuán dài wéi dēng jì ； cháng yòng gōng jù zuì zhǎng jiè sān tiān ， rú guǒ wú rén pái duì ， kě yǐ shēn qǐng yán qī 。 gōng jù guī huán shí ， shuāng fāng gòng tóng jiǎn chá zhuàng tài ， bù bǎ zhèng cháng mó sǔn suàn zuò rén wéi sǔn huài 。 duì yú diàn zuàn 、 diàn jù děng yǒu yí dìng wēi xiǎn xìng de shè bèi ， dì yī cì jiè yòng qián bì xū cān jiā jiǎn duǎn de cāo zuò yǎn shì 。 guī zé kàn qǐ lái bǐ yǐ qián duō le ， què xiāo chú le xǔ duō mó hú zhī chù 。

hòu lái ， gōng jù kù zuì shòu huān yíng de bìng bú shì mǒu jiàn áng guì shè bèi ， ér shì měi yuè yī cì de “ xiū lǐ xià wǔ ”。 dǒng mù gōng de zhōu shī fù jiào nián qīng rén gù dìng sōng dòng de yǐ zi ， xué guò diàn lù wéi xiū de tuì xiū zhí gōng bāng zhù lín jū pàn duàn gù zhàng ， hái zi men zé zài zhì yuàn zhě péi tóng xià gěi jiù gōng jù fēn lèi 。 rén men zhú jiàn fā xiàn ， zì jǐ gòng xiàn de bù yí dìng shì wù pǐn ， yě kě yǐ shì jīng yàn 、 shí jiān hé nài xīn 。 yuán xiān yīn diàn zuàn fā shēng zhēng zhí de liǎng wèi jū mín ， hòu lái hái hé zuò xiū hǎo le huó dòng shì de chǔ wù jià 。

bàn nián hòu ， lín lán méi yǒu jí zhe kuò dà gōng jù kù ， ér shì xiān zhěng lǐ jiè yòng jì lù hé jū mín jiàn yì 。 tā fā xiàn ， jué dìng xiàng mù néng fǒu chí xù de bìng fēi gōng jù shù liàng ， ér shì shuí fù zé wéi hù 、 guī zé shì fǒu gōng píng ， yǐ jí yù dào máo dùn shí yǒu méi yǒu gōu tōng qú dào 。 shè qū yīn cǐ shè lì le lún liú zhí bān zhì dù ， bìng bǎ wéi xiū fèi yòng de yòng tú dìng qī gōng kāi 。 gōng jù kù méi yǒu ràng měi gè rén dōu tíng zhǐ gòu wù ， què shǐ jū mín zài gòu mǎi zhī qián duō le yí gè xuǎn zé ， yě ràng yuán běn hù bù shú xī de lín jū yǒu le hé zuò de lǐ yóu 。
translation: After moving into the Songqiao community, Lin Lan noticed a striking contradiction: residents kept many rarely used tools at home, yet whenever they needed to repair furniture or install a shelf, they would still buy new ones. She herself had bought a power drill to hang a mirror and used it for less than ten minutes before leaving it in a cabinet. While organizing the basement storage room one day, she thought that instead of letting these tools gather dust in separate corners, the community could establish a tool library for neighbors to borrow from.

At first, Lin Lan assumed that the project would run smoothly as long as she cleared a room, arranged the tools, and prepared a borrowing form. The residents' committee allowed her to use a small storeroom beside the activity room on a trial basis, and several residents donated ladders, wrenches, and pruning shears. However, the tool library's first month was disappointing. Some people worried that they would have to pay if a tool was damaged, some did not know how to operate the tools safely, and others found it troublesome to register their names and contact details, preferring to keep borrowing from acquaintances.

The real turning point came when a power drill was not returned on time. The borrower, Mr. Zhou, said he had not finished using it, while the next person with a reservation urgently needed it to repair a leaking kitchen cabinet, and the two began arguing in the group chat. Lin Lan did not simply criticize either person; instead, she invited them to explain their difficulties face to face. From this, she realized that sharing did not mean eliminating boundaries. On the contrary, the more widely an item was shared, the more necessary it became to clarify reservation periods, extension procedures, and rules for handling damage.

Lin Lan and several volunteers then redesigned the borrowing process. Residents could make reservations online or ask the person on duty to register for them. Common tools could be borrowed for up to three days, with extensions available if no one else was waiting. When a tool was returned, both sides inspected its condition together, and ordinary wear was not treated as damage caused by the borrower. For potentially dangerous equipment such as power drills and electric saws, first-time borrowers had to attend a brief operating demonstration. Although there seemed to be more rules than before, they removed many uncertainties.

Later, the most popular part of the tool library proved not to be an expensive piece of equipment but a monthly “repair afternoon.” Mr. Zhou, who was skilled at woodworking, taught younger residents how to secure loose chairs. Retired workers with electrical repair experience helped neighbors diagnose faults, while children sorted old tools under the supervision of volunteers. People gradually discovered that their contributions did not have to be physical objects; they could also offer experience, time, and patience. The two residents who had argued over the power drill later worked together to repair the storage shelves in the activity room.

Six months later, Lin Lan did not rush to expand the tool library. Instead, she first organized the borrowing records and residents' suggestions. She found that the project's sustainability depended not on the number of tools, but on who maintained them, whether the rules were fair, and whether a channel existed for resolving conflicts. The community therefore introduced a rotating duty system and regularly disclosed how repair funds were used. The tool library did not stop everyone from shopping, but it gave residents another option before making a purchase and gave previously unacquainted neighbors a reason to cooperate.

articles.title: 百分之十八之外：一次线上问诊评估的转向
articles.summary: 一名评估人员通过核查数据口径、观察患者就诊过程并听取医护人员意见，发现线上问诊虽然缩短了部分患者的候诊时间，却也可能把成本转移给不熟悉数字工具的人。试点因此调整评估方法，并建立线上与线下互相衔接的服务机制。
articles.topic: 百分之十八之外：一次线上问诊评估的转向
paragraphs: 教学案例中的临江市准备评估一项为期三个月的线上问诊试点。按照流程，居民先在手机上描述症状、上传图片，再由社区医生判断是否需要视频问诊、开具处方或转到医院。项目组提交的阶段报告显示，完成线上问诊的患者平均候诊时间比过去缩短了百分之十八。负责评估的林澈起初也认为，这个结果足以证明试点提高了效率。然而，当他翻到报告附件时，却发现统计对象只包括顺利进入视频环节的人，那些注册失败、资料退回或中途放弃的居民并未被计算在内。

林澈没有立即否定报告，而是要求项目组解释候诊时间的起点。工作人员把患者成功提交资料的时刻当作起点，却没有计算注册账号、学习操作以及反复修改图片所花的时间。对于熟悉手机的上班族，这种计算方式或许影响不大；对于视力不佳或不识字的老人，准备过程可能比正式候诊更漫长。此外，平均值还掩盖了不同科室之间的差异：皮肤科通过照片就能处理部分问题，内科医生却常常需要继续询问病史。林澈因此认为，百分之十八并非错误，却只能说明流程中的某一段变快了。

为了了解数字背后的经历，林澈在社区服务中心连续观察了四天。第二天下午，一位姓吴的老人拿着女儿留下的旧手机前来求助。她膝盖疼了半个月，本想在线咨询，却连续三次把身份证照片传成了药盒照片。志愿者替她完成操作以后，系统又提示必须重新描述疼痛程度。老人叹气说，如果每一步都需要别人帮助，她宁愿像从前一样排队。值得注意的是，她并不排斥线上服务；当医生通过视频告诉她暂时不必去大医院时，她明显放松下来。真正令她不安的不是屏幕，而是不知道自己是否做对了，也不知道出错后该找谁。

医生一侧也出现了报告没有呈现的问题。线上问诊让部分医生减少了重复解释，却增加了判断信息是否完整的压力。一名全科医生提到，患者常把最担心的症状写得很详细，却遗漏过敏史、慢性病或正在服用的药物。如果医生为了提高处理速度而减少追问，风险可能被隐藏；如果每次都重新核实，节省下来的时间又会迅速消失。更复杂的是，平台会按照等待时长提醒医生尽快结束对话，这种设计看似在督促进度，实际上可能把效率指标变成心理负担。林澈据此提出，评价系统不能只问处理了多少人，还要检查转诊是否及时、信息是否完整以及患者能否理解医嘱。

项目组随后调整了评估方案，把患者从产生就医需求到获得明确建议的全过程纳入记录，并分别比较不同年龄、数字能力和疾病类型的使用情况。林澈还建议抽取中途退出者进行电话访谈，因为失败者的沉默本身就是重要信息。与此同时，服务中心在入口处设置线下协助台，允许居民由工作人员代为录入资料；系统则取消必须一次填完的限制，患者可以保存内容，稍后继续。为了避免医生被单一速度指标牵制，管理人员把响应速度与病历完整度、后续转诊结果结合起来审核。新的方案并不追求制造一个更醒目的百分比，而是试图说明便利究竟由谁获得，额外成本又由谁承担。

试点结束前的阶段观察显示，年轻患者仍是线上问诊的主要使用者，但在协助台投入运行后，老年居民中途退出的情况有所减少。这个变化仅属于教学案例中的局部观察，既不是正式统计结论，也不能直接推广到其他地区。最终报告保留了候诊时间缩短百分之十八的原始结果，同时补充说明其统计范围和局限，并建议长期保留电话预约与现场窗口。林澈在结论中写道，技术的价值不在于迫使所有人采用同一种方式，而在于为不同处境的人增加可靠的选择。一次负责任的评估，也不应急于证明试点成功或失败，而应揭示哪些环节真正改善了体验，哪些困难只是从机构转移到了患者身上。
pinyin: jiào xué àn lì zhōng de lín jiāng shì zhǔn bèi píng gū yī xiàng wéi qī sān gè yuè de xiàn shàng wèn zhěn shì diǎn 。 àn zhào liú chéng ， jū mín xiān zài shǒu jī shàng miáo shù zhèng zhuàng 、 shàng chuán tú piàn ， zài yóu shè qū yī shēng pàn duàn shì fǒu xū yào shì pín wèn zhěn 、 kāi jù chǔ fāng huò zhuǎn dào yī yuàn 。 xiàng mù zǔ tí jiāo de jiē duàn bào gào xiǎn shì ， wán chéng xiàn shàng wèn zhěn de huàn zhě píng jūn hòu zhěn shí jiān bǐ guò qù suō duǎn le bǎi fēn zhī shí bā 。 fù zé píng gū de lín chè qǐ chū yě rèn wéi ， zhè ge jié guǒ zú yǐ zhèng míng shì diǎn tí gāo le xiào lǜ 。 rán ér ， dāng tā fān dào bào gào fù jiàn shí ， què fā xiàn tǒng jì duì xiàng zhǐ bāo kuò shùn lì jìn rù shì pín huán jié de rén ， nà xiē zhù cè shī bài 、 zī liào tuì huí huò zhōng tú fàng qì de jū mín bìng wèi bèi jì suàn zài nèi 。

lín chè méi yǒu lì jí fǒu dìng bào gào ， ér shì yāo qiú xiàng mù zǔ jiě shì hòu zhěn shí jiān de qǐ diǎn 。 gōng zuò rén yuán bǎ huàn zhě chéng gōng tí jiāo zī liào de shí kè dàng zuò qǐ diǎn ， què méi yǒu jì suàn zhù cè zhàng hào 、 xué xí cāo zuò yǐ jí fǎn fù xiū gǎi tú piàn suǒ huā de shí jiān 。 duì yú shú xī shǒu jī de shàng bān zú ， zhè zhǒng jì suàn fāng shì huò xǔ yǐng xiǎng bù dà ； duì yú shì lì bù jiā huò bù shí zì de lǎo rén ， zhǔn bèi guò chéng kě néng bǐ zhèng shì hòu zhěn gèng màn cháng 。 cǐ wài ， píng jūn zhí hái yǎn gài le bù tóng kē shì zhī jiān de chā yì ： pí fū kē tōng guò zhào piān jiù néng chǔ lǐ bù fèn wèn tí ， nèi kē yī shēng què cháng cháng xū yào jì xù xún wèn bìng shǐ 。 lín chè yīn cǐ rèn wéi ， bǎi fēn zhī shí bā bìng fēi cuò wù ， què zhǐ néng shuō míng liú chéng zhōng de mǒu yī duàn biàn kuài le 。

wèi le liǎo jiě shù zì bèi hòu de jīng lì ， lín chè zài shè qū fú wù zhōng xīn lián xù guān chá le sì tiān 。 dì èr tiān xià wǔ ， yī wèi xìng wú de lǎo rén ná zhe nǚ ér liú xià de jiù shǒu jī qián lái qiú zhù 。 tā xī gài téng le bàn gè yuè ， běn xiǎng zài xiàn zī xún ， què lián xù sān cì bǎ shēn fèn zhèng zhào piān chuán chéng le yào hé zhào piān 。 zhì yuàn zhě tì tā wán chéng cāo zuò yǐ hòu ， xì tǒng yòu tí shì bì xū chóng xīn miáo shù téng tòng chéng dù 。 lǎo rén tàn qì shuō ， rú guǒ měi yī bù dōu xū yào bié rén bāng zhù ， tā nìng yuàn xiàng cóng qián yī yàng pái duì 。 zhí de zhù yì de shì ， tā bìng bù pái chì xiàn shàng fú wù ； dāng yī shēng tōng guò shì pín gào sù tā zàn shí bù bì qù dà yī yuàn shí ， tā míng xiǎn fàng sōng xià lái 。 zhēn zhèng lìng tā bù ān de bú shì píng mù ， ér shì bù zhī dào zì jǐ shì fǒu zuò duì le ， yě bù zhī dào chū cuò hòu gāi zhǎo shuí 。

yī shēng yī cè yě chū xiàn le bào gào méi yǒu chéng xiàn de wèn tí 。 xiàn shàng wèn zhěn ràng bù fèn yī shēng jiǎn shǎo le chóng fù jiě shì ， què zēng jiā le pàn duàn xìn xī shì fǒu wán zhěng de yā lì 。 yī míng quán kē yī shēng tí dào ， huàn zhě cháng bǎ zuì dān xīn de zhèng zhuàng xiě dé hěn xiáng xì ， què yí lòu guò mǐn shǐ 、 màn xìng bìng huò zhèng zài fú yòng de yào wù 。 rú guǒ yī shēng wèi le tí gāo chǔ lǐ sù dù ér jiǎn shǎo zhuī wèn ， fēng xiǎn kě néng bèi yǐn cáng ； rú guǒ měi cì dōu chóng xīn hé shí ， jié shěng xià lái de shí jiān yòu huì xùn sù xiāo shī 。 gèng fù zá de shì ， píng tái huì àn zhào děng dài shí cháng tí xǐng yī shēng jǐn kuài jié shù duì huà ， zhè zhǒng shè jì kàn shì zài dū cù jìn dù ， shí jì shàng kě néng bǎ xiào lǜ zhǐ biāo biàn chéng xīn lǐ fù dān 。 lín chè jù cǐ tí chū ， píng jià xì tǒng bù néng zhǐ wèn chǔ lǐ le duō shǎo rén ， hái yào jiǎn chá zhuǎn zhěn shì fǒu jí shí 、 xìn xī shì fǒu wán zhěng yǐ jí huàn zhě néng fǒu lǐ jiě yī zhǔ 。

xiàng mù zǔ suí hòu tiáo zhěng le píng gū fāng àn ， bǎ huàn zhě cóng chǎn shēng jiù yī xū qiú dào huò dé míng què jiàn yì de quán guò chéng nà rù jì lù ， bìng fēn bié bǐ jiào bù tóng nián líng 、 shù zì néng lì hé jí bìng lèi xíng de shǐ yòng qíng kuàng 。 lín chè hái jiàn yì chōu qǔ zhōng tú tuì chū zhě jìn xíng diàn huà fǎng tán ， yīn wèi shī bài zhě de chén mò běn shēn jiù shì zhòng yào xìn xī 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， fú wù zhōng xīn zài rù kǒu chù shè zhì xiàn xià xié zhù tái ， yǔn xǔ jū mín yóu gōng zuò rén yuán dài wéi lù rù zī liào ； xì tǒng zé qǔ xiāo bì xū yī cì tián wán de xiàn zhì ， huàn zhě kě yǐ bǎo cún nèi róng ， shāo hòu jì xù 。 wèi le bì miǎn yī shēng bèi dān yī sù dù zhǐ biāo qiān zhì ， guǎn lǐ rén yuán bǎ xiǎng yìng sù dù yǔ bìng lì wán zhěng dù 、 hòu xù zhuǎn zhěn jié guǒ jié hé qǐ lái shěn hé 。 xīn de fāng àn bìng bù zhuī qiú zhì zào yí gè gèng xǐng mù dì bǎi fēn bǐ ， ér shì shì tú shuō míng biàn lì jiū jìng yóu shuí huò dé ， é wài chéng běn yòu yóu shuí chéng dān 。

shì diǎn jié shù qián de jiē duàn guān chá xiǎn shì ， nián qīng huàn zhě réng shì xiàn shàng wèn zhěn de zhǔ yào shǐ yòng zhě ， dàn zài xié zhù tái tóu rù yùn xíng hòu ， lǎo nián jū mín zhōng tú tuì chū de qíng kuàng yǒu suǒ jiǎn shǎo 。 zhè ge biàn huà jǐn shǔ yú jiào xué àn lì zhōng de jú bù guān chá ， jì bú shì zhèng shì tǒng jì jié lùn ， yě bù néng zhí jiē tuī guǎng dào qí tā dì qū 。 zuì zhōng bào gào bǎo liú le hòu zhěn shí jiān suō duǎn bǎi fēn zhī shí bā de yuán shǐ jié guǒ ， tóng shí bǔ chōng shuō míng qí tǒng jì fàn wéi hé jú xiàn ， bìng jiàn yì zhǎng qī bǎo liú diàn huà yù yuē yǔ xiàn chǎng chuāng kǒu 。 lín chè zài jié lùn zhōng xiě dào ， jì shù de jià zhí bù zài yú pò shǐ suǒ yǒu rén cǎi yòng tóng yī zhǒng fāng shì ， ér zài yú wèi bù tóng chǔ jìng de rén zēng jiā kě kào de xuǎn zé 。 yī cì fù zé rèn de píng gū ， yě bù yìng jí yú zhèng míng shì diǎn chéng gōng huò shī bài ， ér yīng jiē shì nǎ xiē huán jié zhēn zhèng gǎi shàn le tǐ yàn ， nǎ xiē kùn nán zhǐ shì cóng jī gòu zhuǎn yí dào le huàn zhě shēn shàng 。
translation: In the teaching case, Linjiang City was preparing to evaluate a three-month pilot program for online medical consultations. Under the procedure, residents first described their symptoms and uploaded images on a mobile phone. A community doctor then decided whether a video consultation, a prescription, or a hospital referral was needed. The interim report submitted by the project team showed that the average waiting time of patients who completed an online consultation was 18 percent shorter than before. Lin Che initially believed that this result was sufficient to demonstrate an improvement in efficiency. However, when he examined the appendix, he found that the data included only those who had successfully reached the video stage. Residents who had failed to register, had their materials returned, or had abandoned the process were excluded.

Instead of rejecting the report immediately, Lin Che asked the project team to explain when the waiting period was considered to begin. The staff used the moment when a patient successfully submitted the required information as the starting point, without counting the time spent creating an account, learning how to use the system, or repeatedly correcting images. This method might make little difference to office workers comfortable with smartphones, but for older people with poor eyesight or limited literacy, the preparation could take longer than the official wait. The average also concealed differences among departments. Dermatology could handle some cases from photographs, whereas internal medicine physicians often needed to ask further questions about medical history. Lin Che therefore concluded that the 18 percent figure was not incorrect, but it showed only that one part of the process had become faster.

To understand the experiences behind the figures, Lin Che observed the community service center for four consecutive days. On the afternoon of the second day, an older woman surnamed Wu arrived with an old phone left by her daughter and asked for help. Her knee had been hurting for half a month, and she had tried to seek advice online, but on three occasions she uploaded a photograph of a medicine box instead of her identification card. After a volunteer completed the steps for her, the system asked her to describe the severity of her pain again. She sighed that if she needed help at every step, she would rather wait in line as she had before. Significantly, she was not opposed to online services. When a doctor told her by video that she did not need to visit a major hospital for the time being, she visibly relaxed. What truly made her uneasy was not the screen, but uncertainty about whether she had acted correctly and whom she could contact after making a mistake.

Problems that did not appear in the report also emerged on the doctors' side. Online consultations reduced repetitive explanations for some doctors, but increased the pressure of determining whether the available information was complete. A general practitioner noted that patients often described their most worrying symptom in detail while omitting allergies, chronic conditions, or current medications. If doctors asked fewer follow-up questions to improve processing speed, risks could remain hidden. If they verified everything again, the time saved would quickly disappear. More troublingly, the platform reminded doctors to end conversations promptly according to the length of the wait. Although this design appeared to encourage progress, it could turn an efficiency indicator into a psychological burden. Based on these findings, Lin Che proposed that the evaluation should not merely ask how many people had been processed. It should also examine whether referrals were timely, whether information was complete, and whether patients understood the medical advice.

The project team then revised the evaluation plan. It began recording the entire process from the emergence of a medical need to the receipt of clear advice, and separately compared usage among people of different ages, levels of digital ability, and types of illness. Lin Che also recommended conducting telephone interviews with a sample of those who had abandoned the process, because the silence of unsuccessful users was itself important information. Meanwhile, the service center established an in-person assistance desk at the entrance, allowing staff members to enter information on behalf of residents. The system removed the requirement to complete everything in one session, enabling patients to save their entries and continue later. To prevent doctors from being constrained by a single speed indicator, managers reviewed response time together with record completeness and subsequent referral outcomes. The revised plan did not seek to produce a more striking percentage, but to explain who actually gained convenience and who bore the additional costs.

The observations made before the end of the pilot showed that young patients remained the main users of online consultations, but fewer older residents abandoned the process after the assistance desk began operating. This change was only a limited observation within the teaching case. It was neither a formal statistical conclusion nor something that could be directly generalized to other regions. The final report retained the original result showing an 18 percent reduction in waiting time, while adding an explanation of its scope and limitations and recommending the continued availability of telephone appointments and in-person service windows. In his conclusion, Lin Che wrote that the value of technology did not lie in forcing everyone to use the same method, but in providing reliable choices to people in different circumstances. A responsible evaluation should not rush to prove that a pilot has succeeded or failed. Instead, it should reveal which steps genuinely improved the experience and which difficulties had merely been transferred from the institution to the patient.

options: 报告中的候诊时间没有比过去缩短
报告只统计了顺利进入视频环节的患者
社区医生拒绝承认线上问诊有效
项目组没有记录任何候诊时间

只比较不同科室的平均候诊时间
抽取中途退出者进行电话访谈

questions.evidence: 林澈在结论中写道，技术的价值不在于迫使所有人采用同一种方式，而在于为不同处境的人增加可靠的选择。

articles.title: 十二个百分点之外：一次智能公交试点评估
articles.summary: 一名独立评估者通过核查统计口径、走访司机与乘客，并比较不同群体的出行体验，指出智能公交调度试点虽改善了部分高峰线路的准点率，却也带来了候车时间转移、司机压力增加和偏远站点服务不足等问题。她建议延长观察期并设置推广条件，而不是仅凭单项指标仓促扩大试点。
articles.topic: 十二个百分点之外：一次智能公交试点评估
paragraphs: 本文是为分级阅读设计的教学案例，其中的城市、人物和数据均为虚构材料，不代表任何真实地区的政策或统计结果。临江市交通中心在六条公交线路上试用智能调度系统，系统会根据车辆位置、道路拥堵程度和车厢客流，临时调整发车间隔。三个月后，项目组提交了一份阶段报告，称早高峰准点率提高了十二个百分点，并据此建议把系统推广到全市。负责独立评估的周岚没有立刻表示赞成。她认为，单项指标的上升固然值得关注，却不足以证明整个出行服务已经改善。

周岚首先核查了报告中的统计口径。她发现，项目组把车辆到达终点的时间作为判断准点与否的依据，却没有计算乘客在中途站等待了多久。智能系统为了保证主干线路按时抵达终点，有时会让后方车辆延迟出站，或者临时跳过客流较少的站点。因此，终点准点率虽然提高了，部分乘客的候车时间却更不稳定。更重要的是，报告只比较了试点前后的平均值，没有把同期道路施工、学校放假以及天气变化等因素排除在外。周岚指出，如果外部条件发生了明显变化，就不能轻易把全部改善归功于新系统。

为了弄清数字背后的实际体验，周岚连续两周跟车观察，并访问了司机、调度员和不同年龄的乘客。上班族普遍认可电子站牌提供的到站预测，认为换乘安排比过去方便；一些老年乘客却表示，临时越站的信息只显示在手机应用里，他们到站后才发现车辆不停靠。几名司机还提到，系统频繁发出缩短间隔的指令，而道路情况未必允许他们按要求行驶。为了避免被记录为延误，他们不得不减少途中休息，精神压力随之增加。一位调度员坦言，算法擅长处理实时数据，却很难识别轮椅乘客上车、车辆发生轻微故障等需要人工判断的情形。

周岚随后把六条线路分成三类。连接商业区的线路客流集中，车辆和站点设施也较完善，系统的预测相对准确；经过老城区的线路道路狭窄，突发拥堵较多，自动调整经常失效；通往郊区的线路班次本来就少，一旦系统把车辆调往客流更大的区域，偏远站点的乘客可能要多等很久。这种差异说明，同一套技术在不同环境中未必产生相同效果。评估公共服务时，不但要观察整体效率，还要确认改善是否以牺牲少数群体的便利为代价。否则，漂亮的平均数可能掩盖服务分配的不均衡。

在评审会上，项目负责人强调，如果迟迟不扩大规模，前期投入可能无法充分发挥作用。周岚承认系统具有潜力，但她反对把已经投入资金当成继续推广的主要理由。过去的成本无法通过扩大项目自动收回，新的决定仍应取决于未来收益、风险和修正空间。她建议再观察六个月，同时补充三类指标：中途站实际候车时间、临时越站对弱势乘客的影响，以及司机在连续工作中的疲劳程度。她还提出，应允许调度员在特殊情况下暂停自动指令，并要求运营方为没有智能手机的乘客提供清晰的现场通知。

最终，评审组没有否定试点，也没有批准立即全面推广。他们决定保留商业区的运行方案，在老城区增加人工调度权限，并为郊区线路设置最低班次保障。只有当新增数据表明服务改善能够持续，而且不同乘客群体没有承担明显不成比例的代价时，推广范围才会扩大。这个结论并不醒目，却体现了评估工作的价值：评估者既不能因为技术新颖就忽略风险，也不该因为存在缺陷就拒绝调整。真正可靠的决策，不是寻找一个足以结束争论的数字，而是不断追问这个数字如何产生、遗漏了谁，又会把成本转移给谁。
pinyin: běn wén shì wèi fēn jí yuè dú shè jì de jiào xué àn lì ， qí zhōng de chéng shì 、 rén wù hé shù jù jūn wèi xū gòu cái liào ， bù dài biǎo rèn hé zhēn shí dì qū de zhèng cè huò tǒng jì jié guǒ 。 lín jiāng shì jiāo tōng zhōng xīn zài liù tiáo gōng jiāo xiàn lù shàng shì yòng zhì néng diào dù xì tǒng ， xì tǒng huì gēn jù chē liàng wèi zhì 、 dào lù yōng dǔ chéng dù hé chē xiāng kè liú ， lín shí diào zhěng fā chē jiàn gé 。 sān gè yuè hòu ， xiàng mù zǔ tí jiāo le yī fèn jiē duàn bào gào ， chēng zǎo gāo fēng zhǔn diǎn lǜ tí gāo le shí èr gè bǎi fēn diǎn ， bìng jù cǐ jiàn yì bǎ xì tǒng tuī guǎng dào quán shì 。 fù zé dú lì píng gū de zhōu lán méi yǒu lì kè biǎo shì zàn chéng 。 tā rèn wéi ， dān xiàng zhǐ biāo dì shàng shēng gù rán zhí de guān zhù ， què bù zú yǐ zhèng míng zhěng gè chū xíng fú wù yǐ jīng gǎi shàn 。

zhōu lán shǒu xiān hé chá le bào gào zhōng de tǒng jì kǒu jìng 。 tā fā xiàn ， xiàng mù zǔ bǎ chē liàng dào dá zhōng diǎn de shí jiān zuò wéi pàn duàn zhǔn diǎn yǔ fǒu de yī jù ， què méi yǒu jì suàn chéng kè zài zhōng tú zhàn děng dài le duō jiǔ 。 zhì néng xì tǒng wèi le bǎo zhèng zhǔ gàn xiàn lù àn shí dǐ dá zhōng diǎn ， yǒu shí huì ràng hòu fāng chē liàng yán chí chū zhàn ， huò zhě lín shí tiào guò kè liú jiào shǎo de zhàn diǎn 。 yīn cǐ ， zhōng diǎn zhǔn diǎn lǜ suī rán tí gāo le ， bù fèn chéng kè de hòu chē shí jiān què gèng bù wěn dìng 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， bào gào zhǐ bǐ jiào le shì diǎn qián hòu de píng jūn zhí ， méi yǒu bǎ tóng qī dào lù shī gōng 、 xué xiào fàng jià yǐ jí tiān qì biàn huà děng yīn sù pái chú zài wài 。 zhōu lán zhǐ chū ， rú guǒ wài bù tiáo jiàn fā shēng le míng xiǎn biàn huà ， jiù bù néng qīng yì bǎ quán bù gǎi shàn guī gōng yú xīn xì tǒng 。

wèi le nòng qīng shù zì bèi hòu de shí jì tǐ yàn ， zhōu lán lián xù liǎng zhōu gēn chē guān chá ， bìng fǎng wèn le sī jī 、 diào dù yuán hé bù tóng nián líng de chéng kè 。 shàng bān zú pǔ biàn rèn kě diàn zi zhàn pái tí gōng de dào zhàn yù cè ， rèn wéi huàn chéng ān pái bǐ guò qù fāng biàn ； yī xiē lǎo nián chéng kè què biǎo shì ， lín shí yuè zhàn de xìn xī zhǐ xiǎn shì zài shǒu jī yìng yòng lǐ ， tā men dào zhàn hòu cái fā xiàn chē liàng bù tíng kào 。 jǐ míng sī jī hái tí dào ， xì tǒng pín fán fā chū suō duǎn jiàn gé de zhǐ lìng ， ér dào lù qíng kuàng wèi bì yǔn xǔ tā men àn yāo qiú xíng shǐ 。 wèi le bì miǎn bèi jì lù wèi yán wù ， tā men bù dé bù jiǎn shǎo tú zhōng xiū xī ， jīng shén yā lì suí zhī zēng jiā 。 yī wèi diào dù yuán tǎn yán ， suàn fǎ shàn cháng chǔ lǐ shí shí shù jù ， què hěn nán shí bié lún yǐ chéng kè shàng chē 、 chē liàng fā shēng qīng wēi gù zhàng děng xū yào rén gōng pàn duàn de qíng xíng 。

zhōu lán suí hòu bǎ liù tiáo xiàn lù fēn chéng sān lèi 。 lián jiē shāng yè qū de xiàn lù kè liú jí zhōng ， chē liàng hé zhàn diǎn shè shī yě jiào wán shàn ， xì tǒng de yù cè xiāng duì zhǔn què ； jīng guò lǎo chéng qū de xiàn lù dào lù xiá zhǎi ， tū fā yōng dǔ jiào duō ， zì dòng tiáo zhěng jīng cháng shī xiào ； tōng wǎng jiāo qū de xiàn lù bān cì běn lái jiù shǎo ， yí dàn xì tǒng bǎ chē liàng diào wǎng kè liú gèng dà de qū yù ， piān yuǎn zhàn diǎn de chéng kè kě néng yào duō děng hěn jiǔ 。 zhè zhǒng chà yì shuō míng ， tóng yī tào jì shù zài bù tóng huán jìng zhōng wèi bì chǎn shēng xiāng tóng xiào guǒ 。 píng gū gōng gòng fú wù shí ， bù dàn yào guān chá zhěng tǐ xiào lǜ ， hái yào què rèn gǎi shàn shì fǒu yǐ xī shēng shǎo shù qún tǐ de biàn lì wèi dài jià 。 fǒu zé ， piào liàng de píng jūn shù kě néng yǎn gài fú wù fēn pèi de bù jūn héng 。

zài píng shěn huì shàng ， xiàng mù fù zé rén qiáng diào ， rú guǒ chí chí bù kuò dà guī mó ， qián qī tóu rù kě néng wú fǎ chōng fèn fā huī zuò yòng 。 zhōu lán chéng rèn xì tǒng jù yǒu qián lì ， dàn tā fǎn duì bǎ yǐ jīng tóu rù zī jīn dàng chéng jì xù tuī guǎng de zhǔ yào lǐ yóu 。 guò qù de chéng běn wú fǎ tōng guò kuò dà xiàng mù zì dòng shōu huí ， xīn de jué dìng réng yīng qǔ jué yú wèi lái shōu yì 、 fēng xiǎn hé xiū zhèng kōng jiān 。 tā jiàn yì zài guān chá liù gè yuè ， tóng shí bǔ chōng sān lèi zhǐ biāo ： zhōng tú zhàn shí jì hòu chē shí jiān 、 lín shí yuè zhàn duì ruò shì chéng kè de yǐng xiǎng ， yǐ jí sī jī zài lián xù gōng zuò zhōng de pí láo chéng dù 。 tā hái tí chū ， yīng yǔn xǔ diào dù yuán zài tè shū qíng kuàng xià zàn tíng zì dòng zhǐ lìng ， bìng yāo qiú yùn yíng fāng wèi méi yǒu zhì néng shǒu jī de chéng kè tí gōng qīng xī de xiàn chǎng tōng zhī 。

zuì zhōng ， píng shěn zǔ méi yǒu fǒu dìng shì diǎn ， yě méi yǒu pī zhǔn lì jí quán miàn tuī guǎng 。 tā men jué dìng bǎo liú shāng yè qū de yùn xíng fāng àn ， zài lǎo chéng qū zēng jiā rén gōng diào dù quán xiàn ， bìng wèi jiāo qū xiàn lù shè zhì zuì dī bān cì bǎo zhàng 。 zhǐ yǒu dāng xīn zēng shù jù biǎo míng fú wù gǎi shàn néng gòu chí xù ， ér qiě bù tóng chéng kè qún tǐ méi yǒu chéng dān míng xiǎn bù chéng bǐ lì de dài jià shí ， tuī guǎng fàn wéi cái huì kuò dà 。 zhè ge jié lùn bìng bù xǐng mù ， què tǐ xiàn le píng gū gōng zuò de jià zhí ： píng gū zhě jì bù néng yīn wèi jì shù xīn yǐng jiù hū lüè fēng xiǎn ， yě bù gāi yīn wèi cún zài quē xiàn jiù jù jué tiáo zhěng 。 zhēn zhèng kě kào de jué cè ， bú shì xún zhǎo yí gè zú yǐ jié shù zhēng lùn de shù zì ， ér shì bù duàn zhuī wèn zhè ge shù zì rú hé chǎn shēng 、 yí lòu le shuí ， yòu huì bǎ chéng běn zhuǎn yí gěi shuí 。
translation: This is a teaching case designed for graded reading. Its city, characters, and data are fictional and do not represent the policies or statistical results of any real place. The Linjiang Municipal Transportation Center tested an intelligent dispatch system on six bus routes. Based on vehicle locations, road congestion, and passenger loads, the system could temporarily adjust departure intervals. Three months later, the project team submitted an interim report stating that on-time performance during the morning rush hour had risen by twelve percentage points. On that basis, it recommended expanding the system across the city. Zhou Lan, who was responsible for an independent evaluation, did not immediately agree. In her view, the rise of a single indicator deserved attention, but it was not enough to prove that the overall travel service had improved.

Zhou Lan first examined how the figures in the report had been calculated. She found that the project team judged punctuality according to the time vehicles reached their final stops, without measuring how long passengers waited at intermediate stops. To ensure that buses on major routes reached their destinations on time, the intelligent system sometimes delayed the departure of following vehicles or temporarily skipped stops with fewer passengers. As a result, although terminal punctuality improved, waiting times became less predictable for some passengers. More importantly, the report compared only the averages before and after the trial. It did not exclude factors such as road construction, school holidays, or changes in weather during the same period. Zhou Lan pointed out that if external conditions had changed substantially, all the improvement could not easily be attributed to the new system.

To understand the actual experiences behind the numbers, Zhou Lan rode buses for two consecutive weeks and interviewed drivers, dispatchers, and passengers of different ages. Commuters generally approved of the arrival forecasts shown on electronic displays and found transfers more convenient than before. Some older passengers, however, said that information about temporarily skipped stops appeared only in the mobile application, so they did not realize that a bus would not stop until they had already reached the station. Several drivers also reported that the system frequently instructed them to shorten intervals, even when road conditions did not allow them to travel as required. To avoid having delays recorded against them, they had to reduce their breaks during the journey, which increased their mental strain. One dispatcher admitted that the algorithm was good at processing real-time data but struggled to recognize situations requiring human judgment, such as a wheelchair user boarding or a minor vehicle malfunction.

Zhou Lan then divided the six routes into three categories. Routes connecting commercial districts had concentrated passenger flows and better vehicles and station facilities, so the system made relatively accurate predictions. Routes passing through the old town faced narrow roads and frequent unexpected congestion, causing automatic adjustments to fail repeatedly. Services to suburban areas already ran infrequently, and if the system transferred buses to busier areas, passengers at remote stops might have to wait much longer. These differences showed that the same technology would not necessarily produce the same results in different environments. When evaluating public services, it is necessary not only to examine overall efficiency but also to determine whether improvement comes at the expense of convenience for a minority. Otherwise, attractive averages may conceal an unequal distribution of services.

At the review meeting, the project director argued that if expansion were delayed, the earlier investment might never achieve its full value. Zhou Lan acknowledged the system's potential, but she opposed treating money already spent as the main reason for further expansion. Past costs could not automatically be recovered by enlarging the project, and the new decision should still depend on future benefits, risks, and room for correction. She recommended another six months of observation and proposed three additional indicators: actual waiting times at intermediate stops, the effects of temporary stop-skipping on vulnerable passengers, and driver fatigue during continuous work. She also suggested allowing dispatchers to suspend automatic instructions in exceptional circumstances and requiring the operator to provide clear on-site notices for passengers without smartphones.

In the end, the review panel neither rejected the trial nor approved immediate citywide expansion. It decided to retain the operating plan in commercial districts, increase the authority of human dispatchers in the old town, and guarantee a minimum service frequency on suburban routes. Expansion would occur only when new data showed that service improvements could be sustained and that no passenger group was bearing a clearly disproportionate cost. This conclusion was not dramatic, but it demonstrated the value of evaluation: evaluators must neither overlook risks merely because a technology is novel nor reject revision merely because defects exist. Truly reliable decision-making does not seek a single number capable of ending the debate. Instead, it keeps asking how that number was produced, whom it left out, and onto whom it might shift the costs.
