lín qiū lán diào chū qī mò xiàn chǎng kǎo hé jì lù ， fā xiàn bù fèn àn shí wán chéng quán bù yuǎn chéng rèn wù de xué shēng ， zài dú lì ān zhuāng wēn dù chuán gǎn qì shí réng huì jiē cuò jiē kǒu ， hái yǒu rén wú fǎ jiě shì lú mén méi yǒu wán quán guān bì wèi hé huì yǐng xiǎng cè liáng jié guǒ 。 zhè xiē wèn tí méi yǒu zào chéng shì gù ， què biǎo míng píng tái shàng de “ wán chéng ” kě néng zhǐ shì àn zhào tí shì zǒu wán liú chéng 。 yuǎn chéng jiè miàn huì zì dòng xiàn zhì wēi xiǎn cān shù ， zhí bān jiào shī yě huì zài hòu tái jiū zhèng míng xiǎn cuò wù ， xué shēng yīn cǐ hěn shǎo miàn duì zhēn shí shè bèi zhōng de zào shēng 、 zǔ lì 、 mó sǔn hé tū fā yì cháng 。 xué shēng dài biǎo gù yán zé tí chū lìng yí miàn ： guò qù kāi fàng shí yàn shì de shí jiān yǔ zhuān yè kè chōng tū ， yǒu xiē xué shēng wèi le gǎn zài guān mén qián wán chéng shí yàn ， zhǐ néng zhào chāo tóng zǔ tóng xué de shù jù ； cǎi yòng yuǎn chéng yù xí hòu ， tā men zhì shǎo néng gòu fǎn fù guān chá bù zhòu ， bìng zài tí jiāo cān shù qián chá yuè zī liào 。 shuāng fāng zhēng lùn de jiāo diǎn yóu “ yào bù yào shǐ yòng jì shù ” zhuǎn xiàng “ nǎ xiē néng lì kě yǐ yuǎn chéng péi yǎng ， nǎ xiē jīng yàn bì xū zài xiàn chǎng huò dé ”。

píng gū xiǎo zǔ suí hòu lái dào cái liào shí yàn lóu èr céng ， àn xué shēng shǐ yòng de liǎng zhǒng fāng shì gè wán chéng yī cì rèn wù 。 yuǎn chéng cāo zuò shí ， jiè miàn qīng chǔ xiǎn shì shēng wēn qū xiàn ， cān shù shū rù yě shí fēn shùn chàng ， dàn guān chá zhě wú fǎ wén dào lěng què yóu yì cháng huī fā de qì wèi ， yě gǎn shòu bú dào jiā jù sōng dòng shí xì wēi de zhèn dòng 。 xiàn chǎng cāo zuò suī rán hào shí gèng zhǎng ， què pò shǐ cāo zuò zhě jiǎn chá fáng hù miàn zhào 、 què rèn yàng pǐn wèi zhì ， bìng yǔ tóng bàn hé duì jǐn jí duàn diàn chéng xù 。 zhí bān jiào shī xǔ dé ān hái zhǐ chū ， dài cāo zuò zhì dù mó hú le zé rèn biān jiè ： rú guǒ xué shēng shū rù de cān shù hé lǐ ， ér jiào shī ān zhuāng yàng pǐn shí chū xiàn piān chā ， zuì zhōng jié guǒ jiū jìng yīng yóu shuí fù zé ， xiàn yǒu kè chéng guī zé bìng wèi shuō míng 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， wán quán qǔ xiāo yuǎn chéng huán jié yě bù xiàn shí 。 cái liào xì zhǐ yǒu liǎng tào kě gōng běn kē shēng shǐ yòng de rè chǔ lǐ shè bèi ， jí zhōng pái kè bù jǐn zēng jiā děng dài shí jiān ， hái huì shǐ jiào shī bǎ jīng lì hào zài chóng fù jiǎng jiě jī chǔ bù zhòu shàng 。

miàn duì kuò dà shì diǎn 、 wéi chí yuán zhuàng hé quán miàn tíng zhǐ sān zhǒng yì jiàn ， píng gū xiǎo zǔ méi yǒu bǎ wán chéng lǜ zuò wéi wéi yī yī jù 。 jīng guò liǎng lún tǎo lùn ， xué yuàn jué dìng chóng xīn huà fēn kè chéng huán jié ： ān quán guī fàn 、 shè bèi jié gòu 、 cān shù jì suàn hé jié guǒ fēn xī jì xù zài xiàn wán chéng ； yàng pǐn ān zhuāng 、 shè bèi jiǎn chá 、 yì cháng shí bié jí jǐn jí chǔ zhì bì xū zài lín gǎng xiào qū shí yàn shì jìn xíng 。 měi míng xué shēng zài jìn rù xiàn chǎng qián ， xū yào tōng guò yī cì bù shè zì dòng tí shì de qíng jìng pàn duàn ； jìn rù shí yàn shì hòu ， zé yào dú lì wán chéng guān jiàn cāo zuò ， bìng dāng chǎng shuō míng měi yī bù kě néng dài lái de fēng xiǎn 。 duì yú yīn tè shū qíng kuàng wú fǎ àn qī dào xiào de xué shēng ， xué yuàn bǎo liú yuǎn chéng guān chá zī gé ， dàn yuǎn chéng rèn wù zhǐ néng jì wèi yù xí ， bù néng tì dài cāo zuò chéng jì 。 xué yuàn tóng shí qǔ xiāo dān chún yǐ rèn wù tí jiāo zuò wéi wán chéng biāo zhì de zuò fǎ ， jiāng wán chéng dìng yì gǎi wéi zài xiàn zhǔn bèi 、 xiàn chǎng cāo zuò hé shí yàn shuō míng sān bù fèn quán bù hé gé 。

tiáo zhěng hòu de shǒu lún kè chéng jié shù shí ， xué yuàn méi yǒu zài fā bù yí gè jiǎn dān de zēng zhǎng bǐ lì ， ér shì gōng kāi shuō míng shì diǎn jiě jué le shén me ， yòu liú xià le shén me wèn tí 。 yuǎn chéng huán jié què shí huǎn jiě le shè bèi jǐn zhāng ， shǐ xué shēng néng gòu zài xiàn chǎng kè qián shú xī liú chéng ； huī fù guān jiàn cāo zuò hòu ， jiào shī yě gèng róng yì fā xiàn cuò wù xí guàn ， bìng jí shí jiū zhèng 。 shǎo shù xué shēng qǐ chū bào yuàn kǎo hé biàn dé má fán ， dàn zài qīn shǒu chǔ lǐ chuán gǎn qì jiē chù bù liáng hé shēng wēn zhōng duàn hòu ， tā men chéng rèn zhè xiē qíng kuàng wú fǎ jǐn kào shì pín lǐ jiě 。 cái liào xì zuì zhōng méi yǒu bǎ shì diǎn bāo zhuāng chéng chéng gōng huò shī bài ， ér shì bǎ tā shì wèi yī cì kè chéng biān jiè de jiào zhǔn ： jì shù shì hé chéng dān chóng fù yǎn shì 、 xìn xī jì lù hé kāi fàng tǎo lùn ， què bù néng tì xué shēng chéng shòu cāo zuò hòu guǒ 。 nà fèn qiáng diào wán chéng lǜ de jiē duàn bào gào yīn cǐ bèi bǎo liú zài dàng àn zhōng ， páng biān fù shàng le xiū dìng shuō míng ， tí xǐng jīn hòu de píng gū zhě ， shù zì kě yǐ zhǐ chū biàn huà ， què bù néng dài tì duì xué xí guò chéng de pàn duàn 。
translation: In early March, the Department of Materials at Haizhou Institute of Technology held an evaluation meeting at its Lingang campus for a pilot remote laboratory course. The pilot involved the course "Heat Treatment of Metallic Materials." Students first watched equipment demonstrations on an online platform, then set parameters remotely, after which the teacher on duty in the laboratory started the furnace temperature-control system on their behalf. In its interim report, the institute listed a 10 percent increase in the course completion rate as a major achievement and recommended extending the model to three additional laboratory courses in the following semester. The report argued that the remote approach reduced time spent waiting in line and gave students who could not attend because of internships, ill health, or off-campus exchanges an opportunity to make up the work. On this basis, Zhou Mingyuan, the associate dean responsible for teaching reform, concluded that the pilot had already demonstrated that laboratory instruction could overcome constraints of time and location. However, Lin Qiulan, the course director, did not immediately agree. She noticed that although the report provided detailed statistics on logins, task submissions, and video viewing, it did not answer a more important question: whether the students had genuinely mastered how to operate the equipment.

Lin Qiulan retrieved the records from the on-site final assessment and found that some students who had completed all the remote tasks on time still connected the wrong ports when independently installing temperature sensors, while others could not explain why a furnace door that was not fully closed would affect the measurement results. These problems did not cause any accidents, but they showed that "completion" on the platform might mean nothing more than following the prompts through the entire procedure. The remote interface automatically restricted dangerous parameter settings, and the teacher on duty corrected obvious mistakes in the background, so students rarely encountered the noise, resistance, wear, and unexpected abnormalities present in real equipment. Student representative Gu Yan presented the other side of the issue: in the past, the laboratory's opening hours had conflicted with courses in their major, and some students, in order to finish their experiments before closing time, had no choice but to copy data from their group members. With remote preparation, they could at least watch the procedures repeatedly and consult reference materials before submitting their parameters. The focus of the debate shifted from whether technology should be used to which abilities could be developed remotely and which kinds of experience had to be acquired on site.

The evaluation team then went to the second floor of the materials laboratory building and completed the same task once using each of the two methods available to students. During remote operation, the interface clearly displayed the heating curve, and entering parameters was very smooth, but observers could not smell the odor produced by abnormal evaporation of the cooling oil or feel the slight vibration caused by a loose fixture. Although on-site operation took longer, it compelled operators to inspect their protective face shields, confirm the position of the samples, and review the emergency power-off procedure with their peers. Xu De'an, the teacher on duty, also pointed out that having teachers operate the equipment on students' behalf blurred the boundaries of responsibility: if a student's parameters were reasonable but the teacher made an error while installing the sample, the existing course rules did not specify who should ultimately be held responsible for the result. At the same time, eliminating the remote component entirely was also unrealistic. The Department of Materials had only two sets of heat-treatment equipment available to undergraduates. Scheduling classes in concentrated blocks would not only increase waiting times but also consume teachers' energy through repeated explanations of basic procedures.

Faced with three proposals—expanding the pilot, maintaining the status quo, and discontinuing it entirely—the evaluation team did not treat the completion rate as its sole criterion. After two rounds of discussion, the institute decided to reorganize the course components. Safety rules, equipment structure, parameter calculations, and analysis of results would continue to be completed online, while sample installation, equipment inspection, anomaly identification, and emergency response had to be carried out in the laboratory at the Lingang campus. Before entering the laboratory, every student was required to pass a scenario-based assessment with no automatic prompts. Once inside, students had to independently perform the critical operations and explain on the spot the risks that could arise at each step. For students unable to reach the campus on schedule because of special circumstances, the institute continued to allow them to observe remotely, but remote tasks could count only as preparation and could not replace the practical-operation grade. The institute also abandoned the practice of treating task submission alone as proof of completion, redefining completion to require passing all three components: online preparation, on-site operation, and an explanation of the experiment.

At the end of the first course cycle following the adjustments, the institute did not release another simple growth percentage. Instead, it publicly explained what problems the pilot had solved and what issues remained. The remote component had indeed eased the shortage of equipment and allowed students to familiarize themselves with the procedures before attending on-site classes. After critical operations were restored to the in-person component, teachers also found it easier to identify and promptly correct improper habits. A small number of students initially complained that the assessment had become cumbersome, but after personally dealing with poor sensor contact and interruptions during heating, they acknowledged that such situations could not be understood through video alone. In the end, the Department of Materials did not present the pilot as either a success or a failure. Instead, it regarded the pilot as an exercise in recalibrating the boundaries of the course: technology was well suited to repetitive demonstrations, information recording, and open discussion, but it could not bear the consequences of operating the equipment on students' behalf. The interim report emphasizing the completion rate was therefore retained in the archives, with a revision note attached to remind future evaluators that numbers can indicate change, but they cannot replace judgment about the learning process.

学生代表坚决反对使用远程技术

articles.title: 两度之差：青槐街区降温试点的复核与抉择
articles.summary: 河州市青槐街区的降温试点报告称街区温度下降了两度，但居民、商户和评估人员对测量方法及改造效果提出质疑。市规划局经过现场复核，决定保留有效措施、调整争议设计，并建立公开透明的长期评估机制。
articles.topic: 两度之差：青槐街区降温试点的复核与抉择
paragraphs: 盛夏来临前，河州市规划局在老城区青槐街区启动了城市降温试点。这里楼房密集，街道狭窄，午后阳光长期照射水泥路面，行人常常要躲进商店避暑。改造工程主要包括在屋顶涂刷浅色隔热材料、增加街边树木、设置遮阳棚，并把中心广场的一部分硬质地面换成透水铺装。三个月后，项目组发布报告，称试点街区的平均温度比改造前下降了两度。这个结果很快被媒体引用，市政府也开始讨论是否把相关措施推广到其他街区。对急于缓解高温问题的城市管理者来说，两度意味着试点取得了足以支持扩大投资的成效。

然而，青槐街区的居民并没有形成一致判断。住在南口公寓的周岚认为，新增树木虽然还未长成浓荫，但遮阳棚已经使她每天接孩子放学时轻松了许多。经营面馆的赵平却抱怨，棚架挡住了招牌，透水路面施工后，店门前一遇暴雨仍会积水。他还发现，报告中的测温点主要位于广场和树荫附近，而餐馆集中的北巷几乎没有设备。更大的争议来自一次居民说明会。会上，一名退休物理教师指出，改造前的数据采集于连续晴热的日子，改造后的测量却包含阴天。如果天气条件不同，所谓下降两度就不能全部归因于工程。项目负责人承认报告没有充分解释这一差异，但强调试点的价值不应仅由一项测量决定。

面对质疑，规划局没有立即批准推广，而是邀请气象站工作人员、社区代表和街道设计师共同复核。复核组沿着青槐路从东站口走到北巷，逐一检查测温位置、树木状态和居民实际使用遮阳设施的情况。他们发现，报告中的结论并非毫无依据：浅色屋顶减少了部分建筑表面对热量的吸收，广场在傍晚也不再像过去那样持续散发热气。但是，两度这一数字容易让公众误以为整个街区在任何时段都获得了同样的降温效果。事实上，是否有树荫、空气能否流通、建筑朝向如何，都会造成明显差别。复核组因此认为，原报告把复杂的空间变化压缩成单一数字，表达过于肯定，无法直接作为全面推广的依据。

这场冲突使规划局必须在两种压力之间作出选择。一方面，市民期待政府迅速采取行动，应对越来越难忍受的夏季高温；另一方面，如果依据不充分就复制工程，不仅可能浪费资金，还可能把不适合窄巷的设计强加给其他社区。最终，规划局决定保留青槐街区的试点，但暂停原定的全城推广。已经证明具有实际作用的浅色屋顶和广场遮阳设施继续使用，北巷影响商户视线的棚架则重新设计。负责评估的人员也调整了测量办法：今后要在日照、树荫、路口和窄巷等不同环境设置固定测温点，并同时记录天气条件。所有原始记录和设备位置都向居民公开，社区还可以推选代表参与现场核查。

入秋后，青槐街区召开第二次说明会。规划局没有再次宣布一个醒目的降温数字，而是展示哪些地点改善明显、哪些区域仍然闷热，以及下一阶段准备怎样调整。赵平看到北巷棚架的修改方案后，同意配合施工；周岚则报名参加社区观察小组，记录老人和儿童使用公共空间时的真实感受。试点最终没有成为一项急于宣传的城市成绩，却促成了更谨慎的决策方式。河州市随后规定，其他街区申请降温改造时，必须先说明当地建筑、风向和居民需求，不能简单照搬青槐街区的方案。两度之差仍被保留在报告中，但它不再被当成唯一答案，而被视为提出问题的起点。城市降温的成败，既要看温度计，也要看措施是否真正改善了不同人群的日常生活。
pinyin: shèng xià lái lín qián ， hé zhōu shì guī huà jú zài lǎo chéng qū qīng huái jiē qū qǐ dòng le chéng shì jiàng wēn shì diǎn 。 zhè lǐ lóu fáng mì jí ， jiē dào xiá zhǎi ， wǔ hòu yáng guāng cháng qī zhào shè shuǐ ní lù miàn ， xíng rén cháng cháng yào duǒ jìn shāng diàn bì shǔ 。 gǎi zào gōng chéng zhǔ yào bāo kuò zài wū dǐng tú shuā qiǎn sè gé rè cái liào 、 zēng jiā jiē biān shù mù 、 shè zhì zhē yáng péng ， bìng bǎ zhōng xīn guǎng chǎng de yī bù fèn yìng zhì dì miàn huàn chéng tòu shuǐ pù zhuāng 。 sān gè yuè hòu ， xiàng mù zǔ fā bù bào gào ， chēng shì diǎn jiē qū de píng jūn wēn dù bǐ gǎi zào qián xià jiàng le liǎng dù 。 zhè ge jié guǒ hěn kuài bèi méi tǐ yǐn yòng ， shì zhèng fǔ yě kāi shǐ tǎo lùn shì fǒu bǎ xiāng guān cuò shī tuī guǎng dào qí tā jiē qū 。 duì jí yú huǎn jiě gāo wēn wèn tí de chéng shì guǎn lǐ zhě lái shuō ， liǎng dù yì wèi zhe shì diǎn qǔ dé le zú yǐ zhī chí kuò dà tóu zī de chéng xiào 。

rán ér ， qīng huái jiē qū de jū mín bìng méi yǒu xíng chéng yí zhì pàn duàn 。 zhù zài nán kǒu gōng yù de zhōu lán rèn wéi ， xīn zēng shù mù suī rán hái wèi zhǎng chéng nóng yīn ， dàn zhē yáng péng yǐ jīng shǐ tā měi tiān jiē hái zi fàng xué shí qīng sōng le xǔ duō 。 jīng yíng miàn guǎn de zhào píng què bào yuàn ， péng jià dǎng zhù le zhāo pái ， tòu shuǐ lù miàn shī gōng hòu ， diàn mén qián yī yù bào yǔ réng huì jī shuǐ 。 tā hái fā xiàn ， bào gào zhōng de cè wēn diǎn zhǔ yào wèi yú guǎng chǎng hé shù yīn fù jìn ， ér cān guǎn jí zhōng de běi xiàng jī hū méi yǒu shè bèi 。 gèng dà de zhēng yì lái zì yī cì jū mín shuō míng huì 。 huì shàng ， yī míng tuì xiū wù lǐ jiào shī zhǐ chū ， gǎi zào qián de shù jù cǎi jí yú lián xù qíng rè de rì zi ， gǎi zào hòu de cè liáng què bāo hán yīn tiān 。 rú guǒ tiān qì tiáo jiàn bù tóng ， suǒ wèi xià jiàng liǎng dù jiù bù néng quán bù guī yīn yú gōng chéng 。 xiàng mù fù zé rén chéng rèn bào gào méi yǒu chōng fèn jiě shì zhè yī chā yì ， dàn qiáng diào shì diǎn de jià zhí bù yīng jǐn yóu yī xiàng cè liáng jué dìng 。

miàn duì zhì yí ， guī huà jú méi yǒu lì jí pī zhǔn tuī guǎng ， ér shì yāo qǐng qì xiàng zhàn gōng zuò rén yuán 、 shè qū dài biǎo hé jiē dào shè jì shī gòng tóng fù hé 。 fù hé zǔ yán zhe qīng huái lù cóng dōng zhàn kǒu zǒu dào běi xiàng ， zhú yī jiǎn chá cè wēn wèi zhì 、 shù mù zhuàng tài hé jū mín shí jì shǐ yòng zhē yáng shè shī de qíng kuàng 。 tā men fā xiàn ， bào gào zhōng de jié lùn bìng fēi háo wú yī jù ： qiǎn sè wū dǐng jiǎn shǎo le bù fèn jiàn zhù biǎo miàn duì rè liàng de xī shōu ， guǎng chǎng zài bàng wǎn yě bù zài xiàng guò qù nà yàng chí xù sàn fà rè qì 。 dàn shì ， liǎng dù zhè yī shù zì róng yì ràng gōng zhòng wù yǐ wéi zhěng gè jiē qū zài rèn hé shí duàn dōu huò dé le tóng yàng de jiàng wēn xiào guǒ 。 shì shí shàng ， shì fǒu yǒu shù yīn 、 kōng qì néng fǒu liú tōng 、 jiàn zhù cháo xiàng rú hé ， dū huì zào chéng míng xiǎn chā bié 。 fù hé zǔ yīn cǐ rèn wéi ， yuán bào gào bǎ fù zá de kōng jiān biàn huà yā suō chéng dān yī shù zì ， biǎo dá guò yú kěn dìng ， wú fǎ zhí jiē zuò wéi quán miàn tuī guǎng de yī jù 。

zhè chǎng chōng tū shǐ guī huà jú bì xū zài liǎng zhǒng yā lì zhī jiàn zuò chū xuǎn zé 。 yì fāng miàn ， shì mín qī dài zhèng fǔ xùn sù cǎi qǔ xíng dòng ， yìng duì yuè lái yuè nán rěn shòu de xià jì gāo wēn ； lìng yì fāng miàn ， rú guǒ yī jù bù chōng fèn jiù fù zhì gōng chéng ， bù jǐn kě néng làng fèi zī jīn ， hái kě néng bǎ bú shì hé zhǎi xiàng de shè jì qiáng jiā gěi qí tā shè qū 。 zuì zhōng ， guī huà jú jué dìng bǎo liú qīng huái jiē qū de shì diǎn ， dàn zàn tíng yuán dìng de quán chéng tuī guǎng 。 yǐ jīng zhèng míng jù yǒu shí jì zuò yòng de qiǎn sè wū dǐng hé guǎng chǎng zhē yáng shè shī jì xù shǐ yòng ， běi xiàng yǐng xiǎng shāng hù shì xiàn de péng jià zé chóng xīn shè jì 。 fù zé píng gū de rén yuán yě tiáo zhěng le cè liáng bàn fǎ ： jīn hòu yào zài rì zhào 、 shù yīn 、 lù kǒu hé zhǎi xiàng děng bù tóng huán jìng shè zhì gù dìng cè wēn diǎn ， bìng tóng shí jì lù tiān qì tiáo jiàn 。 suǒ yǒu yuán shǐ jì lù hé shè bèi wèi zhì dōu xiàng jū mín gōng kāi ， shè qū hái kě yǐ tuī xuǎn dài biǎo cān yù xiàn chǎng hé chá 。

rù qiū hòu ， qīng huái jiē qū zhào kāi dì èr cì shuō míng huì 。 guī huà jú méi yǒu zài cì xuān bù yí gè xǐng mù dì jiàng wēn shù zì ， ér shì zhǎn shì nǎ xiē dì diǎn gǎi shàn míng xiǎn 、 nǎ xiē qū yù réng rán mēn rè ， yǐ jí xià yī jiē duàn zhǔn bèi zěn yàng tiáo zhěng 。 zhào píng kàn dào běi xiàng péng jià de xiū gǎi fāng àn hòu ， tóng yì pèi hé shī gōng ； zhōu lán zé bào míng cān jiā shè qū guān chá xiǎo zǔ ， jì lù lǎo rén hé ér tóng shǐ yòng gōng gòng kōng jiān shí de zhēn shí gǎn shòu 。 shì diǎn zuì zhōng méi yǒu chéng wéi yī xiàng jí yú xuān chuán de chéng shì chéng jì ， què cù chéng le gèng jǐn shèn de jué cè fāng shì 。 hé zhōu shì suí hòu guī dìng ， qí tā jiē qū shēn qǐng xiáng wēn gǎi zào shí ， bì xū xiān shuō míng dāng dì jiàn zhù 、 fēng xiàng hé jū mín xū qiú ， bù néng jiǎn dān zhào bān qīng huái jiē qū de fāng àn 。 liǎng dù zhī chà réng bèi bǎo liú zài bào gào zhōng ， dàn tā bù zài bèi dàng chéng wéi yī dá àn ， ér bèi shì wéi tí chū wèn tí de qǐ diǎn 。 chéng shì jiàng wēn de chéng bài ， jì yào kàn wēn dù jì ， yě yào kàn cuò shī shì fǒu zhēn zhèng gǎi shàn le bù tóng rén qún de rì cháng shēng huó 。
translation: Before the height of summer arrived, the Hezhou City Planning Bureau launched an urban cooling pilot project in the Qinghuai neighborhood of the old city. Buildings there were densely packed, the streets were narrow, and the afternoon sun beat down on the concrete pavement for long periods, often forcing pedestrians to take refuge from the heat in shops. The renovation project mainly involved coating rooftops with light-colored insulating materials, adding roadside trees, installing shade canopies, and replacing part of the hard surface in the central square with permeable paving. Three months later, the project team released a report stating that the average temperature in the pilot neighborhood had fallen by two degrees compared with before the renovation. The result was quickly cited by the media, and the municipal government also began discussing whether to extend the measures to other neighborhoods. For city administrators eager to alleviate the problem of extreme heat, a two-degree reduction meant that the pilot had achieved results sufficient to justify greater investment.

However, residents of the Qinghuai neighborhood did not reach a shared conclusion. Zhou Lan, who lived in Nankou Apartments, felt that although the newly planted trees had not yet grown enough to provide dense shade, the canopies had already made it much easier for her to pick up her child from school each day. Zhao Ping, who ran a noodle shop, complained that the canopy frames blocked his sign and that, even after the permeable pavement was installed, water still pooled outside his shop whenever there was a heavy rainstorm. He also noticed that the temperature-monitoring points in the report were located mainly in the square and near shaded areas, while North Alley, where restaurants were concentrated, had almost no monitoring equipment. A residents' briefing generated even greater controversy. At the meeting, a retired physics teacher pointed out that the pre-renovation data had been collected during a succession of sunny, hot days, whereas the post-renovation measurements included cloudy days. If the weather conditions were different, the purported two-degree decrease could not be attributed entirely to the project. The project leader acknowledged that the report had not adequately explained this difference but stressed that the value of the pilot should not be determined by a single measurement alone.

In response to the questions, the Planning Bureau did not immediately approve a broader rollout. Instead, it invited weather station staff, community representatives, and street designers to conduct a joint review. The review team walked along Qinghuai Road from the East Station entrance to North Alley, examining each temperature-monitoring location, the condition of the trees, and how residents were actually using the shade facilities. They found that the report's conclusion was not entirely without foundation: the light-colored roofs had reduced the amount of heat absorbed by the surfaces of some buildings, and the square no longer continued to radiate heat in the evening as it had in the past. However, the figure of two degrees could easily lead the public to believe that the entire neighborhood had experienced the same cooling effect at all times. In fact, the presence or absence of tree shade, whether air could circulate, and the orientation of buildings all produced noticeable differences. The review team therefore concluded that the original report had compressed complex spatial variations into a single number and stated its findings too definitively, making it unsuitable as a direct basis for a comprehensive rollout.

The conflict forced the Planning Bureau to choose between two competing pressures. On the one hand, residents expected the government to act quickly in response to increasingly unbearable summer heat. On the other hand, replicating the project without sufficient evidence could not only waste money but also impose designs unsuitable for narrow alleys on other communities. In the end, the Planning Bureau decided to retain the pilot project in the Qinghuai neighborhood but suspend the planned citywide rollout. The light-colored roofs and shade facilities in the square, which had already proved useful in practice, remained in use, while the canopy frames in North Alley that obstructed merchants' visibility were redesigned. The evaluators also revised their measurement methods: from then on, fixed temperature-monitoring points would be installed in different settings, including areas exposed to sunlight, shaded areas, intersections, and narrow alleys, while weather conditions would be recorded at the same time. All raw records and equipment locations would be made public to residents, and the community could also elect representatives to take part in on-site inspections.

After autumn began, the Qinghuai neighborhood held a second briefing. Rather than announcing another eye-catching cooling figure, the Planning Bureau showed which locations had improved significantly, which areas remained stifling, and how it planned to make adjustments during the next phase. After seeing the revised plan for the canopy frames in North Alley, Zhao Ping agreed to cooperate with the construction work. Zhou Lan signed up for the community observation group to record the actual experiences of older people and children when using public spaces. The pilot ultimately did not become an urban achievement promoted in haste, but it did lead to a more cautious approach to decision-making. Hezhou subsequently stipulated that other neighborhoods applying for cooling renovations must first explain their local buildings, wind direction, and residents' needs rather than simply copying the Qinghuai neighborhood plan. The two-degree difference remained in the report, but it was no longer treated as the sole answer; instead, it was regarded as the starting point for asking questions. The success or failure of urban cooling must be judged not only by the thermometer but also by whether the measures genuinely improve the daily lives of different groups of people.

grammar.explanation: 表示转折关系，先承认一种情况，再说明与之相对或更重要的情况。
grammar.example: 新增树木虽然还未长成浓荫，但遮阳棚已经使她每天接孩子放学时轻松了许多。

grammar.explanation: 表示条件关系，前一分句提出假设条件，后一分句说明在该条件下产生的结果。
grammar.example: 如果天气条件不同，所谓下降两度就不能全部归因于工程。

grammar.explanation: 表示递进关系，后一项在前一项的基础上进一步说明更严重或更深入的结果。
grammar.example: 另一方面，如果依据不充分就复制工程，不仅可能浪费资金，还可能把不适合窄巷的设计强加给其他社区。

questions.prompt: 退休物理教师为什么认为“下降两度”不能完全证明工程的降温效果？
options: 改造前后测量时的天气条件不同
测温设备全部设置在北巷
浅色屋顶增加了建筑对热量的吸收
居民拒绝参加现场核查
questions.explanation: 改造前的数据来自连续晴热天气，而改造后的测量包含阴天，因此温度变化可能部分来自天气差异，不能全部归因于改造工程。
questions.evidence: 如果天气条件不同，所谓下降两度就不能全部归因于工程。

questions.prompt: 规划局为什么暂停原定的全城推广？
options: 市民已经不再关心夏季高温
依据不充分时复制工程可能浪费资金并造成设计不适配
青槐街区的全部降温设施都没有作用
气象站拒绝参与后续测量工作
questions.explanation: 规划局认识到原报告的依据不够充分，直接复制工程既有资金浪费的风险，也可能把不适合窄巷的设计用于其他社区。
questions.evidence: 另一方面，如果依据不充分就复制工程，不仅可能浪费资金，还可能把不适合窄巷的设计强加给其他社区。

questions.prompt: 文章结尾如何评价报告中保留的“两度之差”？
options: 它是全面推广工程的充分依据
它应当从报告中彻底删除
它不再是唯一答案，而是进一步调查和思考的起点
它证明所有地点和时段都具有相同的降温效果
questions.explanation: 复核后，规划局没有否定这个数字，但也不再把它视为能够解释整个街区降温效果的唯一结论，而是用它引出对空间差异和居民需求的进一步研究。
questions.evidence: 两度之差仍被保留在报告中，但它不再被当成唯一答案，而被视为提出问题的起点。

articles.title: 百分之九十三之后：河湾区暂缓推广小微贷款试点
articles.summary: 河湾区评估组在审查小微贷款试点时发现，百分之九十三的按时还款率掩盖了借款人周转困难、经营改善有限和风险集中等问题。区政府因此决定暂缓全面推广，调整考核方式并完善贷后支持，最终使贷款项目从追求规模转向改善经营质量。
articles.topic: 百分之九十三之后：河湾区暂缓推广小微贷款试点
paragraphs: 初冬，临江市河湾区政府准备审议一项小微贷款试点。试点由区里的融资服务中心与三家银行共同实施，主要面向旧城商业街和城北农产品市场的个体经营者。贷款不要求借款人提供房产抵押，审批时间也比普通经营贷款短。项目运行一年后，承办机构提交了一份颇为乐观的报告，其中最醒目的结论是：借款人的按时还款率达到百分之九十三。部分负责人认为，这说明风险处于可控范围，应当尽快把试点扩大到全区，并把贷款额度进一步提高。然而，负责独立评估的周岚没有在意见书上签字。她认为，还款率只能说明钱是否按期回到银行账户，不能直接证明借款人的经营状况已经改善。

周岚带领评估组重新核对贷款台账、店铺流水和贷后走访记录。他们很快发现，表面整齐的数据背后存在几个容易被忽略的问题。有些商户为了避免逾期，在还款日前向亲友借钱；有些人使用信用卡或网络借款临时填补缺口；还有人压低进货量、推迟支付供货款，以便优先偿还银行贷款。这些做法没有造成账面逾期，却把压力转移到了家庭和上下游商户身上。一家经营早餐铺的夫妇按时还清了每一期贷款，但他们在原材料涨价后不敢更新设备，也没有资金支付临时工工资。若只看银行记录，他们属于表现良好的客户；若观察店铺经营，就会发现其现金流已经十分脆弱。

争议在评审会上集中爆发。银行代表指出，贷款项目首先必须保证资金安全，按时还款率是最直接、最可靠的指标。融资服务中心则担心，一旦暂缓推广，前期投入会被质疑，合作银行也可能降低参与意愿。周岚并不否认还款率的重要性，但她提出，试点的公共目标不是单纯增加贷款，而是帮助缺乏抵押物的小商户获得稳定的经营机会。如果借款人依靠新的高息债务偿还低息贷款，风险只是被延后；如果贷款主要用于填补旧账，而非采购、改造或扩大服务，项目也很难形成持续收益。双方真正的分歧，不在于数据是否准确，而在于应当如何解释这项数据。

为了避免讨论停留在立场上，评估组走进城北农产品市场，与借款人、供货商和市场管理人员分别交谈。他们发现，贷款效果与经营周期密切相关。经营干货的商户能够提前备货，节日期间收入有所增加；销售鲜果的摊主却容易受到天气、运输和损耗影响，每月固定还款给他们造成了更大压力。此外，原方案要求客户在较短时间内开始偿还本金，没有给设备改造和客源积累留下缓冲期。更值得警惕的是，负责推荐客户的机构同时承担规模考核。为了完成放款任务，工作人员更愿意选择已经拥有稳定收入的商户，而真正缺少融资渠道、经营能力尚待提升的人反而较难进入试点。

在最终审议中，周岚建议区政府暂缓全面推广，但保留现有项目，并用六个月完成调整。新的方案取消单纯以放款规模和按时还款率评价承办机构的做法，增加资金用途、经营现金流、续借依赖和家庭负担等观察内容。对季节性明显的行业，银行可以根据实际收入安排还款节奏；对首次经营者，融资服务中心则提供记账、采购和合同咨询。区政府还要求推荐、审批与贷后评估相互分离，避免同一机构既追求客户数量，又负责证明项目成功。这个决定没有满足急于扩张的一方，也没有因为发现问题而终止试点，而是把推广建立在风险能够被识别和纠正的基础上。

调整实施后，最明显的变化并不是贷款数量迅速增加，而是各方开始讨论过去被还款率遮住的问题。银行在回访时不再只询问是否能够按期转账，也会了解库存、应收款和其他债务；商户遇到短期困难时，可以提前说明经营周期，而不必首先寻找新的借款。半年后的复审会上，区政府决定只在经营辅导较完善的两个街道扩大项目，并继续观察其他区域。周岚在结论中写道，百分之九十三不是一个应被否定的成绩，却也不是全面推广的充分理由。负责任的评估既要承认已经取得的成效，也要追问成本由谁承担、风险被转移到哪里，以及政策是否真正改善了目标群体的处境。
pinyin: chū dōng ， lín jiāng shì hé wān qū zhèng fǔ zhǔn bèi shěn yì yī xiàng xiǎo wēi dài kuǎn shì diǎn 。 shì diǎn yóu qū lǐ de róng zī fú wù zhōng xīn yǔ sān jiā yín háng gòng tóng shí shī ， zhǔ yào miàn xiàng jiù chéng shāng yè jiē hé chéng běi nóng chǎn pǐn shì chǎng de gè tǐ jīng yíng zhě 。 dài kuǎn bú yào qiú jiè kuǎn rén tí gōng fáng chǎn dǐ yā ， shěn pī shí jiān yě bǐ pǔ tōng jīng yíng dài kuǎn duǎn 。 xiàng mù yùn xíng yī nián hòu ， chéng bàn jī gòu tí jiāo le yī fèn pǒ wèi lè guān de bào gào ， qí zhōng zuì xǐng mù dì jié lùn shì ： jiè kuǎn rén de àn shí hái kuǎn lǜ dá dào bǎi fēn zhī jiǔ shí sān 。 bù fèn fù zé rén rèn wéi ， zhè shuō míng fēng xiǎn chǔ yú kě kòng fàn wéi ， yīng dāng jǐn kuài bǎ shì diǎn kuò dà dào quán qū ， bìng bǎ dài kuǎn é dù jìn yí bù tí gāo 。 rán ér ， fù zé dú lì píng gū de zhōu lán méi yǒu zài yì jiàn shū shàng qiān zì 。 tā rèn wéi ， hái kuǎn lǜ zhǐ néng shuō míng qián shì fǒu àn qī huí dào yín háng zhàng hù ， bù néng zhí jiē zhèng míng jiè kuǎn rén de jīng yíng zhuàng kuàng yǐ jīng gǎi shàn 。

zhōu lán dài lǐng píng gū zǔ chóng xīn hé duì dài kuǎn tái zhàng 、 diàn pù liú shuǐ hé dài hòu zǒu fǎng jì lù 。 tā men hěn kuài fā xiàn ， biǎo miàn zhěng qí de shù jù bèi hòu cún zài jǐ gè róng yì bèi hū lüè de wèn tí 。 yǒu xiē shāng hù wèi le bì miǎn yú qī ， zài hái kuǎn rì qián xiàng qīn yǒu jiè qián ； yǒu xiē rén shǐ yòng xìn yòng kǎ huò wǎng luò jiè kuǎn lín shí tián bǔ quē kǒu ； hái yǒu rén yā dī jìn huò liàng 、 tuī chí zhī fù gōng huò kuǎn ， yǐ biàn yōu xiān cháng huán yín háng dài kuǎn 。 zhè xiē zuò fǎ méi yǒu zào chéng zhàng miàn yú qī ， què bǎ yā lì zhuǎn yí dào le jiā tíng hé shàng xià yóu shāng hù shēn shàng 。 yī jiā jīng yíng zǎo cān pù de fū fù àn shí huán qīng le měi yī qī dài kuǎn ， dàn tā men zài yuán cái liào zhǎng jià hòu bù gǎn gēng xīn shè bèi ， yě méi yǒu zī jīn zhī fù lín shí gōng gōng zī 。 ruò zhǐ kàn yín háng jì lù ， tā men shǔ yú biǎo xiàn liáng hǎo de kè hù ； ruò guān chá diàn pù jīng yíng ， jiù huì fā xiàn qí xiàn jīn liú yǐ jīng shí fēn cuì ruò 。

zhēng yì zài píng shěn huì shàng jí zhōng bào fā 。 yín háng dài biǎo zhǐ chū ， dài kuǎn xiàng mù shǒu xiān bì xū bǎo zhèng zī jīn ān quán ， àn shí hái kuǎn lǜ shì zuì zhí jiē 、 zuì kě kào de zhǐ biāo 。 róng zī fú wù zhōng xīn zé dān xīn ， yí dàn zàn huǎn tuī guǎng ， qián qī tóu rù huì bèi zhì yí ， hé zuò yín háng yě kě néng jiàng dī cān yù yì yuàn 。 zhōu lán bìng bù fǒu rèn hái kuǎn lǜ de zhòng yào xìng ， dàn tā tí chū ， shì diǎn de gōng gòng mù biāo bú shì dān chún zēng jiā dài kuǎn ， ér shì bāng zhù quē fá dǐ yā wù de xiǎo shāng hù huò dé wěn dìng de jīng yíng jī huì 。 rú guǒ jiè kuǎn rén yī kào xīn de gāo xī zhài wù cháng huán dī xī dài kuǎn ， fēng xiǎn zhǐ shì bèi yán hòu ； rú guǒ dài kuǎn zhǔ yào yòng yú tián bǔ jiù zhàng ， ér fēi cǎi gòu 、 gǎi zào huò kuò dà fú wù ， xiàng mù yě hěn nán xíng chéng chí xù shōu yì 。 shuāng fāng zhēn zhèng de fēn qí ， bù zài yú shù jù shì fǒu zhǔn què ， ér zài yú yīng dāng rú hé jiě shì zhè xiàng shù jù 。

wèi le bì miǎn tǎo lùn tíng liú zài lì chǎng shàng ， píng gū zǔ zǒu jìn chéng běi nóng chǎn pǐn shì chǎng ， yǔ jiè kuǎn rén 、 gōng huò shāng hé shì chǎng guǎn lǐ rén yuán fēn bié jiāo tán 。 tā men fā xiàn ， dài kuǎn xiào guǒ yǔ jīng yíng zhōu qī mì qiè xiāng guān 。 jīng yíng gān huò de shāng hù néng gòu tí qián bèi huò ， jié rì qī jiān shōu rù yǒu suǒ zēng jiā ； xiāo shòu xiān guǒ de tān zhǔ què róng yì shòu dào tiān qì 、 yùn shū hé sǔn hào yǐng xiǎng ， měi yuè gù dìng hái kuǎn gěi tā men zào chéng le gèng dà yā lì 。 cǐ wài ， yuán fāng àn yāo qiú kè hù zài jiào duǎn shí jiān nèi kāi shǐ cháng huán běn jīn ， méi yǒu gěi shè bèi gǎi zào hé kè yuán jī lěi liú xià huǎn chōng qī 。 gèng zhí de jǐng tì de shì ， fù zé tuī jiàn kè hù de jī gòu tóng shí chéng dān guī mó kǎo hé 。 wèi le wán chéng fàng kuǎn rèn wù ， gōng zuò rén yuán gèng yuàn yì xuǎn zé yǐ jīng yōng yǒu wěn dìng shōu rù de shāng hù ， ér zhēn zhèng quē shǎo róng zī qú dào 、 jīng yíng néng lì shàng dài tí shēng de rén fǎn ér jiào nán jìn rù shì diǎn 。

zài zuì zhōng shěn yì zhōng ， zhōu lán jiàn yì qū zhèng fǔ zàn huǎn quán miàn tuī guǎng ， dàn bǎo liú xiàn yǒu xiàng mù ， bìng yòng liù gè yuè wán chéng tiáo zhěng 。 xīn de fāng àn qǔ xiāo dān chún yǐ fàng kuǎn guī mó hé àn shí hái kuǎn lǜ píng jià chéng bàn jī gòu de zuò fǎ ， zēng jiā zī jīn yòng tú 、 jīng yíng xiàn jīn liú 、 xù jiè yī lài hé jiā tíng fù dān děng guān chá nèi róng 。 duì jì jié xìng míng xiǎn de háng yè ， yín háng kě yǐ gēn jù shí jì shōu rù ān pái hái kuǎn jié zòu ； duì shǒu cì jīng yíng zhě ， róng zī fú wù zhōng xīn zé tí gōng jì zhàng 、 cǎi gòu hé hé tóng zī xún 。 qū zhèng fǔ hái yāo qiú tuī jiàn 、 shěn pī yǔ dài hòu píng gū xiāng hù fēn lí ， bì miǎn tóng yī jī gòu jì zhuī qiú kè hù shù liàng ， yòu fù zé zhèng míng xiàng mù chéng gōng 。 zhè ge jué dìng méi yǒu mǎn zú jí yú kuò zhāng de yī fāng ， yě méi yǒu yīn wèi fā xiàn wèn tí ér zhōng zhǐ shì diǎn ， ér shì bǎ tuī guǎng jiàn lì zài fēng xiǎn néng gòu bèi shí bié hé jiū zhèng de jī chǔ shàng 。

tiáo zhěng shí shī hòu ， zuì míng xiǎn de biàn huà bìng bú shì dài kuǎn shù liàng xùn sù zēng jiā ， ér shì gè fāng kāi shǐ tǎo lùn guò qù bèi hái kuǎn lǜ zhē zhù de wèn tí 。 yín háng zài huí fǎng shí bù zài zhǐ xún wèn shì fǒu néng gòu àn qī zhuǎn zhàng ， yě huì liǎo jiě kù cún 、 yīng shōu kuǎn hé qí tā zhài wù ； shāng hù yù dào duǎn qī kùn nán shí ， kě yǐ tí qián shuō míng jīng yíng zhōu qī ， ér bù bì shǒu xiān xún zhǎo xīn de jiè kuǎn 。 bàn nián hòu de fù shěn huì shàng ， qū zhèng fǔ jué dìng zhǐ zài jīng yíng fǔ dǎo jiào wán shàn de liǎng gè jiē dào kuò dà xiàng mù ， bìng jì xù guān chá qí tā qū yù 。 zhōu lán zài jié lùn zhōng xiě dào ， bǎi fēn zhī jiǔ shí sān bú shì yí gè yīng bèi fǒu dìng de chéng jì ， què yě bú shì quán miàn tuī guǎng de chōng fèn lǐ yóu 。 fù zé rèn de píng gū jì yào chéng rèn yǐ jīng qǔ dé de chéng xiào ， yě yào zhuī wèn chéng běn yóu shuí chéng dān 、 fēng xiǎn bèi zhuǎn yí dào nǎ lǐ ， yǐ jí zhèng cè shì fǒu zhēn zhèng gǎi shàn le mù biāo qún tǐ de chǔ jìng 。
translation: In early winter, the government of Hewan District in Lingjiang City was preparing to review a microloan pilot program. The pilot was jointly implemented by the district's financing service center and three banks, primarily serving self-employed business owners in the old city's commercial street and the agricultural produce market in the north of the city. Borrowers were not required to provide real estate as collateral, and the approval process was shorter than that for ordinary business loans. After the program had been operating for a year, the implementing organizations submitted a highly optimistic report. Its most striking conclusion was that 93 percent of borrowers had made their repayments on time. Some officials believed that this showed the risks were under control and that the pilot should be expanded across the district as soon as possible, with the loan limits raised further. However, Zhou Lan, who was responsible for the independent evaluation, did not sign the assessment. In her view, the repayment rate showed only whether money had been returned to the banks' accounts on schedule; it did not directly prove that the borrowers' business conditions had improved.

Zhou Lan led the evaluation team in rechecking the loan ledgers, store transaction records, and post-loan follow-up records. They soon discovered several easily overlooked problems behind the apparently orderly data. Some merchants borrowed money from relatives and friends before repayment dates to avoid falling overdue. Some used credit cards or online loans to cover temporary shortfalls. Others reduced their purchases of inventory or delayed paying suppliers so that they could give priority to repaying their bank loans. These practices did not result in recorded delinquencies, but they shifted the pressure onto families and businesses elsewhere in the supply chain. A couple who ran a breakfast shop repaid every loan installment on time, but after the prices of raw materials rose, they did not dare replace their equipment and lacked the funds to pay temporary workers. Judging only from the bank's records, they were customers with a good repayment record; an examination of the shop's operations, however, revealed that its cash flow had already become extremely fragile.

The dispute came to a head at the review meeting. Bank representatives pointed out that a lending program must first ensure the safety of its funds and that the on-time repayment rate was the most direct and reliable indicator. The financing service center, meanwhile, worried that if the expansion were postponed, its earlier investment would be called into question and the partner banks might become less willing to participate. Zhou Lan did not deny the importance of the repayment rate, but she argued that the pilot's public objective was not simply to increase lending. It was to help small merchants who lacked collateral gain stable business opportunities. If borrowers relied on new, high-interest debt to repay low-interest loans, the risk was merely being deferred. If the loans were used mainly to cover old debts rather than for purchasing goods, making improvements, or expanding services, the program would also struggle to generate sustainable returns. The real disagreement between the two sides was not over whether the data was accurate, but over how it should be interpreted.

To prevent the discussion from remaining a clash of positions, the evaluation team visited the agricultural produce market in the north of the city and spoke separately with borrowers, suppliers, and market managers. They found that the effects of the loans were closely related to business cycles. Merchants selling dried goods were able to stock up in advance and saw their income increase during holiday periods. Vendors selling fresh fruit, however, were vulnerable to weather, transportation problems, and spoilage, and fixed monthly repayments placed greater pressure on them. In addition, the original plan required customers to begin repaying the principal within a relatively short period, leaving no buffer for equipment upgrades or the development of a customer base. More concerning still, the organizations responsible for recommending customers were also assessed on the scale of lending. To meet their lending targets, staff members preferred to select merchants who already had stable incomes, while those who genuinely lacked access to financing and still needed to improve their business capabilities found it harder to enter the pilot.

During the final review, Zhou Lan recommended that the district government postpone a district-wide expansion while retaining the existing program and spending six months making adjustments. The new plan abandoned the practice of evaluating implementing organizations solely on the amount lent and the on-time repayment rate. It added indicators covering the use of funds, operating cash flow, dependence on loan renewals, and the burden on borrowers' families. For industries with pronounced seasonal patterns, banks could arrange repayment schedules based on actual income. For first-time business owners, the financing service center would provide advice on bookkeeping, purchasing, and contracts. The district government also required the functions of recommendation, approval, and post-loan evaluation to be kept separate, preventing the same organization from both pursuing higher customer numbers and bearing responsibility for demonstrating the program's success. The decision neither satisfied those eager to expand nor terminated the pilot simply because problems had been discovered. Instead, it made expansion contingent on risks being identifiable and correctable.

After the adjustments were implemented, the most conspicuous change was not a rapid increase in the number of loans, but that the parties began discussing problems previously obscured by the repayment rate. During follow-up visits, banks no longer asked only whether borrowers could transfer payments on schedule; they also looked into inventory, accounts receivable, and other debts. When merchants encountered short-term difficulties, they could explain their business cycles in advance instead of having to seek new loans first. At a review meeting six months later, the district government decided to expand the program only in two subdistricts with relatively well-developed business advisory services and to continue monitoring the other areas. In her conclusion, Zhou Lan wrote that 93 percent was not an achievement that should be dismissed, but neither was it sufficient justification for a comprehensive expansion. A responsible evaluation must acknowledge the results already achieved while also asking who bears the costs, where the risks have been shifted, and whether the policy has genuinely improved the circumstances of the group it was intended to serve.

vocabulary.meaning: 对重要事项进行讨论、审查并作出决定。

补足资金、数量等方面的不足。
一定时期内资金流入和流出的情况。
暂时推迟将某个项目扩大实施。
需要支付较高利息的债务。
经营活动从投入到获得收入所经历的周期。

依靠不断获得新借款来维持经营或偿还旧债的状态。
彼此独立，不由同一个主体同时负责。
某项政策或项目主要希望帮助和影响的人群。

grammar.explanation: 用两个并列的假设复句分别说明不同条件及其结果，常用于分析多种风险或可能性。
grammar.example: 如果借款人依靠新的高息债务偿还低息贷款，风险只是被延后；如果贷款主要用于填补旧账，而非采购、改造或扩大服务，项目也很难形成持续收益。

grammar.explanation: 表示同一主体同时具有两种行为、状态或职责，本文用于说明利益冲突。
grammar.example: 区政府还要求推荐、审批与贷后评估相互分离，避免同一机构既追求客户数量，又负责证明项目成功。

grammar.explanation: 先排除并非关键的方面，再指出真正的重点或原因。
grammar.example: 双方真正的分歧，不在于数据是否准确，而在于应当如何解释这项数据。

articles.title: 江湾校区心理咨询预约试点：效率提升之后，如何守住公平与专业边界
articles.summary: 东江大学江湾校区评估心理咨询预约试点时发现，首次等待时间缩短了百分之二十五，但热门时段集中、紧急需求识别不足等问题也随之显现。校方最终决定保留预约平台，同时通过分类接待、人工复核和动态排班完善服务。
articles.topic: 江湾校区心理咨询预约试点：效率提升之后，如何守住公平与专业边界
paragraphs: 春季学期开学后，东江大学在江湾校区学生发展中心启动了心理咨询预约试点。过去，学生通常要先到办公室登记，再等待工作人员电话联系，不仅程序烦琐，而且难以了解自己的排队进度。新平台允许学生选择咨询时段、填写基本诉求，并在预约成功后收到提醒。试点运行一个月后，现有结果显示，学生从提出申请到接受首次咨询的等待时间缩短了百分之二十五。这个变化令校方看到了数字化服务的价值，也促使学生事务委员会提前召开评估会，讨论平台能否在全校推广。

然而，等待时间缩短并不意味着所有问题都已解决。平台采用先到先得的方式开放号源，每周一上午更新下一周的预约时段。消息灵通、课程安排灵活的学生往往能迅速完成预约，而需要上课、实习或不习惯使用手机的学生则容易错过。晚间时段尤其紧张，一些学生连续几次没有约到，只能选择放弃。此外，为了保护隐私，申请表没有要求学生详细描述处境，这虽然减轻了填写压力，却使咨询中心难以及时区分一般情绪困扰与可能危及安全的紧急情况。效率上的进步，反而暴露了公平和风险识别方面的缺口。

评估会上，平台负责人主张尽快扩大试点范围。他认为，线上预约减少了重复登记，也让咨询师能够提前安排工作。几名院系辅导员却表示反对：若仅根据平均等待时间判断成效，那些始终没有成功进入系统的人就会被排除在评估之外。咨询师代表还提醒，与普通场地预订不同，心理服务不能把“填表最快”视为最合理的分配原则。学生代表则提出另一个矛盾：申请表若过于简单，工作人员无法判断轻重缓急；若询问过细，学生可能因为担心隐私泄露而不敢求助。各方争论的核心，已不再是平台是否方便，而是学校应当怎样在便利、隐私、公平与安全之间作出取舍。

委员会没有立即表决，而是到学生发展中心查看实际流程。工作人员演示后发现，平台虽然设置了“情况紧急”选项，却没有说明什么情形属于紧急，也没有明确告知学生：若本人或他人面临即时危险，不应等待普通预约，而应直接联系校医院、值班辅导员或当地急救机构。与此同时，取消预约的名额只能在下一轮统一释放，咨询师临时出现空闲时，也无法通知正在等待的学生。这些问题并非技术故障，而是流程设计没有充分反映心理咨询的特殊性。委员会因此认为，单纯增加号源或优化页面，都不足以消除现有冲突。

经过讨论，学校决定保留试点，但暂不直接复制到其他校区。新的安排把需求分为普通咨询、优先评估和即时危机三类。普通咨询仍可自主选择时段；选择优先评估的学生只需简要说明当前影响，不必提交完整经历，之后由受过训练的工作人员进行人工复核；涉及即时危险的情况，则由页面清楚引导至紧急支持渠道。学校还决定保留电话和现场登记窗口，为使用数字工具不便的学生提供同等入口。对于晚间等热门时段，平台不再一次性放出全部名额，而是分批开放，并建立候补通知机制，以降低时间安排不同所造成的不公平。

两周后，学生事务委员会再次检查试点，没有急于用单一数字宣布成功，而是逐项查看预约是否顺畅、紧急情况能否及时转接、未约到的学生是否仍有求助渠道。委员会最终确认，新平台可以继续运行，但每月必须由咨询师、辅导员和学生代表共同审查流程，任何扩展计划都要先解决发现的问题。此次评估说明，首次等待时间缩短百分之二十五是一项明确成果，却只能回答“服务是否更快”，不能独自回答“服务是否更好”。校园心理咨询面对的是处境各异的个人，真正可靠的制度既要提高效率，也要确保最需要帮助的人不会被速度和技术挡在门外。
pinyin: chūn jì xué qī kāi xué hòu ， dōng jiāng dà xué zài jiāng wān xiào qū xué shēng fà zhǎn zhōng xīn qǐ dòng le xīn lǐ zī xún yù yuē shì diǎn 。 guò qù ， xué shēng tōng cháng yào xiān dào bàn gōng shì dēng jì ， zài děng dài gōng zuò rén yuán diàn huà lián xì ， bù jǐn chéng xù fán suǒ ， ér qiě nán yǐ liǎo jiě zì jǐ de pái duì jìn dù 。 xīn píng tái yǔn xǔ xué shēng xuǎn zé zī xún shí duàn 、 tián xiě jī běn sù qiú ， bìng zài yù yuē chéng gōng hòu shōu dào tí xǐng 。 shì diǎn yùn xíng yí gè yuè hòu ， xiàn yǒu jié guǒ xiǎn shì ， xué shēng cóng tí chū shēn qǐng dào jiē shòu shǒu cì zī xún de děng dài shí jiān suō duǎn le bǎi fēn zhī èr shí wǔ 。 zhè ge biàn huà lìng xiào fāng kàn dào le shù zì huà fú wù de jià zhí ， yě cù shǐ xué shēng shì wù wěi yuán huì tí qián zhào kāi píng gū huì ， tǎo lùn píng tái néng fǒu zài quán xiào tuī guǎng 。

rán ér ， děng dài shí jiān suō duǎn bìng bù yì wèi zhe suǒ yǒu wèn tí dōu yǐ jiě jué 。 píng tái cǎi yòng xiān dào xiān dé de fāng shì kāi fàng hào yuán ， měi zhōu yī shàng wǔ gēng xīn xià yī zhōu de yù yuē shí duàn 。 xiāo xī líng tōng 、 kè chéng ān pái líng huó de xué shēng wǎng wǎng néng xùn sù wán chéng yù yuē ， ér xū yào shàng kè 、 shí xí huò bù xí guàn shǐ yòng shǒu jī de xué shēng zé róng yì cuò guò 。 wǎn jiān shí duàn yóu qí jǐn zhāng ， yī xiē xué shēng lián xù jǐ cì méi yǒu yuē dào ， zhǐ néng xuǎn zé fàng qì 。 cǐ wài ， wèi le bǎo hù yǐn sī ， shēn qǐng biǎo méi yǒu yāo qiú xué shēng xiáng xì miáo shù chǔ jìng ， zhè suī rán jiǎn qīng le tián xiě yā lì ， què shǐ zī xún zhōng xīn nán yǐ jí shí qū fēn yì bān qíng xù kùn rǎo yǔ kě néng wēi jí ān quán de jǐn jí qíng kuàng 。 xiào lǜ shàng de jìn bù ， fǎn ér bào lù le gōng píng hé fēng xiǎn shí bié fāng miàn de quē kǒu 。

píng gū huì shàng ， píng tái fù zé rén zhǔ zhāng jǐn kuài kuò dà shì diǎn fàn wéi 。 tā rèn wéi ， xiàn shàng yù yuē jiǎn shǎo le chóng fù dēng jì ， yě ràng zī xún shī néng gòu tí qián ān pái gōng zuò 。 jǐ míng yuàn xì fǔ dǎo yuán què biǎo shì fǎn duì ： ruò jǐn gēn jù píng jūn děng dài shí jiān pàn duàn chéng xiào ， nà xiē shǐ zhōng méi yǒu chéng gōng jìn rù xì tǒng de rén jiù huì bèi pái chú zài píng gū zhī wài 。 zī xún shī dài biǎo hái tí xǐng ， yǔ pǔ tōng chǎng dì yù dìng bù tóng ， xīn lǐ fú wù bù néng bǎ “ tián biǎo zuì kuài ” shì wèi zuì hé lǐ de fēn pèi yuán zé 。 xué shēng dài biǎo zé tí chū lìng yí gè máo dùn ： shēn qǐng biǎo ruò guò yú jiǎn dān ， gōng zuò rén yuán wú fǎ pàn duàn qīng zhòng huǎn jí ； ruò xún wèn guò xì ， xué shēng kě néng yīn wèi dān xīn yǐn sī xiè lòu ér bù gǎn qiú zhù 。 gè fāng zhēng lùn de hé xīn ， yǐ bù zài shì píng tái shì fǒu fāng biàn ， ér shì xué xiào yīng dāng zěn yàng zài biàn lì 、 yǐn sī 、 gōng píng yǔ ān quán zhī jiàn zuò chū qǔ shě 。

wěi yuán huì méi yǒu lì jí biǎo jué ， ér shì dào xué shēng fà zhǎn zhōng xīn chá kàn shí jì liú chéng 。 gōng zuò rén yuán yǎn shì hòu fā xiàn ， píng tái suī rán shè zhì le “ qíng kuàng jǐn jí ” xuǎn xiàng ， què méi yǒu shuō míng shén me qíng xíng shǔ yú jǐn jí ， yě méi yǒu míng què gào zhī xué shēng ： ruò běn rén huò tā rén miàn lín jí shí wēi xiǎn ， bù yīng děng dài pǔ tōng yù yuē ， ér yīng zhí jiē lián xì xiào yī yuàn 、 zhí bān fǔ dǎo yuán huò dāng dì jí jiù jī gòu 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， qǔ xiāo yù yuē de míng é zhǐ néng zài xià yī lún tǒng yī shì fàng ， zī xún shī lín shí chū xiàn kòng xián shí ， yě wú fǎ tōng zhī zhèng zài děng dài de xué shēng 。 zhè xiē wèn tí bìng fēi jì shù gù zhàng ， ér shì liú chéng shè jì méi yǒu chōng fèn fǎn yìng xīn lǐ zī xún de tè shū xìng 。 wěi yuán huì yīn cǐ rèn wéi ， dān chún zēng jiā hào yuán huò yōu huà yè miàn ， dōu bù zú yǐ xiāo chú xiàn yǒu chōng tū 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， xué xiào jué dìng bǎo liú shì diǎn ， dàn zàn bù zhí jiē fù zhì dào qí tā xiào qū 。 xīn de ān pái bǎ xū qiú fēn wéi pǔ tōng zī xún 、 yōu xiān píng gū hé jí shí wēi jī sān lèi 。 pǔ tōng zī xún réng kě zì zhǔ xuǎn zé shí duàn ； xuǎn zé yōu xiān píng gū de xué shēng zhǐ xū jiǎn yào shuō míng dāng qián yǐng xiǎng ， bù bì tí jiāo wán zhěng jīng lì ， zhī hòu yóu shòu guò xùn liàn de gōng zuò rén yuán jìn xíng rén gōng fù hé ； shè jí jí shí wēi xiǎn de qíng kuàng ， zé yóu yè miàn qīng chǔ yǐn dǎo zhì jǐn jí zhī chí qú dào 。 xué xiào hái jué dìng bǎo liú diàn huà hé xiàn chǎng dēng jì chuāng kǒu ， wèi shǐ yòng shù zì gōng jù bù biàn de xué shēng tí gōng tóng děng rù kǒu 。 duì yú wǎn jiān děng rè mén shí duàn ， píng tái bù zài yí cì xìng fàng chū quán bù míng é ， ér shì fēn pī kāi fàng ， bìng jiàn lì hòu bǔ tōng zhī jī zhì ， yǐ jiàng dī shí jiān ān pái bù tóng suǒ zào chéng de bù gōng píng 。

liǎng zhōu hòu ， xué shēng shì wù wěi yuán huì zài cì jiǎn chá shì diǎn ， méi yǒu jí yú yòng dān yī shù zì xuān bù chéng gōng ， ér shì zhú xiàng chá kàn yù yuē shì fǒu shùn chàng 、 jǐn jí qíng kuàng néng fǒu jí shí zhuǎn jiē 、 wèi yuē dào de xué shēng shì fǒu réng yǒu qiú zhù qú dào 。 wěi yuán huì zuì zhōng què rèn ， xīn píng tái kě yǐ jì xù yùn xíng ， dàn měi yuè bì xū yóu zī xún shī 、 fǔ dǎo yuán hé xué shēng dài biǎo gòng tóng shěn chá liú chéng ， rèn hé kuò zhǎn jì huà dōu yào xiān jiě jué fā xiàn de wèn tí 。 cǐ cì píng gū shuō míng ， shǒu cì děng dài shí jiān suō duǎn bǎi fēn zhī èr shí wǔ shì yī xiàng míng què chéng guǒ ， què zhǐ néng huí dá “ fú wù shì fǒu gèng kuài ”， bù néng dú zì huí dá “ fú wù shì fǒu gèng hǎo ”。 xiào yuán xīn lǐ zī xún miàn duì de shì chǔ jìng gè yì de gè rén ， zhēn zhèng kě kào de zhì dù jì yào tí gāo xiào lǜ ， yě yào què bǎo zuì xū yào bāng zhù de rén bú huì bèi sù dù hé jì shù dǎng zài mén wài 。
translation: After the spring semester began, Dongjiang University launched a pilot appointment system for psychological counseling at the Student Development Center on its Jiangwan Campus. Previously, students generally had to register at the office first and then wait for staff to contact them by phone. The process was cumbersome, and students also found it difficult to track their progress in the queue. The new platform allows students to select a counseling time slot, provide basic information about what they need help with, and receive a reminder once their appointment has been confirmed. After one month of operation, the results so far show that the time students wait between submitting a request and receiving their first counseling session has decreased by 25 percent. This change demonstrated the value of digital services to the university and prompted the Student Affairs Committee to hold an evaluation meeting ahead of schedule to discuss whether the platform could be introduced across the university.

However, the shorter waiting time does not mean that every problem has been resolved. The platform makes appointments available on a first-come, first-served basis, updating the time slots for the following week every Monday morning. Students who are well informed and have flexible class schedules can often book appointments quickly, while those who must attend classes or internships, or who are not accustomed to using mobile phones, are more likely to miss out. Evening slots are particularly scarce, and some students have failed to secure an appointment several times in a row and ultimately had to give up. In addition, to protect privacy, the application form does not require students to describe their circumstances in detail. Although this reduces the burden of completing the form, it makes it difficult for the counseling center to promptly distinguish ordinary emotional distress from emergencies that may pose a safety risk. The improvement in efficiency has instead exposed gaps in fairness and risk identification.

At the evaluation meeting, the head of the platform argued that the pilot should be expanded as soon as possible. In his view, online appointments reduce duplicate registration and also allow counselors to plan their work in advance. Several departmental student advisers, however, objected. They argued that if effectiveness were judged solely by the average waiting time, those who had never successfully gained access to the system would be excluded from the evaluation. The counselors' representative also pointed out that, unlike ordinary venue reservations, psychological services cannot treat being the fastest to complete a form as the most reasonable principle for allocating appointments. The student representative raised another dilemma: if the application form is too simple, staff cannot assess the urgency or severity of each case; if it asks for too much detail, students may be deterred from seeking help because they fear that their privacy could be compromised. The central issue in the debate was no longer whether the platform was convenient, but how the university should balance convenience, privacy, fairness, and safety.

Rather than voting immediately, the committee visited the Student Development Center to observe the actual process. During a staff demonstration, the committee found that although the platform included an option labeled “urgent situation,” it did not explain what kinds of situations qualified as urgent. Nor did it clearly inform students that if they or someone else faced immediate danger, they should not wait for a regular appointment but should contact the university hospital, the student adviser on duty, or local emergency services directly. At the same time, slots freed by cancellations could only be released together in the next round, and when counselors unexpectedly became available, the system could not notify students on the waiting list. These were not technical failures; rather, the process had not been designed to adequately reflect the distinctive nature of psychological counseling. The committee therefore concluded that neither simply adding more appointment slots nor improving the interface would be enough to eliminate the existing conflicts.

After discussion, the university decided to retain the pilot but not to replicate it immediately on other campuses. Under the new arrangement, needs are divided into three categories: regular counseling, priority assessment, and immediate crisis. Students seeking regular counseling may still select their own time slots. Those choosing priority assessment need only briefly describe how they are currently being affected, without submitting a full account of their experiences, after which trained staff members conduct a manual review. Cases involving immediate danger are clearly directed by the webpage to emergency support channels. The university also decided to retain telephone and in-person registration, providing equivalent means of access for students who have difficulty using digital tools. For popular periods such as evening hours, the platform no longer releases all slots at once. Instead, it makes them available in batches and uses a waitlist notification system to reduce unfairness caused by differences in students' schedules.

Two weeks later, the Student Affairs Committee reviewed the pilot again. Rather than rushing to declare success on the basis of a single figure, it examined item by item whether appointments could be made smoothly, whether emergencies could be referred promptly, and whether students unable to secure appointments still had channels through which to seek help. The committee ultimately confirmed that the new platform could continue operating, but required counselors, student advisers, and student representatives to review the process jointly every month, and stipulated that any expansion plan must first address the problems identified. This evaluation shows that the 25 percent reduction in the waiting time for a first counseling session is a clear achievement, but it answers only whether the service is faster, not whether the service is better. Campus psychological counseling serves individuals facing widely varying circumstances. A truly reliable system must not only improve efficiency but also ensure that those most in need of help are not shut out by speed and technology.

articles.title: 一份损耗率报告引发的冷链路线调整
articles.summary: 松岭县评估农村冷链配送试点时，发现生鲜损耗率下降百分之十四的结论掩盖了偏远村庄成本上升和服务不稳定的问题。评估组经过实地核查与公开协商，决定保留试点，但调整评价方法、配送路线和责任机制，使冷链服务更符合农村实际需求。
articles.topic: 一份损耗率报告引发的冷链路线调整
paragraphs: 九月初，松岭县农业服务中心召开农村冷链配送试点评估会。试点覆盖柳湾镇及附近村庄，县里的阶段性报告把“生鲜损耗率下降了百分之十四”列为主要进展，并建议扩大服务范围。报告显示，统一预冷、集中装车和全程记录温度后，蔬菜、水果在运输中的腐烂现象有所减少。负责项目的工作人员认为，这一变化足以证明试点方向正确。然而，参加会议的石桥村合作社负责人周远提出异议。他说，损耗虽然下降了，但配送车辆不再进入位置偏远的山村，村民必须把货物送到镇上的中转站。有些农户凌晨出发，经过盘山路才能赶上装车时间，增加的人工和短途运输成本并没有写进报告。

为核实双方说法，评估组没有立即通过扩建方案，而是沿着实际配送路线进行了一次完整调查。清晨五点，工作人员来到石桥村，看见农户把刚采摘的菌菇装进普通塑料筐，再用三轮车送往柳湾中转站。由于三轮车没有保温设备，菌菇在这一段路上仍可能受到挤压或高温影响，但企业的损耗统计只从货物进入冷藏车之后开始计算。中午，评估组又检查了镇上的冷库，发现库内温度记录完整，操作流程也符合要求。问题不在于企业伪造数据，而在于统计边界过窄：报告准确描述了冷藏运输环节，却没有呈现农户从田间到中转站的负担，也没有说明部分偏远村庄因订单较少而被取消上门服务。

冲突在第二次会议上变得更加明显。承运企业表示，冷藏车驶入山区后经常空载返程，狭窄道路还会增加安全风险。如果恢复每村上门，现有费用难以维持。合作社则认为，试点使用了公共资金，不能只选择货量大、道路好的村庄，否则最需要改善运输条件的农户反而会被排除。县财政部门担心继续补贴会形成长期依赖，主张先暂停山区线路。农业服务中心内部也有分歧：一部分人强调损耗率下降来之不易，不应因局部问题否定整个项目；另一部分人认为，若评价只关注进入冷藏车后的商品，就会把成本转移误认为效率提高。面对争议，评估组明确提出，百分之十四只能作为阶段性现象，不能单独用于判断试点是否成功。

经过讨论，松岭县决定保留试点，但不按原方案直接扩大。新的配送方式以柳湾中转站为中心，同时在石桥村旧粮站设置固定收集点，由合作社组织农户在规定时段交货，再由具备保温条件的小型车辆接驳至镇上。对于货量不足的村庄，不再要求冷藏车逐户行驶，而是允许相邻村庄合并订单。县里要求承运企业公开计费项目、车辆到达时间和温度异常记录；合作社负责登记货物离开农户后的交接情况，避免责任只落在某一方。更重要的是，后续评估不再只计算运输损耗，还要分别说明田间交货、中转等待、冷藏运输和末端签收各环节出现的问题。涉及农户额外承担的接驳费用，也必须在报告中单独列明，不能被笼统地归入生产成本。

调整实施后，石桥村合作社重新参加了集中配送。农户不必再各自前往镇上，承运企业也避免了大型冷藏车频繁进入狭窄山路。一次暴雨导致接驳车辆晚到，合作社根据交接记录及时通知中转站调整装车顺序，并将延误原因写入公开台账。过去遇到类似情况，农户、合作社和企业往往互相指责；有了清楚的责任界限后，各方能够先处理货物，再讨论费用承担。县里没有因此宣布试点已经成熟，也没有删除原报告中的百分之十四，而是在结论旁增加说明：这一数字反映的是特定运输环节的改善，不能代表所有参与者都获得了同等收益。

这次评估最终保住了冷链项目，也纠正了只凭单一指标作决定的倾向。生鲜损耗率下降具有现实价值，但公共项目还必须回答三个具体问题：改善发生在哪个环节，成本由谁承担，服务是否到达原定对象。松岭县没有在“立即扩张”和“全面停止”之间简单选择，而是通过调整路线、补充接驳服务和公开责任记录来解决冲突。试点的真正成果并不是一份更漂亮的报告，而是建立了一套能够发现遗漏、承认限制并及时修正的机制。只有当数据与农户的实际经历能够相互印证，冷链配送的进展才具有可信度，也才值得在更多乡村推广。
pinyin: jiǔ yuè chū ， sōng lǐng xiàn nóng yè fú wù zhōng xīn zhào kāi nóng cūn lěng liàn pèi sòng shì diǎn píng gū huì 。 shì diǎn fù gài liǔ wān zhèn jí fù jìn cūn zhuāng ， xiàn lǐ de jiē duàn xìng bào gào bǎ “ shēng xiān sǔn hào lǜ xià jiàng le bǎi fēn zhī shí sì ” liè wéi zhǔ yào jìn zhǎn ， bìng jiàn yì kuò dà fú wù fàn wéi 。 bào gào xiǎn shì ， tǒng yī yù lěng 、 jí zhōng zhuāng chē hé quán chéng jì lù wēn dù hòu ， shū cài 、 shuǐ guǒ zài yùn shū zhōng de fǔ làn xiàn xiàng yǒu suǒ jiǎn shǎo 。 fù zé xiàng mù dì gōng zuò rén yuán rèn wéi ， zhè yī biàn huà zú yǐ zhèng míng shì diǎn fāng xiàng zhèng què 。 rán ér ， cān jiā huì yì de shí qiáo cūn hé zuò shè fù zé rén zhōu yuǎn tí chū yì yì 。 tā shuō ， sǔn hào suī rán xià jiàng le ， dàn pèi sòng chē liàng bù zài jìn rù wèi zhì piān yuǎn de shān cūn ， cūn mín bì xū bǎ huò wù sòng dào zhèn shàng de zhōng zhuǎn zhàn 。 yǒu xiē nóng hù líng chén chū fā ， jīng guò pán shān lù cái néng gǎn shàng zhuāng chē shí jiān ， zēng jiā de rén gōng hé duǎn tú yùn shū chéng běn bìng méi yǒu xiě jìn bào gào 。

wèi hé shí shuāng fāng shuō fǎ ， píng gū zǔ méi yǒu lì jí tōng guò kuò jiàn fāng àn ， ér shì yán zhe shí jì pèi sòng lù xiàn jìn xíng le yī cì wán zhěng diào chá 。 qīng chén wǔ diǎn ， gōng zuò rén yuán lái dào shí qiáo cūn ， kàn jiàn nóng hù bǎ gāng cǎi zhāi de jūn gū zhuāng jìn pǔ tōng sù liào kuāng ， zài yòng sān lún chē sòng wǎng liǔ wān zhōng zhuǎn zhàn 。 yóu yú sān lún chē méi yǒu bǎo wēn shè bèi ， jūn gū zài zhè yī duàn lù shàng réng kě néng shòu dào jǐ yā huò gāo wēn yǐng xiǎng ， dàn qǐ yè de sǔn hào tǒng jì zhǐ cóng huò wù jìn rù lěng cáng chē zhī hòu kāi shǐ jì suàn 。 zhōng wǔ ， píng gū zǔ yòu jiǎn chá le zhèn shàng de lěng kù ， fā xiàn kù nèi wēn dù jì lù wán zhěng ， cāo zuò liú chéng yě fú hé yāo qiú 。 wèn tí bù zài yú qǐ yè wěi zào shù jù ， ér zài yú tǒng jì biān jiè guò zhǎi ： bào gào zhǔn què miáo shù le lěng cáng yùn shū huán jié ， què méi yǒu chéng xiàn nóng hù cóng tián jiān dào zhōng zhuǎn zhàn de fù dān ， yě méi yǒu shuō míng bù fèn piān yuǎn cūn zhuāng yīn dìng dān jiào shǎo ér bèi qǔ xiāo shàng mén fú wù 。

chōng tū zài dì èr cì huì yì shàng biàn dé gèng jiā míng xiǎn 。 chéng yùn qǐ yè biǎo shì ， lěng cáng chē shǐ rù shān qū hòu jīng cháng kōng zài fǎn chéng ， xiá zhǎi dào lù hái huì zēng jiā ān quán fēng xiǎn 。 rú guǒ huī fù měi cūn shàng mén ， xiàn yǒu fèi yòng nán yǐ wéi chí 。 hé zuò shè zé rèn wéi ， shì diǎn shǐ yòng le gōng gòng zī jīn ， bù néng zhǐ xuǎn zé huò liàng dà 、 dào lù hǎo de cūn zhuāng ， fǒu zé zuì xū yào gǎi shàn yùn shū tiáo jiàn de nóng hù fǎn ér huì bèi pái chú 。 xiàn cái zhèng bù mén dān xīn jì xù bǔ tiē huì xíng chéng zhǎng qī yī lài ， zhǔ zhāng xiān zàn tíng shān qū xiàn lù 。 nóng yè fú wù zhōng xīn nèi bù yě yǒu fēn qí ： yī bù fèn rén qiáng diào sǔn hào lǜ xià jiàng lái zhī bù yì ， bù yīng yīn jú bù wèn tí fǒu dìng zhěng gè xiàng mù ； lìng yī bù fèn rén rèn wéi ， ruò píng jià zhǐ guān zhù jìn rù lěng cáng chē hòu de shāng pǐn ， jiù huì bǎ chéng běn zhuǎn yí wù rèn wèi xiào lǜ tí gāo 。 miàn duì zhēng yì ， píng gū zǔ míng què tí chū ， bǎi fēn zhī shí sì zhǐ néng zuò wéi jiē duàn xìng xiàn xiàng ， bù néng dān dú yòng yú pàn duàn shì diǎn shì fǒu chéng gōng 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， sōng lǐng xiàn jué dìng bǎo liú shì diǎn ， dàn bù àn yuán fāng àn zhí jiē kuò dà 。 xīn de pèi sòng fāng shì yǐ liǔ wān zhōng zhuǎn zhàn wèi zhōng xīn ， tóng shí zài shí qiáo cūn jiù liáng zhàn shè zhì gù dìng shōu jí diǎn ， yóu hé zuò shè zǔ zhī nóng hù zài guī dìng shí duàn jiāo huò ， zài yóu jù bèi bǎo wēn tiáo jiàn de xiǎo xíng chē liàng jiē bó zhì zhèn shàng 。 duì yú huò liàng bù zú de cūn zhuāng ， bù zài yāo qiú lěng cáng chē zhú hù xíng shǐ ， ér shì yǔn xǔ xiāng lín cūn zhuāng hé bìng dìng dān 。 xiàn lǐ yāo qiú chéng yùn qǐ yè gōng kāi jì fèi xiàng mù 、 chē liàng dào dá shí jiān hé wēn dù yì cháng jì lù ； hé zuò shè fù zé dēng jì huò wù lí kāi nóng hù hòu de jiāo jiē qíng kuàng ， bì miǎn zé rèn zhǐ luò zài mǒu yī fāng 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， hòu xù píng gū bù zài zhǐ jì suàn yùn shū sǔn hào ， hái yào fēn bié shuō míng tián jiān jiāo huò 、 zhōng zhuǎn děng dài 、 lěng cáng yùn shū hé mò duān qiān shōu gè huán jié chū xiàn de wèn tí 。 shè jí nóng hù é wài chéng dān de jiē bó fèi yòng ， yě bì xū zài bào gào zhōng dān dú liè míng ， bù néng bèi lǒng tǒng dì guī rù shēng chǎn chéng běn 。

tiáo zhěng shí shī hòu ， shí qiáo cūn hé zuò shè chóng xīn cān jiā le jí zhōng pèi sòng 。 nóng hù bù bì zài gè zì qián wǎng zhèn shàng ， chéng yùn qǐ yè yě bì miǎn le dà xíng lěng cáng chē pín fán jìn rù xiá zhǎi shān lù 。 yī cì bào yǔ dǎo zhì jiē bó chē liàng wǎn dào ， hé zuò shè gēn jù jiāo jiē jì lù jí shí tōng zhī zhōng zhuǎn zhàn tiáo zhěng zhuāng chē shùn xù ， bìng jiāng yán wù yuán yīn xiě rù gōng kāi tái zhàng 。 guò qù yù dào lèi sì qíng kuàng ， nóng hù 、 hé zuò shè hé qǐ yè wǎng wǎng hù xiāng zhǐ zé ； yǒu le qīng chǔ de zé rèn jiè xiàn hòu ， gè fāng néng gòu xiān chǔ lǐ huò wù ， zài tǎo lùn fèi yòng chéng dān 。 xiàn lǐ méi yǒu yīn cǐ xuān bù shì diǎn yǐ jīng chéng shú ， yě méi yǒu shān chú yuán bào gào zhōng de bǎi fēn zhī shí sì ， ér shì zài jié lùn páng zēng jiā shuō míng ： zhè yī shù zì fǎn yìng de shì tè dìng yùn shū huán jié de gǎi shàn ， bù néng dài biǎo suǒ yǒu cān yù zhě dōu huò dé le tóng děng shōu yì 。

zhè cì píng gū zuì zhōng bǎo zhù le lěng liàn xiàng mù ， yě jiū zhèng le zhǐ píng dān yī zhǐ biāo zuò jué dìng de qīng xiàng 。 shēng xiān sǔn hào lǜ xià jiàng jù yǒu xiàn shí jià zhí ， dàn gōng gòng xiàng mù hái bì xū huí dá sān gè jù tǐ wèn tí ： gǎi shàn fā shēng zài nǎ ge huán jié ， chéng běn yóu shuí chéng dān ， fú wù shì fǒu dào dá yuán dìng duì xiàng 。 sōng lǐng xiàn méi yǒu zài “ lì jí kuò zhāng ” hé “ quán miàn tíng zhǐ ” zhī jiān jiǎn dān xuǎn zé ， ér shì tōng guò tiáo zhěng lù xiàn 、 bǔ chōng jiē bó fú wù hé gōng kāi zé rèn jì lù lái jiě jué chōng tū 。 shì diǎn de zhēn zhèng chéng guǒ bìng bú shì yī fèn gèng piào liàng de bào gào ， ér shì jiàn lì le yī tào néng gòu fā xiàn yí lòu 、 chéng rèn xiàn zhì bìng jí shí xiū zhèng de jī zhì 。 zhǐ yǒu dāng shù jù yǔ nóng hù de shí jì jīng lì néng gòu xiāng hù yìn zhèng ， lěng liàn pèi sòng de jìn zhǎn cái jù yǒu kě xìn dù ， yě cái zhí de zài gèng duō xiāng cūn tuī guǎng 。
translation: In early September, the Songling County Agricultural Service Center held an evaluation meeting for its rural cold-chain delivery pilot program. The pilot covered Liuwan Town and nearby villages. The county's interim report listed “a 14 percent decrease in the fresh-produce loss rate” as a major achievement and recommended expanding the service area. According to the report, vegetables and fruit suffered somewhat less spoilage during transportation after standardized precooling, centralized loading, and continuous temperature recording were introduced. The staff responsible for the project believed this change was sufficient to prove that the pilot was moving in the right direction. However, Zhou Yuan, head of the Shiqiao Village cooperative, raised an objection at the meeting. He said that although losses had decreased, delivery vehicles no longer entered remote mountain villages, so villagers had to take their goods to the transfer station in town. Some farmers had to set out before dawn and travel along winding mountain roads to meet the loading schedule, but the additional labor and short-haul transportation costs were not included in the report.

To verify the claims made by both sides, the evaluation team did not immediately approve the expansion plan. Instead, it conducted a complete investigation along the actual delivery route. At five in the morning, the staff arrived in Shiqiao Village and saw farmers placing freshly harvested mushrooms in ordinary plastic crates before transporting them by three-wheeled vehicles to the Liuwan transfer station. Because the three-wheelers had no temperature-control equipment, the mushrooms could still be affected by crushing or high temperatures along this section of the route. However, the company's loss statistics began only after the goods entered the refrigerated trucks. At noon, the evaluation team also inspected the town's cold-storage facility and found that its temperature records were complete and its operating procedures met the requirements. The problem was not that the company had falsified data, but that the statistical boundaries were too narrow: the report accurately described the refrigerated transportation stage, yet it did not show the burden farmers faced in moving their goods from the fields to the transfer station, nor did it explain that door-to-door service had been canceled for some remote villages because they had fewer orders.

The conflict became more apparent at the second meeting. The carrier said that refrigerated trucks often returned empty after entering the mountain areas and that narrow roads also increased safety risks. The existing fee structure could not be sustained if door-to-door service to every village was restored. The cooperative argued that because the pilot used public funds, it could not serve only villages with large shipment volumes and good roads; otherwise, the farmers most in need of better transportation conditions would instead be excluded. Concerned that continued subsidies would create long-term dependence, the county finance department advocated suspending the mountain routes for the time being. There were also disagreements within the Agricultural Service Center. Some emphasized that the reduction in the loss rate had been hard-won and that the entire project should not be dismissed because of localized problems. Others believed that if the evaluation focused only on goods after they entered refrigerated trucks, it would mistake a transfer of costs for an improvement in efficiency. In response to the dispute, the evaluation team stated clearly that the 14 percent figure could only be treated as an interim observation and could not be used on its own to determine whether the pilot had succeeded.

After discussion, Songling County decided to retain the pilot but not expand it directly under the original plan. The new delivery system centered on the Liuwan transfer station while also establishing a permanent collection point at the former grain depot in Shiqiao Village. The cooperative would organize farmers to deliver their goods during designated periods, after which small vehicles with temperature-control capabilities would carry them to the town. For villages with insufficient shipment volumes, refrigerated trucks would no longer be required to visit each household; instead, neighboring villages would be allowed to combine their orders. The county required the carrier to disclose its chargeable items, vehicle arrival times, and records of temperature anomalies. The cooperative was responsible for documenting each handover after goods left the farmers, preventing responsibility from falling solely on any one party. More importantly, subsequent evaluations would no longer calculate only transportation losses. They would also separately describe problems arising at each stage: delivery from the fields, waiting at the transfer point, refrigerated transportation, and final receipt. Any additional feeder-transport costs borne by farmers also had to be listed separately in the report and could not be broadly classified as production costs.

After the adjustments were implemented, the Shiqiao Village cooperative rejoined the centralized delivery program. Farmers no longer had to travel individually to the town, while the carrier avoided sending large refrigerated trucks frequently onto narrow mountain roads. When a rainstorm once delayed a feeder vehicle, the cooperative used the handover records to promptly notify the transfer station to adjust the loading sequence and entered the reason for the delay in the public ledger. In the past, when similar situations arose, farmers, the cooperative, and the company often blamed one another. With clear boundaries of responsibility in place, the parties could deal with the goods first and discuss how to allocate the costs afterward. The county did not therefore declare that the pilot had matured, nor did it remove the 14 percent figure from the original report. Instead, it added a note beside the conclusion stating that the figure reflected improvement in a particular transportation stage and did not mean that all participants had benefited equally.

This evaluation ultimately preserved the cold-chain project while also correcting the tendency to make decisions based on a single indicator. The decrease in the fresh-produce loss rate had practical value, but a public project also had to answer three specific questions: at which stage did the improvement occur, who bore the costs, and did the service reach its intended recipients? Rather than making a simple choice between “immediate expansion” and “complete termination,” Songling County addressed the conflict by adjusting routes, adding feeder services, and making responsibility records public. The pilot's real achievement was not a more impressive report, but the establishment of a system capable of identifying omissions, acknowledging limitations, and making timely corrections. Only when the data and the farmers' actual experiences corroborate each other can progress in cold-chain delivery be credible and worthy of expansion to more villages.
