articles.title: 松柏苑六部老旧电梯更新：一次筹资与八年分期的取舍
articles.summary: 临江市松柏苑比较一次筹资和八年分期两种电梯更新方案。两者折算后的平均年度支出相近，但分期方案存在利息调整、维修追加和后期费用波动，对收入较低住户尤其不利。业主最终选择一次筹资为主、困难家庭定向缓缴的组合办法，六部电梯最终完成更新。
articles.topic: 松柏苑六部老旧电梯更新：一次筹资与八年分期的取舍
paragraphs: 临江市河西街道松柏苑建于二十多年前，三栋十八层住宅共有六部电梯。近两年，控制系统故障、轿厢门反复失灵，零部件也越来越难采购。五月的一场暴雨后，两部电梯连续停运，其中一部困住了四名居民。虽然维修人员很快排除了故障，但物业公司明确表示，继续修补只能延缓问题，无法消除设备老化带来的风险。业主委员会因此启动整体更新程序，并取得了三家企业的报价。扣除可使用的住宅专项维修资金后，仍有一笔缺口需要业主承担。争议随即出现：住在高层的家庭希望尽快一次筹齐，尽早施工；部分退休居民和经营状况不稳定的住户则担心短期支出过大，主张采用分期方案。原本有关安全的共识，逐渐演变成一场围绕付款时间、风险归属和邻里公平的争论。

第一种方案是一次筹资。业主按照房屋面积和楼层使用系数分担更新缺口，在施工合同签订前缴清款项。其优点是资金边界清楚：设备价格、拆装费用、检验费用和首期保养费一并写进总价合同，除非业主主动变更功能，承包方不得临时加价。由于不需要外部垫资，这一方案没有融资利息，业主委员会也能依据到账金额确定开工日期。缺点同样明显，一笔集中支出会挤压部分家庭当月乃至数月的生活预算。尤其是独居老人、临时失业者和需要长期支付医疗费用的住户，即使承认换梯必要，也可能无法在规定期限内缴清。如果简单地把未付款者视为反对更新，不仅会激化矛盾，还可能因筹资不足而拖延整个项目。

第二种方案由电梯服务企业联合金融机构先行垫付，业主在八年内随物业费按月偿还。宣传材料把它概括为“每天少喝一杯饮料就能换新梯”，听起来压力较小。业主委员会把合同附件逐项拆开后，却发现月供只是基础部分。垫资利息可以随约定的参考利率调整；超过免费范围的零件更换、年度保险费和远程监测服务费，需要根据实际情况结算；如果连续欠费的住户增多，企业还有权要求小区补足风险准备金。也就是说，前几年账单较平稳，进入设备维护需求上升的阶段后，费用可能出现波动。分期并没有消除成本，只是把当前确定的支出，转换成未来若干笔不完全确定的义务。对收入稳定的家庭而言，这种波动或许可以吸收；对每月结余很少的家庭而言，一次临时追加款就可能打乱基本生活安排。

为了避免只比较表面上的月供，业主委员会把两种方案放到同一时间范围内核算。一次筹资方案的支出集中在开工前，后续仅承担正常保养费；分期方案的初始负担较轻，但要支付垫资成本，并保留若干据实结算项目。按照现有合同条件折算，两种方案的平均年度支出相差不大。然而，平均数掩盖了付款路径的差异。一次筹资的困难发生在开始阶段，金额虽高，却能提前确认；分期方案把困难推向后期，单次账单看似较小，却可能因利率、维修和欠费情况而改变。更重要的是，同样一笔追加费用对不同家庭并不具有同等影响。收入较高的住户可以通过储蓄应付，收入较低的住户却可能被迫借款，甚至因逾期承担违约责任。因此，判断融资方案不能只问八年总额或年度平均数，还要追问谁在什么时候付款，以及谁最缺乏承受波动的能力。

在第二次业主大会上，双方的冲突达到顶点。一名高层业主认为，若为了照顾少数人而继续等待，所有居民都要承担旧电梯停运的风险；一名靠养老金生活的低层住户则反问，安全改善为何必须以她立即拿出大笔现金为条件。街道调解员提醒大家，设备更新和困难救助原本是两个问题，不应被迫塞进同一种融资合同。经过讨论，业主委员会提出第三种处理方式，但没有改变对两种主要方案的比较结论：项目仍采用一次筹资，以锁定工程总价和施工期限；与此同时，从小区公共收益中设立周转账户，只为经过申请确认的困难家庭垫付其应承担的款项。这些家庭可以在三年内无息归还，若收入恢复也可提前结清。周转账户只解决付款时间问题，不替任何业主免除责任，也不会把个别家庭的欠款转嫁给其他住户。

最终，表决通过了这一决定。大多数业主在规定期限内完成缴费，十二户家庭申请了无息缓缴，其中几户在子女协助下提前归还。六部电梯分两批施工，楼栋之间轮换停梯，行动不便的居民由社区志愿者协助采购生活用品。工程验收后，业主委员会公开了合同、付款记录和周转账户余额，避免救助安排变成含糊的人情账。松柏苑的选择并不意味着一次筹资永远优于分期，而是说明融资比较必须同时考察总成本、支出波动和住户差异。平均年度支出接近，只能回答两种方案总体上要花多少钱；它无法说明后期追加款由谁承受，也无法判断某个家庭是否会在最脆弱的时候被账单击中。把确定的工程成本与有针对性的缓缴措施结合起来，既控制了长期风险，也让支付能力较弱的居民没有被排除在安全更新之外。
pinyin: lín jiāng shì hé xī jiē dào sōng bǎi yuàn jiàn yú èr shí duō nián qián ， sān dòng shí bā céng zhù zhái gòng yǒu liù bù diàn tī 。 jìn liǎng nián ， kòng zhì xì tǒng gù zhàng 、 jiào xiāng mén fǎn fù shī líng ， líng bù jiàn yě yuè lái yuè nán cǎi gòu 。 wǔ yuè de yī cháng bào yǔ hòu ， liǎng bù diàn tī lián xù tíng yùn ， qí zhōng yī bù kùn zhù le sì míng jū mín 。 suī rán wéi xiū rén yuán hěn kuài pái chú le gù zhàng ， dàn wù yè gōng sī míng què biǎo shì ， jì xù xiū bǔ zhǐ néng yán huǎn wèn tí ， wú fǎ xiāo chú shè bèi lǎo huà dài lái de fēng xiǎn 。 yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì yīn cǐ qǐ dòng zhěng tǐ gēng xīn chéng xù ， bìng qǔ dé le sān jiā qǐ yè de bào jià 。 kòu chú kě shǐ yòng de zhù zhái zhuān xiàng wéi xiū zī jīn hòu ， réng yǒu yī bǐ quē kǒu xū yào yè zhǔ chéng dān 。 zhēng yì suí jí chū xiàn ： zhù zài gāo céng de jiā tíng xī wàng jǐn kuài yī cì chóu qí ， jǐn zǎo shī gōng ； bù fèn tuì xiū jū mín hé jīng yíng zhuàng kuàng bù wěn dìng de zhù hù zé dān xīn duǎn qī zhī chū guò dà ， zhǔ zhāng cǎi yòng fēn qī fāng àn 。 yuán běn yǒu guān ān quán de gòng shí ， zhú jiàn yǎn biàn chéng yī cháng wéi rào fù kuǎn shí jiān 、 fēng xiǎn guī shǔ hé lín lǐ gōng píng de zhēng lùn 。

dì yī zhǒng fāng àn shì yī cì chóu zī 。 yè zhǔ àn zhào fáng wū miàn jī hé lóu céng shǐ yòng xì shù fēn dān gēng xīn quē kǒu ， zài shī gōng hé tóng qiān dìng qián jiǎo qīng kuǎn xiàng 。 qí yōu diǎn shì zī jīn biān jiè qīng chǔ ： shè bèi jià gé 、 chāi zhuāng fèi yòng 、 jiǎn yàn fèi yòng hé shǒu qī bǎo yǎng fèi yī bìng xiě jìn zǒng jià hé tóng ， chú fēi yè zhǔ zhǔ dòng biàn gēng gōng néng ， chéng bāo fāng bù dé lín shí jiā jià 。 yóu yú bù xū yào wài bù diàn zī ， zhè yī fāng àn méi yǒu róng zī lì xī ， yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì yě néng yī jù dào zhàng jīn é què dìng kāi gōng rì qī 。 quē diǎn tóng yàng míng xiǎn ， yī bǐ jí zhōng zhī chū huì jǐ yā bù fèn jiā tíng dàng yuè nǎi zhì shù yuè de shēng huó yù suàn 。 yóu qí shì dú jū lǎo rén 、 lín shí shī yè zhě hé xū yào cháng qī zhī fù yī liáo fèi yòng de zhù hù ， jí shǐ chéng rèn huàn tī bì yào ， yě kě néng wú fǎ zài guī dìng qī xiàn nèi jiǎo qīng 。 rú guǒ jiǎn dān dì bǎ wèi fù kuǎn zhě shì wèi fǎn duì gēng xīn ， bù jǐn huì jī huà máo dùn ， hái kě néng yīn chóu zī bù zú ér tuō yán zhěng gè xiàng mù 。

dì èr zhǒng fāng àn yóu diàn tī fú wù qǐ yè lián hé jīn róng jī gòu xiān xíng diàn fù ， yè zhǔ zài bā nián nèi suí wù yè fèi àn yuè cháng huán 。 xuān chuán cái liào bǎ tā gài kuò wèi “ měi tiān shǎo hē yī bēi yǐn liào jiù néng huàn xīn tī ”， tīng qǐ lái yā lì jiào xiǎo 。 yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì bǎ hé tóng fù jiàn zhú xiàng chāi kāi hòu ， què fā xiàn yuè gōng zhǐ shì jī chǔ bù fèn 。 diàn zī lì xī kě yǐ suí yuē dìng de cān kǎo lì lǜ tiáo zhěng ； chāo guò miǎn fèi fàn wéi de líng jiàn gēng huàn 、 nián dù bǎo xiǎn fèi hé yuǎn chéng jiān cè fú wù fèi ， xū yào gēn jù shí jì qíng kuàng jié suàn ； rú guǒ lián xù qiàn fèi de zhù hù zēng duō ， qǐ yè hái yǒu quán yāo qiú xiǎo qū bǔ zú fēng xiǎn zhǔn bèi jīn 。 yě jiù shì shuō ， qián jǐ nián zhàng dān jiào píng wěn ， jìn rù shè bèi wéi hù xū qiú shàng shēng de jiē duàn hòu ， fèi yòng kě néng chū xiàn bō dòng 。 fēn qī bìng méi yǒu xiāo chú chéng běn ， zhǐ shì bǎ dāng qián què dìng de zhī chū ， zhuǎn huàn chéng wèi lái ruò gān bǐ bù wán quán què dìng de yì wù 。 duì shōu rù wěn dìng de jiā tíng ér yán ， zhè zhǒng bō dòng huò xǔ kě yǐ xī shōu ； duì měi yuè jié yú hěn shǎo de jiā tíng ér yán ， yī cì lín shí zhuī jiā kuǎn jiù kě néng dǎ luàn jī běn shēng huó ān pái 。

wèi le bì miǎn zhǐ bǐ jiào biǎo miàn shàng de yuè gōng ， yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì bǎ liǎng zhǒng fāng àn fàng dào tóng yī shí jiān fàn wéi nèi hé suàn 。 yī cì chóu zī fāng àn de zhī chū jí zhōng zài kāi gōng qián ， hòu xù jǐn chéng dān zhèng cháng bǎo yǎng fèi ； fēn qī fāng àn de chū shǐ fù dān jiào qīng ， dàn yào zhī fù diàn zī chéng běn ， bìng bǎo liú ruò gān jù shí jié suàn xiàng mù 。 àn zhào xiàn yǒu hé tóng tiáo jiàn zhé suàn ， liǎng zhǒng fāng àn de píng jūn nián dù zhī chū xiāng chā bú dà 。 rán ér ， píng jūn shù yǎn gài le fù kuǎn lù jìng de chā yì 。 yī cì chóu zī de kùn nán fā shēng zài kāi shǐ jiē duàn ， jīn é suī gāo ， què néng tí qián què rèn ； fēn qī fāng àn bǎ kùn nán tuī xiàng hòu qī ， dān cì zhàng dān kàn shì jiào xiǎo ， què kě néng yīn lì lǜ 、 wéi xiū hé qiàn fèi qíng kuàng ér gǎi biàn 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， tóng yàng yī bǐ zhuī jiā fèi yòng duì bù tóng jiā tíng bìng bù jù yǒu tóng děng yǐng xiǎng 。 shōu rù jiào gāo de zhù hù kě yǐ tōng guò chǔ xù yìng fù ， shōu rù jiào dī de zhù hù què kě néng bèi pò jiè kuǎn ， shèn zhì yīn yú qī chéng dān wéi yuē zé rèn 。 yīn cǐ ， pàn duàn róng zī fāng àn bù néng zhǐ wèn bā nián zǒng é huò nián dù píng jūn shù ， hái yào zhuī wèn shuí zài shén me shí hòu fù kuǎn ， yǐ jí shuí zuì quē fá chéng shòu bō dòng de néng lì 。

zài dì èr cì yè zhǔ dà huì shàng ， shuāng fāng de chōng tū dá dào dǐng diǎn 。 yī míng gāo céng yè zhǔ rèn wéi ， ruò wèi le zhào gù shǎo shù rén ér jì xù děng dài ， suǒ yǒu jū mín dōu yào chéng dān jiù diàn tī tíng yùn de fēng xiǎn ； yī míng kào yǎng lǎo jīn shēng huó de dī céng zhù hù zé fǎn wèn ， ān quán gǎi shàn wèi hé bì xū yǐ tā lì jí ná chū dà bǐ xiàn jīn wèi tiáo jiàn 。 jiē dào tiáo jiě yuán tí xǐng dà jiā ， shè bèi gēng xīn hé kùn nán jiù zhù yuán běn shì liǎng gè wèn tí ， bù yīng bèi pò sāi jìn tóng yī zhǒng róng zī hé tóng 。 jīng guò tǎo lùn ， yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì tí chū dì sān zhǒng chǔ lǐ fāng shì ， dàn méi yǒu gǎi biàn duì liǎng zhǒng zhǔ yào fāng àn de bǐ jiào jié lùn ： xiàng mù réng cǎi yòng yī cì chóu zī ， yǐ suǒ dìng gōng chéng zǒng jià hé shī gōng qī xiàn ； yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， cóng xiǎo qū gōng gòng shōu yì zhōng shè lì zhōu zhuǎn zhàng hù ， zhǐ wèi jīng guò shēn qǐng què rèn de kùn nán jiā tíng diàn fù qí yìng chéng dān de kuǎn xiàng 。 zhè xiē jiā tíng kě yǐ zài sān nián nèi wú xī guī huán ， ruò shōu rù huī fù yě kě tí qián jié qīng 。 zhōu zhuǎn zhàng hù zhǐ jiě jué fù kuǎn shí jiān wèn tí ， bù tì rèn hé yè zhǔ miǎn chú zé rèn ， yě bú huì bǎ gè bié jiā tíng de qiàn kuǎn zhuǎn jià gěi qí tā zhù hù 。

zuì zhōng ， biǎo jué tōng guò le zhè yī jué dìng 。 dà duō shù yè zhǔ zài guī dìng qī xiàn nèi wán chéng jiǎo fèi ， shí èr hù jiā tíng shēn qǐng liǎo wú xī huǎn jiǎo ， qí zhōng jǐ hù zài zǐ nǚ xié zhù xià tí qián guī huán 。 liù bù diàn tī fēn liǎng pī shī gōng ， lóu dòng zhī jiān lún huàn tíng tī ， xíng dòng bù biàn de jū mín yóu shè qū zhì yuàn zhě xié zhù cǎi gòu shēng huó yòng pǐn 。 gōng chéng yàn shōu hòu ， yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì gōng kāi le hé tóng 、 fù kuǎn jì lù hé zhōu zhuǎn zhàng hù yú é ， bì miǎn jiù zhù ān pái biàn chéng hán hú de rén qíng zhàng 。 sōng bǎi yuàn de xuǎn zé bìng bù yì wèi zhe yī cì chóu zī yǒng yuǎn yōu yú fēn qī ， ér shì shuō míng róng zī bǐ jiào bì xū tóng shí kǎo chá zǒng chéng běn 、 zhī chū bō dòng hé zhù hù chā yì 。 píng jūn nián dù zhī chū jiē jìn ， zhǐ néng huí dá liǎng zhǒng fāng àn zǒng tǐ shàng yào huā duō shǎo qián ； tā wú fǎ shuō míng hòu qī zhuī jiā kuǎn yóu shuí chéng shòu ， yě wú fǎ pàn duàn mǒu gè jiā tíng shì fǒu huì zài zuì cuì ruò de shí hòu bèi zhàng dān jī zhòng 。 bǎ què dìng de gōng chéng chéng běn yǔ yǒu zhēn duì xìng de huǎn jiǎo cuò shī jié hé qǐ lái ， jì kòng zhì le cháng qī fēng xiǎn ， yě ràng zhī fù néng lì jiào ruò de jū mín méi yǒu bèi pái chú zài ān quán gēng xīn zhī wài 。
translation: Songbaiyuan, a residential complex in the Hexi Subdistrict of Linjiang City, was built more than twenty years ago. Its three eighteen-story residential buildings have six elevators in total. Over the past two years, the control systems have malfunctioned, the elevator car doors have repeatedly failed, and replacement parts have become increasingly difficult to obtain. After a torrential rainstorm in May, two elevators went out of service in succession, one of them trapping four residents. Although maintenance workers quickly fixed the faults, the property management company made it clear that continued patchwork repairs could only delay the problem, not eliminate the risks caused by aging equipment. The homeowners’ committee therefore initiated a comprehensive replacement process and obtained quotations from three companies. Even after deducting the available special residential maintenance funds, a funding gap still had to be covered by the homeowners. A dispute soon arose: families on higher floors wanted to raise the full amount as quickly as possible so that construction could begin early, while some retired residents and households with unstable business income were concerned that the short-term expense would be too great and advocated an installment plan. What had originally been a consensus on safety gradually turned into a debate over the timing of payments, the allocation of risk, and fairness among neighbors.

The first option was to raise the money in a single payment. Homeowners would share the funding gap according to the floor area of their homes and a floor-based usage coefficient, and would pay the full amount before the construction contract was signed. The advantage was that the financial boundaries were clear: the price of the equipment, dismantling and installation costs, inspection fees, and the initial maintenance fee would all be included in a fixed-price contract. Unless the homeowners requested functional changes, the contractor would not be permitted to impose temporary price increases. Because no outside financing was required, this option involved no financing interest, and the homeowners’ committee could also set the construction start date based on the amount of money received. The disadvantage was equally clear: a large one-time expense would strain some families’ budgets for that month or even for several months. In particular, elderly people living alone, temporarily unemployed residents, and households facing long-term medical expenses might be unable to pay the full amount by the deadline even if they acknowledged that replacing the elevators was necessary. Simply treating those who had not paid as opponents of the replacement would not only intensify the conflict but could also delay the entire project because of insufficient funding.

Under the second option, an elevator service company and a financial institution would jointly provide the funds upfront, and the homeowners would repay the money monthly over eight years together with their property management fees. Promotional materials summarized the plan as being able to “replace the elevators by drinking one fewer beverage a day,” which made the burden sound relatively light. However, after the homeowners’ committee examined each item in the contract appendices, it found that the monthly installment was only the basic component. Interest on the advance funding could be adjusted in line with an agreed benchmark rate; replacement of parts beyond the free coverage, annual insurance premiums, and remote monitoring service fees would have to be settled according to actual circumstances; and if the number of households that remained in arrears increased, the company would also have the right to require the residential complex to replenish a risk reserve fund. In other words, the bills would be relatively stable during the first few years, but costs might fluctuate once the equipment entered a stage of increasing maintenance needs. Installments did not eliminate the cost; they merely converted a known present expense into several future obligations that were not entirely certain. Families with stable incomes might be able to absorb such fluctuations, but for families with very little left over each month, a single temporary surcharge could disrupt their basic living arrangements.

To avoid comparing only the apparent monthly payments, the homeowners’ committee calculated the two options over the same time horizon. Under the single-payment option, expenses would be concentrated before construction began, with only routine maintenance fees payable afterward. The installment option carried a lighter initial burden, but required payment of financing costs and retained several items to be settled according to actual expenses. Based on the existing contract terms, the two options had similar average annual costs. However, the averages concealed the differences in their payment paths. The difficulty with raising the money all at once arose at the beginning; although the amount was large, it could be determined in advance. The installment option pushed the difficulty into later years; each bill appeared smaller, but could change because of interest rates, repairs, and payment arrears. More importantly, the same additional charge did not affect every family equally. Higher-income households could draw on savings to cover it, while lower-income households might be forced to borrow money or even incur liability for breach of contract due to late payment. Therefore, evaluating a financing plan required asking not only about the eight-year total or the annual average, but also who would pay at what time and who had the least capacity to withstand fluctuations.

At the second homeowners’ assembly, the conflict between the two sides reached its peak. One homeowner on a higher floor argued that if they continued to wait in order to accommodate a minority, all residents would have to bear the risk of the old elevators going out of service. A resident on a lower floor who lived on a pension responded by asking why improving safety had to depend on her immediately producing a large sum of cash. The subdistrict mediator reminded everyone that equipment replacement and assistance for households in difficulty were originally two separate issues and should not be forced into the same financing contract. After discussion, the homeowners’ committee proposed a third approach, without changing its conclusions from the comparison of the two main options: the project would still use a single round of fundraising to lock in the total project price and construction schedule; at the same time, a revolving account would be established using the residential complex’s shared revenue solely to advance the required payments for families whose financial difficulties had been confirmed through an application process. These families could repay the money interest-free within three years, or settle the balance early if their incomes recovered. The revolving account would address only the timing of payments. It would not relieve any homeowner of responsibility, nor would it shift the debts of individual families onto other residents.

The decision was ultimately approved by a vote. Most homeowners completed their payments within the specified period, while twelve households applied for interest-free deferred payment, several of which repaid early with assistance from their children. The six elevators were replaced in two batches, with elevator shutdowns rotated among the buildings. Community volunteers helped residents with limited mobility purchase daily necessities. After the project passed inspection, the homeowners’ committee disclosed the contract, payment records, and revolving account balance, preventing the assistance arrangement from becoming a vague ledger of personal favors. Songbaiyuan’s choice did not mean that raising the money all at once was always better than paying in installments. Rather, it showed that financing comparisons must consider total cost, fluctuations in expenditure, and differences among households at the same time. Similar average annual costs could answer only how much the two options would cost overall; they could not show who would bear later surcharges or determine whether a particular family would be hit by a bill at its most vulnerable moment. Combining a fixed project cost with targeted deferred-payment measures both controlled long-term risks and ensured that residents with less ability to pay were not excluded from the safety upgrade.

articles.title: 临江市听证会：在按袋计费与定额收费之间选择
articles.summary: 临江市比较垃圾专用袋收费与家庭定额收费两套制度。两者造成的家庭平均费用相近，真正的分歧却在于费用波动、违规风险和执行压力由谁承担。经过听证，市政府提出并试行定额保障与超量按袋收费相结合的方案；社区试行后，市议会最终通过该方案，并设置特殊家庭减免、追缴告知和申诉程序。
articles.topic: 临江市听证会：在按袋计费与定额收费之间选择
paragraphs: 临江市是一座河网密集的旅游城市。近几年，老城区垃圾转运站经常超负荷运行，沿河商住混合街区还出现过垃圾袋堆到人行道上的现象。市政府决定改革原有的统一垃圾处理费，提出两套备选制度。第一套是按袋计费：居民必须购买印有防伪标志的专用袋，袋子越大、使用越多，支付的费用就越高。第二套是家庭定额收费：每户按月缴纳固定费用，由物业或社区统一收集生活垃圾；如果整栋楼连续超出核定总量，再对该楼住户追加费用。财政部门测算后认为，在垃圾总量不明显变化的情况下，两套制度给普通家庭带来的平均支出相差不大。因此，最初的新闻报道把争论概括为“选袋子还是选账单”，仿佛只是收费形式不同。然而，在市民听证会上，人们很快发现，平均数掩盖了更重要的问题：垃圾突然增加时，额外费用由哪一户承担；有人逃避缴费时，管理成本又会落到谁身上。

按袋计费的支持者认为，这套制度把价格信号直接传递给个人。一个家庭如果主动减少一次性用品、修理旧物并认真分类，就能少买专用袋；制造垃圾越多的人则付得越多。制度在责任上显得清楚，也避免了节约者为浪费者分摊费用。但反对者指出，家庭产生的垃圾量并不总是能够自主控制。新生儿需要大量尿布，卧床病人会产生护理废弃物，逢年过节或房屋搬迁时，垃圾量也会短期上升。对收入稳定的家庭而言，多买几个袋子只是轻微波动；对独居老人、临时失业者或多子女家庭而言，同样的波动可能挤占食品和交通开支。此外，专用袋价格越能促使人节约，就越可能诱发逃避行为。有人会把普通袋塞进公共垃圾桶，有人会把垃圾带到没有检查的街区，清洁工则不得不辨认、拒收并处理争执。表面上由制造者承担的风险，最终可能转移给公共空间和一线工作人员。

家庭定额收费看起来更稳定。住户每月事先知道要付多少钱，不必担心疾病、搬家或节庆造成账单突然增加；社区也无须逐袋检查，收运流程相对简单。可是，这套制度把另一类风险集中到了守规则的人身上。如果一栋楼按照总量接受考核，某些住户持续丢弃大量垃圾，追加费用却可能由全楼共同承担。租户频繁更换的公寓尤其容易发生责任不清：垃圾是谁产生的、应该向房东还是租客追缴，往往很难查明。更麻烦的是，固定费用削弱了个人减量的回报。认真分类的居民即使把厨余和可回收物处理得很好，也无法立刻减少支出，久而久之可能失去动力。物业为了避免整栋楼超量，还可能制定比市政府更严厉的内部规则，甚至限制投放时间。这样一来，政府虽然向家庭提供了费用稳定性，却把监督邻居、处理纠纷和承担集体超量的风险交给了社区。

听证会上的冲突在梧桐里小区的代表发言后变得具体。该小区既有年轻租客，也有不少需要长期护理的老人。业主委员会主任支持定额收费，因为他担心按袋计费会让行动不便的居民反复购买专用袋；一名餐馆员工却反对集体追加费用，因为她白天在店里吃饭，家中垃圾很少，不愿替短租住户承担超量成本。环卫工代表补充说，如果只强调“谁污染谁付费”，却没有方便的购买渠道和合理豁免，非法投放往往首先增加清洁工的工作，而不是立即惩罚逃费者。会议由此不再围绕哪套制度“总体更便宜”争论，而是转向三个具体问题：无法减少垃圾的人是否应承受价格波动，无法识别责任人的社区是否应承受集体处罚，一线执行者是否有足够资源处理违规。市政府也承认，任何方案都不能消除风险，只能决定风险由个人、邻里、物业还是财政承担。

经过讨论，临江市没有完整采用任何一套方案，而是作出一项边界清楚的组合决定。每户每月获得与常住人口相对应的基本投放额度，这部分费用固定，保证日常生活不会因垃圾量轻微变化而受到冲击；超过额度后，居民必须使用专用袋，额外费用随投放量增加。新生儿家庭、经社区核实的护理家庭和暂时生活困难者可以申请免费补充袋，但减免设有期限，需要定期确认，以免特殊安排演变成永久漏洞。公寓楼不再因总量超标自动向全体住户收费，只有在物业能够说明异常来源并完成告知程序后，才能启动追缴。市政府同时要求超市、社区服务站和夜间便利店销售专用袋，防止购买不便变成违规借口。对于乱扔垃圾，执法人员先记录地点和时间，优先改善投放设施；只有存在清楚证据时才追究个人责任，不能让清洁工通过翻查私人垃圾来代替正式调查。

新制度先在梧桐里及附近三个街区试行。实施初期，居民最常提出的问题不是价格，而是家庭人口如何登记、护理减免怎样续办以及搬家后剩余专用袋能否退换。市政府据此简化证明材料，并要求服务站公开处理期限。几个月后，试点没有被宣布为某一套理论的胜利，市政府只公布了投诉类型、违规处置和流程调整，没有用单一平均费用来证明制度完美。梧桐里业主委员会也取消了原先准备实行的全楼罚款，改为提醒异常投放并协助困难家庭申请补充额度。最终，市议会通过组合方案，同时规定每年审查减免覆盖、非法投放和一线工作负担。临江市的选择说明，比较公共收费制度不能只问多数人平均支付多少，还要追问最坏情况下谁会突然付不起、谁会替陌生人承担责任，以及谁必须处理制度留下的麻烦。平均表现决定方案是否经济，风险分布则决定它是否公平、可执行并能长期获得信任。
pinyin: lín jiāng shì shì yī zuò hé wǎng mì jí de lǚ yóu chéng shì 。 jìn jǐ nián ， lǎo chéng qū lā jī zhuǎn yùn zhàn jīng cháng chāo fù hè yùn xíng ， yán hé shāng zhù hùn hé jiē qū hái chū xiàn guò lā jī dài duī dào rén xíng dào shàng de xiàn xiàng 。 shì zhèng fǔ jué dìng gǎi gé yuán yǒu de tǒng yī lā jī chǔ lǐ fèi ， tí chū liǎng tào bèi xuǎn zhì dù 。 dì yī tào shì àn dài jì fèi ： jū mín bì xū gòu mǎi yìn yǒu fáng wěi biāo zhì de zhuān yòng dài ， dài zi yuè dà 、 shǐ yòng yuè duō ， zhī fù de fèi yòng jiù yuè gāo 。 dì èr tào shì jiā tíng dìng é shōu fèi ： měi hù àn yuè jiǎo nà gù dìng fèi yòng ， yóu wù yè huò shè qū tǒng yī shōu jí shēng huó lā jī ； rú guǒ zhěng dòng lóu lián xù chāo chū hé dìng zǒng liàng ， zài duì gāi lóu zhù hù zhuī jiā fèi yòng 。 cái zhèng bù mén cè suàn hòu rèn wéi ， zài lā jī zǒng liàng bù míng xiǎn biàn huà de qíng kuàng xià ， liǎng tào zhì dù gěi pǔ tōng jiā tíng dài lái de píng jūn zhī chū xiāng chā bú dà 。 yīn cǐ ， zuì chū de xīn wén bào dào bǎ zhēng lùn gài kuò wèi “ xuǎn dài zi hái shì xuǎn zhàng dān ”， fǎng fú zhǐ shì shōu fèi xíng shì bù tóng 。 rán ér ， zài shì mín tīng zhèng huì shàng ， rén men hěn kuài fā xiàn ， píng jūn shù yǎn gài le gèng zhòng yào de wèn tí ： lā jī tū rán zēng jiā shí ， é wài fèi yòng yóu nǎ yī hù chéng dān ； yǒu rén táo bì jiǎo fèi shí ， guǎn lǐ chéng běn yòu huì luò dào shuí shēn shàng 。

àn dài jì fèi de zhī chí zhě rèn wéi ， zhè tào zhì dù bǎ jià gé xìn hào zhí jiē chuán dì gěi gè rén 。 yí gè jiā tíng rú guǒ zhǔ dòng jiǎn shǎo yí cì xìng yòng pǐn 、 xiū lǐ jiù wù bìng rèn zhēn fēn lèi ， jiù néng shǎo mǎi zhuān yòng dài ； zhì zào lā jī yuè duō de rén zé fù dé yuè duō 。 zhì dù zài zé rèn shàng xiǎn de qīng chǔ ， yě bì miǎn le jié yuē zhě wèi làng fèi zhě fēn tān fèi yòng 。 dàn fǎn duì zhě zhǐ chū ， jiā tíng chǎn shēng de lā jī liàng bìng bù zǒng shì néng gòu zì zhǔ kòng zhì 。 xīn shēng ér xū yào dà liàng niào bù ， wò chuáng bìng rén huì chǎn shēng hù lǐ fèi qì wù ， féng nián guò jié huò fáng wū bān qiān shí ， lā jī liàng yě huì duǎn qī shàng shēng 。 duì shōu rù wěn dìng de jiā tíng ér yán ， duō mǎi jǐ gè dài zi zhǐ shì qīng wēi bō dòng ； duì dú jū lǎo rén 、 lín shí shī yè zhě huò duō zǐ nǚ jiā tíng ér yán ， tóng yàng de bō dòng kě néng jǐ zhàn shí pǐn hé jiāo tōng kāi zhī 。 cǐ wài ， zhuān yòng dài jià gé yuè néng cù shǐ rén jié yuē ， jiù yuè kě néng yòu fā táo bì xíng wéi 。 yǒu rén huì bǎ pǔ tōng dài sāi jìn gōng gòng lā jī tǒng ， yǒu rén huì bǎ lā jī dài dào méi yǒu jiǎn chá de jiē qū ， qīng jié gōng zé bù dé bù biàn rèn 、 jù shōu bìng chǔ lǐ zhēng zhí 。 biǎo miàn shàng yóu zhì zào zhě chéng dān de fēng xiǎn ， zuì zhōng kě néng zhuǎn yí gěi gōng gòng kōng jiān hé yī xiàn gōng zuò rén yuán 。

jiā tíng dìng é shōu fèi kàn qǐ lái gèng wěn dìng 。 zhù hù měi yuè shì xiān zhī dào yào fù duō shǎo qián ， bù bì dān xīn jí bìng 、 bān jiā huò jié qìng zào chéng zhàng dān tū rán zēng jiā ； shè qū yě wú xū zhú dài jiǎn chá ， shōu yùn liú chéng xiāng duì jiǎn dān 。 kě shì ， zhè tào zhì dù bǎ lìng yī lèi fēng xiǎn jí zhōng dào le shǒu guī zé de rén shēn shàng 。 rú guǒ yī dòng lóu àn zhào zǒng liàng jiē shòu kǎo hé ， mǒu xiē zhù hù chí xù diū qì dà liàng lā jī ， zhuī jiā fèi yòng què kě néng yóu quán lóu gòng tóng chéng dān 。 zū hù pín fán gēng huàn de gōng yù yóu qí róng yì fā shēng zé rèn bù qīng ： lā jī shì shuí chǎn shēng de 、 yīng gāi xiàng fáng dōng hái shì zū kè zhuī jiǎo ， wǎng wǎng hěn nán chá míng 。 gèng má fán de shì ， gù dìng fèi yòng xuē ruò le gè rén jiǎn liàng de huí bào 。 rèn zhēn fēn lèi de jū mín jí shǐ bǎ chú yú hé kě huí shōu wù chǔ lǐ dé hěn hǎo ， yě wú fǎ lì kè jiǎn shǎo zhī chū ， jiǔ ér jiǔ zhī kě néng shī qù dòng lì 。 wù yè wèi le bì miǎn zhěng dòng lóu chāo liàng ， hái kě néng zhì dìng bǐ shì zhèng fǔ gèng yán lì de nèi bù guī zé ， shèn zhì xiàn zhì tóu fàng shí jiān 。 zhè yàng yī lái ， zhèng fǔ suī rán xiàng jiā tíng tí gōng le fèi yòng wěn dìng xìng ， què bǎ jiān dū lín jū 、 chǔ lǐ jiū fēn hé chéng dān jí tǐ chāo liàng de fēng xiǎn jiāo gěi le shè qū 。

tīng zhèng huì shàng de chōng tū zài wú tóng lǐ xiǎo qū de dài biǎo fā yán hòu biàn dé jù tǐ 。 gāi xiǎo qū jì yǒu nián qīng zū kè ， yě yǒu bù shǎo xū yào cháng qī hù lǐ de lǎo rén 。 yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì zhǔ rèn zhī chí dìng é shōu fèi ， yīn wèi tā dān xīn àn dài jì fèi huì ràng xíng dòng bù biàn de jū mín fǎn fù gòu mǎi zhuān yòng dài ； yī míng cān guǎn yuán gōng què fǎn duì jí tǐ zhuī jiā fèi yòng ， yīn wèi tā bái tiān zài diàn lǐ chī fàn ， jiā zhōng lā jī hěn shǎo ， bù yuàn tì duǎn zū zhù hù chéng dān chāo liàng chéng běn 。 huán wèi gōng dài biǎo bǔ chōng shuō ， rú guǒ zhǐ qiáng diào “ shuí wū rǎn shuí fù fèi ”， què méi yǒu fāng biàn de gòu mǎi qú dào hé hé lǐ huò miǎn ， fēi fǎ tóu fàng wǎng wǎng shǒu xiān zēng jiā qīng jié gōng de gōng zuò ， ér bú shì lì jí chéng fá táo fèi zhě 。 huì yì yóu cǐ bù zài wéi rào nǎ tào zhì dù “ zǒng tǐ gèng pián yi ” zhēng lùn ， ér shì zhuǎn xiàng sān gè jù tǐ wèn tí ： wú fǎ jiǎn shǎo lā jī de rén shì fǒu yìng chéng shòu jià gé bō dòng ， wú fǎ shí bié zé rèn rén de shè qū shì fǒu yìng chéng shòu jí tǐ chǔ fá ， yī xiàn zhí xíng zhě shì fǒu yǒu zú gòu zī yuán chǔ lǐ wéi guī 。 shì zhèng fǔ yě chéng rèn ， rèn hé fāng àn dōu bù néng xiāo chú fēng xiǎn ， zhǐ néng jué dìng fēng xiǎn yóu gè rén 、 lín lǐ 、 wù yè hái shì cái zhèng chéng dān 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， lín jiāng shì méi yǒu wán zhěng cǎi yòng rèn hé yī tào fāng àn ， ér shì zuò chū yī xiàng biān jiè qīng chǔ de zǔ hé jué dìng 。 měi hù měi yuè huò dé yǔ cháng zhù rén kǒu xiāng duì yīng de jī běn tóu fàng é dù ， zhè bù fèn fèi yòng gù dìng ， bǎo zhèng rì cháng shēng huó bú huì yīn lā jī liàng qīng wēi biàn huà ér shòu dào chōng jī ； chāo guò é dù hòu ， jū mín bì xū shǐ yòng zhuān yòng dài ， é wài fèi yòng suí tóu fàng liàng zēng jiā 。 xīn shēng ér jiā tíng 、 jīng shè qū hé shí de hù lǐ jiā tíng hé zàn shí shēng huó kùn nán zhě kě yǐ shēn qǐng miǎn fèi bǔ chōng dài ， dàn jiǎn miǎn shè yǒu qī xiàn ， xū yào dìng qī què rèn ， yǐ miǎn tè shū ān pái yǎn biàn chéng yǒng jiǔ lòu dòng 。 gōng yù lóu bù zài yīn zǒng liàng chāo biāo zì dòng xiàng quán tǐ zhù hù shōu fèi ， zhǐ yǒu zài wù yè néng gòu shuō míng yì cháng lái yuán bìng wán chéng gào zhī chéng xù hòu ， cái néng qǐ dòng zhuī jiǎo 。 shì zhèng fǔ tóng shí yāo qiú chāo shì 、 shè qū fú wù zhàn hé yè jiān biàn lì diàn xiāo shòu zhuān yòng dài ， fáng zhǐ gòu mǎi bù biàn biàn chéng wéi guī jiè kǒu 。 duì yú luàn rēng lā jī ， zhí fǎ rén yuán xiān jì lù dì diǎn hé shí jiān ， yōu xiān gǎi shàn tóu fàng shè shī ； zhǐ yǒu cún zài qīng chǔ zhèng jù shí cái zhuī jiū gè rén zé rèn ， bù néng ràng qīng jié gōng tōng guò fān chá sī rén lā jī lái dài tì zhèng shì diào chá 。

xīn zhì dù xiān zài wú tóng lǐ jí fù jìn sān gè jiē qū shì xíng 。 shí shī chū qī ， jū mín zuì cháng tí chū de wèn tí bú shì jià gé ， ér shì jiā tíng rén kǒu rú hé dēng jì 、 hù lǐ jiǎn miǎn zěn yàng xù bàn yǐ jí bān jiā hòu shèng yú zhuān yòng dài néng fǒu tuì huàn 。 shì zhèng fǔ jù cǐ jiǎn huà zhèng míng cái liào ， bìng yāo qiú fú wù zhàn gōng kāi chǔ lǐ qī xiàn 。 jǐ gè yuè hòu ， shì diǎn méi yǒu bèi xuān bù wèi mǒu yī tào lǐ lùn de shèng lì ， shì zhèng fǔ zhǐ gōng bù le tóu sù lèi xíng 、 wéi guī chǔ zhì hé liú chéng tiáo zhěng ， méi yǒu yòng dān yī píng jūn fèi yòng lái zhèng míng zhì dù wán měi 。 wú tóng lǐ yè zhǔ wěi yuán huì yě qǔ xiāo le yuán xiān zhǔn bèi shí xíng de quán lóu fá kuǎn ， gǎi wéi tí xǐng yì cháng tóu fàng bìng xié zhù kùn nán jiā tíng shēn qǐng bǔ chōng é dù 。 zuì zhōng ， shì yì huì tōng guò zǔ hé fāng àn ， tóng shí guī dìng měi nián shěn chá jiǎn miǎn fù gài 、 fēi fǎ tóu fàng hé yī xiàn gōng zuò fù dān 。 lín jiāng shì de xuǎn zé shuō míng ， bǐ jiào gōng gòng shōu fèi zhì dù bù néng zhǐ wèn duō shù rén píng jūn zhī fù duō shǎo ， hái yào zhuī wèn zuì huài qíng kuàng xià shuí huì tū rán fù bù qǐ 、 shuí huì tì mò shēng rén chéng dān zé rèn ， yǐ jí shuí bì xū chǔ lǐ zhì dù liú xià de má fán 。 píng jūn biǎo xiàn jué dìng fāng àn shì fǒu jīng jì ， fēng xiǎn fēn bù zé jué dìng tā shì fǒu gōng píng 、 kě zhí xíng bìng néng cháng qī huò dé xìn rèn 。
translation: Linjiang is a tourist city with a dense network of waterways. In recent years, waste transfer stations in the old city have often operated beyond capacity, and garbage bags have even piled up on sidewalks in mixed commercial and residential neighborhoods along the river. The municipal government decided to reform the existing uniform waste disposal fee and proposed two alternatives. The first was a pay-per-bag system: residents would have to purchase designated bags bearing anti-counterfeiting marks, and the larger and more numerous the bags they used, the more they would pay. The second was a flat household fee: each household would pay a fixed monthly amount, and property management companies or community organizations would collect household waste centrally; if an entire building repeatedly exceeded its approved total allowance, its residents would then be charged an additional fee. After making estimates, the finance department concluded that if the total amount of waste did not change significantly, the two systems would result in little difference in average spending for ordinary households. Initial news reports therefore reduced the debate to “bags or bills,” as though only the form of payment differed. At the public hearing, however, people quickly discovered that the averages obscured more important questions: when waste suddenly increased, which household would bear the additional cost, and when someone evaded payment, who would end up shouldering the resulting administrative costs?

Supporters of the pay-per-bag system argued that it would transmit price signals directly to individuals. If a household voluntarily reduced its use of disposable products, repaired old items, and sorted its waste carefully, it could buy fewer designated bags; those who produced more waste would pay more. The system appeared to assign responsibility clearly and prevented people who conserved resources from sharing the costs of those who wasted them. Opponents, however, pointed out that households cannot always control how much waste they generate. Newborn babies require large numbers of diapers, bedridden patients generate caregiving waste, and the amount of waste may also rise temporarily during holidays or when people move. For households with stable incomes, buying a few extra bags would mean only a minor fluctuation; for elderly people living alone, temporarily unemployed people, or families with several children, the same fluctuation could cut into spending on food and transportation. Moreover, the more effectively the price of designated bags encouraged conservation, the more likely it was to induce evasion. Some people might stuff ordinary bags into public trash cans, while others might take their garbage to neighborhoods where inspections were absent, leaving sanitation workers to identify and reject it and deal with disputes. Risks that appeared to be borne by those who generated the waste might ultimately be transferred to public spaces and frontline workers.

The flat household fee appeared more stable. Residents would know in advance how much they had to pay each month and would not have to worry about illness, moving, or holiday celebrations causing their bills to rise suddenly; communities would also have no need to inspect every bag, making collection and transportation relatively simple. Yet this system concentrated another kind of risk on those who followed the rules. If a building was assessed according to its total waste, some residents might continually discard large quantities, while the resulting additional charges could be shared by everyone in the building. Responsibility was especially likely to be unclear in apartment buildings with frequent tenant turnover: it was often difficult to determine who had generated the waste and whether payment should be recovered from the landlord or the tenant. More troublingly, a fixed fee weakened the personal reward for reducing waste. Even residents who carefully sorted their waste and handled food scraps and recyclables well could not immediately lower their expenses, and over time they might lose motivation. To prevent an entire building from exceeding its allowance, property management companies might also impose internal rules stricter than those of the municipal government, or even restrict disposal times. Thus, although the government would provide households with stable fees, it would leave communities with the risks of monitoring neighbors, resolving disputes, and bearing the consequences of collective excess.

The conflict at the hearing became concrete after a representative of the Wutongli residential community spoke. The community was home both to young tenants and to many elderly people who needed long-term care. The head of the homeowners’ committee supported the flat fee because he worried that a pay-per-bag system would force residents with limited mobility to purchase designated bags repeatedly. A restaurant employee, however, opposed collective additional charges because she ate at the restaurant during the day, generated very little waste at home, and did not want to bear the cost of excess waste produced by short-term tenants. A representative of sanitation workers added that if the city emphasized only that “those who pollute must pay” without providing convenient purchasing channels and reasonable exemptions, illegal dumping would usually increase sanitation workers’ workload before it punished those evading payment. The meeting consequently stopped debating which system was “cheaper overall” and turned instead to three specific questions: whether people unable to reduce their waste should bear price fluctuations, whether communities unable to identify those responsible should face collective penalties, and whether frontline personnel had sufficient resources to handle violations. The municipal government also acknowledged that no proposal could eliminate risk; it could only determine whether that risk would be borne by individuals, neighbors, property management companies, or the public budget.

After discussion, Linjiang did not adopt either proposal in full, but instead made a clearly bounded decision to combine them. Each household would receive a basic monthly disposal allowance corresponding to the number of permanent residents, with a fixed fee for that portion to ensure that ordinary life would not be disrupted by minor changes in waste volume. Once the allowance was exceeded, residents would have to use designated bags, and the additional cost would increase with the amount discarded. Families with newborns, caregiving households verified by the community, and people experiencing temporary financial hardship could apply for free supplementary bags, but the exemptions would be time-limited and would require periodic confirmation to prevent special arrangements from becoming permanent loopholes. Apartment buildings would no longer automatically charge all residents when their total waste exceeded the limit. Additional charges could be pursued only after the property management company identified the source of the abnormal amount and completed the notification procedure. The municipal government also required supermarkets, community service centers, and late-night convenience stores to sell designated bags, so that difficulty purchasing them could not become an excuse for violations. In cases of illegal dumping, enforcement officers would first record the place and time and give priority to improving disposal facilities. Individual responsibility would be pursued only when clear evidence existed, and sanitation workers could not be made to search through private garbage as a substitute for a formal investigation.

The new system was first piloted in Wutongli and three nearby neighborhoods. During the initial phase, residents’ most frequent questions concerned not prices, but how household members should be registered, how caregiving exemptions could be renewed, and whether unused designated bags could be returned or exchanged after a move. In response, the municipal government simplified the required documentation and instructed service centers to publish processing deadlines. Several months later, the pilot was not declared a victory for either theory. The municipal government published only the types of complaints received, the handling of violations, and procedural adjustments, rather than using a single average fee to claim that the system was perfect. The Wutongli homeowners’ committee also abandoned its planned building-wide fines, choosing instead to issue reminders about unusual disposal activity and help struggling families apply for supplementary allowances. Ultimately, the city council adopted the combined system and required annual reviews of exemption coverage, illegal dumping, and frontline workloads. Linjiang’s choice demonstrated that comparing public fee systems requires asking not only how much most people pay on average, but also who might suddenly be unable to pay in the worst-case scenario, who might be held responsible for strangers’ actions, and who would have to deal with the problems left behind by the system. Average performance determines whether a system is economical, while the distribution of risk determines whether it is fair, workable, and capable of earning lasting trust.

articles.title: 临江市如何选择降温投资：高反射改造与绿荫网络之争
articles.summary: 临江市阶段报告显示，高反射设施与绿荫网络的平均降温幅度相近，但二者在见效速度、空间分布、维护责任和社会效益方面差异明显。市政府最终放弃非此即彼的选择，按照街区条件组合投资，并建立长期评估与调整机制。
articles.topic: 临江市如何选择降温投资：高反射改造与绿荫网络之争
paragraphs: 七月中旬，临江市连续出现高温天气。位于旧城区的长安路菜市场缺少遮蔽物，摊主不得不用纸板挡住阳光；河东新区虽然道路宽阔，却因大片水泥广场吸收热量，傍晚仍然闷热。此前，市政府准备启动新一轮城市降温工程，并委托规划院比较两种投资路径。第一种以高反射屋顶、浅色路面、固定遮阳棚和公共喷雾设施为主，强调迅速降低建筑与道路表面的温度；第二种以行道树、口袋公园、透水地面和连续绿廊为核心，希望借助树荫、蒸腾和空气流动改善街区环境。阶段报告公布后，一个结论格外引人注意：从全市平均情况看，两条路径带来的降温幅度相近。这个看似明确的结论，却没有使决策变得更容易，反而引发了激烈争论。

支持第一条路径的财政部门认为，工程设施施工周期较短，成本边界相对清楚，也容易验收。学校屋顶、公交站台和大型停车场都能在较短时间内完成改造，不必等待树木生长。尤其在建筑密集、地下管线复杂的老城区，种植高大乔木往往受到空间限制，而更换屋面材料或增加遮阳结构具有较强的可操作性。然而，这条路径也存在明显缺陷。浅色材料容易积灰，反射效果会随着维护不足而下降；喷雾设施需要持续用水并定期清洗；部分高反射表面如果位置设计不当，还可能把强光投向附近住宅。更重要的是，这些设施主要解决暴露在阳光下的局部热量问题，却未必能为步行者提供舒适、连续的通行环境。一个屋顶变凉，并不意味着住在顶层的老人能够安全地走到社区诊所。

园林和公共卫生部门更倾向于第二条路径。他们指出，树木与绿地不仅能够遮阳，还能改善雨水管理、降低噪声，并为居民提供休息和交往的空间。若把学校、菜市场、养老院和公交站之间的零散绿地连接起来，降温便不再是若干孤立项目，而会成为覆盖日常生活路线的公共网络。不过，生态投资同样没有想象中简单。幼树无法立即形成浓密树冠，树种若不适应本地土壤与降水条件，后续养护负担会不断增加。狭窄街巷还可能出现树根挤压路面、枝叶遮挡店铺招牌等矛盾。临江市过去也曾重建设、轻管理，一些小公园建成后缺乏稳定经费，灌溉设备损坏，绿化效果逐年减弱。因此，不能仅凭“自然方案”这一名称，就假定它必然更经济、更公平。

争议的关键在于，平均降温幅度掩盖了时间和空间上的差异。在市议事厅举行的公开说明会上，财政人员把两条曲线放在同一张图上，主张优先选择见效更快的工程设施；长安路的社区代表却提出，居民真正关心的不是全市平均温度，而是中午买菜时有没有树荫，孩子放学时能否避开灼热路面。河东新区的物业负责人则担心，大量新增绿地会把养护责任转嫁给小区。双方一度把讨论简化为“立即见效”与“长期价值”的对抗。负责评审的副市长随后要求各部门停止争论哪条路径绝对优越，改为回答三个具体问题：哪些地点必须在下一个夏季前降温，哪些街区具备形成绿荫网络的条件，以及设施建成后由谁维护、经费从何处持续支付。

经过重新梳理，市政府作出了一项分区组合的决定，而不是把预算机械地平均分给两类项目。对医院急诊入口、学校操场、露天公交换乘区等高风险场所，先铺设经过眩光评估的高反射材料，并安装可维修的遮阳设施，以便尽快减少直接暴晒。对居民步行频繁、沿线又有种植空间的街道，则优先补齐行道树，在菜市场、社区食堂和养老院之间形成连续阴影。地下管线密集的窄巷不强行种大树，而采用墙面绿化、小型棚架和浅色铺装。新建项目的资金也不再只计算施工费，而要同时列出清洁、灌溉、修剪和更换费用。市政府还规定，评估不能只看某个测温点的变化，必须记录老人、儿童、户外劳动者常用路线在不同时段的遮阴状况，并公开居民投诉与维护进度。

决定实施后的第一个夏季，临江市没有出现所谓一劳永逸的奇迹，却产生了可以看见的变化。公交换乘区先完成遮阳改造，长安路市场周边则调整了摊位和停车位置，为树木留出连续生长空间。检查人员发现一处浅色广场在午后造成反光，施工单位随即降低材料反射强度；另有几段新植绿带因商户卸货受损，街道办便重新划定装卸时间，而不是简单拆除绿化。阶段报告原本只说明两条路径的平均降温幅度接近，最终决策却揭示了平均值之外更重要的事实：城市降温并不是购买某种技术，而是在紧迫需求、长期收益与维护能力之间建立具体秩序。临江市因此保留了两条路径，也为它们划定了不同职责。真正有效的投资，不在于宣布哪一种方案获胜，而在于让每一笔资金对应明确地点、明确人群和能够长期承担的责任。
pinyin: qī yuè zhōng xún ， lín jiāng shì lián xù chū xiàn gāo wēn tiān qì 。 wèi yú jiù chéng qū de cháng ān lù cài shì chǎng quē shǎo zhē bì wù ， tān zhǔ bù dé bù yòng zhǐ bǎn dǎng zhù yáng guāng ； hé dōng xīn qū suī rán dào lù kuān kuò ， què yīn dà piàn shuǐ ní guǎng chǎng xī shōu rè liàng ， bàng wǎn réng rán mēn rè 。 cǐ qián ， shì zhèng fǔ zhǔn bèi qǐ dòng xīn yī lún chéng shì jiàng wēn gōng chéng ， bìng wěi tuō guī huà yuàn bǐ jiào liǎng zhǒng tóu zī lù jìng 。 dì yī zhǒng yǐ gāo fǎn shè wū dǐng 、 qiǎn sè lù miàn 、 gù dìng zhē yáng péng hé gōng gòng pēn wù shè shī wéi zhǔ ， qiáng diào xùn sù jiàng dī jiàn zhù yǔ dào lù biǎo miàn de wēn dù ； dì èr zhǒng yǐ xíng dào shù 、 kǒu dài gōng yuán 、 tòu shuǐ dì miàn hé lián xù lǜ láng wèi hé xīn ， xī wàng jiè zhù shù yīn 、 zhēng téng hé kōng qì liú dòng gǎi shàn jiē qū huán jìng 。 jiē duàn bào gào gōng bù hòu ， yí gè jié lùn gé wài yǐn rén zhù yì ： cóng quán shì píng jūn qíng kuàng kàn ， liǎng tiáo lù jìng dài lái de jiàng wēn fú dù xiāng jìn 。 zhè ge kàn shì míng què de jié lùn ， què méi yǒu shǐ jué cè biàn dé gèng róng yì ， fǎn ér yǐn fā le jī liè zhēng lùn 。

zhī chí dì yī tiáo lù jìng de cái zhèng bù mén rèn wéi ， gōng chéng shè shī shī gōng zhōu qī jiào duǎn ， chéng běn biān jiè xiāng duì qīng chǔ ， yě róng yì yàn shōu 。 xué xiào wū dǐng 、 gōng jiāo zhàn tái hé dà xíng tíng chē chǎng dōu néng zài jiào duǎn shí jiān nèi wán chéng gǎi zào ， bù bì děng dài shù mù shēng zhǎng 。 yóu qí zài jiàn zhù mì jí 、 dì xià guǎn xiàn fù zá de lǎo chéng qū ， zhòng zhí gāo dà qiáo mù wǎng wǎng shòu dào kōng jiān xiàn zhì ， ér gēng huàn wū miàn cái liào huò zēng jiā zhē yáng jié gòu jù yǒu jiào qiáng de kě cāo zuò xìng 。 rán ér ， zhè tiáo lù jìng yě cún zài míng xiǎn quē xiàn 。 qiǎn sè cái liào róng yì jī huī ， fǎn shè xiào guǒ huì suí zhe wéi hù bù zú ér xià jiàng ； pēn wù shè shī xū yào chí xù yòng shuǐ bìng dìng qī qīng xǐ ； bù fèn gāo fǎn shè biǎo miàn rú guǒ wèi zhì shè jì bù dàng ， hái kě néng bǎ qiáng guāng tóu xiàng fù jìn zhù zhái 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， zhè xiē shè shī zhǔ yào jiě jué bào lù zài yáng guāng xià de jú bù rè liàng wèn tí ， què wèi bì néng wèi bù xíng zhě tí gōng shū shì 、 lián xù de tōng xíng huán jìng 。 yí gè wū dǐng biàn liáng ， bìng bù yì wèi zhe zhù zài dǐng céng de lǎo rén néng gòu ān quán dì zǒu dào shè qū zhěn suǒ 。

yuán lín hé gōng gòng wèi shēng bù mén gèng qīng xiàng yú dì èr tiáo lù jìng 。 tā men zhǐ chū ， shù mù yǔ lǜ dì bù jǐn néng gòu zhē yáng ， hái néng gǎi shàn yǔ shuǐ guǎn lǐ 、 jiàng dī zào shēng ， bìng wèi jū mín tí gōng xiū xī hé jiāo wǎng de kōng jiān 。 ruò bǎ xué xiào 、 cài shì chǎng 、 yǎng lǎo yuàn hé gōng jiāo zhàn zhī jiān de líng sǎn lǜ dì lián jiē qǐ lái ， jiàng wēn biàn bù zài shì ruò gān gū lì xiàng mù ， ér huì chéng wéi fù gài rì cháng shēng huó lù xiàn de gōng gòng wǎng luò 。 bù guò ， shēng tài tóu zī tóng yàng méi yǒu xiǎng xiàng zhōng jiǎn dān 。 yòu shù wú fǎ lì jí xíng chéng nóng mì shù guān ， shù zhǒng ruò bù shì yīng běn dì tǔ rǎng yǔ jiàng shuǐ tiáo jiàn ， hòu xù yǎng hù fù dān huì bù duàn zēng jiā 。 xiá zhǎi jiē xiàng hái kě néng chū xiàn shù gēn jǐ yā lù miàn 、 zhī yè zhē dǎng diàn pù zhāo pái děng máo dùn 。 lín jiāng shì guò qù yě céng chóng jiàn shè 、 qīng guǎn lǐ ， yī xiē xiǎo gōng yuán jiàn chéng hòu quē fá wěn dìng jīng fèi ， guàn gài shè bèi sǔn huài ， lǜ huà xiào guǒ zhú nián jiǎn ruò 。 yīn cǐ ， bù néng jǐn píng “ zì rán fāng àn ” zhè yī míng chēng ， jiù jiǎ dìng tā bì rán gèng jīng jì 、 gèng gōng píng 。

zhēng yì de guān jiàn zài yú ， píng jūn jiàng wēn fú dù yǎn gài le shí jiān hé kōng jiān shàng de chā yì 。 zài shì yì shì tīng jǔ xíng de gōng kāi shuō míng huì shàng ， cái zhèng rén yuán bǎ liǎng tiáo qū xiàn fàng zài tóng yī zhāng tú shàng ， zhǔ zhāng yōu xiān xuǎn zé jiàn xiào gèng kuài de gōng chéng shè shī ； cháng ān lù de shè qū dài biǎo què tí chū ， jū mín zhēn zhèng guān xīn de bú shì quán shì píng jūn wēn dù ， ér shì zhōng wǔ mǎi cài shí yǒu méi yǒu shù yīn ， hái zi fàng xué shí néng fǒu bì kāi zhuó rè lù miàn 。 hé dōng xīn qū de wù yè fù zé rén zé dān xīn ， dà liàng xīn zēng lǜ dì huì bǎ yǎng hù zé rèn zhuǎn jià gěi xiǎo qū 。 shuāng fāng yí dù bǎ tǎo lùn jiǎn huà wèi “ lì jí jiàn xiào ” yǔ “ cháng qī jià zhí ” de duì kàng 。 fù zé píng shěn de fù shì zhǎng suí hòu yāo qiú gè bù mén tíng zhǐ zhēng lùn nǎ tiáo lù jìng jué duì yōu yuè ， gǎi wéi huí dá sān gè jù tǐ wèn tí ： nǎ xiē dì diǎn bì xū zài xià yí gè xià jì qián jiàng wēn ， nǎ xiē jiē qū jù bèi xíng chéng lǜ yīn wǎng luò de tiáo jiàn ， yǐ jí shè shī jiàn chéng hòu yóu shuí wéi hù 、 jīng fèi cóng hé chù chí xù zhī fù 。

jīng guò chóng xīn shū lǐ ， shì zhèng fǔ zuò chū le yī xiàng fēn qū zǔ hé de jué dìng ， ér bú shì bǎ yù suàn jī xiè dì píng jūn fēn gěi liǎng lèi xiàng mù 。 duì yī yuàn jí zhěn rù kǒu 、 xué xiào cāo chǎng 、 lù tiān gōng jiāo huàn chéng qū děng gāo fēng xiǎn chǎng suǒ ， xiān pū shè jīng guò xuàn guāng píng gū de gāo fǎn shè cái liào ， bìng ān zhuāng kě wéi xiū de zhē yáng shè shī ， yǐ biàn jǐn kuài jiǎn shǎo zhí jiē pù shài 。 duì jū mín bù xíng pín fán 、 yán xiàn yòu yǒu zhǒng zhí kōng jiān de jiē dào ， zé yōu xiān bǔ qí xíng dào shù ， zài cài shì chǎng 、 shè qū shí táng hé yǎng lǎo yuàn zhī jiān xíng chéng lián xù yīn yǐng 。 dì xià guǎn xiàn mì jí de zhǎi xiàng bù qiáng xíng zhǒng dà shù ， ér cǎi yòng qiáng miàn lǜ huà 、 xiǎo xíng péng jià hé qiǎn sè pù zhuāng 。 xīn jiàn xiàng mù dì zī jīn yě bù zài zhǐ jì suàn shī gōng fèi ， ér yào tóng shí liè chū qīng jié 、 guàn gài 、 xiū jiǎn hé gēng huàn fèi yòng 。 shì zhèng fǔ hái guī dìng ， píng gū bù néng zhǐ kàn mǒu gè cè wēn diǎn de biàn huà ， bì xū jì lù lǎo rén 、 ér tóng 、 hù wài láo dòng zhě cháng yòng lù xiàn zài bù tóng shí duàn de zhē yīn zhuàng kuàng ， bìng gōng kāi jū mín tóu sù yǔ wéi hù jìn dù 。

jué dìng shí shī hòu de dì yí gè xià jì ， lín jiāng shì méi yǒu chū xiàn suǒ wèi yì láo yǒng yì de qí jì ， què chǎn shēng le kě yǐ kàn jiàn de biàn huà 。 gōng jiāo huàn chéng qū xiān wán chéng zhē yáng gǎi zào ， cháng ān lù shì chǎng zhōu biān zé tiáo zhěng le tān wèi hé tíng chē wèi zhì ， wèi shù mù liú chū lián xù shēng zhǎng kōng jiān 。 jiǎn chá rén yuán fā xiàn yī chù qiǎn sè guǎng chǎng zài wǔ hòu zào chéng fǎn guāng ， shī gōng dān wèi suí jí jiàng dī cái liào fǎn shè qiáng dù ； lìng yǒu jǐ duàn xīn zhí lǜ dài yīn shāng hù xiè huò shòu sǔn ， jiē dào bàn biàn chóng xīn huà dìng zhuāng xiè shí jiān ， ér bú shì jiǎn dān chāi chú lǜ huà 。 jiē duàn bào gào yuán běn zhǐ shuō míng liǎng tiáo lù jìng de píng jūn jiàng wēn fú dù jiē jìn ， zuì zhōng jué cè què jiē shì le píng jūn zhí zhī wài gèng zhòng yào de shì shí ： chéng shì jiàng wēn bìng bú shì gòu mǎi mǒu zhǒng jì shù ， ér shì zài jǐn pò xū qiú 、 cháng qī shōu yì yǔ wéi hù néng lì zhī jiān jiàn lì jù tǐ zhì xù 。 lín jiāng shì yīn cǐ bǎo liú le liǎng tiáo lù jìng ， yě wèi tā men huà dìng le bù tóng zhí zé 。 zhēn zhèng yǒu xiào de tóu zī ， bù zài yú xuān bù nǎ yī zhǒng fāng àn huò shèng ， ér zài yú ràng měi yī bǐ zī jīn duì yìng míng què dì diǎn 、 míng què rén qún hé néng gòu cháng qī chéng dān de zé rèn 。
translation: In mid-July, Linjiang City experienced several consecutive days of high temperatures. At the Chang'an Road produce market in the old city, the lack of shelter forced vendors to use cardboard to block the sun. Although roads in the Hedong New District were wide, its vast concrete plazas absorbed heat, leaving the area oppressively hot even in the evening. The municipal government had previously prepared to launch a new round of urban cooling projects and commissioned the planning institute to compare two investment approaches. The first centered on highly reflective roofs, light-colored pavement, permanent canopies, and public misting facilities, emphasizing rapid reductions in the surface temperatures of buildings and roads. The second focused on street trees, pocket parks, permeable surfaces, and continuous green corridors, with the aim of improving neighborhood conditions through shade, transpiration, and air circulation. After the interim report was released, one conclusion attracted particular attention: on average across the city, the two approaches produced similar degrees of cooling. Yet this seemingly clear conclusion did not make the decision any easier; instead, it sparked fierce debate.

The finance department, which supported the first approach, argued that engineered facilities had shorter construction periods, relatively predictable cost limits, and were also easier to inspect and approve. School roofs, bus stops, and large parking lots could all be renovated in a relatively short time without waiting for trees to grow. In the old city in particular, where buildings were densely packed and underground utility lines were complex, planting tall trees was often constrained by limited space, whereas replacing roofing materials or adding shade structures was highly practicable. This approach, however, also had obvious shortcomings. Light-colored materials readily accumulated dust, and their reflective performance would decline if maintenance was inadequate. Misting facilities required a continuous water supply and regular cleaning. Some highly reflective surfaces, if poorly positioned, could also direct intense glare toward nearby homes. More importantly, these facilities mainly addressed localized heat in places exposed to sunlight, but did not necessarily provide pedestrians with a comfortable, continuous travel environment. A cooler roof did not mean that an older person living on the top floor could walk safely to the community clinic.

The landscaping and public health departments favored the second approach. They noted that trees and green spaces could not only provide shade but also improve stormwater management, reduce noise, and give residents places to rest and socialize. If the scattered green spaces between schools, produce markets, nursing homes, and bus stops were connected, cooling would no longer consist of several isolated projects but would become a public network covering people's everyday routes. Ecological investment, however, was likewise not as simple as it might seem. Young trees could not immediately form dense canopies, and if the species planted were unsuited to local soil and rainfall conditions, the burden of subsequent maintenance would continue to grow. In narrow streets and alleys, tree roots might also push up pavement, while branches and leaves could obscure shop signs. In the past, Linjiang City had likewise emphasized construction while neglecting management. After some small parks were completed, they lacked stable funding, irrigation equipment fell into disrepair, and the landscaping became less effective year by year. It was therefore impossible to assume that an approach would necessarily be more economical and equitable merely because it was called a “nature-based solution.”

The crux of the dispute was that the average degree of cooling concealed differences across time and space. At a public briefing held in the city council chamber, finance officials placed two curves on the same chart and argued that engineered facilities, which would deliver results more quickly, should be prioritized. Community representatives from Chang'an Road countered that residents were not truly concerned about the city's average temperature, but about whether there was shade when they shopped for groceries at noon and whether children could avoid scorching pavement on their way home from school. Property managers in the Hedong New District, meanwhile, worried that the addition of extensive green space would shift maintenance responsibilities onto residential communities. For a time, the two sides reduced the discussion to a conflict between “immediate results” and “long-term value.” The deputy mayor overseeing the review then instructed all departments to stop arguing over which approach was absolutely superior and instead answer three specific questions: which locations had to be cooled before the following summer, which neighborhoods had the conditions needed to create a network of shaded greenery, and who would maintain the facilities after completion and where the funding for their ongoing upkeep would come from.

After reassessing the issue, the municipal government decided on a zoned combination of measures rather than mechanically dividing the budget equally between the two types of projects. At high-risk locations such as hospital emergency entrances, school playgrounds, and open-air bus interchange areas, highly reflective materials that had undergone glare assessments would be installed first, along with repairable shade structures, to reduce direct exposure to the sun as quickly as possible. On streets frequently used by pedestrians and with sufficient planting space along their routes, priority would instead be given to filling gaps in rows of street trees and creating continuous shade between produce markets, community dining halls, and nursing homes. Large trees would not be forcibly planted in narrow alleys crowded with underground utility lines; wall greenery, small trellises, and light-colored paving would be used instead. Funding for new projects would no longer cover construction costs alone but would also itemize the costs of cleaning, irrigation, pruning, and replacement. The municipal government further stipulated that evaluations could not rely solely on changes at a single temperature-monitoring point. They had to record shade conditions at different times along routes commonly used by older people, children, and outdoor workers, while making residents' complaints and maintenance progress public.

During the first summer after the decision was implemented, Linjiang City saw no supposedly permanent, once-and-for-all miracle, but visible changes did occur. Shade improvements were completed first at bus interchange areas, while stall and parking locations around the Chang'an Road market were rearranged to leave continuous space for trees to grow. Inspectors found that one light-colored plaza produced glare in the afternoon, so the contractor promptly reduced the material's reflectivity. Several newly planted green strips were damaged by merchants unloading goods, so the subdistrict office rescheduled loading and unloading hours rather than simply removing the greenery. The interim report had originally stated only that the two approaches achieved similar average degrees of cooling, but the final decision revealed a more important fact beyond the averages: urban cooling was not about purchasing a particular technology, but about establishing a concrete order among urgent needs, long-term benefits, and maintenance capacity. Linjiang City therefore retained both approaches while assigning each a distinct role. Truly effective investment lies not in declaring one approach the winner, but in ensuring that every expenditure corresponds to a clearly defined location, a clearly defined population, and a responsibility that can be sustained over the long term.

articles.title: 相近的成绩之后：明川二中教材改革的重新选择
articles.summary: 明川市第二中学比较纸质教材与混合教材的阶段报告显示，两组学生期末平均成绩相近。围绕这一结果，教师、学生和家长对学习效率、阅读深度、技术负担及教育公平展开争论。学校最终放弃简单判断教材优劣，决定保留纸质教材作为共同基础，同时有条件地引入数字资源，并通过调整课堂任务与评价方式推动改革。
articles.topic: 相近的成绩之后：明川二中教材改革的重新选择
paragraphs: 秋季学期结束后，明川市第二中学在图书馆报告厅召开教材改革阶段说明会。此前，高一年级两个教学进度相同的班分别使用纸质教材和混合教材：前者以课本、练习册和教师板书为主，后者除保留核心课文外，还使用电子批注、音视频材料、在线讨论区和分层练习。校方原本希望借此判断哪一种教材更适合下一学年的课程。然而，阶段报告给出的结论并不鲜明：两组学生的期末平均成绩相近，常规测验中的差距也不足以支持学校立即全面更换教材。这个看似平静的结果反而引发了争议，因为教师、学生和家长都发现，平均成绩掩盖了两种学习方式在过程、习惯和负担上的明显差别。

支持混合教材的教师首先提出，期末试卷只能测量部分学习成果，无法完整呈现学生搜索、筛选和组织信息的能力。在使用混合教材的班级里，学生可以反复收听课文录音，对照地图理解作品背景，也能在讨论区阅读不同解释。遇到抽象概念时，动态示意图往往比一页文字更容易帮助学生建立初步认识。一些平时不愿当众发言的学生，也愿意先在网上写下观点，再到课堂上参与讨论。教师还可以根据作业中暴露的问题补充材料，而不必等到统一印刷的新版本出版。在他们看来，混合教材的价值不应只由一次考试决定，它更重要的作用，是扩大接触知识的途径，并使课堂从单向讲解转向持续交流。

但纸质教材组的教师提出了相反意见。他们发现，纸面阅读虽然缺少声音和动画，却更有利于学生保持长时间注意。学生能在同一页上看到段落关系，把批注、箭头和疑问集中留在稳定的位置，复习时也更容易恢复当时的思考路径。相比之下，混合教材中的链接不断把学习者带往新的页面，丰富的信息有时并未加深理解，反而造成选择疲劳。部分学生表面上完成了许多互动任务，实际阅读原文的时间却缩短了。还有教师指出，电子平台提供的即时提示容易让学生过早寻找答案。一旦系统撤去帮助，他们未必能够独立处理复杂文本。因此，技术带来的便利如果没有清楚边界，也可能削弱耐心、记忆和判断。

争论很快超出了教学方法本身。家长代表顾岚在说明会上说，她的女儿使用家中电脑学习时十分顺利，但同组一名同学只能依靠旧手机查看材料，屏幕小、网络也不稳定。两人名义上使用同一套混合教材，实际获得的学习条件并不相同。另一些家长担心，孩子以查资料为由频繁切换应用，家庭很难判断他们是在学习还是娱乐。学生代表周启则提醒大家，纸质教材也并非天然公平：有人能够购买词典、参考书和课外读物，有人只能使用学校发放的课本。真正的问题不是纸张与屏幕谁更先进，而是学校能否保证必要资源、明确使用规则，并教会学生在信息过多时作出选择。

阶段报告的撰写小组随后重新查看课堂观察记录、学生作业、教师备课笔记和家长反馈。他们没有继续追问哪一组“获胜”，而是把问题改成：两种教材分别在什么任务中有效，又需要什么条件。记录显示，阅读篇幅较长、结构严密的文章时，固定版面便于反复定位和整体把握；学习发音、观察过程或比较多个地区的资料时，数字资源更具优势。混合教材组中，自我管理能力较强的学生能主动安排进度，缺乏规划的学生却容易在大量选项面前拖延。纸质教材组的课堂秩序较稳定，但如果教师仍以追求唯一答案为目标，学生的讨论空间也会受到限制。由此可见，教材只是学习环境的一部分，教学任务、设备条件和教师指导共同决定了实际效果。

校务会议最终没有批准全面取消纸质教材，也没有把混合教材退回试验状态。学校作出一项更具体的决定：所有学生继续领取统一的纸质核心教材，以保证基本内容稳定可得；需要声音、影像、更新资料或协作练习的单元，再由教师选择经过审核的数字资源。电子任务必须说明学习目标、预计步骤和离线替代方案，未经审核的链接不得进入必做任务清单。学校机房在课后向有需要的学生开放，同时允许学生借用设备。教师培训也从学习平台操作转向课程设计，重点讨论何时应让技术介入、何时应让学生关掉屏幕，独立完成阅读、推理和书面表达。

新方案实施后，最明显的变化不是成绩突然上升，而是课堂中的选择变得更有依据。教师不再为了显得新颖而增加视频，也不再因为担心分心而拒绝一切数字工具。学生阅读长文时先在纸上标出论点和证据，处理需要多种材料的问题时再进入共享资料库；完成在线讨论后，还要把零散意见整理成连贯文字。学期末，学校把这次比较写入教材选用说明：期末平均成绩相近，并不意味着两种教材毫无差别，也不能证明其中一种适用于所有人。真正值得保留的结论是，纸质教材提供稳定、专注和共同起点，混合教材提供延伸、反馈和多样表达；只有当学校承担起资源保障与教学设计的责任，两者的结合才不会成为简单叠加，而会转化为更成熟的学习方式。
pinyin: qiū jì xué qī jié shù hòu ， míng chuān shì dì èr zhōng xué zài tú shū guǎn bào gào tīng zhào kāi jiào cái gǎi gé jiē duàn shuō míng huì 。 cǐ qián ， gāo yì nián jí liǎng gè jiào xué jìn dù xiāng tóng de bān fēn bié shǐ yòng zhǐ zhì jiào cái hé hùn hé jiào cái ： qián zhě yǐ kè běn 、 liàn xí cè hé jiào shī bǎn shū wéi zhǔ ， hòu zhě chú bǎo liú hé xīn kè wén wài ， hái shǐ yòng diàn zi pī zhù 、 yīn shì pín cái liào 、 zài xiàn tǎo lùn qū hé fēn céng liàn xí 。 xiào fāng yuán běn xī wàng jiè cǐ pàn duàn nǎ yī zhǒng jiào cái gèng shì hé xià yī xué nián de kè chéng 。 rán ér ， jiē duàn bào gào gěi chū de jié lùn bìng bù xiān míng ： liǎng zǔ xué shēng de qī mò píng jūn chéng jì xiāng jìn ， cháng guī cè yàn zhōng de chā jù yě bù zú yǐ zhī chí xué xiào lì jí quán miàn gēng huàn jiào cái 。 zhè ge kàn shì píng jìng de jié guǒ fǎn ér yǐn fā le zhēng yì ， yīn wèi jiào shī 、 xué shēng hé jiā zhǎng dōu fā xiàn ， píng jūn chéng jì yǎn gài le liǎng zhǒng xué xí fāng shì zài guò chéng 、 xí guàn hé fù dān shàng de míng xiǎn chā bié 。

zhī chí hùn hé jiào cái de jiào shī shǒu xiān tí chū ， qī mò shì juàn zhǐ néng cè liáng bù fèn xué xí chéng guǒ ， wú fǎ wán zhěng chéng xiàn xué shēng sōu suǒ 、 shāi xuǎn hé zǔ zhī xìn xī de néng lì 。 zài shǐ yòng hùn hé jiào cái de bān jí lǐ ， xué shēng kě yǐ fǎn fù shōu tīng kè wén lù yīn ， duì zhào dì tú lǐ jiě zuò pǐn bèi jǐng ， yě néng zài tǎo lùn qū yuè dú bù tóng jiě shì 。 yù dào chōu xiàng gài niàn shí ， dòng tài shì yì tú wǎng wǎng bǐ yī yè wén zì gèng róng yì bāng zhù xué shēng jiàn lì chū bù rèn shí 。 yī xiē píng shí bù yuàn dāng zhòng fā yán de xué shēng ， yě yuàn yì xiān zài wǎng shàng xiě xià guān diǎn ， zài dào kè táng shàng cān yù tǎo lùn 。 jiào shī hái kě yǐ gēn jù zuò yè zhōng bào lù de wèn tí bǔ chōng cái liào ， ér bù bì děng dào tǒng yī yìn shuā de xīn bǎn běn chū bǎn 。 zài tā men kàn lái ， hùn hé jiào cái de jià zhí bù yīng zhǐ yóu yī cì kǎo shì jué dìng ， tā gèng zhòng yào de zuò yòng ， shì kuò dà jiē chù zhī shí de tú jìng ， bìng shǐ kè táng cóng dān xiàng jiǎng jiě zhuǎn xiàng chí xù jiāo liú 。

dàn zhǐ zhì jiào cái zǔ de jiào shī tí chū le xiāng fǎn yì jiàn 。 tā men fā xiàn ， zhǐ miàn yuè dú suī rán quē shǎo shēng yīn hé dòng huà ， què gèng yǒu lì yú xué shēng bǎo chí zhǎng shí jiān zhù yì 。 xué shēng néng zài tóng yī yè shàng kàn dào duàn luò guān xì ， bǎ pī zhù 、 jiàn tóu hé yí wèn jí zhōng liú zài wěn dìng de wèi zhì ， fù xí shí yě gèng róng yì huī fù dāng shí de sī kǎo lù jìng 。 xiāng bǐ zhī xià ， hùn hé jiào cái zhōng de liàn jiē bù duàn bǎ xué xí zhě dài wǎng xīn de yè miàn ， fēng fù de xìn xī yǒu shí bìng wèi jiā shēn lǐ jiě ， fǎn ér zào chéng xuǎn zé pí láo 。 bù fèn xué shēng biǎo miàn shàng wán chéng le xǔ duō hù dòng rèn wù ， shí jì yuè dú yuán wén de shí jiān què suō duǎn le 。 hái yǒu jiào shī zhǐ chū ， diàn zi píng tái tí gōng de jí shí tí shì róng yì ràng xué shēng guò zǎo xún zhǎo dá àn 。 yí dàn xì tǒng chè qù bāng zhù ， tā men wèi bì néng gòu dú lì chǔ lǐ fù zá wén běn 。 yīn cǐ ， jì shù dài lái de biàn lì rú guǒ méi yǒu qīng chǔ biān jiè ， yě kě néng xuē ruò nài xīn 、 jì yì hé pàn duàn 。

zhēng lùn hěn kuài chāo chū le jiào xué fāng fǎ běn shēn 。 jiā zhǎng dài biǎo gù lán zài shuō míng huì shàng shuō ， tā de nǚ ér shǐ yòng jiā zhōng diàn nǎo xué xí shí shí fēn shùn lì ， dàn tóng zǔ yī míng tóng xué zhǐ néng yī kào jiù shǒu jī chá kàn cái liào ， píng mù xiǎo 、 wǎng luò yě bù wěn dìng 。 liǎng rén míng yì shàng shǐ yòng tóng yī tào hùn hé jiào cái ， shí jì huò dé de xué xí tiáo jiàn bìng bù xiāng tóng 。 lìng yī xiē jiā zhǎng dān xīn ， hái zi yǐ chá zī liào wèi yóu pín fán qiè huàn yìng yòng ， jiā tíng hěn nán pàn duàn tā men shì zài xué xí hái shì yú lè 。 xué shēng dài biǎo zhōu qǐ zé tí xǐng dà jiā ， zhǐ zhì jiào cái yě bìng fēi tiān rán gōng píng ： yǒu rén néng gòu gòu mǎi cí diǎn 、 cān kǎo shū hé kè wài dú wù ， yǒu rén zhǐ néng shǐ yòng xué xiào fā fàng de kè běn 。 zhēn zhèng de wèn tí bú shì zhǐ zhāng yǔ píng mù shuí gèng xiān jìn ， ér shì xué xiào néng fǒu bǎo zhèng bì yào zī yuán 、 míng què shǐ yòng guī zé ， bìng jiào huì xué shēng zài xìn xī guò duō shí zuò chū xuǎn zé 。

jiē duàn bào gào de zhuàn xiě xiǎo zǔ suí hòu chóng xīn chá kàn kè táng guān chá jì lù 、 xué shēng zuò yè 、 jiào shī bèi kè bǐ jì hé jiā zhǎng fǎn kuì 。 tā men méi yǒu jì xù zhuī wèn nǎ yī zǔ “ huò shèng ”， ér shì bǎ wèn tí gǎi chéng ： liǎng zhǒng jiào cái fēn bié zài shén me rèn wù zhōng yǒu xiào ， yòu xū yào shén me tiáo jiàn 。 jì lù xiǎn shì ， yuè dú piān fú jiào zhǎng 、 jié gòu yán mì de wén zhāng shí ， gù dìng bǎn miàn biàn yú fǎn fù dìng wèi hé zhěng tǐ bǎ wò ； xué xí fā yīn 、 guān chá guò chéng huò bǐ jiào duō gè dì qū de zī liào shí ， shù zì zī yuán gèng jù yōu shì 。 hùn hé jiào cái zǔ zhōng ， zì wǒ guǎn lǐ néng lì jiào qiáng de xué shēng néng zhǔ dòng ān pái jìn dù ， quē fá guī huà de xué shēng què róng yì zài dà liàng xuǎn xiàng miàn qián tuō yán 。 zhǐ zhì jiào cái zǔ de kè táng zhì xù jiào wěn dìng ， dàn rú guǒ jiào shī réng yǐ zhuī qiú wéi yī dá àn wèi mù biāo ， xué shēng de tǎo lùn kōng jiān yě huì shòu dào xiàn zhì 。 yóu cǐ kě jiàn ， jiào cái zhǐ shì xué xí huán jìng de yī bù fèn ， jiào xué rèn wù 、 shè bèi tiáo jiàn hé jiào shī zhǐ dǎo gòng tóng jué dìng le shí jì xiào guǒ 。

xiào wù huì yì zuì zhōng méi yǒu pī zhǔn quán miàn qǔ xiāo zhǐ zhì jiào cái ， yě méi yǒu bǎ hùn hé jiào cái tuì huí shì yàn zhuàng tài 。 xué xiào zuò chū yī xiàng gèng jù tǐ de jué dìng ： suǒ yǒu xué shēng jì xù lǐng qǔ tǒng yī de zhǐ zhì hé xīn jiào cái ， yǐ bǎo zhèng jī běn nèi róng wěn dìng kě dé ； xū yào shēng yīn 、 yǐng xiàng 、 gēng xīn zī liào huò xié zuò liàn xí de dān yuán ， zài yóu jiào shī xuǎn zé jīng guò shěn hé de shù zì zī yuán 。 diàn zi rèn wù bì xū shuō míng xué xí mù biāo 、 yù jì bù zhòu hé lí xiàn tì dài fāng àn ， wèi jīng shěn hé de liàn jiē bù dé jìn rù bì zuò rèn wù qīng dān 。 xué xiào jī fáng zài kè hòu xiàng yǒu xū yào de xué shēng kāi fàng ， tóng shí yǔn xǔ xué shēng jiè yòng shè bèi 。 jiào shī péi xùn yě cóng xué xí píng tái cāo zuò zhuǎn xiàng kè chéng shè jì ， zhòng diǎn tǎo lùn hé shí yīng ràng jì shù jiè rù 、 hé shí yīng ràng xué shēng guān diào píng mù ， dú lì wán chéng yuè dú 、 tuī lǐ hé shū miàn biǎo dá 。

xīn fāng àn shí shī hòu ， zuì míng xiǎn de biàn huà bú shì chéng jì tū rán shàng shēng ， ér shì kè táng zhōng de xuǎn zé biàn dé gèng yǒu yī jù 。 jiào shī bù zài wèi le xiǎn de xīn yǐng ér zēng jiā shì pín ， yě bù zài yīn wèi dān xīn fēn xīn ér jù jué yī qiè shù zì gōng jù 。 xué shēng yuè dú zhǎng wén shí xiān zài zhǐ shàng biāo chū lùn diǎn hé zhèng jù ， chǔ lǐ xū yào duō zhǒng cái liào de wèn tí shí zài jìn rù gòng xiǎng zī liào kù ； wán chéng zài xiàn tǎo lùn hòu ， hái yào bǎ líng sǎn yì jiàn zhěng lǐ chéng lián guàn wén zì 。 xué qī mò ， xué xiào bǎ zhè cì bǐ jiào xiě rù jiào cái xuǎn yòng shuō míng ： qī mò píng jūn chéng jì xiāng jìn ， bìng bù yì wèi zhe liǎng zhǒng jiào cái háo wú chā bié ， yě bù néng zhèng míng qí zhōng yī zhǒng shì yòng yú suǒ yǒu rén 。 zhēn zhèng zhí de bǎo liú de jié lùn shì ， zhǐ zhì jiào cái tí gōng wěn dìng 、 zhuān zhù hé gòng tóng qǐ diǎn ， hùn hé jiào cái tí gōng yán shēn 、 fǎn kuì hé duō yàng biǎo dá ； zhǐ yǒu dāng xué xiào chéng dān qǐ zī yuán bǎo zhàng yǔ jiào xué shè jì de zé rèn ， liǎng zhě de jié hé cái bú huì chéng wéi jiǎn dān dié jiā ， ér huì zhuǎn huà wèi gèng chéng shú de xué xí fāng shì 。
translation: After the fall semester ended, Mingchuan No. 2 Secondary School held a briefing on the current stage of its textbook reform in the library lecture hall. Previously, two first-year classes following the same teaching schedule had used printed textbooks and blended textbooks respectively. The former relied mainly on textbooks, workbooks, and teachers’ notes on the board, while the latter retained the core texts but also used digital annotations, audio and video materials, online discussion forums, and tiered exercises. The school had originally hoped this comparison would help determine which type of textbook was more suitable for the following academic year’s curriculum. However, the interim report did not reach a clear conclusion: the two groups had similar average scores on their final examinations, and the differences in routine tests were not large enough to justify an immediate school-wide switch of textbooks. This seemingly uneventful result instead sparked controversy, because teachers, students, and parents all found that the average scores concealed clear differences between the two approaches in learning processes, habits, and workload.

Teachers who supported blended textbooks first argued that final examinations could measure only some learning outcomes and could not fully demonstrate students’ ability to search for, evaluate, and organize information. In the class using blended textbooks, students could listen to recordings of the texts repeatedly, consult maps to understand the background of literary works, and read different interpretations in the discussion forum. When they encountered abstract concepts, animated diagrams often helped them form an initial understanding more readily than a page of text did. Some students who were usually unwilling to speak in public were also willing to write down their views online first and then participate in classroom discussions. Teachers could also add materials in response to problems revealed in assignments rather than waiting for a newly revised edition to be uniformly printed. In their view, the value of blended textbooks should not be determined solely by a single examination. Their more important function was to broaden the channels through which students encountered knowledge and to transform the classroom from one-way instruction into continuous exchange.

Teachers in the printed-textbook group, however, expressed the opposite view. They found that although reading on paper lacked sound and animation, it was more conducive to sustaining students’ attention for long periods. Students could see the relationships between paragraphs on the same page and keep annotations, arrows, and questions together in fixed locations, making it easier to retrace their original thought processes when reviewing. By contrast, links in blended textbooks continually took learners to new pages. The abundance of information sometimes failed to deepen understanding and instead caused decision fatigue. Some students appeared to complete many interactive tasks, but the time they actually spent reading the original text decreased. Some teachers also pointed out that the instant prompts provided by digital platforms made students too quick to look for answers. Once the system withdrew its assistance, they might not be able to handle complex texts independently. Therefore, if the convenience brought by technology was not kept within clear boundaries, it could also weaken patience, memory, and judgment.

The debate soon extended beyond teaching methods themselves. Gu Lan, a parent representative, said at the briefing that her daughter studied smoothly on the family computer, but one of her classmates in the same group could access the materials only on an old mobile phone, with a small screen and an unstable internet connection. Although the two students nominally used the same set of blended textbooks, the learning conditions actually available to them were not the same. Other parents worried that their children frequently switched between apps on the pretext of researching information, making it difficult for families to tell whether they were studying or entertaining themselves. Zhou Qi, the student representative, reminded everyone that printed textbooks were not inherently fair either: some students could buy dictionaries, reference books, and extracurricular reading materials, while others could use only the textbooks issued by the school. The real question was not whether paper or screens were more advanced, but whether the school could guarantee access to essential resources, establish clear rules for their use, and teach students how to make choices when faced with too much information.

The team that wrote the interim report subsequently reviewed the classroom observation records, student assignments, teachers’ lesson-preparation notes, and parental feedback. Instead of continuing to ask which group had “won,” they reframed the question: for which tasks was each type of textbook effective, and what conditions did each require? The records showed that when students read long, tightly structured texts, a fixed page layout made repeated reference and an overall grasp of the text easier; when they studied pronunciation, observed processes, or compared information from multiple regions, digital resources had an advantage. In the blended-textbook group, students with stronger self-management skills could take the initiative in scheduling their progress, whereas those who lacked planning skills were prone to procrastination when faced with numerous options. Classroom order was more stable in the printed-textbook group, but if teachers still aimed to pursue a single correct answer, the scope for student discussion would also be restricted. This showed that textbooks were only one part of the learning environment: teaching tasks, access to equipment, and teacher guidance jointly determined the actual results.

The school administration ultimately approved neither the complete elimination of printed textbooks nor the return of blended textbooks to experimental status. Instead, the school made a more specific decision: all students would continue to receive the same core printed textbooks to ensure stable access to essential content, while teachers would select approved digital resources for units requiring sound, video, updated information, or collaborative exercises. Digital assignments had to specify their learning objectives, expected steps, and offline alternatives; links that had not been reviewed could not be included in required assignments. The school’s computer rooms would be open after class to students who needed them, and students would also be allowed to borrow devices. Teacher training would shift from operating learning platforms to curriculum design, focusing on when technology should be introduced and when students should turn off their screens and complete reading, reasoning, and written expression independently.

After the new plan was implemented, the most obvious change was not a sudden rise in scores, but that classroom choices became better grounded. Teachers no longer added videos merely to appear innovative, nor did they reject every digital tool out of concern that students might become distracted. When reading long texts, students first marked the arguments and evidence on paper; when addressing questions that required multiple kinds of material, they then entered the shared resource library. After completing online discussions, they also had to organize the scattered comments into coherent writing. At the end of the semester, the school incorporated this comparison into its guidelines for textbook selection: the similarity in average final-examination scores did not mean that the two types of textbook were no different, nor did it prove that either one was suitable for everyone. The conclusion truly worth retaining was that printed textbooks provided stability, concentration, and a common starting point, while blended textbooks provided extension, feedback, and diverse forms of expression. Only when the school assumed responsibility for guaranteeing resources and designing instruction would combining the two cease to be a simple accumulation and instead develop into a more mature approach to learning.

vocabulary.meaning: 事物发展过程中具有特定特征的一段时期。
清楚突出，容易辨别。
遮盖事实，使其不容易被发现。
按照一定标准进行选择和淘汰。
不直接指向具体事物、需要通过思考理解的概念。
用简单图形说明结构、过程或关系的图。
使隐藏的问题或情况显现出来。
由教师向学生单方面传递知识、缺少互动的讲授方式。
因面对过多选项、反复作出决定而产生的心理疲惫。
在操作或学习过程中立即提供的提醒或帮助。
取消或移走原来提供的事物。
从名称或表面说法来看，实际情况可能并非如此。
不需要额外条件或人为调整就自然具有公平性。
结构完整、逻辑周全，没有明显漏洞。
个人主动规划、控制和调整自身行为的能力。
把应当及时完成的事情推迟。
进入某种过程并对其产生影响。
分散而不集中，缺少完整联系。
内容或表达前后衔接，条理完整。
只把不同事物放在一起，却没有形成有效整合。

grammar.pattern: 并不意味着……，也不能证明……
grammar.explanation: 用于否定从某一现象直接推出的两种结论，强调现有事实不足以支持这些判断。
grammar.example: 期末平均成绩相近，并不意味着两种教材毫无差别，也不能证明其中一种适用于所有人。

grammar.explanation: 表示某个条件出现以后，后面的结果不一定能够实现，常用于指出潜在风险。
grammar.example: 一旦系统撤去帮助，他们未必能够独立处理复杂文本。

grammar.explanation: 表示前一条件是实现后一结果的必要条件，强调条件的重要性。
grammar.example: 只有当学校承担起资源保障与教学设计的责任，两者的结合才不会成为简单叠加，而会转化为更成熟的学习方式。
