questions.prompt: 周宁为什么认为仅凭减税前后的登记总量变化不能证明减税产生了效果？
options: 同期还可能存在市场需求、审批改革、招商活动和融资环境变化等其他影响因素
高新区在减税之后没有出现任何企业登记增长
所有新增登记企业都来自中心商务区
减税文件是在企业登记数量下降之后才公布的
questions.explanation: 文章指出，企业成立可能受到市场需求、行政审批改革、园区招商活动和融资环境等多种因素影响；如果不排除这些替代解释，就不能把登记增长完全归因于减税。
questions.evidence: 企业可能因市场需求扩大而成立，也可能受到行政审批改革、园区招商活动或融资环境变化的影响。

questions.prompt: 线上登记平台启用后，哪种情况可能在数据中造成短期激增？
options: 企业因税费上涨而集中迁出高新区
平台上线前积压的申请集中计入上线后的记录
研究团队删除了所有迁入企业的登记信息
各开发区同时停止受理营业执照申请
questions.explanation: 记录方式调整后，如果按照核准日期统计，平台上线前尚未处理完的申请可能集中显示在上线后的数据中，因此形成并非真实创业突然增加所导致的短期高峰。
questions.evidence: 若按核准日期统计，平台上线前积压的申请可能集中出现在上线后的记录中，造成短期激增。

questions.prompt: 研究团队复核后对“减税导致新企业增加”这一表述作出了什么处理？
options: 保留原表述，并把登记增长全部视为减税成效
改称减税已经独立推动了全市就业和生产增长
撤回因果表述，改为登记增长存在但尚不能确认减税的独立影响
彻底否定减税可能产生的任何作用，并建议立即取消政策
questions.explanation: 现有材料只能证明减税实施后登记数量上升，无法排除同期改革、企业迁移和统计变化等解释，因此团队撤回了确定性的因果结论，换成与证据强度更匹配的谨慎表述。
questions.evidence: 面对这种情况，研究团队作出明确决定：撤回报告中“减税导致新企业增加”的表述，改为“减税实施后观察到登记增长，但因同期改革、企业迁移及统计变化，尚不能确认其独立影响”。

articles.title: 临江大学复核毕业率报告：取消统一考试并不等于提高毕业率
articles.summary: 临江大学取消统一毕业考试后，校内报告把毕业率上升归因于考核制度改革。复核小组发现，入学标准、课程要求、延期毕业认定和学生基础也在同期发生变化，原有比较无法排除替代解释。学校最终撤回因果性表述，公开数据口径，并决定采用分届追踪、跨学院参照和不同统计口径复核来重新评估政策效果。
articles.topic: 临江大学复核毕业率报告：取消统一考试并不等于提高毕业率
paragraphs: 六月下旬，临江大学东校区行政楼举行年度教学质量会议。教务处在会上展示了一份政策评估报告，报告的核心结论是：学校取消统一毕业考试以后，学生按期毕业的比例有所提高，因此，统一考试曾经构成不必要的毕业障碍。主管教学的副校长希望尽快把这一结论写进学校年度报告，并据此建议各学院进一步减少终结性考试。然而，坐在会场后排的教育评估委员会成员周岚注意到，报告只比较了改革前后两个时期的毕业率，没有说明同期还发生过哪些变化。她当场提出，时间上的先后关系只能证明两件事相继出现，不能单独证明前一项改革导致了后一项结果。如果学校把相关性直接表述为因果关系，不仅可能误判政策，也可能使今后的课程改革建立在不可靠的证据之上。会议因此没有按原计划通过报告，而是转为一场针对研究设计的公开复核。

争议首先集中在“取消统一考试”究竟包含什么。改革以前，所有本科生必须在最后一学年参加由学校统一命题的综合考试，不合格者不能按期毕业。改革以后，各学院可以采用课程论文、项目展示、实习报告或分阶段测验进行综合评价。表面上看，统一考试确实是最明显的制度变化，但档案显示，同一时期学校还调整了招生办法，提高了部分专业的入学要求，并扩大了对学习困难学生的辅导。同时，一些学院压缩了必修课程，另一些学院允许学生用实践项目替代难度较高的理论课程。教务处认为，这些变化都属于改革的配套措施，没有必要分别处理；周岚则指出，正因为多项措施同时发生，研究才无法确定毕业率变化应归功于哪一项。如果入学学生的基础更强，或者毕业要求本身有所降低，即使保留统一考试，毕业率也可能上升。双方的分歧并非是否支持考试改革，而是学校有没有足够证据宣称改革产生了特定效果。

复核小组随后检查了报告对不同年级学生的比较方式。原报告把改革前入学的一届学生与改革后入学的一届学生直接并列，却没有校正他们入学时的学业水平、专业构成、家庭经济压力和休学经历。这样的比较默认两届学生除了考试制度以外完全相同，但这一前提显然过强。某些专业在改革后扩大招生，某些专业则缩小规模；就业市场的变化也可能促使学生更积极地按时完成学业。更重要的是，学校曾在改革期间修改“按期毕业”的统计口径，把部分因交换学习而延期的学生从计算范围中剔除。统计口径一变，表面上的毕业率就可能提高，即使学生实际完成学业的速度没有改变。复核小组因此要求教务处区分三个问题：学生是否真正更快完成全部课程，学校是否改变了毕业资格的认定方式，以及统计部门是否改变了分母。只有把这些问题分开，才能讨论制度改革的独立作用。

支持原结论的管理人员提出，统一考试取消以后，学生投诉减少，教师也普遍认为评价方式更灵活，这些现象足以说明改革方向正确。周岚承认，投诉数量和教师体验可以用于判断政策是否容易执行、是否获得接受，却不能代替对毕业率因果关系的检验。投诉减少可能是因为申诉渠道改变，也可能是因为学生不再面对一次决定毕业资格的高风险考试；它能说明压力结构发生变化，却不能说明学生掌握的知识更多。教师赞成灵活评价，也不意味着所有学院执行了同等严格的标准。假如某学院用经过多轮修改的课程论文替代闭卷考试，学生通过评价的机会自然增加，但这既可能代表评价更加全面，也可能代表合格门槛下降。要判断哪种解释更合理，研究者必须比较作业要求、评分规则、课程完成情况以及后续学习表现，而不能把“更容易通过”自动解释为“教学质量更高”。这场冲突由此揭示出一个常被忽略的区别：政策可能改善学生体验，同时并未改善学习成果；也可能提高毕业率，却没有提高学生能力。

经过讨论，校长办公会作出三项具体决定。第一，暂时撤回年度报告中“取消统一考试提高了毕业率”的句子，改为“取消统一考试后观察到毕业率上升，但现有资料不足以确认因果关系”。第二，由教育评估委员会重新制定分析方案，把不同入学年份的学生持续追踪到离校，并预先列出需要控制的背景差异；对于改革前后没有同时改变招生和课程要求的学院，优先进行比较，以减少其他政策的干扰。第三，公开毕业率的定义、延期学生的处理办法和各学院评价制度的变化，允许教师和学生检查结论是否依赖某一种统计口径。委员会还建议寻找改革推进时间不同的学院作为参照，观察它们在改革前是否已经呈现不同趋势。如果改革学院原本就在改善，那么改革后的继续上升便不能全部算作取消考试的效果。相反，如果不同学院在改革前走势接近，而只有实施改革的学院随后出现稳定变化，因果解释才会更有说服力。

一个学期后，学校公布的不是一个更加醒目的宣传结论，而是一份说明证据边界的复核报告。报告确认，取消统一考试与毕业率上升在时间上相伴出现，但入学条件、课程结构、支持服务和统计规则的同步变化，使任何单一原因都无法从现有比较中被可靠识别。学校没有因此恢复统一考试，也没有否定多元评价的价值，而是把政策目标重新表述为降低一次性考试的风险、扩大评价方式，并持续监测学习质量。各学院必须保存评分标准和课程要求的变更记录，今后的毕业率报告也必须同时呈现延期、转专业和退出情况。这个结果没有提供一句简单的胜利口号，却避免了更严重的误导：把先后发生误当成因果关系。对公共政策而言，承认暂时无法确定原因并不是研究失败，而是负责任判断的起点。只有在比较对象合理、统计口径稳定、替代解释得到检验以后，学校才有资格回答取消统一考试究竟提高了毕业率，还是仅仅与其他变化共同出现。
pinyin: liù yuè xià xún ， lín jiāng dà xué dōng xiào qū xíng zhèng lóu jǔ xíng nián dù jiào xué zhì liàng huì yì 。 jiào wù chù zài huì shàng zhǎn shì le yī fèn zhèng cè píng gū bào gào ， bào gào de hé xīn jié lùn shì ： xué xiào qǔ xiāo tǒng yī bì yè kǎo shì yǐ hòu ， xué shēng àn qī bì yè de bǐ lì yǒu suǒ tí gāo ， yīn cǐ ， tǒng yī kǎo shì céng jīng gòu chéng bù bì yào de bì yè zhàng ài 。 zhǔ guǎn jiào xué de fù xiào zhǎng xī wàng jǐn kuài bǎ zhè yī jié lùn xiě jìn xué xiào nián dù bào gào ， bìng jù cǐ jiàn yì gè xué yuàn jìn yí bù jiǎn shǎo zhōng jié xìng kǎo shì 。 rán ér ， zuò zài huì chǎng hòu pái de jiào yù píng gū wěi yuán huì chéng yuán zhōu lán zhù yì dào ， bào gào zhǐ bǐ jiào le gǎi gé qián hòu liǎng gè shí qī de bì yè lǜ ， méi yǒu shuō míng tóng qī hái fā shēng guò nǎ xiē biàn huà 。 tā dāng chǎng tí chū ， shí jiān shàng de xiān hòu guān xì zhǐ néng zhèng míng liǎng jiàn shì xiāng jì chū xiàn ， bù néng dān dú zhèng míng qián yī xiàng gǎi gé dǎo zhì le hòu yī xiàng jié guǒ 。 rú guǒ xué xiào bǎ xiāng guān xìng zhí jiē biǎo shù wèi yīn guǒ guān xì ， bù jǐn kě néng wù pàn zhèng cè ， yě kě néng shǐ jīn hòu de kè chéng gǎi gé jiàn lì zài bù kě kào de zhèng jù zhī shàng 。 huì yì yīn cǐ méi yǒu àn yuán jì huà tōng guò bào gào ， ér shì zhuǎn wéi yī cháng zhēn duì yán jiū shè jì de gōng kāi fù hé 。

zhēng yì shǒu xiān jí zhōng zài “ qǔ xiāo tǒng yī kǎo shì ” jiū jìng bāo hán shén me 。 gǎi gé yǐ qián ， suǒ yǒu běn kē shēng bì xū zài zuì hòu yī xué nián cān jiā yóu xué xiào tǒng yī mìng tí de zōng hé kǎo shì ， bù hé gé zhě bù néng àn qī bì yè 。 gǎi gé yǐ hòu ， gè xué yuàn kě yǐ cǎi yòng kè chéng lùn wén 、 xiàng mù zhǎn shì 、 shí xí bào gào huò fēn jiē duàn cè yàn jìn xíng zōng hé píng jià 。 biǎo miàn shàng kàn ， tǒng yī kǎo shì què shí shì zuì míng xiǎn de zhì dù biàn huà ， dàn dàng àn xiǎn shì ， tóng yī shí qī xué xiào hái tiáo zhěng le zhāo shēng bàn fǎ ， tí gāo le bù fèn zhuān yè de rù xué yāo qiú ， bìng kuò dà le duì xué xí kùn nán xué shēng de fǔ dǎo 。 tóng shí ， yī xiē xué yuàn yā suō le bì xiū kè chéng ， lìng yī xiē xué yuàn yǔn xǔ xué shēng yòng shí jiàn xiàng mù tì dài nán dù jiào gāo de lǐ lùn kè chéng 。 jiào wù chù rèn wéi ， zhè xiē biàn huà dōu shǔ yú gǎi gé de pèi tào cuò shī ， méi yǒu bì yào fēn bié chǔ lǐ ； zhōu lán zé zhǐ chū ， zhèng yīn wèi duō xiàng cuò shī tóng shí fā shēng ， yán jiū cái wú fǎ què dìng bì yè lǜ biàn huà yīng guī gōng yú nǎ yī xiàng 。 rú guǒ rù xué xué shēng de jī chǔ gèng qiáng ， huò zhě bì yè yāo qiú běn shēn yǒu suǒ jiàng dī ， jí shǐ bǎo liú tǒng yī kǎo shì ， bì yè lǜ yě kě néng shàng shēng 。 shuāng fāng de fēn qí bìng fēi shì fǒu zhī chí kǎo shì gǎi gé ， ér shì xué xiào yǒu méi yǒu zú gòu zhèng jù xuān chēng gǎi gé chǎn shēng le tè dìng xiào guǒ 。

fù hé xiǎo zǔ suí hòu jiǎn chá le bào gào duì bù tóng nián jí xué shēng de bǐ jiào fāng shì 。 yuán bào gào bǎ gǎi gé qián rù xué de yī jiè xué shēng yǔ gǎi gé hòu rù xué de yī jiè xué shēng zhí jiē bìng liè ， què méi yǒu jiào zhèng tā men rù xué shí de xué yè shuǐ píng 、 zhuān yè gòu chéng 、 jiā tíng jīng jì yā lì hé xiū xué jīng lì 。 zhè yàng de bǐ jiào mò rèn liǎng jiè xué shēng chú le kǎo shì zhì dù yǐ wài wán quán xiāng tóng ， dàn zhè yī qián tí xiǎn rán guò qiáng 。 mǒu xiē zhuān yè zài gǎi gé hòu kuò dà zhāo shēng ， mǒu xiē zhuān yè zé suō xiǎo guī mó ； jiù yè shì chǎng de biàn huà yě kě néng cù shǐ xué shēng gèng jī jí dì àn shí wán chéng xué yè 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， xué xiào céng zài gǎi gé qī jiān xiū gǎi “ àn qī bì yè ” de tǒng jì kǒu jìng ， bǎ bù fèn yīn jiāo huàn xué xí ér yán qī de xué shēng cóng jì suàn fàn wéi zhōng tī chú 。 tǒng jì kǒu jìng yī biàn ， biǎo miàn shàng de bì yè lǜ jiù kě néng tí gāo ， jí shǐ xué shēng shí jì wán chéng xué yè de sù dù méi yǒu gǎi biàn 。 fù hé xiǎo zǔ yīn cǐ yāo qiú jiào wù chù qū fēn sān gè wèn tí ： xué shēng shì fǒu zhēn zhèng gèng kuài wán chéng quán bù kè chéng ， xué xiào shì fǒu gǎi biàn le bì yè zī gé de rèn dìng fāng shì ， yǐ jí tǒng jì bù mén shì fǒu gǎi biàn le fēn mǔ 。 zhǐ yǒu bǎ zhè xiē wèn tí fēn kāi ， cái néng tǎo lùn zhì dù gǎi gé de dú lì zuò yòng 。

zhī chí yuán jié lùn de guǎn lǐ rén yuán tí chū ， tǒng yī kǎo shì qǔ xiāo yǐ hòu ， xué shēng tóu sù jiǎn shǎo ， jiào shī yě pǔ biàn rèn wéi píng jià fāng shì gèng líng huó ， zhè xiē xiàn xiàng zú yǐ shuō míng gǎi gé fāng xiàng zhèng què 。 zhōu lán chéng rèn ， tóu sù shù liàng hé jiào shī tǐ yàn kě yǐ yòng yú pàn duàn zhèng cè shì fǒu róng yì zhí xíng 、 shì fǒu huò dé jiē shòu ， què bù néng dài tì duì bì yè lǜ yīn guǒ guān xì de jiǎn yàn 。 tóu sù jiǎn shǎo kě néng shì yīn wèi shēn sù qú dào gǎi biàn ， yě kě néng shì yīn wèi xué shēng bù zài miàn duì yī cì jué dìng bì yè zī gé de gāo fēng xiǎn kǎo shì ； tā néng shuō míng yā lì jié gòu fā shēng biàn huà ， què bù néng shuō míng xué shēng zhǎng wò de zhī shí gèng duō 。 jiào shī zàn chéng líng huó píng jià ， yě bù yì wèi zhe suǒ yǒu xué yuàn zhí xíng le tóng děng yán gé de biāo zhǔn 。 jiǎ rú mǒu xué yuàn yòng jīng guò duō lún xiū gǎi de kè chéng lùn wén tì dài bì juàn kǎo shì ， xué shēng tōng guò píng jià de jī huì zì rán zēng jiā ， dàn zhè jì kě néng dài biǎo píng jià gèng jiā quán miàn ， yě kě néng dài biǎo hé gé mén kǎn xià jiàng 。 yào pàn duàn nǎ zhǒng jiě shì gèng hé lǐ ， yán jiū zhě bì xū bǐ jiào zuò yè yāo qiú 、 píng fēn guī zé 、 kè chéng wán chéng qíng kuàng yǐ jí hòu xù xué xí biǎo xiàn ， ér bù néng bǎ “ gèng róng yì tōng guò ” zì dòng jiě shì wèi “ jiào xué zhì liàng gèng gāo ”。 zhè chǎng chōng tū yóu cǐ jiē shì chū yí gè cháng bèi hū lüè de qū bié ： zhèng cè kě néng gǎi shàn xué shēng tǐ yàn ， tóng shí bìng wèi gǎi shàn xué xí chéng guǒ ； yě kě néng tí gāo bì yè lǜ ， què méi yǒu tí gāo xué shēng néng lì 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， xiào zhǎng bàn gōng huì zuò chū sān xiàng jù tǐ jué dìng 。 dì yī ， zàn shí chè huí nián dù bào gào zhōng “ qǔ xiāo tǒng yī kǎo shì tí gāo le bì yè lǜ ” de jù zi ， gǎi wéi “ qǔ xiāo tǒng yī kǎo shì hòu guān chá dào bì yè lǜ shàng shēng ， dàn xiàn yǒu zī liào bù zú yǐ què rèn yīn guǒ guān xì ”。 dì èr ， yóu jiào yù píng gū wěi yuán huì chóng xīn zhì dìng fēn xī fāng àn ， bǎ bù tóng rù xué nián fèn de xué shēng chí xù zhuī zōng dào lí xiào ， bìng yù xiān liè chū xū yào kòng zhì de bèi jǐng chā yì ； duì yú gǎi gé qián hòu méi yǒu tóng shí gǎi biàn zhāo shēng hé kè chéng yāo qiú de xué yuàn ， yōu xiān jìn xíng bǐ jiào ， yǐ jiǎn shǎo qí tā zhèng cè de gān rǎo 。 dì sān ， gōng kāi bì yè lǜ de dìng yì 、 yán qī xué shēng de chǔ lǐ bàn fǎ hé gè xué yuàn píng jià zhì dù de biàn huà ， yǔn xǔ jiào shī hé xué shēng jiǎn chá jié lùn shì fǒu yī lài mǒu yī zhǒng tǒng jì kǒu jìng 。 wěi yuán huì hái jiàn yì xún zhǎo gǎi gé tuī jìn shí jiān bù tóng de xué yuàn zuò wéi cān zhào ， guān chá tā men zài gǎi gé qián shì fǒu yǐ jīng chéng xiàn bù tóng qū shì 。 rú guǒ gǎi gé xué yuàn yuán běn jiù zài gǎi shàn ， nà me gǎi gé hòu de jì xù shàng shēng biàn bù néng quán bù suàn zuò qǔ xiāo kǎo shì de xiào guǒ 。 xiāng fǎn ， rú guǒ bù tóng xué yuàn zài gǎi gé qián zǒu shì jiē jìn ， ér zhǐ yǒu shí shī gǎi gé de xué yuàn suí hòu chū xiàn wěn dìng biàn huà ， yīn guǒ jiě shì cái huì gèng yǒu shuō fú lì 。

yí gè xué qī hòu ， xué xiào gōng bù de bú shì yí gè gèng jiā xǐng mù dì xuān chuán jié lùn ， ér shì yī fèn shuō míng zhèng jù biān jiè de fù hé bào gào 。 bào gào què rèn ， qǔ xiāo tǒng yī kǎo shì yǔ bì yè lǜ shàng shēng zài shí jiān shàng xiàng bàn chū xiàn ， dàn rù xué tiáo jiàn 、 kè chéng jié gòu 、 zhī chí fú wù hé tǒng jì guī zé de tóng bù biàn huà ， shǐ rèn hé dān yī yuán yīn dōu wú fǎ cóng xiàn yǒu bǐ jiào zhōng bèi kě kào shí bié 。 xué xiào méi yǒu yīn cǐ huī fù tǒng yī kǎo shì ， yě méi yǒu fǒu dìng duō yuán píng jià de jià zhí ， ér shì bǎ zhèng cè mù biāo chóng xīn biǎo shù wèi jiàng dī yí cì xìng kǎo shì de fēng xiǎn 、 kuò dà píng jià fāng shì ， bìng chí xù jiān cè xué xí zhì liàng 。 gè xué yuàn bì xū bǎo cún píng fēn biāo zhǔn hé kè chéng yāo qiú de biàn gēng jì lù ， jīn hòu de bì yè lǜ bào gào yě bì xū tóng shí chéng xiàn yán qī 、 zhuǎn zhuān yè hé tuì chū qíng kuàng 。 zhè ge jié guǒ méi yǒu tí gōng yī jù jiǎn dān de shèng lì kǒu hào ， què bì miǎn le gèng yán zhòng de wù dǎo ： bǎ xiān hòu fā shēng wù dàng chéng yīn guǒ guān xì 。 duì gōng gòng zhèng cè ér yán ， chéng rèn zàn shí wú fǎ què dìng yuán yīn bìng bú shì yán jiū shī bài ， ér shì fù zé rèn pàn duàn de qǐ diǎn 。 zhǐ yǒu zài bǐ jiào duì xiàng hé lǐ 、 tǒng jì kǒu jìng wěn dìng 、 tì dài jiě shì dé dào jiǎn yàn yǐ hòu ， xué xiào cái yǒu zī gé huí dá qǔ xiāo tǒng yī kǎo shì jiū jìng tí gāo le bì yè lǜ ， hái shì jǐn jǐn yǔ qí tā biàn huà gòng tóng chū xiàn 。
translation: In late June, the administration building on the East Campus of Linjiang University hosted the annual teaching quality conference. At the meeting, the Office of Academic Affairs presented a policy evaluation report whose central conclusion was that the proportion of students graduating on time had increased after the university abolished the standardized graduation examination and that the examination had therefore constituted an unnecessary barrier to graduation. The vice president responsible for academic affairs hoped to incorporate this conclusion into the university's annual report as soon as possible and, on that basis, recommend that the colleges further reduce summative examinations. However, Zhou Lan, a member of the Educational Evaluation Committee seated at the back of the conference hall, noticed that the report merely compared graduation rates in the periods before and after the reform without explaining what other changes had occurred during the same period. She pointed out on the spot that temporal sequence could establish only that two events had occurred one after the other; it could not, by itself, prove that the earlier reform had caused the later outcome. If the university directly presented correlation as causation, it might not only misjudge the policy but also cause future curriculum reforms to be based on unreliable evidence. The meeting therefore did not approve the report as originally planned and instead became an open review of the research design.

The dispute initially centered on what exactly was included in the "abolition of the standardized examination." Before the reform, all undergraduates had to take a comprehensive examination prepared by the university during their final academic year, and those who failed could not graduate on time. After the reform, each college was allowed to conduct comprehensive assessments using course papers, project presentations, internship reports, or tests administered in stages. On the surface, the standardized examination was indeed the most conspicuous institutional change, but archival records showed that during the same period, the university had also revised its admissions procedures, raised entrance requirements for some majors, and expanded tutoring for students experiencing academic difficulties. At the same time, some colleges reduced the number of required courses, while others allowed students to replace difficult theoretical courses with practical projects. The Office of Academic Affairs argued that all these changes were supporting measures for the reform and did not need to be treated separately. Zhou Lan, however, pointed out that precisely because multiple measures had been introduced simultaneously, the study could not determine which one deserved credit for the change in graduation rates. If incoming students had stronger academic foundations, or if the graduation requirements themselves had been lowered, the graduation rate might have risen even if the standardized examination had been retained. The disagreement between the two sides was not over whether to support examination reform, but over whether the university had sufficient evidence to claim that the reform had produced a particular effect.

The review panel then examined how the report compared students from different cohorts. The original report directly compared a cohort that had entered before the reform with one that had entered afterward, without adjusting for their academic levels upon admission, distribution across majors, family financial pressures, or histories of taking leaves of absence. Such a comparison assumed that the two cohorts were identical in every respect other than the examination system, but that assumption was clearly too strong. Some majors expanded enrollment after the reform, while others reduced their intake; changes in the job market might also have given students stronger incentives to complete their studies on time. More importantly, during the reform, the university had revised the statistical definition of "on-time graduation" by excluding from the calculation some students whose graduation had been delayed because of exchange programs. A change in statistical definitions could raise the apparent graduation rate even if the actual speed at which students completed their studies remained unchanged. The review panel therefore required the Office of Academic Affairs to distinguish among three questions: whether students were genuinely completing all their courses more quickly, whether the university had changed the way it determined eligibility for graduation, and whether the statistics department had changed the denominator. Only by separating these questions could the independent effect of the institutional reform be discussed.

Administrators who supported the original conclusion argued that student complaints had declined after the standardized examination was abolished and that teachers generally considered the assessment methods more flexible, and that these phenomena were sufficient to show that the reform was moving in the right direction. Zhou Lan acknowledged that the number of complaints and teachers' experiences could be used to judge whether a policy was easy to implement and broadly accepted, but they could not substitute for testing the causal relationship between the reform and graduation rates. Complaints might have declined because the appeals process had changed, or because students no longer faced a high-stakes examination that determined their eligibility for graduation in a single sitting. This could show that the structure of pressure had changed, but not that students had acquired more knowledge. Teachers' support for flexible assessment also did not mean that all colleges had applied equally rigorous standards. If a college replaced a closed-book examination with a course paper that students could revise through multiple rounds, their chances of passing the assessment would naturally increase. Yet this might indicate either that the assessment had become more comprehensive or that the threshold for passing had been lowered. To determine which explanation was more reasonable, researchers would have to compare assignment requirements, grading rules, course completion, and subsequent academic performance rather than automatically interpreting "easier to pass" as "higher teaching quality." The conflict thus revealed an often-overlooked distinction: a policy might improve the student experience without improving learning outcomes, or it might raise the graduation rate without improving students' abilities.

After discussion, the university's executive committee made three specific decisions. First, it temporarily withdrew the sentence "abolishing the standardized examination increased the graduation rate" from the annual report and replaced it with: "An increase in the graduation rate was observed after the standardized examination was abolished, but the available data are insufficient to establish a causal relationship." Second, the Educational Evaluation Committee was instructed to develop a new analysis plan, track students from different admission years continuously until they left the university, and specify in advance the background differences that needed to be controlled for. Comparisons would prioritize colleges in which admissions and course requirements had not also changed around the time of the reform, thereby reducing interference from other policies. Third, the university would disclose the definition of the graduation rate, the method for handling students whose graduation was delayed, and changes in each college's assessment system, allowing teachers and students to examine whether the conclusions depended on any particular statistical definition. The committee also recommended identifying colleges that implemented the reform at different times as comparison groups and examining whether they had already shown different trends before the reform. If the colleges implementing the reform had already been improving, the continued increase afterward could not be attributed entirely to the abolition of the examination. Conversely, if different colleges had followed similar trajectories before the reform and only those implementing it subsequently showed a sustained change, the causal explanation would be more convincing.

One semester later, the university published not a more striking promotional claim but a review report explaining the limits of the evidence. The report confirmed that the abolition of the standardized examination and the rise in the graduation rate had occurred together over time, but simultaneous changes in admission conditions, curriculum structure, support services, and statistical rules made it impossible to identify any single cause reliably from the existing comparison. The university did not reinstate the standardized examination as a result, nor did it deny the value of diversified assessment. Instead, it reframed the policy objectives as reducing the risks of a one-time examination, expanding assessment methods, and continuously monitoring the quality of learning. Every college was required to retain records of changes to grading standards and course requirements, and future graduation-rate reports would also have to present data on delayed graduation, changes of major, and withdrawal. This outcome did not provide a simple victory slogan, but it prevented a more serious misrepresentation: mistaking temporal sequence for causation. In public policy, acknowledging that the cause cannot yet be determined is not a failure of research but the starting point for responsible judgment. Only after the comparison groups are appropriate, the statistical definitions are stable, and alternative explanations have been tested will the university be in a position to answer whether abolishing the standardized examination actually increased the graduation rate or merely occurred alongside other changes.

vocabulary.meaning: 在规定的时间内完成学业并取得毕业资格。
在一个学习阶段结束时，用于综合评定学习成果的考试。
两个或多个现象在变化上存在联系或共同趋势的性质。
一个因素直接引起另一个结果的关系。
以公开方式重新检查研究过程、资料或结论。
为了使主要政策顺利实施而同时采取的辅助性措施。
统计时采用的定义、范围、标准和计算方法。
进行统计或计算时所包括的对象和数据界限。
排除其他因素影响后，某一因素单独产生的效果。
当事人对处理结果有异议时提出复查请求的途径。
被认定为达到合格标准所必须满足的最低要求。
学习者经过学习后获得的知识、能力或其他实际成效。
在较长时期内连续观察和记录研究对象的变化。
比较对象在原有条件、经历或环境方面存在的不同。
现有证据能够支持结论的范围及其局限。
除主要假设以外，也可能合理说明同一现象的其他原因。

grammar.explanation: 表示递进关系，后一分句在前一分句的基础上补充更进一步的影响。
grammar.example: 如果学校把相关性直接表述为因果关系，不仅可能误判政策，也可能使今后的课程改革建立在不可靠的证据之上。

grammar.explanation: 表示让步关系，说明即便前面的假设条件成立，后面的结果仍然可能发生。
grammar.example: 如果入学学生的基础更强，或者毕业要求本身有所降低，即使保留统一考试，毕业率也可能上升。

grammar.explanation: 表示必要条件，强调必须满足前面的条件，才有可能得到后面的结果。
grammar.example: 只有在比较对象合理、统计口径稳定、替代解释得到检验以后，学校才有资格回答取消统一考试究竟提高了毕业率，还是仅仅与其他变化共同出现。

questions.prompt: 周岚为什么反对把毕业率上升直接归因于取消统一考试？
options: 因为改革同期还发生了招生、课程、辅导和统计等多方面变化
因为统一考试取消后学生投诉数量反而明显增加
因为改革前后的所有学院都降低了毕业要求
因为学校没有保存任何改革前的毕业率数据
questions.explanation: 周岚认为，多项措施在同一时期发生，现有研究无法分离各项措施的作用，因此不能确定毕业率上升应归因于取消统一考试。
questions.evidence: 周岚则指出，正因为多项措施同时发生，研究才无法确定毕业率变化应归功于哪一项。

questions.prompt: 学校修改“按期毕业”的统计口径可能造成什么结果？
options: 延期学生全部被重新认定为按期毕业
实际完成学业的速度不变，表面毕业率却可能提高
改革前入学学生的学业水平被自动调高
不同专业的招生规模会因此完全相同
questions.explanation: 把部分交换学习延期者剔除出计算范围会改变统计分母，因此即便学生完成学业的实际速度没有变化，计算出的毕业率也可能上升。
questions.evidence: 统计口径一变，表面上的毕业率就可能提高，即使学生实际完成学业的速度没有改变。

questions.prompt: 根据校长办公会的决定，什么情况会使取消统一考试的因果解释更有说服力？
options: 所有学院在改革后都采用完全相同的评价方式
改革学院在改革前就已经呈现持续改善趋势
改革前各学院走势接近，改革后只有实施改革的学院稳定变化
教师普遍认为新的评价方式比闭卷考试更加灵活
questions.explanation: 如果改革前不同学院的发展趋势相近，而改革后只有实施改革的学院出现稳定变化，就更容易排除原有趋势等替代解释，从而加强因果推断。
questions.evidence: 相反，如果不同学院在改革前走势接近，而只有实施改革的学院随后出现稳定变化，因果解释才会更有说服力。

articles.title: 从桂香社区绿地改造争议看居民健康改善的因果检验
articles.summary: 东江市临江区桂香社区将闲置停车场改造成公共绿地后，居民健康自评有所改善，街道办据此准备宣布绿地建设直接促进了健康。社区卫生服务中心对此提出异议，指出同期人口流动、医疗服务调整、问卷偏差等因素均可能造成表面关联。多方最终决定重新界定问题，采用分阶段改造、对照社区、持续追踪和访谈相结合的方式检验因果关系，并将原有宣传口径改为审慎表述。
articles.topic: 从桂香社区绿地改造争议看居民健康改善的因果检验
paragraphs: 东江市临江区桂香社区曾有一片长期闲置的露天停车场。场地中央堆放着废弃围栏，雨天积水，夏季地面温度很高。经过居民议事会讨论，街道办撤去部分停车位，将其改造成包含乔木、步道、座椅和儿童活动区的公共绿地。改造完成一年后，社区居委会整理年度问卷时发现，填写“总体健康状况良好”的居民比过去更多，关于失眠、情绪低落和活动不便的抱怨也有所减少。街道办据此拟定新闻稿，准备以“增加绿地显著改善居民健康”为标题介绍改造经验，并建议在临江区其他老旧社区复制这一方案。在汇报会上，项目负责人把绿地开放与健康评分上升依次放在同一张图上，认为两者发生时间紧密衔接，因果关系已经十分清楚。然而，桂香社区卫生服务中心的周医生当场提出反对意见：先后发生的两件事固然可能存在联系，却不能仅凭时间顺序断定前者造成了后者。围绕这句话，原本用于总结成绩的会议转变成了一场关于证据标准的争论。

周医生首先追问，前后两次问卷是否由同一批居民填写。居委会核对资料后发现，社区在绿地开放前后经历了明显的人口更替，一些行动不便的老年居民搬去与子女同住，附近新建公寓则吸引了较年轻的住户。即使每个人的健康状况都没有变化，调查对象变得年轻，也可能抬高整个社区的平均评分。其次，填写问卷本身并非随机行为。经常到绿地散步、参加社区活动的人，更容易看到通知并主动答卷；长期卧床、工作繁忙或对社区事务缺乏兴趣的人，反而可能被遗漏。再次，改造期间社区卫生服务中心延长了门诊时间，街道还增设了助餐点和慢性病咨询。居民健康若确有改善，也不能立即判定功劳只属于绿地。更复杂的是，健康评分来自个人判断。绿地落成后，社区宣传频繁强调环境更新，一些居民可能因自豪感增强而给出更积极的评价，但这种变化未必等同于身体机能改善。规划部门担心，若把这些限制写进新闻稿，会削弱公众对项目的支持；卫生部门则坚持，夸大结论不仅有损公信力，还可能使有限经费被错误配置。双方的冲突并不在于是否喜欢绿地，而在于是否有资格把相关性表述为确定的因果关系。

为摆脱各说各话的局面，临江区成立了一个由社区居民、规划人员、基层医生和方法顾问组成的小组。小组没有急于选择复杂模型，而是先把问题写得足够明确：要检验的不是“绿地通常是否有益”，也不是“桂香社区是否变得更宜居”，而是与维持原状相比，这次特定改造是否使原有居民在随后一段时间内获得了可归因于绿地的健康改善。这个表述限定了干预、对象、时间和比较条件，也迫使各方区分不同结果。步行次数增加、邻里交往增多、主观压力减轻和血压变化可能处在同一作用链条上，却不能混成一个含义模糊的“健康总分”。小组还画出可能的因果路径：绿地或许通过遮阴、运动机会和社会交往影响健康，也可能因夜间噪声、花粉或安全顾虑给部分居民带来负担；年龄、收入、既往疾病、居住年限和附近交通状况既可能影响居民使用绿地的频率，也可能影响健康结局。若只比较常去绿地者与不常去者，得到的很可能是生活习惯和身体条件的差异，而不是绿地本身的效果。至此，会议形成第一个决定：撤回原新闻稿，不再把问卷变化直接写成因果事实。

为了获得更可信的证据，小组利用全区绿地改造分批实施的安排，制定了前瞻性评估方案。桂香社区附近尚未开工、人口结构和公共服务较为接近的社区被列为同期参照，但小组明确指出，“看起来相似”并不意味着天然可比，因此必须记录两地在改造前已经存在的变化趋势。调查对象尽量固定为持续居住的居民，同时为高龄者、残障人士和不熟悉手机操作的人提供入户或纸质填写方式，以减少选择性失访。除主观健康评价外，评估还分别记录步行、睡眠、社交参与和基层医疗服务使用情况，并提前确定主要结果，避免事后从大量指标中挑选最有利的发现。对于搬入和搬出的居民，资料不被简单删除，而是单独说明人口流动可能怎样改变社区整体表现。小组还安排访谈，了解居民究竟因为树荫、步道还是邻里活动而改变日常行为，并收集对拥挤、蚊虫和噪声的负面体验。这些材料不能替代因果比较，却能帮助解释作用机制和群体差异。所有参与者都被告知资料用途，公开报告只呈现无法识别个人的信息。评估方案在观察结果之前确定，从程序上限制了为了迎合政策预期而临时修改口径的空间。

新的方案实施后，工作组没有把任务简化为寻找一个能够证明项目成功的数字，而是依次核查几个关键问题：改造前，桂香社区与参照社区的健康变化是否大致平行；改造后出现的差异，能否由同期门诊调整、人口迁移或其他环境工程解释；结论在排除短期住户、改变缺失资料处理方式或分别考察不同年龄群体时，是否仍保持一致。评议过程中，各方发现，原先的年度问卷不足以独立承担因果判断，因为它没有稳定追踪同一批人，也没有完整记录同期变化。新收集的多来源材料能够说明绿地开放后部分居民更愿意外出和停留，却仍需持续观察这些行为变化能否转化为稳定的健康收益。基于这一结果，临江区作出第二个具体决定：保留绿地，不因证据尚未完备而否定其休闲、景观和公共交往价值；同时暂停使用“已经证实改善健康”的宣传语，把正式表述改为“居民健康评价与活动方式出现积极变化，因果效应仍在跟踪评估”。区里还将无障碍通道、夜间照明和噪声管理纳入后续改进，以回应访谈中暴露出的使用障碍。这个结果既没有把谨慎误解为反对建设，也没有让良好的政策愿望取代证据。

桂香社区的争议说明，因果检验的核心并不是给一组前后数字加上更权威的措辞，而是认真回答反事实问题：如果没有这片新增绿地，同一群居民的健康会怎样变化？现实中无法同时观察同一社区“改造”和“未改造”的两种状态，因此只能借助合适的比较对象、清楚的时间顺序、稳定的测量方式以及对替代解释的系统排查，逐步逼近答案。即使最终发现绿地确有益处，效果也未必平均落在每个人身上；经常使用步道的居民可能受益较多，害怕拥挤或行动不便者则可能无法分享便利。政策结论因而应同时说明适用范围、不确定性和可能机制。桂香社区最终获得的，不是一句更响亮的口号，而是一套更可靠的决策程序：先界定主张，再寻找可比较的证据；先承认局限，再决定宣传和投资尺度。只有这样，社区治理才能既珍惜环境改善带来的希望，又避免把希望过早包装成已经得到证明的事实。
pinyin: dōng jiāng shì lín jiāng qū guì xiāng shè qū céng yǒu yī piàn cháng qī xián zhì de lù tiān tíng chē chǎng 。 chǎng dì zhōng yāng duī fàng zhe fèi qì wéi lán ， yǔ tiān jī shuǐ ， xià jì dì miàn wēn dù hěn gāo 。 jīng guò jū mín yì shì huì tǎo lùn ， jiē dào bàn chè qù bù fèn tíng chē wèi ， jiāng qí gǎi zào chéng bāo hán qiáo mù 、 bù dào 、 zuò yǐ hé ér tóng huó dòng qū de gōng gòng lǜ dì 。 gǎi zào wán chéng yī nián hòu ， shè qū jū wěi huì zhěng lǐ nián dù wèn juǎn shí fā xiàn ， tián xiě “ zǒng tǐ jiàn kāng zhuàng kuàng liáng hǎo ” de jū mín bǐ guò qù gèng duō ， guān yú shī mián 、 qíng xù dī luò hé huó dòng bù biàn de bào yuàn yě yǒu suǒ jiǎn shǎo 。 jiē dào bàn jù cǐ nǐ dìng xīn wén gǎo ， zhǔn bèi yǐ “ zēng jiā lǜ dì xiǎn zhù gǎi shàn jū mín jiàn kāng ” wèi biāo tí jiè shào gǎi zào jīng yàn ， bìng jiàn yì zài lín jiāng qū qí tā lǎo jiù shè qū fù zhì zhè yī fāng àn 。 zài huì bào huì shàng ， xiàng mù fù zé rén bǎ lǜ dì kāi fàng yǔ jiàn kāng píng fēn shàng shēng yī cì fàng zài tóng yī zhāng tú shàng ， rèn wéi liǎng zhě fā shēng shí jiān jǐn mì xián jiē ， yīn guǒ guān xì yǐ jīng shí fēn qīng chǔ 。 rán ér ， guì xiāng shè qū wèi shēng fú wù zhōng xīn de zhōu yī shēng dāng chǎng tí chū fǎn duì yì jiàn ： xiān hòu fā shēng de liǎng jiàn shì gù rán kě néng cún zài lián xì ， què bù néng jǐn píng shí jiān shùn xù duàn dìng qián zhě zào chéng le hòu zhě 。 wéi rào zhè jù huà ， yuán běn yòng yú zǒng jié chéng jì de huì yì zhuǎn biàn chéng le yī cháng guān yú zhèng jù biāo zhǔn de zhēng lùn 。

zhōu yī shēng shǒu xiān zhuī wèn ， qián hòu liǎng cì wèn juǎn shì fǒu yóu tóng yī pī jū mín tián xiě 。 jū wěi huì hé duì zī liào hòu fā xiàn ， shè qū zài lǜ dì kāi fàng qián hòu jīng lì le míng xiǎn de rén kǒu gēng tì ， yī xiē xíng dòng bù biàn de lǎo nián jū mín bān qù yǔ zǐ nǚ tóng zhù ， fù jìn xīn jiàn gōng yù zé xī yǐn le jiào nián qīng de zhù hù 。 jí shǐ měi gè rén de jiàn kāng zhuàng kuàng dōu méi yǒu biàn huà ， diào chá duì xiàng biàn dé nián qīng ， yě kě néng tái gāo zhěng gè shè qū de píng jūn píng fēn 。 qí cì ， tián xiě wèn juǎn běn shēn bìng fēi suí jī xíng wéi 。 jīng cháng dào lǜ dì sàn bù 、 cān jiā shè qū huó dòng de rén ， gèng róng yì kàn dào tōng zhī bìng zhǔ dòng dá juàn ； cháng qī wò chuáng 、 gōng zuò fán máng huò duì shè qū shì wù quē fá xìng qù de rén ， fǎn ér kě néng bèi yí lòu 。 zài cì ， gǎi zào qī jiān shè qū wèi shēng fú wù zhōng xīn yán cháng le mén zhěn shí jiān ， jiē dào hái zēng shè le zhù cān diǎn hé màn xìng bìng zī xún 。 jū mín jiàn kāng ruò què yǒu gǎi shàn ， yě bù néng lì jí pàn dìng gōng láo zhǐ shǔ yú lǜ dì 。 gèng fù zá de shì ， jiàn kāng píng fēn lái zì gè rén pàn duàn 。 lǜ dì luò chéng hòu ， shè qū xuān chuán pín fán qiáng diào huán jìng gēng xīn ， yī xiē jū mín kě néng yīn zì háo gǎn zēng qiáng ér gěi chū gèng jī jí de píng jià ， dàn zhè zhǒng biàn huà wèi bì děng tóng yú shēn tǐ jī néng gǎi shàn 。 guī huà bù mén dān xīn ， ruò bǎ zhè xiē xiàn zhì xiě jìn xīn wén gǎo ， huì xuē ruò gōng zhòng duì xiàng mù dì zhī chí ； wèi shēng bù mén zé jiān chí ， kuā dà jié lùn bù jǐn yǒu sǔn gōng xìn lì ， hái kě néng shǐ yǒu xiàn jīng fèi bèi cuò wù pèi zhì 。 shuāng fāng de chōng tū bìng bù zài yú shì fǒu xǐ huān lǜ dì ， ér zài yú shì fǒu yǒu zī gé bǎ xiāng guān xìng biǎo shù wèi què dìng de yīn guǒ guān xì 。

wèi bǎi tuō gè shuō gè huà de jú miàn ， lín jiāng qū chéng lì le yí gè yóu shè qū jū mín 、 guī huà rén yuán 、 jī céng yī shēng hé fāng fǎ gù wèn zǔ chéng de xiǎo zǔ 。 xiǎo zǔ méi yǒu jí yú xuǎn zé fù zá mó xíng ， ér shì xiān bǎ wèn tí xiě dé zú gòu míng què ： yào jiǎn yàn de bú shì “ lǜ dì tōng cháng shì fǒu yǒu yì ”， yě bú shì “ guì xiāng shè qū shì fǒu biàn dé gèng yí jū ”， ér shì yǔ wéi chí yuán zhuàng xiāng bǐ ， zhè cì tè dìng gǎi zào shì fǒu shǐ yuán yǒu jū mín zài suí hòu yī duàn shí jiān nèi huò dé le kě guī yīn yú lǜ dì de jiàn kāng gǎi shàn 。 zhè ge biǎo shù xiàn dìng le gān yù 、 duì xiàng 、 shí jiān hé bǐ jiào tiáo jiàn ， yě pò shǐ gè fāng qū fēn bù tóng jié guǒ 。 bù xíng cì shù zēng jiā 、 lín lǐ jiāo wǎng zēng duō 、 zhǔ guān yā lì jiǎn qīng hé xuè yā biàn huà kě néng chù zài tóng yī zuò yòng liàn tiáo shàng ， què bù néng hùn chéng yí gè hán yì mó hú de “ jiàn kāng zǒng fēn ”。 xiǎo zǔ hái huà chū kě néng de yīn guǒ lù jìng ： lǜ dì huò xǔ tōng guò zhē yīn 、 yùn dòng jī huì hé shè huì jiāo wǎng yǐng xiǎng jiàn kāng ， yě kě néng yīn yè jiān zào shēng 、 huā fěn huò ān quán gù lǜ gěi bù fèn jū mín dài lái fù dān ； nián líng 、 shōu rù 、 jì wǎng jí bìng 、 jū zhù nián xiàn hé fù jìn jiāo tōng zhuàng kuàng jì kě néng yǐng xiǎng jū mín shǐ yòng lǜ dì de pín lǜ ， yě kě néng yǐng xiǎng jiàn kāng jié jú 。 ruò zhǐ bǐ jiào cháng qù lǜ dì zhě yǔ bù cháng qù zhě ， dé dào de hěn kě néng shì shēng huó xí guàn hé shēn tǐ tiáo jiàn de chā yì ， ér bú shì lǜ dì běn shēn de xiào guǒ 。 zhì cǐ ， huì yì xíng chéng dì yí gè jué dìng ： chè huí yuán xīn wén gǎo ， bù zài bǎ wèn juǎn biàn huà zhí jiē xiě chéng yīn guǒ shì shí 。

wèi le huò dé gèng kě xìn de zhèng jù ， xiǎo zǔ lì yòng quán qū lǜ dì gǎi zào fēn pī shí shī de ān pái ， zhì dìng le qián zhān xìng píng gū fāng àn 。 guì xiāng shè qū fù jìn shàng wèi kāi gōng 、 rén kǒu jié gòu hé gōng gòng fú wù jiào wéi jiē jìn de shè qū bèi liè wèi tóng qī cān zhào ， dàn xiǎo zǔ míng què zhǐ chū ，“ kàn qǐ lái xiāng sì ” bìng bù yì wèi zhe tiān rán kě bǐ ， yīn cǐ bì xū jì lù liǎng dì zài gǎi zào qián yǐ jīng cún zài de biàn huà qū shì 。 diào chá duì xiàng jǐn liàng gù dìng wèi chí xù jū zhù de jū mín ， tóng shí wèi gāo líng zhě 、 cán zhàng rén shì hé bù shú xī shǒu jī cāo zuò de rén tí gōng rù hù huò zhǐ zhì tián xiě fāng shì ， yǐ jiǎn shǎo xuǎn zé xìng shī fǎng 。 chú zhǔ guān jiàn kāng píng jià wài ， píng gū hái fēn bié jì lù bù xíng 、 shuì mián 、 shè jiāo cān yù hé jī céng yī liáo fú wù shǐ yòng qíng kuàng ， bìng tí qián què dìng zhǔ yào jié guǒ ， bì miǎn shì hòu cóng dà liàng zhǐ biāo zhōng tiāo xuǎn zuì yǒu lì de fā xiàn 。 duì yú bān rù hé bān chū de jū mín ， zī liào bù bèi jiǎn dān shān chú ， ér shì dān dú shuō míng rén kǒu liú dòng kě néng zěn yàng gǎi biàn shè qū zhěng tǐ biǎo xiàn 。 xiǎo zǔ hái ān pái fǎng tán ， liǎo jiě jū mín jiū jìng yīn wèi shù yīn 、 bù dào hái shì lín lǐ huó dòng ér gǎi biàn rì cháng xíng wéi ， bìng shōu jí duì yōng jǐ 、 wén chóng hé zào shēng de fù miàn tǐ yàn 。 zhè xiē cái liào bù néng tì dài yīn guǒ bǐ jiào ， què néng bāng zhù jiě shì zuò yòng jī zhì hé qún tǐ chā yì 。 suǒ yǒu cān yù zhě dōu bèi gào zhī zī liào yòng tú ， gōng kāi bào gào zhǐ chéng xiàn wú fǎ shí bié gè rén de xìn xī 。 píng gū fāng àn zài guān chá jié guǒ zhī qián què dìng ， cóng chéng xù shàng xiàn zhì le wèi le yíng hé zhèng cè yù qī ér lín shí xiū gǎi kǒu jìng de kōng jiān 。

xīn de fāng àn shí shī hòu ， gōng zuò zǔ méi yǒu bǎ rèn wù jiǎn huà wèi xún zhǎo yí gè néng gòu zhèng míng xiàng mù chéng gōng de shù zì ， ér shì yī cì hé chá jǐ gè guān jiàn wèn tí ： gǎi zào qián ， guì xiāng shè qū yǔ cān zhào shè qū de jiàn kāng biàn huà shì fǒu dà zhì píng xíng ； gǎi zào hòu chū xiàn de chā yì ， néng fǒu yóu tóng qī mén zhěn tiáo zhěng 、 rén kǒu qiān yí huò qí tā huán jìng gōng chéng jiě shì ； jié lùn zài pái chú duǎn qī zhù hù 、 gǎi biàn quē shī zī liào chǔ lǐ fāng shì huò fēn bié kǎo chá bù tóng nián líng qún tǐ shí ， shì fǒu réng bǎo chí yí zhì 。 píng yì guò chéng zhōng ， gè fāng fā xiàn ， yuán xiān de nián dù wèn juǎn bù zú yǐ dú lì chéng dān yīn guǒ pàn duàn ， yīn wèi tā méi yǒu wěn dìng zhuī zōng tóng yī pī rén ， yě méi yǒu wán zhěng jì lù tóng qī biàn huà 。 xīn shōu jí de duō lái yuán cái liào néng gòu shuō míng lǜ dì kāi fàng hòu bù fèn jū mín gèng yuàn yì wài chū hé tíng liú ， què réng xū chí xù guān chá zhè xiē xíng wéi biàn huà néng fǒu zhuǎn huà wèi wěn dìng de jiàn kāng shōu yì 。 jī yú zhè yī jié guǒ ， lín jiāng qū zuò chū dì èr gè jù tǐ jué dìng ： bǎo liú lǜ dì ， bù yīn zhèng jù shàng wèi wán bèi ér fǒu dìng qí xiū xián 、 jǐng guān hé gōng gòng jiāo wǎng jià zhí ； tóng shí zàn tíng shǐ yòng “ yǐ jīng zhèng shí gǎi shàn jiàn kāng ” de xuān chuán yǔ ， bǎ zhèng shì biǎo shù gǎi wéi “ jū mín jiàn kāng píng jià yǔ huó dòng fāng shì chū xiàn jī jí biàn huà ， yīn guǒ xiào yìng réng zài gēn zōng píng gū ”。 qū lǐ hái jiāng wú zhàng ài tōng dào 、 yè jiān zhào míng hé zào shēng guǎn lǐ nà rù hòu xù gǎi jìn ， yǐ huí yìng fǎng tán zhōng bào lù chū de shǐ yòng zhàng ài 。 zhè ge jié guǒ jì méi yǒu bǎ jǐn shèn wù jiě wèi fǎn duì jiàn shè ， yě méi yǒu ràng liáng hǎo de zhèng cè yuàn wàng qǔ dài zhèng jù 。

guì xiāng shè qū de zhēng yì shuō míng ， yīn guǒ jiǎn yàn de hé xīn bìng bú shì gěi yī zǔ qián hòu shù zì jiā shàng gèng quán wēi de cuò cí ， ér shì rèn zhēn huí dá fǎn shì shí wèn tí ： rú guǒ méi yǒu zhè piàn xīn zēng lǜ dì ， tóng yī qún jū mín de jiàn kāng huì zěn yàng biàn huà ？ xiàn shí zhōng wú fǎ tóng shí guān chá tóng yī shè qū “ gǎi zào ” hé “ wèi gǎi zào ” de liǎng zhǒng zhuàng tài ， yīn cǐ zhǐ néng jiè zhù hé shì de bǐ jiào duì xiàng 、 qīng chǔ de shí jiān shùn xù 、 wěn dìng de cè liáng fāng shì yǐ jí duì tì dài jiě shì de xì tǒng pái chá ， zhú bù bī jìn dá àn 。 jí shǐ zuì zhōng fā xiàn lǜ dì què yǒu yì chù ， xiào guǒ yě wèi bì píng jūn luò zài měi gè rén shēn shàng ； jīng cháng shǐ yòng bù dào de jū mín kě néng shòu yì jiào duō ， hài pà yōng jǐ huò xíng dòng bù biàn zhě zé kě néng wú fǎ fēn xiǎng biàn lì 。 zhèng cè jié lùn yīn ér yīng tóng shí shuō míng shì yòng fàn wéi 、 bù què dìng xìng hé kě néng jī zhì 。 guì xiāng shè qū zuì zhōng huò dé de ， bú shì yī jù gèng xiǎng liàng de kǒu hào ， ér shì yī tào gèng kě kào de jué cè chéng xù ： xiān jiè dìng zhǔ zhāng ， zài xún zhǎo kě bǐ jiào de zhèng jù ； xiān chéng rèn jú xiàn ， zài jué dìng xuān chuán hé tóu zī chǐ dù 。 zhǐ yǒu zhè yàng ， shè qū zhì lǐ cái néng jì zhēn xī huán jìng gǎi shàn dài lái de xī wàng ， yòu bì miǎn bǎ xī wàng guò zǎo bāo zhuāng chéng yǐ jīng dé dào zhèng míng de shì shí 。
translation: Guixiang Community in Linjiang District, Dongjiang City, once had an open-air parking lot that had long stood idle. Discarded fencing was piled in the middle of the site, water accumulated on rainy days, and the ground became extremely hot in summer. After discussion by the residents’ council, the subdistrict office removed some of the parking spaces and transformed the site into a public green space with trees, paths, seating, and a children’s activity area. One year after the renovation was completed, the community residents’ committee, while compiling its annual questionnaire, found that more residents than before described their “overall health status as good,” while complaints about insomnia, low mood, and difficulty moving around had also declined. On this basis, the subdistrict office drafted a press release introducing the renovation experience under the proposed headline “Increasing Green Space Significantly Improves Residents’ Health” and recommended replicating the plan in other older communities in Linjiang District. At a briefing, the project leader placed the opening of the green space and the rise in health scores sequentially on the same chart, arguing that because the two events occurred in close succession, the causal relationship was already quite clear. However, Dr. Zhou of the Guixiang Community Health Service Center objected on the spot: although two events occurring one after the other may indeed be related, their temporal order alone is not enough to establish that the former caused the latter. That remark turned what had originally been a meeting to summarize achievements into a debate about standards of evidence.

Dr. Zhou first asked whether the two questionnaires, before and after the renovation, had been completed by the same group of residents. After checking the records, the residents’ committee found that the community had undergone substantial population turnover around the time the green space opened. Some elderly residents with limited mobility had moved in with their children, while newly built apartments nearby had attracted younger residents. Even if no individual’s health had changed, a younger survey population could still have raised the community’s average score. Second, completing the questionnaire was not itself a random behavior. People who often walked in the green space or participated in community activities were more likely to see the notice and voluntarily respond, whereas those who were bedridden for long periods, busy with work, or uninterested in community affairs might have been missed. Third, during the renovation, the community health service center extended its outpatient hours, and the subdistrict also added a meal assistance site and chronic disease consultations. Even if residents’ health had genuinely improved, the credit could not immediately be attributed solely to the green space. More complicated still, the health scores were based on personal judgment. After the green space was completed, community publicity repeatedly emphasized the environmental improvements. Some residents may have provided more positive assessments because of a heightened sense of pride, but such a change was not necessarily equivalent to improved physical functioning. The planning department worried that including these limitations in the press release would weaken public support for the project, while the health department insisted that overstating the conclusion would not only undermine public credibility but might also lead to the misallocation of limited funds. The conflict between the two sides was not about whether they liked green spaces, but about whether they were justified in presenting a correlation as a definite causal relationship.

To move beyond a situation in which each side simply asserted its own position, Linjiang District established a group consisting of community residents, planning officials, primary care physicians, and methodological advisers. Rather than rushing to choose a complex model, the group first formulated the question with sufficient precision: what needed to be tested was not whether green spaces are generally beneficial, nor whether Guixiang Community had become more livable, but whether, compared with maintaining the status quo, this specific renovation had produced health improvements among existing residents over the subsequent period that could be attributed to the green space. This formulation defined the intervention, population, time frame, and comparison condition, while also forcing all parties to distinguish among different outcomes. Increased walking, more interaction among neighbors, reduced subjective stress, and changes in blood pressure might lie along the same causal chain, but they could not be merged into a vaguely defined “overall health score.” The group also mapped possible causal pathways: the green space might affect health through shade, opportunities for exercise, and social interaction, but it might also burden some residents through nighttime noise, pollen, or safety concerns. Age, income, preexisting illness, length of residence, and nearby traffic conditions could influence both how often residents used the green space and their health outcomes. Comparing only frequent users with infrequent users would most likely reveal differences in lifestyles and physical conditions rather than the effect of the green space itself. At this point, the meeting reached its first decision: to withdraw the original press release and stop presenting the questionnaire changes directly as causal facts.

To obtain more credible evidence, the group used the district-wide phased schedule for green-space renovations to devise a prospective evaluation plan. A community near Guixiang where construction had not yet begun and whose population structure and public services were relatively similar was designated as a concurrent comparison site. However, the group made it clear that “looking similar” did not mean being inherently comparable, so trends already present in the two areas before the renovation had to be recorded. The survey sample was kept, as far as possible, to residents who continued to live in the communities, while home visits or paper forms were provided for elderly people, people with disabilities, and those unfamiliar with smartphone use in order to reduce selective loss to follow-up. In addition to subjective health assessments, the evaluation separately recorded walking, sleep, social participation, and the use of primary healthcare services. Primary outcomes were specified in advance to avoid selecting the most favorable findings afterward from a large number of indicators. Data on residents who moved in or out were not simply deleted; instead, the ways in which population movement might alter the community’s overall results were explained separately. The group also arranged interviews to determine whether residents changed their daily behavior because of the shade from the trees, the paths, or neighborhood activities, and it collected negative experiences involving crowding, mosquitoes, and noise. These materials could not replace causal comparisons, but they could help explain the mechanisms at work and differences among groups. All participants were informed of how their data would be used, and public reports presented only information from which individuals could not be identified. The evaluation plan was finalized before the results were observed, procedurally limiting the scope for last-minute changes in criteria designed to conform to policy expectations.

After the new plan was implemented, the working group did not reduce its task to finding a single number that could prove the project successful. Instead, it examined several key questions in sequence: before the renovation, had health trends in Guixiang Community and the comparison community been broadly parallel; could the differences that emerged afterward be explained by concurrent changes in outpatient services, population migration, or other environmental projects; and did the conclusions remain consistent when short-term residents were excluded, the method for handling missing data was changed, or different age groups were examined separately? During the review, all parties found that the original annual questionnaire was not sufficient on its own to support a causal judgment because it had not consistently followed the same group of people or fully recorded concurrent changes. The newly collected material from multiple sources could show that some residents became more willing to go outdoors and spend time there after the green space opened, but continued observation was still needed to determine whether these behavioral changes would translate into lasting health benefits. Based on this result, Linjiang District made a second specific decision: it would retain the green space and would not deny its recreational, aesthetic, and public social value merely because the evidence was not yet complete. At the same time, it suspended use of the promotional claim that the project had “been proven to improve health” and changed the official wording to “Residents’ health assessments and activity patterns have shown positive changes, while the causal effects remain under ongoing evaluation.” The district also incorporated accessible pathways, nighttime lighting, and noise management into subsequent improvements in response to barriers to use revealed in the interviews. This outcome neither mistook caution for opposition to development nor allowed well-intentioned policy aspirations to substitute for evidence.

The dispute in Guixiang Community shows that the essence of causal testing is not to attach more authoritative language to a set of before-and-after figures, but to answer the counterfactual question seriously: without the newly added green space, how would the health of the same group of residents have changed? In reality, it is impossible to observe the same community simultaneously in both a “renovated” and an “unrenovated” state. The answer can therefore be approached only gradually through appropriate comparison groups, a clear temporal sequence, consistent methods of measurement, and a systematic examination of alternative explanations. Even if the green space is ultimately found to provide genuine benefits, its effects may not be distributed evenly across everyone. Residents who frequently use the paths may benefit more, whereas those who fear crowds or have limited mobility may be unable to share in the convenience. Policy conclusions should therefore also specify the scope of applicability, the uncertainty, and the possible mechanisms. What Guixiang Community ultimately gained was not a more resounding slogan, but a more reliable decision-making process: first define the claim, then seek comparable evidence; first acknowledge the limitations, then determine the appropriate scale of publicity and investment. Only in this way can community governance both cherish the promise brought by environmental improvements and avoid prematurely packaging that promise as an already proven fact.

vocabulary.meaning: 放着不用，没有得到有效利用。
由相关人员共同讨论公共事务的会议或组织。
根据这一情况或依据。
经过考虑后起草或制定。
前后事物相互连接。
表示承认某个事实，后面通常有转折。
一个地区原有居民迁出、新居民迁入而导致人口组成变化。
应当包括的人或事物没有被包括进去。
公众对机构、组织或信息的信任程度。

着眼于未来发展或在结果发生前进行安排的性质。
在相同时间段内用于对照和比较的对象。
某些特定类型的调查对象更容易退出或未被继续调查，从而造成样本偏差。

grammar.explanation: 先承认前一情况具有一定合理性，再用“却”引出与之相反或需要限制的结论。
grammar.example: 然而，桂香社区卫生服务中心的周医生当场提出反对意见：先后发生的两件事固然可能存在联系，却不能仅凭时间顺序断定前者造成了后者。

grammar.explanation: 表示让步关系，说明即便前面的假设成立，后面的结果仍然可能出现。
grammar.example: 即使每个人的健康状况都没有变化，调查对象变得年轻，也可能抬高整个社区的平均评分。

grammar.explanation: 先否定真正关键之处在前项，再强调关键之处在后项。
grammar.example: 双方的冲突并不在于是否喜欢绿地，而在于是否有资格把相关性表述为确定的因果关系。

questions.prompt: 周医生为什么反对直接使用“增加绿地显著改善居民健康”这一结论？
options: 绿地开放与健康评分上升在时间上先后出现，不能单凭这一点确认因果关系
社区居民普遍反对把停车场改造成公共绿地
卫生服务中心已经证明居民的健康评分没有变化
项目负责人没有把绿地开放时间放入汇报图表
questions.explanation: 周医生承认两件事可能有关，但强调时间上的先后和紧密衔接不足以证明绿地造成了健康改善。
questions.evidence: 然而，桂香社区卫生服务中心的周医生当场提出反对意见：先后发生的两件事固然可能存在联系，却不能仅凭时间顺序断定前者造成了后者。

questions.prompt: 评估方案为什么为部分居民提供入户或纸质填写方式？
options: 为了让新建公寓的年轻住户优先参加调查
为了减少高龄者、残障人士等群体因填写困难而产生的选择性失访
为了用纸质问卷取代所有主观健康评价
为了把已经搬出的居民重新纳入持续居住者样本
questions.explanation: 部分居民可能因行动或手机操作方面的困难而无法参与调查，提供其他填写方式可以降低这类人被系统性遗漏的风险。
questions.evidence: 调查对象尽量固定为持续居住的居民，同时为高龄者、残障人士和不熟悉手机操作的人提供入户或纸质填写方式，以减少选择性失访。

questions.prompt: 面对尚未完备的因果证据，临江区作出了什么决定？
options: 拆除绿地并恢复全部停车位，等待新的研究结果
继续使用已经证实改善健康的宣传语，但停止收集问卷
保留绿地，同时改用更谨慎的宣传表述并继续跟踪因果效应
只宣传绿地的健康作用，不再提及休闲和公共交往价值
questions.explanation: 区里没有因证据不足而否定绿地的其他价值，但暂停了确定性的健康宣传，明确说明因果效应仍需跟踪评估。
questions.evidence: 基于这一结果，临江区作出第二个具体决定：保留绿地，不因证据尚未完备而否定其休闲、景观和公共交往价值；同时暂停使用“已经证实改善健康”的宣传语，把正式表述改为“居民健康评价与活动方式出现积极变化，因果效应仍在跟踪评估”。

articles.title: 从同步变化到因果证据：澄清海岳软件四天工作制的产出争议
articles.summary: 杭州海岳软件在缩短工作周后观察到交付量上升，管理层却无法据此断定制度改革提高了产出。公司通过核对指标、追查同期变化并设计分阶段比较，最终撤回过度宣传，保留各部门依据任务特征选择工作安排的空间，并建立了更审慎的政策评估程序。
articles.topic: 从同步变化到因果证据：澄清海岳软件四天工作制的产出争议
paragraphs: 六月初，位于杭州滨江区的海岳软件召开季度经营会。公司从三月起试行四天工作制，每周五原则上不安排常规工作。运营负责人在会上展示内部看板：试行后的几个开发周期里，已经验收的功能数量比此前多，延期项目也有所减少。他据此建议对外宣布“四天工作制显著提升产出”，并把这句话写进招聘网页。人力资源部门赞成立即宣传，因为技术人才招聘正面临激烈竞争；部分投资人也希望公司借此塑造先进管理形象。然而，负责数据治理的周岚提出异议。她指出，制度调整与产出增长确实先后发生，但时间上的相邻并不等于因果关系。若公司没有排除其他解释，就不能断言少工作一天导致了更多成果。会议的分歧由此产生：管理层关注传播时机，数据团队则坚持先判断证据究竟能够支持多强的结论。

周岚首先检查“产出”的定义。运营看板统计的是通过验收的功能数量，但不同功能的规模、难度和商业价值差别很大。修正一个按钮的位置和重构支付系统都可能被记作一个功能；开发人员还可能为了让数字好看，把一项完整任务拆成多个小项。更重要的是，软件公司的真实产出不只包括交付速度，还包括系统稳定性、客户满意度、维护成本和长期创新。某个周期验收项目增多，可能只是过去积压的任务集中完成，未必意味着整体效率提高。她要求团队同时查看缺陷返工、线上故障、客户续约意见以及员工加班记录。这样做不是故意降低改革的成绩，而是防止单一指标代替复杂事实。若测量本身偏离了公司真正关心的目标，那么随后再精细的计算也只能给出貌似准确的误判。

接着，她梳理试行前后同时发生的变化。三月，公司刚结束一个持续半年的底层系统改造，许多依赖该系统的功能终于能够进入验收；两个长期拖延的项目也恰好在四月收尾。与此同时，销售部门暂停接受高度定制的临时需求，产品经理开始提前冻结每周任务，开发团队还启用了自动测试工具。人员结构也发生改变：经验丰富的工程师从维护组转入核心产品组，而几名新人结束培训后开始独立承担工作。这些因素都有可能提高看板上的交付量。季节变化同样不可忽视，春节后的业务节奏本来就与年初不同。假如把所有变化产生的效果都归功于四天工作制，公司就犯了遗漏变量的错误。反过来，也不能因为存在其他因素便认定改革毫无作用；合理的态度是承认现有观察无法把各种影响彼此分离。

讨论中还出现了选择偏差。最先参加试行的是流程成熟、任务边界清楚的三个产品组，承担紧急运维和客户现场支持的团队暂未加入。前者原本就更容易压缩会议和集中工作，不能代表全公司。员工问卷也主要由愿意表达意见的人填写，其中既可能有改革的积极支持者，也可能有担心制度取消而刻意报喜的人。管理层曾以为员工满意度提高能够间接证明效率上升，周岚却提醒，满意度与产出可能互相影响，也可能共同受到管理方式改善的推动。此外，大家知道公司正在评估新制度，便可能暂时更加投入，这种短期反应未必能够长期维持。因果判断需要回答的是：如果同一批团队在相同条件下没有实行四天工作制，他们的产出会怎样？现实中无法同时观察这两种状态，只能寻找尽量可信的比较对象。

周岚提出分阶段推进，而不是仓促地在全公司统一实施或取消。公司先按业务性质把团队分组，在确保客户服务不被中断的前提下，确定若干条件相近、且都愿意参与评估的团队。部分团队先采用四天工作制，另一部分暂时保持原安排，随后再交换。任务口径、项目复杂度和节假日影响需要提前记录，评价标准也要在看到结果之前确定，避免管理者事后挑选有利指标。为降低制度差异造成的不公平，公司允许暂未进入试行阶段的员工获得相应调休，并明确评估不用于个人绩效排名。周岚还建议访谈项目负责人和客户，因为数字能够显示变化，却未必解释变化为何发生。若会议减少使专注时间增加，这是支持改革的机制证据；若交付增长只是旧项目集中结项，就应作出不同解释。

这一方案遭到市场负责人的反对。他认为招聘旺季稍纵即逝，等分阶段评估结束再宣传，公司会失去话题热度；他还担心公开承认证据不足会显得管理层犹豫。周岚回应，因果表述不是文案风格问题，而是对员工和求职者的事实承诺。公司完全可以说“试行期间观察到交付增加，员工普遍欢迎更完整的休息时间”，却不能把尚未排除的相关关系包装成已经证实的效果。如果后来缺陷增加、员工在四个工作日内被迫延长工时，夸张宣传不仅损害信誉，还会掩盖实际成本。总经理最终作出决定：暂缓使用“产出增加由四天工作制带来”的广告语，保留试行，不把周五休息变成变相待命，并由数据治理、人力资源和客户服务部门共同监督后续比较。

经过数轮项目周期，公司得到的结论比最初口号更克制，也更有用。不同团队的表现并不一致：工作可预先规划、会议较多的团队在压缩协作环节后更容易维持交付；必须连续响应客户的岗位则需要轮班和备用人员，否则休息日可能转化为隐性加班。管理层因此没有宣布四天工作制必然提高产出，也没有因效果不整齐而彻底放弃改革，而是允许各部门依据任务特征选择固定休息日、轮换值班或维持原工作周。招聘网页最终写明公司提供四天工作制试点及弹性安排，并说明制度仍在持续评估。更重要的结果是，公司建立了政策评估程序：先界定目标和指标，再识别同期变化，设置可比较条件，最后才讨论因果。产出增加与制度实施同时出现，是值得调查的线索，却不是结论本身。真正负责任的决策，不是把一次令人满意的变化迅速归功于某项政策，而是在不夸大证据的前提下，判断它对哪些人、在什么条件下、通过何种机制发挥作用。
pinyin: liù yuè chū ， wèi yú háng zhōu bīn jiāng qū de hǎi yuè ruǎn jiàn zhào kāi jì dù jīng yíng huì 。 gōng sī cóng sān yuè qǐ shì xíng sì tiān gōng zuò zhì ， měi zhōu wǔ yuán zé shàng bù ān pái cháng guī gōng zuò 。 yùn yíng fù zé rén zài huì shàng zhǎn shì nèi bù kàn bǎn ： shì xíng hòu de jǐ gè kāi fā zhōu qī lǐ ， yǐ jīng yàn shōu de gōng néng shù liàng bǐ cǐ qián duō ， yán qī xiàng mù yě yǒu suǒ jiǎn shǎo 。 tā jù cǐ jiàn yì duì wài xuān bù “ sì tiān gōng zuò zhì xiǎn zhù tí shēng chǎn chū ”， bìng bǎ zhè jù huà xiě jìn zhāo pìn wǎng yè 。 rén lì zī yuán bù mén zàn chéng lì jí xuān chuán ， yīn wèi jì shù rén cái zhāo pìn zhèng miàn lín jī liè jìng zhēng ； bù fèn tóu zī rén yě xī wàng gōng sī jiè cǐ sù zào xiān jìn guǎn lǐ xíng xiàng 。 rán ér ， fù zé shù jù zhì lǐ de zhōu lán tí chū yì yì 。 tā zhǐ chū ， zhì dù tiáo zhěng yǔ chǎn chū zēng zhǎng què shí xiān hòu fā shēng ， dàn shí jiān shàng de xiāng lín bìng bù děng yú yīn guǒ guān xì 。 ruò gōng sī méi yǒu pái chú qí tā jiě shì ， jiù bù néng duàn yán shǎo gōng zuò yī tiān dǎo zhì le gèng duō chéng guǒ 。 huì yì de fēn qí yóu cǐ chǎn shēng ： guǎn lǐ céng guān zhù chuán bō shí jī ， shù jù tuán duì zé jiān chí xiān pàn duàn zhèng jù jiū jìng néng gòu zhī chí duō qiáng de jié lùn 。

zhōu lán shǒu xiān jiǎn chá “ chǎn chū ” de dìng yì 。 yùn yíng kàn bǎn tǒng jì de shì tōng guò yàn shōu de gōng néng shù liàng ， dàn bù tóng gōng néng de guī mó 、 nán dù hé shāng yè jià zhí chā bié hěn dà 。 xiū zhèng yí gè àn niǔ de wèi zhì hé zhòng gòu zhī fù xì tǒng dōu kě néng bèi jì zuò yí gè gōng néng ； kāi fā rén yuán hái kě néng wèi le ràng shù zì hǎo kàn ， bǎ yī xiàng wán zhěng rèn wù chāi chéng duō gè xiǎo xiàng 。 gèng zhòng yào de shì ， ruǎn jiàn gōng sī de zhēn shí chǎn chū bù zhǐ bāo kuò jiāo fù sù dù ， hái bāo kuò xì tǒng wěn dìng xìng 、 kè hù mǎn yì dù 、 wéi hù chéng běn hé cháng qī chuàng xīn 。 mǒu gè zhōu qī yàn shōu xiàng mù zēng duō ， kě néng zhǐ shì guò qù jī yā de rèn wù jí zhōng wán chéng ， wèi bì yì wèi zhe zhěng tǐ xiào lǜ tí gāo 。 tā yāo qiú tuán duì tóng shí chá kàn quē xiàn fǎn gōng 、 xiàn shàng gù zhàng 、 kè hù xù yuē yì jiàn yǐ jí yuán gōng jiā bān jì lù 。 zhè yàng zuò bú shì gù yì jiàng dī gǎi gé de chéng jì ， ér shì fáng zhǐ dān yī zhǐ biāo dài tì fù zá shì shí 。 ruò cè liáng běn shēn piān lí le gōng sī zhēn zhèng guān xīn de mù biāo ， nà me suí hòu zài jīng xì de jì suàn yě zhǐ néng gěi chū mào sì zhǔn què de wù pàn 。

jiē zhe ， tā shū lǐ shì xíng qián hòu tóng shí fā shēng de biàn huà 。 sān yuè ， gōng sī gāng jié shù yí gè chí xù bàn nián de dǐ céng xì tǒng gǎi zào ， xǔ duō yī lài gāi xì tǒng de gōng néng zhōng yú néng gòu jìn rù yàn shōu ； liǎng gè cháng qī tuō yán de xiàng mù yě qià hǎo zài sì yuè shōu wěi 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， xiāo shòu bù mén zàn tíng jiē shòu gāo dù dìng zhì de lín shí xū qiú ， chǎn pǐn jīng lǐ kāi shǐ tí qián dòng jié měi zhōu rèn wù ， kāi fā tuán duì hái qǐ yòng le zì dòng cè shì gōng jù 。 rén yuán jié gòu yě fā shēng gǎi biàn ： jīng yàn fēng fù de gōng chéng shī cóng wéi hù zǔ zhuǎn rù hé xīn chǎn pǐn zǔ ， ér jǐ míng xīn rén jié shù péi xùn hòu kāi shǐ dú lì chéng dān gōng zuò 。 zhè xiē yīn sù dōu yǒu kě néng tí gāo kàn bǎn shàng de jiāo fù liàng 。 jì jié biàn huà tóng yàng bù kě hū shì ， chūn jié hòu de yè wù jié zòu běn lái jiù yǔ nián chū bù tóng 。 jiǎ rú bǎ suǒ yǒu biàn huà chǎn shēng de xiào guǒ dōu guī gōng yú sì tiān gōng zuò zhì ， gōng sī jiù fàn le yí lòu biàn liàng de cuò wù 。 fǎn guò lái ， yě bù néng yīn wèi cún zài qí tā yīn sù biàn rèn dìng gǎi gé háo wú zuò yòng ； hé lǐ de tài dù shì chéng rèn xiàn yǒu guān chá wú fǎ bǎ gè zhǒng yǐng xiǎng bǐ cǐ fēn lí 。

tǎo lùn zhōng hái chū xiàn le xuǎn zé piān chā 。 zuì xiān cān jiā shì xíng de shì liú chéng chéng shú 、 rèn wù biān jiè qīng chǔ de sān gè chǎn pǐn zǔ ， chéng dān jǐn jí yùn wéi hé kè hù xiàn chǎng zhī chí de tuán duì zàn wèi jiā rù 。 qián zhě yuán běn jiù gèng róng yì yā suō huì yì hé jí zhōng gōng zuò ， bù néng dài biǎo quán gōng sī 。 yuán gōng wèn juǎn yě zhǔ yào yóu yuàn yì biǎo dá yì jiàn de rén tián xiě ， qí zhōng jì kě néng yǒu gǎi gé de jī jí zhī chí zhě ， yě kě néng yǒu dān xīn zhì dù qǔ xiāo ér kè yì bào xǐ de rén 。 guǎn lǐ céng céng yǐ wéi yuán gōng mǎn yì dù tí gāo néng gòu jiàn jiē zhèng míng xiào lǜ shàng shēng ， zhōu lán què tí xǐng ， mǎn yì dù yǔ chǎn chū kě néng hù xiāng yǐng xiǎng ， yě kě néng gòng tóng shòu dào guǎn lǐ fāng shì gǎi shàn de tuī dòng 。 cǐ wài ， dà jiā zhī dào gōng sī zhèng zài píng gū xīn zhì dù ， biàn kě néng zàn shí gèng jiā tóu rù ， zhè zhǒng duǎn qī fǎn yìng wèi bì néng gòu cháng qī wéi chí 。 yīn guǒ pàn duàn xū yào huí dá de shì ： rú guǒ tóng yī pī tuán duì zài xiāng tóng tiáo jiàn xià méi yǒu shí xíng sì tiān gōng zuò zhì ， tā men de chǎn chū huì zěn yàng ？ xiàn shí zhōng wú fǎ tóng shí guān chá zhè liǎng zhǒng zhuàng tài ， zhǐ néng xún zhǎo jǐn liàng kě xìn de bǐ jiào duì xiàng 。

zhōu lán tí chū fēn jiē duàn tuī jìn ， ér bú shì cāng cù dì zài quán gōng sī tǒng yī shí shī huò qǔ xiāo 。 gōng sī xiān àn yè wù xìng zhì bǎ tuán duì fēn zǔ ， zài què bǎo kè hù fú wù bù bèi zhōng duàn de qián tí xià ， què dìng ruò gān tiáo jiàn xiāng jìn 、 qiě dōu yuàn yì cān yù píng gū de tuán duì 。 bù fèn tuán duì xiān cǎi yòng sì tiān gōng zuò zhì ， lìng yī bù fèn zàn shí bǎo chí yuán ān pái ， suí hòu zài jiāo huàn 。 rèn wù kǒu jìng 、 xiàng mù fù zá dù hé jié jià rì yǐng xiǎng xū yào tí qián jì lù ， píng jià biāo zhǔn yě yào zài kàn dào jié guǒ zhī qián què dìng ， bì miǎn guǎn lǐ zhě shì hòu tiāo xuǎn yǒu lì zhǐ biāo 。 wèi jiàng dī zhì dù chā yì zào chéng de bù gōng píng ， gōng sī yǔn xǔ zàn wèi jìn rù shì xíng jiē duàn de yuán gōng huò dé xiāng yìng diào xiū ， bìng míng què píng gū bù yòng yú gè rén jì xiào pái míng 。 zhōu lán hái jiàn yì fǎng tán xiàng mù fù zé rén hé kè hù ， yīn wèi shù zì néng gòu xiǎn shì biàn huà ， què wèi bì jiě shì biàn huà wèi hé fā shēng 。 ruò huì yì jiǎn shǎo shǐ zhuān zhù shí jiān zēng jiā ， zhè shì zhī chí gǎi gé de jī zhì zhèng jù ； ruò jiāo fù zēng zhǎng zhǐ shì jiù xiàng mù jí zhōng jié xiàng ， jiù yīng zuò chū bù tóng jiě shì 。

zhè yī fāng àn zāo dào shì chǎng fù zé rén de fǎn duì 。 tā rèn wéi zhāo pìn wàng jì shāo zòng jí shì ， děng fēn jiē duàn píng gū jié shù zài xuān chuán ， gōng sī huì shī qù huà tí rè dù ； tā hái dān xīn gōng kāi chéng rèn zhèng jù bù zú huì xiǎn de guǎn lǐ céng yóu yù 。 zhōu lán huí yìng ， yīn guǒ biǎo shù bú shì wén àn fēng gé wèn tí ， ér shì duì yuán gōng hé qiú zhí zhě de shì shí chéng nuò 。 gōng sī wán quán kě yǐ shuō “ shì xíng qī jiān guān chá dào jiāo fù zēng jiā ， yuán gōng pǔ biàn huān yíng gèng wán zhěng de xiū xī shí jiān ”， què bù néng bǎ shàng wèi pái chú de xiāng guān guān xì bāo zhuāng chéng yǐ jīng zhèng shí de xiào guǒ 。 rú guǒ hòu lái quē xiàn zēng jiā 、 yuán gōng zài sì gè gōng zuò rì nèi bèi pò yán cháng gōng shí ， kuā zhāng xuān chuán bù jǐn sǔn hài xìn yù ， hái huì yǎn gài shí jì chéng běn 。 zǒng jīng lǐ zuì zhōng zuò chū jué dìng ： zàn huǎn shǐ yòng “ chǎn chū zēng jiā yóu sì tiān gōng zuò zhì dài lái ” de guǎng gào yǔ ， bǎo liú shì xíng ， bù bǎ zhōu wǔ xiū xī biàn chéng biàn xiàng dài mìng ， bìng yóu shù jù zhì lǐ 、 rén lì zī yuán hé kè hù fú wù bù mén gòng tóng jiān dū hòu xù bǐ jiào 。

jīng guò shù lún xiàng mù zhōu qī ， gōng sī dé dào de jié lùn bǐ zuì chū kǒu hào gèng kè zhì ， yě gèng yǒu yòng 。 bù tóng tuán duì de biǎo xiàn bìng bù yī zhì ： gōng zuò kě yù xiān guī huà 、 huì yì jiào duō de tuán duì zài yā suō xié zuò huán jié hòu gèng róng yì wéi chí jiāo fù ； bì xū lián xù xiǎng yìng kè hù de gǎng wèi zé xū yào lún bān hé bèi yòng rén yuán ， fǒu zé xiū xī rì kě néng zhuǎn huà wèi yǐn xìng jiā bān 。 guǎn lǐ céng yīn cǐ méi yǒu xuān bù sì tiān gōng zuò zhì bì rán tí gāo chǎn chū ， yě méi yǒu yīn xiào guǒ bù zhěng qí ér chè dǐ fàng qì gǎi gé ， ér shì yǔn xǔ gè bù mén yī jù rèn wù tè zhēng xuǎn zé gù dìng xiū xī rì 、 lún huàn zhí bān huò wéi chí yuán gōng zuò zhōu 。 zhāo pìn wǎng yè zuì zhōng xiě míng gōng sī tí gōng sì tiān gōng zuò zhì shì diǎn jí tán xìng ān pái ， bìng shuō míng zhì dù réng zài chí xù píng gū 。 gèng zhòng yào de jié guǒ shì ， gōng sī jiàn lì le zhèng cè píng gū chéng xù ： xiān jiè dìng mù biāo hé zhǐ biāo ， zài shí bié tóng qī biàn huà ， shè zhì kě bǐ jiào tiáo jiàn ， zuì hòu cái tǎo lùn yīn guǒ 。 chǎn chū zēng jiā yǔ zhì dù shí shī tóng shí chū xiàn ， shì zhí de diào chá de xiàn suǒ ， què bú shì jié lùn běn shēn 。 zhēn zhèng fù zé rèn de jué cè ， bú shì bǎ yī cì lìng rén mǎn yì de biàn huà xùn sù guī gōng yú mǒu xiàng zhèng cè ， ér shì zài bù kuā dà zhèng jù de qián tí xià ， pàn duàn tā duì nǎ xiē rén 、 zài shén me tiáo jiàn xià 、 tōng guò hé zhǒng jī zhì fā huī zuò yòng 。
translation: In early June, Haiyue Software, located in Hangzhou's Binjiang District, held its quarterly business meeting. Since March, the company had been piloting a four-day workweek, with no routine work scheduled on Fridays in principle. At the meeting, the head of operations presented an internal dashboard: during several development cycles after the pilot began, more features had passed acceptance testing than before, while the number of delayed projects had also declined somewhat. On this basis, he proposed publicly announcing that "the four-day workweek has significantly increased output" and adding this statement to the company's recruitment webpage. The human resources department supported promoting it immediately because competition for technical talent was intense; some investors also hoped that the company could use it to cultivate an image of advanced management. However, Zhou Lan, who was responsible for data governance, objected. She noted that the policy change and the increase in output had indeed occurred one after the other, but proximity in time did not establish a causal relationship. Unless the company ruled out other explanations, it could not assert that working one fewer day had produced more results. This gave rise to a disagreement at the meeting: management focused on the timing of the publicity, while the data team insisted on first determining how strong a conclusion the evidence could actually support.

Zhou Lan first examined the definition of "output." The operations dashboard counted the number of features that had passed acceptance testing, but features varied greatly in scale, difficulty, and commercial value. Correcting the position of a button and restructuring the payment system could each be recorded as one feature; developers might also divide one complete task into several smaller items to make the figures look better. More importantly, a software company's true output includes not only delivery speed but also system stability, customer satisfaction, maintenance costs, and long-term innovation. An increase in accepted projects during a particular cycle might merely reflect the concentrated completion of previously backlogged tasks and would not necessarily indicate an improvement in overall efficiency. She asked the team to examine defect-related rework, production incidents, customer feedback on renewals, and employee overtime records as well. This was not an attempt to deliberately diminish the reform's achievements, but a way to prevent a single metric from substituting for a complex reality. If the measurement itself diverged from the goals the company truly cared about, even the most sophisticated subsequent calculations could produce only a seemingly precise misjudgment.

She then catalogued the changes that had occurred alongside the pilot. In March, the company had just completed a six-month overhaul of its underlying systems, finally allowing many features that depended on those systems to enter acceptance testing; two projects that had been delayed for a long time also happened to conclude in April. Meanwhile, the sales department stopped accepting highly customized ad hoc requests, product managers began freezing each week's tasks in advance, and the development teams adopted automated testing tools. The composition of the workforce also changed: experienced engineers moved from the maintenance group to the core product group, while several new employees began working independently after completing their training. Any of these factors could have increased the delivery volume shown on the dashboard. Seasonal changes could not be ignored either, as the pace of business after the Spring Festival naturally differed from that at the beginning of the year. If the company credited the four-day workweek with the effects of all these changes, it would be making an omitted-variable error. Conversely, the existence of other factors did not justify concluding that the reform had no effect. The reasonable position was to acknowledge that the existing observations could not separate the various influences from one another.

Selection bias also emerged during the discussion. The first participants in the pilot were three product groups with mature processes and clearly defined task boundaries, while the teams responsible for emergency operations and maintenance and on-site customer support had not yet joined. The former were already better positioned to reduce meetings and concentrate their work, so they could not represent the entire company. The employee survey was also completed mainly by people willing to express their views. These respondents might include both enthusiastic supporters of the reform and employees who deliberately reported positive experiences because they feared the policy would be withdrawn. Management had assumed that higher employee satisfaction could indirectly prove an increase in efficiency, but Zhou Lan cautioned that satisfaction and output might influence each other or might both be driven by improvements in management practices. In addition, because everyone knew the company was evaluating the new policy, they might temporarily become more engaged, and this short-term response might not be sustainable. The causal question was this: if the same teams had not adopted the four-day workweek under otherwise identical conditions, what would their output have been? Because these two states could not be observed simultaneously in reality, the company could only seek comparison groups that were as credible as possible.

Zhou Lan proposed proceeding in stages rather than hastily implementing or abolishing the policy uniformly throughout the company. The company would first group teams by the nature of their work and, while ensuring that customer service was not interrupted, identify several teams that operated under similar conditions and were all willing to participate in the evaluation. Some teams would adopt the four-day workweek first, while others would temporarily retain their existing schedules, after which they would switch. The definitions used for tasks, project complexity, and the effects of public holidays would need to be documented in advance, and the evaluation criteria would have to be established before the results were seen so that managers could not selectively choose favorable metrics afterward. To reduce the unfairness caused by differences in the policy, the company would allow employees who had not yet entered the pilot phase to receive corresponding compensatory time off and would make clear that the evaluation would not be used to rank individual performance. Zhou Lan also recommended interviewing project leaders and customers because figures could reveal that a change had occurred but might not explain why it had occurred. If reducing meetings increased time for focused work, that would provide evidence of a mechanism supporting the reform; if delivery growth merely resulted from a cluster of old projects reaching completion, it should be interpreted differently.

The head of marketing opposed this proposal. He argued that the peak recruitment season would quickly pass and that, if the company waited until the phased evaluation was complete before promoting the policy, it would lose the topic's momentum. He also worried that publicly acknowledging insufficient evidence would make management appear indecisive. Zhou Lan responded that causal wording was not a matter of copywriting style but a factual commitment to employees and job applicants. The company could certainly say, "During the pilot, we observed an increase in deliveries, and employees generally welcomed having a more substantial period of rest," but it could not present a correlation that had not yet been disentangled from other explanations as a proven effect. If defects later increased or employees were forced to work longer hours during the four working days, exaggerated publicity would not only damage the company's credibility but also conceal the actual costs. The general manager ultimately decided to postpone using the advertising claim that "the increase in output was caused by the four-day workweek," continue the pilot, prevent Friday leave from turning into disguised on-call duty, and have the data governance, human resources, and customer service departments jointly oversee subsequent comparisons.

After several rounds of project cycles, the company reached a conclusion that was more restrained than its original slogan but also more useful. Performance was not consistent across teams: teams whose work could be planned in advance and that held many meetings found it easier to maintain delivery levels after streamlining coordination, whereas roles requiring continuous responses to customers needed rotating shifts and backup personnel, without which days off could turn into hidden overtime. Management therefore neither declared that a four-day workweek would necessarily increase output nor abandoned the reform entirely because its effects were uneven. Instead, it allowed each department to choose fixed days off, rotating on-call schedules, or the original workweek according to the characteristics of its tasks. The recruitment webpage ultimately stated that the company offered a four-day workweek pilot and flexible arrangements, while explaining that the policy remained under ongoing evaluation. More importantly, the company established a policy evaluation procedure: first define the goals and metrics, then identify concurrent changes, establish comparable conditions, and only afterward discuss causation. The fact that increased output and the policy's implementation occurred at the same time was a lead worth investigating, not a conclusion in itself. Truly responsible decision-making does not mean quickly attributing a satisfying change to a particular policy. It means determining, without overstating the evidence, for whom the policy works, under what conditions, and through what mechanisms.

grammar.explanation: 用于否定一种目的、性质或判断，并强调真正的目的、性质或判断。
grammar.example: 这样做不是故意降低改革的成绩，而是防止单一指标代替复杂事实。

grammar.explanation: 表示前一种做法在证据或条件允许的范围内可行，但后一种做法超出了合理边界。
grammar.example: 公司完全可以说“试行期间观察到交付增加，员工普遍欢迎更完整的休息时间”，却不能把尚未排除的相关关系包装成已经证实的效果。

grammar.explanation: 表示不能仅依据某个原因就仓促得出后面的结论，强调推断需要更充分的证据。
grammar.example: 反过来，也不能因为存在其他因素便认定改革毫无作用；合理的态度是承认现有观察无法把各种影响彼此分离。

questions.prompt: 周岚为什么反对立即宣称“四天工作制显著提升产出”？
options: 制度实施和产出增长在时间上相邻，但这不足以证明两者存在因果关系
公司尚未统计四天工作制实施前的功能数量
投资人明确反对公司宣传新的工作制度
员工满意度在试行期间出现了明显下降
questions.explanation: 周岚认为，两个现象先后发生只能说明时间上的相关性；在排除同期变化等其他解释之前，不能认定四天工作制导致了产出增长。
questions.evidence: 她指出，制度调整与产出增长确实先后发生，但时间上的相邻并不等于因果关系。

questions.prompt: 周岚建议如何安排不同团队，以获得更可信的比较结果？
options: 让全公司同时采用四天工作制，再与其他公司比较
让部分团队先采用新制度，另一部分保持原安排，之后再交换
只选择流程成熟的三个产品组长期参加试行
立即取消试行，等所有项目完成后重新开始
questions.explanation: 她提出让条件相近的团队在不同时段采用不同安排并随后交换，这样可以形成更可比的观察条件，减少团队固定差异对结果的影响。
questions.evidence: 部分团队先采用四天工作制，另一部分暂时保持原安排，随后再交换。

questions.prompt: 招聘网页最终如何介绍公司的工作制度？

只宣传员工欢迎更完整的休息时间，不提制度是否仍在评估
说明公司提供四天工作制试点及弹性安排，并明确制度仍在持续评估
