questions.prompt: 周岚认为最初的项目设计存在哪一项关键问题？
options: 学生由自愿报名进入课程，两组在课程开始前可能已经存在差异
学校强制所有学生观看短视频，无法设置普通课程组
两组学生入学时的词汇成绩差距过大，无法进行比较
负责两组课程的教师完全没有提供答疑和练习
questions.explanation: 最初没有进行随机分组，而是让学生自愿报名。愿意报名者可能在学习动机、时间安排和设备使用习惯等方面本来就不同，因此不能直接把成绩差异归因于短视频。
questions.evidence: 原来，项目开始时并没有随机分组，而是由学生自愿报名。

questions.prompt: 重新设计的新测验为什么尽量采用课程中没有原样出现的语境？
options: 为了缩短测试时间并减少学生中途退出的可能
为了同时检验词义识别以及在新语境中推断、辨析和表达的能力
为了让视频组依靠对字幕和原句的熟悉感提高成绩
为了使测试内容只反映学生对视频例句的短期记忆
questions.explanation: 采用未原样出现的语境，可以避免测验仅仅考查学生是否记住课程例句，并进一步判断他们能否把词汇知识迁移到新的语言环境中。
questions.evidence: 新测验尽量使用课程中没有原样出现的语境，既检查词义识别，也要求学生在短文中推断含义、辨析近义词并完成恰当表达。

questions.prompt: 文章最后如何评价承认证据边界与教学创新之间的关系？
options: 承认证据存在局限会妨碍学校尝试任何新教学工具
只要教学工具受到学生欢迎，就不必继续检验其长期效果
承认证据边界并不排斥创新，反而有助于把资源投入经得起检验的改进
学校应停止使用短视频，把全部经费投入传统阅读讲解
questions.explanation: 文章并未把谨慎检验证据与支持创新对立起来，而是认为明确证据的适用边界能够防止把短期热度误判为稳定效果，从而提高时间和经费的使用质量。
questions.evidence: 承认现有证据的边界，并不妨碍创新；相反，它能防止学校把一时的热度当成稳定效果，让有限的时间和经费用在经得起检验的改进上。

articles.title: 永安步行街空铺率下降，究竟是不是改造的功劳
articles.summary: 临江市永安步行街完成改造后，沿街空铺率连续两个季度下降。市商业更新办公室没有立即把变化归功于改造，而是核对统计口径、比较未改造街区，并追查租金减免、地铁施工结束和商户迁移等因素，最终形成了一项更谨慎的因果判断与后续政策决定。
articles.topic: 永安步行街空铺率下降，究竟是不是改造的功劳
paragraphs: 临江市老城区的永安步行街全长一千多米，连接火车站、中心菜市场和滨河居民区。过去几年，街上车辆与行人混行，雨天积水，店铺招牌彼此遮挡，夜间照明也不充分。市政府随后实施改造：调整路面铺装，限制机动车进入，增设座椅、树池和公共厕所，并统一整治杂乱招牌。工程结束半年后，市商业更新办公室发布阶段报告，指出沿街空铺率已经连续两个季度下降。消息很快被媒体概括成一句醒目的结论：“步行街改造显著降低空铺率。”负责该项目评估的周岚却没有在报告发布会上重复这句话。她认为，空铺率下降是真实观察到的现象，但“改造之后发生”并不等于“由改造造成”。如果没有弄清其他变化，仅凭时间上的先后关系就宣布因果成立，不仅可能误导公众，还会影响下一轮财政资金投向。

周岚首先要求工作人员回到最基础的问题：所谓空铺，究竟怎样认定。工程开始前，街道办主要依靠巡查人员观察卷帘门是否关闭；工程结束后，物业公司则把没有有效租赁合同的店面列为空铺。两套口径看似相近，实际并不一致。一家正在装修、尚未营业的店铺，在巡查记录中可能被算作空铺，在物业台账中却可能已经出租；一家偶尔开门、实际停止经营的商店，又可能逃过现场观察。更复杂的是，改造期间有十几家商户被临时安置到附近市场，工程结束后才陆续迁回。如果把迁回视为新店入驻，就会夸大改造后的改善幅度。评估组于是逐户核对租赁合同、用电情况、营业登记和现场照片，并用同一标准重新整理改造前后的记录。复核结果仍然显示空铺减少，却也证明原报告中的降幅包含统计口径变化。围绕结论的第一个冲突由此出现：项目施工部门担心修正数据会削弱工程成绩，评估组则坚持，成绩是否经得起核验，比数字是否漂亮更重要。

即使统一了口径，因果问题仍未解决。评估组选择老城区另外两条尚未改造的商业街作为参照。这两条街与永安街的店铺规模、客源结构和租金水平较为接近，但位置并不完全相同，因此不能把它们当成完美的“另一个永安街”。工作人员比较后发现，同一时期，参照街区的空铺也有所减少，只是变化没有永安街明显。这说明当地消费和租赁市场可能正在共同回暖，永安街的下降不能全部归因于改造。随后，他们又梳理时间线：步行街开放前后，火车站地铁施工结束，原先封闭的两个出入口恢复通行；区属商业公司还对新签约的小店提供了短期租金减免；一家连锁书店进驻街口后，带来了几家餐饮和文创商户。这些事件都可能同时提高店铺出租率。若忽略它们，所谓改造效果便会混入交通恢复、优惠政策和主力店带动等因素。评估组没有声称能够把每种因素精确分离，而是明确列出哪些影响已经控制，哪些仍无法排除。

为了判断改造是否至少发挥了独立作用，周岚把调查重点从“空了多少间”转向“为什么有人愿意租”。她和同事访谈了房东、老商户、新租户、外卖骑手及附近居民，并查看不同路段的客流变化。靠近恢复开放的地铁口，店铺回租主要受交通改善推动；靠近连锁书店的路段，则明显存在主力店聚集效应。然而在距离这两处较远的中段，多位经营者反复提到相同细节：人车分流后，顾客愿意停留，夜间照明改善后，晚间营业不再显得冷清，公共座椅也让老人和带孩子的家庭停留更久。这些陈述不能单独证明因果，却与现场观察互相印证。评估组还发现，并非所有改造内容都产生积极影响。统一招牌削弱了部分老店的辨识度，禁止临时卸货增加了商户成本，节假日摊位又遮挡了几家固定门店。商户协会因此反对把改造包装成毫无代价的成功案例，施工部门则认为负面意见只是适应期现象。双方争论的核心，不是街道是否变美，而是环境改善能否稳定转化为经营收益。

在第二次项目协调会上，分管副市长原本希望直接批准另外三条街照搬永安模式。周岚建议暂缓整体复制，只确认一个范围有限的结论：在排除统计口径变化并考虑市场回暖、租金减免和交通恢复后，现有证据支持步行环境改善对部分路段的出租恢复作出了贡献，但不足以证明空铺率下降完全由改造导致，更不能保证同样方案在别处取得相同结果。她提出把下一阶段政策拆成两部分。对于排水、照明、无障碍通行和人车分流等使用效果较明确的措施，可以在其他街区推进；对于统一招牌、全面禁行和固定摊位布局，则应先做小范围试点，并保留未改造路段作为比较对象。同时，商业部门不得把租金优惠与街道改造合并宣传，相关费用和受益商户必须单独记录。这个决定令施工部门失望，因为它无法提供一句简单有力的政绩口号，却得到商户协会支持。市政府最终接受了分阶段实施方案，并要求后续报告公开口径、时间线和无法排除的解释。

又过两个季度，永安街的空铺率没有反弹，但下降速度趋缓。租金减免陆续退出后，一些依赖优惠入驻的店铺离开；与此同时，中段几家经营稳定的新店续签了合同，夜间餐饮客流也保持活跃。评估组据此更新判断：改造并非一把可以单独解决空铺问题的钥匙，它更像是改善经营条件的基础工程。它能降低顾客停留和通行的障碍，却不能替代合理租金、清晰定位、稳定客源和便利物流。市政府因此没有宣布“因果关系已被彻底证明”，而是把结论改为“改造具有促进作用，其效果取决于配套条件”。三条拟改造街道也不再复制同一套外观方案，而是分别针对积水、夜间安全和交通冲突制定措施。永安街的案例最终提供的，不只是一次街区更新经验，更是一条公共决策原则：面对一个看似顺理成章的因果说法，应先统一测量标准，再寻找可以比较的对象，检查同期事件，辨认作用机制，并诚实说明证据边界。承认不确定性并不会削弱决策，反而能避免把偶然变化误当成普遍规律。
pinyin: lín jiāng shì lǎo chéng qū de yǒng ān bù xíng jiē quán zhǎng yī qiān duō mǐ ， lián jiē huǒ chē zhàn 、 zhōng xīn cài shì chǎng hé bīn hé jū mín qū 。 guò qù jǐ nián ， jiē shàng chē liàng yǔ xíng rén hùn xíng ， yǔ tiān jī shuǐ ， diàn pù zhāo pái bǐ cǐ zhē dǎng ， yè jiān zhào míng yě bù chōng fèn 。 shì zhèng fǔ suí hòu shí shī gǎi zào ： tiáo zhěng lù miàn pù zhuāng ， xiàn zhì jī dòng chē jìn rù ， zēng shè zuò yǐ 、 shù chí hé gōng gòng cè suǒ ， bìng tǒng yī zhěng zhì zá luàn zhāo pái 。 gōng chéng jié shù bàn nián hòu ， shì shāng yè gēng xīn bàn gōng shì fā bù jiē duàn bào gào ， zhǐ chū yán jiē kōng pù lǜ yǐ jīng lián xù liǎng gè jì dù xià jiàng 。 xiāo xī hěn kuài bèi méi tǐ gài kuò chéng yī jù xǐng mù dì jié lùn ：“ bù xíng jiē gǎi zào xiǎn zhù jiàng dī kōng pù lǜ 。” fù zé gāi xiàng mù píng gū de zhōu lán què méi yǒu zài bào gào fā bù huì shàng chóng fù zhè jù huà 。 tā rèn wéi ， kōng pù lǜ xià jiàng shì zhēn shí guān chá dào de xiàn xiàng ， dàn “ gǎi zào zhī hòu fā shēng ” bìng bù děng yú “ yóu gǎi zào zào chéng ”。 rú guǒ méi yǒu nòng qīng qí tā biàn huà ， jǐn píng shí jiān shàng de xiān hòu guān xì jiù xuān bù yīn guǒ chéng lì ， bù jǐn kě néng wù dǎo gōng zhòng ， hái huì yǐng xiǎng xià yī lún cái zhèng zī jīn tóu xiàng 。

zhōu lán shǒu xiān yāo qiú gōng zuò rén yuán huí dào zuì jī chǔ de wèn tí ： suǒ wèi kōng pù ， jiū jìng zěn yàng rèn dìng 。 gōng chéng kāi shǐ qián ， jiē dào bàn zhǔ yào yī kào xún chá rén yuán guān chá juàn lián mén shì fǒu guān bì ； gōng chéng jié shù hòu ， wù yè gōng sī zé bǎ méi yǒu yǒu xiào zū lìn hé tóng de diàn miàn liè wèi kōng pù 。 liǎng tào kǒu jìng kàn shì xiāng jìn ， shí jì bìng bù yī zhì 。 yī jiā zhèng zài zhuāng xiū 、 shàng wèi yíng yè de diàn pù ， zài xún chá jì lù zhōng kě néng bèi suàn zuò kōng pù ， zài wù yè tái zhàng zhōng què kě néng yǐ jīng chū zū ； yī jiā ǒu ěr kāi mén 、 shí jì tíng zhǐ jīng yíng de shāng diàn ， yòu kě néng táo guò xiàn chǎng guān chá 。 gèng fù zá de shì ， gǎi zào qī jiān yǒu shí jǐ jiā shāng hù bèi lín shí ān zhì dào fù jìn shì chǎng ， gōng chéng jié shù hòu cái lù xù qiān huí 。 rú guǒ bǎ qiān huí shì wèi xīn diàn rù zhù ， jiù huì kuā dà gǎi zào hòu de gǎi shàn fú dù 。 píng gū zǔ yú shì zhú hù hé duì zū lìn hé tóng 、 yòng diàn qíng kuàng 、 yíng yè dēng jì hé xiàn chǎng zhào piān ， bìng yòng tóng yī biāo zhǔn chóng xīn zhěng lǐ gǎi zào qián hòu de jì lù 。 fù hé jié guǒ réng rán xiǎn shì kōng pù jiǎn shǎo ， què yě zhèng míng yuán bào gào zhōng de jiàng fú bāo hán tǒng jì kǒu jìng biàn huà 。 wéi rào jié lùn de dì yí gè chōng tū yóu cǐ chū xiàn ： xiàng mù shī gōng bù mén dān xīn xiū zhèng shù jù huì xuē ruò gōng chéng chéng jì ， píng gū zǔ zé jiān chí ， chéng jì shì fǒu jīng dé qǐ hé yàn ， bǐ shù zì shì fǒu piào liàng gèng zhòng yào 。

jí shǐ tǒng yī liǎo kǒu jìng ， yīn guǒ wèn tí réng wèi jiě jué 。 píng gū zǔ xuǎn zé lǎo chéng qū lìng wài liǎng tiáo shàng wèi gǎi zào de shāng yè jiē zuò wéi cān zhào 。 zhè liǎng tiáo jiē yǔ yǒng ān jiē de diàn pù guī mó 、 kè yuán jié gòu hé zū jīn shuǐ píng jiào wéi jiē jìn ， dàn wèi zhì bìng bù wán quán xiāng tóng ， yīn cǐ bù néng bǎ tā men dàng chéng wán měi de “ lìng yí gè yǒng ān jiē ”。 gōng zuò rén yuán bǐ jiào hòu fā xiàn ， tóng yī shí qī ， cān zhào jiē qū de kōng pù yě yǒu suǒ jiǎn shǎo ， zhǐ shì biàn huà méi yǒu yǒng ān jiē míng xiǎn 。 zhè shuō míng dāng dì xiāo fèi hé zū lìn shì chǎng kě néng zhèng zài gòng tóng huí nuǎn ， yǒng ān jiē de xià jiàng bù néng quán bù guī yīn yú gǎi zào 。 suí hòu ， tā men yòu shū lǐ shí jiān xiàn ： bù xíng jiē kāi fàng qián hòu ， huǒ chē zhàn dì tiě shī gōng jié shù ， yuán xiān fēng bì de liǎng gè chū rù kǒu huī fù tōng xíng ； qū shǔ shāng yè gōng sī hái duì xīn qiān yuē de xiǎo diàn tí gōng le duǎn qī zū jīn jiǎn miǎn ； yī jiā lián suǒ shū diàn jìn zhù jiē kǒu hòu ， dài lái le jǐ jiā cān yǐn hé wén chuàng shāng hù 。 zhè xiē shì jiàn dōu kě néng tóng shí tí gāo diàn pù chū zū lǜ 。 ruò hū lüè tā men ， suǒ wèi gǎi zào xiào guǒ biàn huì hùn rù jiāo tōng huī fù 、 yōu huì zhèng cè hé zhǔ lì diàn dài dòng děng yīn sù 。 píng gū zǔ méi yǒu shēng chēng néng gòu bǎ měi zhǒng yīn sù jīng què fēn lí ， ér shì míng què liè chū nǎ xiē yǐng xiǎng yǐ jīng kòng zhì ， nǎ xiē réng wú fǎ pái chú 。

wèi le pàn duàn gǎi zào shì fǒu zhì shǎo fā huī le dú lì zuò yòng ， zhōu lán bǎ diào chá zhòng diǎn cóng “ kōng le duō shǎo jiān ” zhuǎn xiàng “ wèi shén me yǒu rén yuàn yì zū ”。 tā hé tóng shì fǎng tán le fáng dōng 、 lǎo shāng hù 、 xīn zū hù 、 wài mài qí shǒu jí fù jìn jū mín ， bìng chá kàn bù tóng lù duàn de kè liú biàn huà 。 kào jìn huī fù kāi fàng de dì tiě kǒu ， diàn pù huí zū zhǔ yào shòu jiāo tōng gǎi shàn tuī dòng ； kào jìn lián suǒ shū diàn de lù duàn ， zé míng xiǎn cún zài zhǔ lì diàn jù jí xiào yìng 。 rán ér zài jù lí zhè liǎng chù jiào yuǎn de zhōng duàn ， duō wèi jīng yíng zhě fǎn fù tí dào xiāng tóng xì jié ： rén chē fēn liú hòu ， gù kè yuàn yì tíng liú ， yè jiān zhào míng gǎi shàn hòu ， wǎn jiān yíng yè bù zài xiǎn de lěng qīng ， gōng gòng zuò yǐ yě ràng lǎo rén hé dài hái zi de jiā tíng tíng liú gèng jiǔ 。 zhè xiē chén shù bù néng dān dú zhèng míng yīn guǒ ， què yǔ xiàn chǎng guān chá hù xiāng yìn zhèng 。 píng gū zǔ hái fā xiàn ， bìng fēi suǒ yǒu gǎi zào nèi róng dōu chǎn shēng jī jí yǐng xiǎng 。 tǒng yī zhāo pái xuē ruò le bù fèn lǎo diàn de biàn shí dù ， jìn zhǐ lín shí xiè huò zēng jiā le shāng hù chéng běn ， jié jià rì tān wèi yòu zhē dǎng le jǐ jiā gù dìng mén diàn 。 shāng hù xié huì yīn cǐ fǎn duì bǎ gǎi zào bāo zhuāng chéng háo wú dài jià de chéng gōng àn lì ， shī gōng bù mén zé rèn wéi fù miàn yì jiàn zhǐ shì shì yìng qī xiàn xiàng 。 shuāng fāng zhēng lùn de hé xīn ， bú shì jiē dào shì fǒu biàn měi ， ér shì huán jìng gǎi shàn néng fǒu wěn dìng zhuǎn huà wèi jīng yíng shōu yì 。

zài dì èr cì xiàng mù xié tiáo huì shàng ， fēn guǎn fù shì zhǎng yuán běn xī wàng zhí jiē pī zhǔn lìng wài sān tiáo jiē zhào bān yǒng ān mó shì 。 zhōu lán jiàn yì zàn huǎn zhěng tǐ fù zhì ， zhǐ què rèn yí gè fàn wéi yǒu xiàn de jié lùn ： zài pái chú tǒng jì kǒu jìng biàn huà bìng kǎo lǜ shì chǎng huí nuǎn 、 zū jīn jiǎn miǎn hé jiāo tōng huī fù hòu ， xiàn yǒu zhèng jù zhī chí bù xíng huán jìng gǎi shàn duì bù fèn lù duàn de chū zū huī fù zuò chū le gòng xiàn ， dàn bù zú yǐ zhèng míng kōng pù lǜ xià jiàng wán quán yóu gǎi zào dǎo zhì ， gèng bù néng bǎo zhèng tóng yàng fāng àn zài bié chù qǔ dé xiāng tóng jié guǒ 。 tā tí chū bǎ xià yī jiē duàn zhèng cè chāi chéng liǎng bù fèn 。 duì yú pái shuǐ 、 zhào míng 、 wú zhàng ài tōng xíng hé rén chē fēn liú děng shǐ yòng xiào guǒ jiào míng què de cuò shī ， kě yǐ zài qí tā jiē qū tuī jìn ； duì yú tǒng yī zhāo pái 、 quán miàn jìn xíng hé gù dìng tān wèi bù jú ， zé yīng xiān zuò xiǎo fàn wéi shì diǎn ， bìng bǎo liú wèi gǎi zào lù duàn zuò wéi bǐ jiào duì xiàng 。 tóng shí ， shāng yè bù mén bù dé bǎ zū jīn yōu huì yǔ jiē dào gǎi zào hé bìng xuān chuán ， xiāng guān fèi yòng hé shòu yì shāng hù bì xū dān dú jì lù 。 zhè ge jué dìng lìng shī gōng bù mén shī wàng ， yīn wèi tā wú fǎ tí gōng yī jù jiǎn dān yǒu lì de zhèng jì kǒu hào ， què dé dào shāng hù xié huì zhī chí 。 shì zhèng fǔ zuì zhōng jiē shòu le fēn jiē duàn shí shī fāng àn ， bìng yāo qiú hòu xù bào gào gōng kāi kǒu jìng 、 shí jiān xiàn hé wú fǎ pái chú de jiě shì 。

yòu guò liǎng gè jì dù ， yǒng ān jiē de kōng pù lǜ méi yǒu fǎn tán ， dàn xià jiàng sù dù qū huǎn 。 zū jīn jiǎn miǎn lù xù tuì chū hòu ， yī xiē yī lài yōu huì rù zhù de diàn pù lí kāi ； yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， zhōng duàn jǐ jiā jīng yíng wěn dìng de xīn diàn xù qiān le hé tóng ， yè jiān cān yǐn kè liú yě bǎo chí huó yuè 。 píng gū zǔ jù cǐ gēng xīn pàn duàn ： gǎi zào bìng fēi yī bǎ kě yǐ dān dú jiě jué kōng pù wèn tí de yào shi ， tā gèng xiàng shì gǎi shàn jīng yíng tiáo jiàn de jī chǔ gōng chéng 。 tā néng jiàng dī gù kè tíng liú hé tōng xíng de zhàng ài ， què bù néng tì dài hé lǐ zū jīn 、 qīng xī dìng wèi 、 wěn dìng kè yuán hé biàn lì wù liú 。 shì zhèng fǔ yīn cǐ méi yǒu xuān bù “ yīn guǒ guān xì yǐ bèi chè dǐ zhèng míng ”， ér shì bǎ jié lùn gǎi wéi “ gǎi zào jù yǒu cù jìn zuò yòng ， qí xiào guǒ qǔ jué yú pèi tào tiáo jiàn ”。 sān tiáo nǐ gǎi zào jiē dào yě bù zài fù zhì tóng yī tào wài guān fāng àn ， ér shì fēn bié zhēn duì jī shuǐ 、 yè jiān ān quán hé jiāo tōng chōng tū zhì dìng cuò shī 。 yǒng ān jiē de àn lì zuì zhōng tí gōng de ， bù zhǐ shì yī cì jiē qū gēng xīn jīng yàn ， gèng shì yī tiáo gōng gòng jué cè yuán zé ： miàn duì yí gè kàn shì shùn lǐ chéng zhāng de yīn guǒ shuō fǎ ， yīng xiān tǒng yī cè liáng biāo zhǔn ， zài xún zhǎo kě yǐ bǐ jiào de duì xiàng ， jiǎn chá tóng qī shì jiàn ， biàn rèn zuò yòng jī zhì ， bìng chéng shí shuō míng zhèng jù biān jiè 。 chéng rèn bù què dìng xìng bìng bú huì xuē ruò jué cè ， fǎn ér néng bì miǎn bǎ ǒu rán biàn huà wù dàng chéng pǔ biàn guī lǜ 。
translation: Yong'an Pedestrian Street in Linjiang's old city is more than one kilometer long, connecting the railway station, the central produce market, and a riverside residential area. In previous years, vehicles and pedestrians shared the street, water accumulated on rainy days, storefront signs blocked one another, and nighttime lighting was inadequate. The municipal government subsequently carried out a renovation project: it adjusted the pavement, restricted motor vehicle access, added seating, tree pits, and public restrooms, and standardized the disorderly storefront signs. Six months after the project was completed, the municipal Office of Commercial Renewal issued an interim report stating that the vacancy rate among storefronts along the street had fallen for two consecutive quarters. The media quickly condensed the news into a striking conclusion: “The pedestrian street renovation significantly reduced the storefront vacancy rate.” Zhou Lan, who was responsible for evaluating the project, did not repeat that statement at the report's release event. In her view, the decline in the vacancy rate was a genuinely observed phenomenon, but “happened after the renovation” did not mean “was caused by the renovation.” Declaring a causal relationship solely on the basis of chronological sequence, without clarifying what else had changed, could not only mislead the public but also affect where fiscal funding was directed in the next round.

Zhou Lan first asked the staff to return to the most basic question: exactly how should a vacant storefront be identified? Before the project began, the subdistrict office mainly relied on inspectors to observe whether roll-up doors were closed; after the project ended, the property management company classified storefronts without valid leases as vacant. The two criteria appeared similar but were not actually consistent. A shop that was being renovated and had not yet opened might be counted as vacant in inspection records even though the property ledger showed that it had already been leased. Conversely, a shop that opened only occasionally but had effectively ceased operating might escape detection during an on-site inspection. Complicating matters further, more than a dozen merchants were temporarily relocated to a nearby market during the renovation and moved back only gradually after the work was completed. Treating their return as the arrival of new shops would exaggerate the scale of the post-renovation improvement. The evaluation team therefore checked every storefront's lease, electricity consumption, business registration, and site photographs, then reorganized the records from before and after the renovation using the same standard. The review still showed that the number of vacant storefronts had decreased, but it also demonstrated that part of the decline reported originally resulted from a change in statistical criteria. This gave rise to the first dispute over the conclusion: the project construction department worried that revising the data would diminish the project's achievements, while the evaluation team insisted that whether the results could withstand verification mattered more than whether the figures looked impressive.

Even after the criteria were standardized, the question of causality remained unresolved. The evaluation team selected two other commercial streets in the old city that had not yet been renovated as comparisons. These streets were relatively similar to Yong'an Street in store size, customer composition, and rent levels, but their locations were not identical, so they could not be treated as perfect versions of “another Yong'an Street.” The staff's comparison showed that storefront vacancies in the comparison areas had also declined during the same period, though less markedly than on Yong'an Street. This indicated that the local consumer economy and rental market might have been recovering more broadly, so the decline on Yong'an Street could not be attributed entirely to the renovation. The team then reconstructed the timeline. Around the time the pedestrian street reopened, subway construction at the railway station was completed, and two previously closed entrances and exits reopened to traffic. A district-owned commercial company also offered short-term rent reductions to newly contracted small businesses. After a chain bookstore moved into a location at the entrance to the street, it attracted several food-service and cultural and creative businesses. All these events could have increased the storefront occupancy rate at the same time. If they were ignored, the supposed effect of the renovation would be mixed together with factors such as restored transportation access, preferential policies, and the draw of an anchor store. The evaluation team did not claim that it could precisely separate every factor. Instead, it clearly listed which influences had been accounted for and which still could not be ruled out.

To determine whether the renovation had at least played an independent role, Zhou Lan shifted the investigation's focus from “how many storefronts were vacant” to “why people were willing to rent them.” She and her colleagues interviewed landlords, established merchants, new tenants, delivery riders, and nearby residents, and examined changes in pedestrian traffic across different sections of the street. Near the reopened subway entrance, storefronts were leased again mainly because of improved transportation access. The section near the chain bookstore, meanwhile, clearly showed an anchor-store clustering effect. Yet in the middle section, farther from both locations, multiple business operators repeatedly mentioned the same details: after pedestrians and vehicles were separated, customers were more willing to linger; after nighttime lighting improved, evening business no longer felt deserted; and public seating encouraged older people and families with children to stay longer. These statements could not prove causation on their own, but they corroborated the team's on-site observations. The evaluation team also found that not every element of the renovation had a positive effect. Standardized signs reduced the visibility of some long-established shops, the ban on temporary loading and unloading increased merchants' costs, and holiday stalls obstructed several permanent storefronts. The merchants' association therefore opposed presenting the renovation as a success story without any costs, while the construction department maintained that the negative reactions were merely a feature of the adjustment period. The central issue in their dispute was not whether the street had become more attractive, but whether the environmental improvements could be converted reliably into business returns.

At the second project coordination meeting, the deputy mayor overseeing the initiative had originally hoped to approve the direct replication of the Yong'an model on three other streets. Zhou Lan recommended postponing wholesale replication and endorsing only a limited conclusion: after eliminating the effects of changed statistical criteria and taking into account the market recovery, rent reductions, and restored transportation access, the available evidence supported the finding that improvements to the pedestrian environment had contributed to a recovery in storefront leasing in some sections. It was not sufficient, however, to prove that the decline in the vacancy rate was caused entirely by the renovation, much less to guarantee that the same plan would produce identical results elsewhere. She proposed dividing the next stage of policy into two parts. Measures with relatively clear practical benefits, such as drainage, lighting, accessibility, and the separation of pedestrians and vehicles, could be advanced in other commercial areas. Standardized signs, comprehensive traffic bans, and fixed stall layouts, however, should first undergo small-scale trials, with unrenovated sections retained as comparison sites. At the same time, the commerce department was prohibited from promoting rent incentives and street renovations as a single measure, and the associated costs and beneficiary merchants had to be recorded separately. The decision disappointed the construction department because it could not provide a simple, forceful slogan highlighting its achievements, but it won the support of the merchants' association. The municipal government ultimately accepted the phased implementation plan and required subsequent reports to disclose their criteria, timelines, and explanations that could not be ruled out.

Two more quarters later, the storefront vacancy rate on Yong'an Street had not rebounded, but its rate of decline had slowed. As the rent reductions were gradually withdrawn, some shops that had moved in because of the incentives left. At the same time, several new shops with stable operations in the middle section renewed their leases, and nighttime restaurant traffic remained strong. The evaluation team updated its assessment accordingly: the renovation was not a key that could solve the storefront vacancy problem by itself; it was more like a foundational project that improved operating conditions. It could reduce obstacles to customers' movement and willingness to linger, but it could not substitute for reasonable rents, clear positioning, a stable customer base, and convenient logistics. The municipal government therefore did not declare that “the causal relationship has been conclusively proven.” Instead, it revised the conclusion to state that “the renovation has a beneficial effect, but its results depend on supporting conditions.” The three streets scheduled for renovation also stopped replicating the same visual design and instead developed separate measures addressing water accumulation, nighttime safety, and conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles. Ultimately, the Yong'an Street case offered more than experience in neighborhood renewal. It also provided a principle for public decision-making: when faced with a causal claim that appears self-evident, decision-makers should first standardize measurement criteria, then find suitable comparison cases, examine concurrent events, identify the mechanisms at work, and honestly state the limits of the evidence. Acknowledging uncertainty does not weaken decision-making; rather, it prevents accidental changes from being mistaken for universal patterns.

grammar.explanation: 用于递进关系，表示后一结果在前一结果的基础上进一步加重或扩展影响。
grammar.example: 如果没有弄清其他变化，仅凭时间上的先后关系就宣布因果成立，不仅可能误导公众，还会影响下一轮财政资金投向。

grammar.explanation: 用于让步关系，表示虽然承认前面的条件，但后面的情况依然存在。
grammar.example: 即使统一了口径，因果问题仍未解决。

grammar.explanation: 用于否定一种理解并肯定另一种理解，以突出真正的重点。
grammar.example: 双方争论的核心，不是街道是否变美，而是环境改善能否稳定转化为经营收益。

questions.prompt: 评估组为什么要用同一标准重新整理改造前后的记录？
options: 工程前后认定空铺的统计口径并不一致
参照街区与永安街的位置完全相同
施工部门没有保存任何现场照片
物业公司拒绝提供有效租赁合同
questions.explanation: 工程开始前依据卷帘门是否关闭判断，工程结束后则依据是否存在有效租赁合同判断，两套标准并不一致，可能造成降幅被夸大，因此必须统一口径后重新整理记录。
questions.evidence: 两套口径看似相近，实际并不一致。

questions.prompt: 中段经营者的陈述主要支持了哪一种判断？
options: 连锁书店是所有路段出租恢复的唯一原因
步行环境改善可能提高顾客停留意愿并促进经营
统一招牌显著增强了所有老店的辨识度
租金减免退出后店铺出租率立即大幅反弹
questions.explanation: 远离地铁口和连锁书店的中段经营者反复提到人车分流、夜间照明和公共座椅带来的停留改善，这说明步行环境改善可能通过改变顾客行为促进经营。
questions.evidence: 然而在距离这两处较远的中段，多位经营者反复提到相同细节：人车分流后，顾客愿意停留，夜间照明改善后，晚间营业不再显得冷清，公共座椅也让老人和带孩子的家庭停留更久。

questions.prompt: 永安街案例最终提出的公共决策原则是什么？
options: 只要改造后指标改善，就可以直接确认因果关系
为了形成有力的政绩口号，应当忽略无法排除的因素
应统一测量标准、设置比较对象、检查同期事件并说明证据边界
所有商业街都应完整复制永安街的外观方案
questions.explanation: 文章强调，面对看似合理的因果说法，不能只依据时间先后下结论，而要统一标准、寻找参照、检查其他同期变化、辨认机制，并如实说明证据能够支持到什么程度。
questions.evidence: 永安街的案例最终提供的，不只是一次街区更新经验，更是一条公共决策原则：面对一个看似顺理成章的因果说法，应先统一测量标准，再寻找可以比较的对象，检查同期事件，辨认作用机制，并诚实说明证据边界。

articles.title: 低离职率究竟是不是远程办公带来的
articles.summary: 杭州澄川科技的阶段报告称，采用远程办公的团队离职率较低。数据分析负责人林岚重新审查人员分配、管理方式和离职时间后发现，这一差异只能证明相关性，不能直接证明因果关系。公司因此暂缓宣传结论，决定通过分阶段试行、统一记录和员工访谈继续检验，并将原报告改写为边界清楚的阶段性说明。
articles.topic: 低离职率究竟是不是远程办公带来的
paragraphs: 九月初，位于杭州高新区的企业软件公司澄川科技召开季度经营会。会上，人力资源部展示了一份题为《远程办公与员工稳定性》的阶段报告。报告指出，允许员工每周在家工作的几个产品团队，人员流动明显少于长期到办公室上班的团队。人力资源总监周明据此提出，公司可以在招聘页面上宣布“远程办公能够减少离职”，并把扩大远程制度列为下一季度的重点措施。这个判断很受欢迎，因为它同时迎合了员工对灵活安排的期待，也为公司节省办公场地提供了理由。然而，负责数据分析的林岚没有立即赞同。她注意到，报告比较的是已经采用不同制度的团队，而不是在相同条件下随机分配的员工。两个群体之间原本就可能存在许多差别，较低的离职率未必是远程办公造成的。

林岚首先回到公司滨江园区的人事档案室，核对报告所使用的记录。她发现，最早获得远程资格的并不是随机挑选的团队，而是工作流程成熟、项目周期较长、成员经验较丰富的后台产品组。需要频繁接触客户的新业务组和刚刚组建的实施团队，则被要求每天到岗。换句话说，远程团队在制度实施之前，人员结构可能已经更加稳定。资深员工掌握的业务资源较多，岗位自主性也较强，本来就不容易离开；新团队面临目标调整、职责不清和管理磨合，离职风险自然更高。如果忽略这些先行差异，就等于把团队成熟度产生的影响算在远程办公名下。阶段报告虽然准确描述了表面现象，却没有回答最关键的问题：假如同一批人在其他条件不变的情况下继续到岗，他们是否会更容易辞职。

进一步审查还暴露出选择机制。公司开放远程申请后，直属经理可以根据岗位性质和个人表现决定是否批准。能够按时交付、沟通记录完整的员工更容易得到许可，而处于绩效辅导期或需要现场培训的人通常不会获批。于是，“采用远程办公”既代表一种工作地点安排，也暗含了管理者对员工可靠程度的判断。即使远程制度毫无作用，被经理认为可靠的人也可能保持更久。此外，一些原本打算离职的员工会在提出申请前寻找新工作，他们还没有进入远程名单便已离开；另一些员工则因为准备照顾家人而主动申请远程，并且恰好更重视工作的连续性。这些路径方向不同，却都可能造成远程组看起来更加稳定。仅凭两组最终离职情况，无法把制度效果与人员自我选择分开。

争议在第二次评审会上公开化。周明认为，公司不必等待学术意义上的完美证据，因为管理决定总要在信息有限时作出；如果远程团队确实更稳定，就应尽快推广。林岚则指出，是否推广制度与是否宣称已证明因果，是两个不同问题。企业可以基于员工需求、通勤成本和招聘竞争采取行动，但不能把尚未排除其他解释的观察结果包装成确定事实。她还发现，原报告把调岗、合同到期和主动辞职合并为“人员流失”，却没有区分其原因。某些到岗团队承担的项目刚刚结束，合同终止与办公地点没有直接关系。与此同时，远程团队的负责人普遍拥有更大的预算权限，可以更快调整薪酬和岗位。如果这些管理差异没有被纳入分析，所谓远程效应很可能包含了主管能力、项目阶段与报酬变化的共同作用。

为了说明时间顺序的重要性，林岚逐一查看制度变更记录。部分团队是在出现连续离职之后才获准远程办公，原因是负责人希望安抚留下来的成员。若只比较批准之后仍在职的人，就会遗漏制度实施前已经离开的员工，从而产生一种错觉：远程政策一开始，团队便稳定下来。还有一些员工名义上属于到岗组，实际上经常在客户现场或异地出差；另一些登记为远程的员工，每周仍会参加现场会议。粗糙的分类掩盖了真实的工作状态。林岚建议把“是否远程”改为按周记录实际地点、协作方式和制度变化，并明确观察起点。只有先确定原因发生在结果之前，再处理人员进入和退出样本的规则，分析才不会因事后筛选而偏向一个看似有利的结论。

经过讨论，管理层没有取消远程安排，也没有接受那句过于肯定的宣传语。总经理杜衡作出三个具体决定。第一，人力资源部立即修改阶段报告，把“远程办公减少离职”改为“目前观察到远程团队与较低离职率同时出现，因果关系尚待检验”，并在附录中说明岗位、资历、主管权限和项目阶段等潜在混杂因素。第二，公司选择尚未实行远程制度、但工作性质相近的几个内部支持团队，按照预先公布的顺序分阶段开放申请。开放时间不由经理根据近期表现临时决定，以减少选择偏差。第三，分析人员在方案开始前确定离职的定义、观察期限和比较方法，之后不得因为结果不理想而随意更换口径。涉及照护、健康或无障碍需求的员工仍可直接申请特殊安排，不被当作试验工具。

林岚还要求在量化记录之外加入保密访谈。离职是一项最终结果，却不能解释制度通过什么机制发挥作用。远程办公可能减少通勤疲劳，也可能加剧孤立感；它可能提高专注程度，也可能让新人难以获得非正式指导。同一项制度对资深工程师和刚入职的顾问未必产生相同影响。访谈将由不参与绩效考核的人员进行，问题集中在工作自主性、会议负担、晋升预期、团队归属和家庭责任，整理时删除能够识别个人的信息。公司同时设立申诉渠道，防止主管把到岗要求当成惩罚，也防止员工因拒绝参加分析而失去远程资格。这样做不是为了给既定结论寻找生动例子，而是为了检查数据中看不见的机制和副作用。

一个月后，修订后的报告在公司内网公开。它没有宣布远程办公必然留住员工，而是清楚区分了已知事实、合理假设与尚待验证的问题。招聘部门撤下了准备发布的因果宣传，办公管理部门则保留弹性工位计划，因为这一决定还可以由员工便利和空间利用等独立理由支持。周明最初担心谨慎措辞会削弱改革，后来发现，明确证据边界并不等于拒绝行动，反而使政策目标更加诚实：公司是在试行一种可能改善体验的安排，同时持续观察它是否影响离职。此次审查的结果不是证明远程办公有效或无效，而是阻止了一项相关性被过早解释为因果。真正可靠的结论，需要透明的比较规则、稳定的指标、对替代解释的检验，以及在新证据出现后修正判断的勇气。
pinyin: jiǔ yuè chū ， wèi yú háng zhōu gāo xīn qū de qǐ yè ruǎn jiàn gōng sī chéng chuān kē jì zhào kāi jì dù jīng yíng huì 。 huì shàng ， rén lì zī yuán bù zhǎn shì le yī fèn tí wèi 《 yuǎn chéng bàn gōng yǔ yuán gōng wěn dìng xìng 》 de jiē duàn bào gào 。 bào gào zhǐ chū ， yǔn xǔ yuán gōng měi zhōu zài jiā gōng zuò de jǐ gè chǎn pǐn tuán duì ， rén yuán liú dòng míng xiǎn shǎo yú cháng qī dào bàn gōng shì shàng bān de tuán duì 。 rén lì zī yuán zǒng jiān zhōu míng jù cǐ tí chū ， gōng sī kě yǐ zài zhāo pìn yè miàn shàng xuān bù “ yuǎn chéng bàn gōng néng gòu jiǎn shǎo lí zhí ”， bìng bǎ kuò dà yuǎn chéng zhì dù liè wèi xià yī jì dù de zhòng diǎn cuò shī 。 zhè ge pàn duàn hěn shòu huān yíng ， yīn wèi tā tóng shí yíng hé le yuán gōng duì líng huó ān pái de qī dài ， yě wèi gōng sī jié shěng bàn gōng chǎng dì tí gōng le lǐ yóu 。 rán ér ， fù zé shù jù fēn xī de lín lán méi yǒu lì jí zàn tóng 。 tā zhù yì dào ， bào gào bǐ jiào de shì yǐ jīng cǎi yòng bù tóng zhì dù de tuán duì ， ér bú shì zài xiāng tóng tiáo jiàn xià suí jī fēn pèi de yuán gōng 。 liǎng gè qún tǐ zhī jiān yuán běn jiù kě néng cún zài xǔ duō chā bié ， jiào dī de lí zhí lǜ wèi bì shì yuǎn chéng bàn gōng zào chéng de 。

lín lán shǒu xiān huí dào gōng sī bīn jiāng yuán qū de rén shì dàng àn shì ， hé duì bào gào suǒ shǐ yòng de jì lù 。 tā fā xiàn ， zuì zǎo huò dé yuǎn chéng zī gé de bìng bú shì suí jī tiāo xuǎn de tuán duì ， ér shì gōng zuò liú chéng chéng shú 、 xiàng mù zhōu qī jiào zhǎng 、 chéng yuán jīng yàn jiào fēng fù de hòu tái chǎn pǐn zǔ 。 xū yào pín fán jiē chù kè hù de xīn yè wù zǔ hé gāng gāng zǔ jiàn de shí shī tuán duì ， zé bèi yāo qiú měi tiān dào gǎng 。 huàn jù huà shuō ， yuǎn chéng tuán duì zài zhì dù shí shī zhī qián ， rén yuán jié gòu kě néng yǐ jīng gèng jiā wěn dìng 。 zī shēn yuán gōng zhǎng wò de yè wù zī yuán jiào duō ， gǎng wèi zì zhǔ xìng yě jiào qiáng ， běn lái jiù bù róng yì lí kāi ； xīn tuán duì miàn lín mù biāo tiáo zhěng 、 zhí zé bù qīng hé guǎn lǐ mó hé ， lí zhí fēng xiǎn zì rán gèng gāo 。 rú guǒ hū lüè zhè xiē xiān xíng chā yì ， jiù děng yú bǎ tuán duì chéng shú dù chǎn shēng de yǐng xiǎng suàn zài yuǎn chéng bàn gōng míng xià 。 jiē duàn bào gào suī rán zhǔn què miáo shù le biǎo miàn xiàn xiàng ， què méi yǒu huí dá zuì guān jiàn de wèn tí ： jiǎ rú tóng yī pī rén zài qí tā tiáo jiàn bù biàn de qíng kuàng xià jì xù dào gǎng ， tā men shì fǒu huì gèng róng yì cí zhí 。

jìn yí bù shěn chá hái bào lù chū xuǎn zé jī zhì 。 gōng sī kāi fàng yuǎn chéng shēn qǐng hòu ， zhí shǔ jīng lǐ kě yǐ gēn jù gǎng wèi xìng zhì hé gè rén biǎo xiàn jué dìng shì fǒu pī zhǔn 。 néng gòu àn shí jiāo fù 、 gōu tōng jì lù wán zhěng de yuán gōng gèng róng yì dé dào xǔ kě ， ér chǔ yú jì xiào fǔ dǎo qī huò xū yào xiàn chǎng péi xùn de rén tōng cháng bú huì huò pī 。 yú shì ，“ cǎi yòng yuǎn chéng bàn gōng ” jì dài biǎo yī zhǒng gōng zuò dì diǎn ān pái ， yě àn hán le guǎn lǐ zhě duì yuán gōng kě kào chéng dù de pàn duàn 。 jí shǐ yuǎn chéng zhì dù háo wú zuò yòng ， bèi jīng lǐ rèn wéi kě kào de rén yě kě néng bǎo chí gèng jiǔ 。 cǐ wài ， yī xiē yuán běn dǎ suàn lí zhí de yuán gōng huì zài tí chū shēn qǐng qián xún zhǎo xīn gōng zuò ， tā men hái méi yǒu jìn rù yuǎn chéng míng dān biàn yǐ lí kāi ； lìng yī xiē yuán gōng zé yīn wèi zhǔn bèi zhào gù jiā rén ér zhǔ dòng shēn qǐng yuǎn chéng ， bìng qiě qià hǎo gèng zhòng shì gōng zuò de lián xù xìng 。 zhè xiē lù jìng fāng xiàng bù tóng ， què dōu kě néng zào chéng yuǎn chéng zǔ kàn qǐ lái gèng jiā wěn dìng 。 jǐn píng liǎng zǔ zuì zhōng lí zhí qíng kuàng ， wú fǎ bǎ zhì dù xiào guǒ yǔ rén yuán zì wǒ xuǎn zé fēn kāi 。

zhēng yì zài dì èr cì píng shěn huì shàng gōng kāi huà 。 zhōu míng rèn wéi ， gōng sī bù bì děng dài xué shù yì yì shàng de wán měi zhèng jù ， yīn wèi guǎn lǐ jué dìng zǒng yào zài xìn xī yǒu xiàn shí zuò chū ； rú guǒ yuǎn chéng tuán duì què shí gèng wěn dìng ， jiù yīng jǐn kuài tuī guǎng 。 lín lán zé zhǐ chū ， shì fǒu tuī guǎng zhì dù yǔ shì fǒu xuān chēng yǐ zhèng míng yīn guǒ ， shì liǎng gè bù tóng wèn tí 。 qǐ yè kě yǐ jī yú yuán gōng xū qiú 、 tōng qín chéng běn hé zhāo pìn jìng zhēng cǎi qǔ xíng dòng ， dàn bù néng bǎ shàng wèi pái chú qí tā jiě shì de guān chá jié guǒ bāo zhuāng chéng què dìng shì shí 。 tā hái fā xiàn ， yuán bào gào bǎ diào gǎng 、 hé tóng dào qī hé zhǔ dòng cí zhí hé bìng wèi “ rén yuán liú shī ”， què méi yǒu qū fēn qí yuán yīn 。 mǒu xiē dào gǎng tuán duì chéng dān de xiàng mù gāng gāng jié shù ， hé tóng zhōng zhǐ yǔ bàn gōng dì diǎn méi yǒu zhí jiē guān xì 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， yuǎn chéng tuán duì de fù zé rén pǔ biàn yōng yǒu gèng dà de yù suàn quán xiàn ， kě yǐ gèng kuài tiáo zhěng xīn chóu hè gǎng wèi 。 rú guǒ zhè xiē guǎn lǐ chā yì méi yǒu bèi nà rù fēn xī ， suǒ wèi yuǎn chéng xiào yìng hěn kě néng bāo hán le zhǔ guǎn néng lì 、 xiàng mù jiē duàn yǔ bào chóu biàn huà de gòng tóng zuò yòng 。

wèi le shuō míng shí jiān shùn xù de zhòng yào xìng ， lín lán zhú yī chá kàn zhì dù biàn gēng jì lù 。 bù fèn tuán duì shì zài chū xiàn lián xù lí zhí zhī hòu cái huò zhǔn yuǎn chéng bàn gōng ， yuán yīn shì fù zé rén xī wàng ān fǔ liú xià lái de chéng yuán 。 ruò zhǐ bǐ jiào pī zhǔn zhī hòu réng zài zhí de rén ， jiù huì yí lòu zhì dù shí shī qián yǐ jīng lí kāi de yuán gōng ， cóng ér chǎn shēng yī zhǒng cuò jué ： yuǎn chéng zhèng cè yī kāi shǐ ， tuán duì biàn wěn dìng xià lái 。 hái yǒu yī xiē yuán gōng míng yì shàng shǔ yú dào gǎng zǔ ， shí jì shàng jīng cháng zài kè hù xiàn chǎng huò yì dì chū chāi ； lìng yī xiē dēng jì wèi yuǎn chéng de yuán gōng ， měi zhōu réng huì cān jiā xiàn chǎng huì yì 。 cū cāo de fēn lèi yǎn gài le zhēn shí de gōng zuò zhuàng tài 。 lín lán jiàn yì bǎ “ shì fǒu yuǎn chéng ” gǎi wéi àn zhōu jì lù shí jì dì diǎn 、 xié zuò fāng shì hé zhì dù biàn huà ， bìng míng què guān chá qǐ diǎn 。 zhǐ yǒu xiān què dìng yuán yīn fā shēng zài jié guǒ zhī qián ， zài chǔ lǐ rén yuán jìn rù hé tuì chū yàng běn de guī zé ， fēn xī cái bú huì yīn shì hòu shāi xuǎn ér piān xiàng yí gè kàn shì yǒu lì de jié lùn 。

jīng guò tǎo lùn ， guǎn lǐ céng méi yǒu qǔ xiāo yuǎn chéng ān pái ， yě méi yǒu jiē shòu nà jù guò yú kěn dìng de xuān chuán yǔ 。 zǒng jīng lǐ dù héng zuò chū sān gè jù tǐ jué dìng 。 dì yī ， rén lì zī yuán bù lì jí xiū gǎi jiē duàn bào gào ， bǎ “ yuǎn chéng bàn gōng jiǎn shǎo lí zhí ” gǎi wéi “ mù qián guān chá dào yuǎn chéng tuán duì yǔ jiào dī lí zhí lǜ tóng shí chū xiàn ， yīn guǒ guān xì shàng dài jiǎn yàn ”， bìng zài fù lù zhōng shuō míng gǎng wèi 、 zī lì 、 zhǔ guǎn quán xiàn hé xiàng mù jiē duàn děng qián zài hùn zá yīn sù 。 dì èr ， gōng sī xuǎn zé shàng wèi shí xíng yuǎn chéng zhì dù 、 dàn gōng zuò xìng zhì xiāng jìn de jǐ gè nèi bù zhī chí tuán duì ， àn zhào yù xiān gōng bù de shùn xù fēn jiē duàn kāi fàng shēn qǐng 。 kāi fàng shí jiān bù yóu jīng lǐ gēn jù jìn qī biǎo xiàn lín shí jué dìng ， yǐ jiǎn shǎo xuǎn zé piān chā 。 dì sān ， fēn xī rén yuán zài fāng àn kāi shǐ qián què dìng lí zhí de dìng yì 、 guān chá qī xiàn hé bǐ jiào fāng fǎ ， zhī hòu bù dé yīn wèi jié guǒ bù lǐ xiǎng ér suí yì gēng huàn kǒu jìng 。 shè jí zhào hù 、 jiàn kāng huò wú zhàng ài xū qiú de yuán gōng réng kě zhí jiē shēn qǐng tè shū ān pái ， bù bèi dàng zuò shì yàn gōng jù 。

lín lán hái yāo qiú zài liàng huà jì lù zhī wài jiā rù bǎo mì fǎng tán 。 lí zhí shì yī xiàng zuì zhōng jié guǒ ， què bù néng jiě shì zhì dù tōng guò shén me jī zhì fā huī zuò yòng 。 yuǎn chéng bàn gōng kě néng jiǎn shǎo tōng qín pí láo ， yě kě néng jiā jù gū lì gǎn ； tā kě néng tí gāo zhuān zhù chéng dù ， yě kě néng ràng xīn rén nán yǐ huò dé fēi zhèng shì zhǐ dǎo 。 tóng yī xiàng zhì dù duì zī shēn gōng chéng shī hé gāng rù zhí de gù wèn wèi bì chǎn shēng xiāng tóng yǐng xiǎng 。 fǎng tán jiāng yóu bù cān yù jì xiào kǎo hé de rén yuán jìn xíng ， wèn tí jí zhōng zài gōng zuò zì zhǔ xìng 、 huì yì fù dān 、 jìn shēng yù qī 、 tuán duì guī shǔ hé jiā tíng zé rèn ， zhěng lǐ shí shān chú néng gòu shí bié gè rén de xìn xī 。 gōng sī tóng shí shè lì shēn sù qú dào ， fáng zhǐ zhǔ guǎn bǎ dào gǎng yāo qiú dàng chéng chéng fá ， yě fáng zhǐ yuán gōng yīn jù jué cān jiā fēn xī ér shī qù yuǎn chéng zī gé 。 zhè yàng zuò bú shì wèi le gěi jì dìng jié lùn xún zhǎo shēng dòng lì zi ， ér shì wèi le jiǎn chá shù jù zhōng kàn bú jiàn de jī zhì hé fù zuò yòng 。

yí gè yuè hòu ， xiū dìng hòu de bào gào zài gōng sī nèi wǎng gōng kāi 。 tā méi yǒu xuān bù yuǎn chéng bàn gōng bì rán liú zhù yuán gōng ， ér shì qīng chǔ qū fēn le yǐ zhī shì shí 、 hé lǐ jiǎ shè yǔ shàng dài yàn zhèng de wèn tí 。 zhāo pìn bù mén chè xià le zhǔn bèi fā bù de yīn guǒ xuān chuán ， bàn gōng guǎn lǐ bù mén zé bǎo liú tán xìng gōng wèi jì huà ， yīn wèi zhè yī jué dìng hái kě yǐ yóu yuán gōng biàn lì hé kōng jiān lì yòng děng dú lì lǐ yóu zhī chí 。 zhōu míng zuì chū dān xīn jǐn shèn cuò cí huì xuē ruò gǎi gé ， hòu lái fā xiàn ， míng què zhèng jù biān jiè bìng bù děng yú jù jué xíng dòng ， fǎn ér shǐ zhèng cè mù biāo gèng jiā chéng shí ： gōng sī shì zài shì xíng yī zhǒng kě néng gǎi shàn tǐ yàn de ān pái ， tóng shí chí xù guān chá tā shì fǒu yǐng xiǎng lí zhí 。 cǐ cì shěn chá de jié guǒ bú shì zhèng míng yuǎn chéng bàn gōng yǒu xiào huò wú xiào ， ér shì zǔ zhǐ le yī xiàng xiāng guān xìng bèi guò zǎo jiě shì wèi yīn guǒ 。 zhēn zhèng kě kào de jié lùn ， xū yào tòu míng de bǐ jiào guī zé 、 wěn dìng de zhǐ biāo 、 duì tì dài jiě shì de jiǎn yàn ， yǐ jí zài xīn zhèng jù chū xiàn hòu xiū zhèng pàn duàn de yǒng qì 。
translation: In early September, Chengchuan Technology, an enterprise software company based in the Hangzhou High-Tech Zone, held its quarterly business meeting. At the meeting, the Human Resources Department presented an interim report titled “Remote Work and Employee Stability.” The report noted that several product teams whose employees were allowed to work from home each week had substantially lower turnover than teams that had long been required to work in the office. Based on this finding, Human Resources Director Zhou Ming proposed that the company announce on its recruitment page that “remote work can reduce employee turnover” and make expanding the remote-work policy a priority for the next quarter. This conclusion was well received because it both catered to employees’ desire for flexible arrangements and gave the company a reason to reduce spending on office space. However, Lin Lan, who was responsible for data analysis, did not immediately agree. She noticed that the report compared teams that had already adopted different policies rather than employees randomly assigned under identical conditions. Many differences may already have existed between the two groups, so the lower turnover rate was not necessarily caused by remote work.

Lin Lan first returned to the personnel records office at the company’s Binjiang campus to verify the records used in the report. She found that the teams first granted remote-work eligibility had not been selected at random. Instead, they were back-end product groups with mature workflows, longer project cycles, and more experienced members. New business groups requiring frequent customer contact and newly formed implementation teams, by contrast, were required to report to the office every day. In other words, the remote teams may already have had more stable staffing before the policy was introduced. Senior employees possessed more business resources and had greater autonomy in their roles, making them inherently less likely to leave. New teams faced changing objectives, unclear responsibilities, and the challenges of adapting to new management, so their risk of turnover was naturally higher. Ignoring these preexisting differences would amount to attributing the effects of team maturity to remote work. Although the interim report accurately described the pattern on the surface, it did not answer the most important question: if the same group of people had continued reporting to the office while all other conditions remained unchanged, would they have been more likely to resign?

Further review also revealed a selection mechanism. After the company began accepting remote-work applications, direct managers could decide whether to approve them based on the nature of an employee’s position and the employee’s individual performance. Employees who delivered work on time and maintained complete communication records were more likely to receive permission, while those undergoing performance coaching or requiring on-site training were generally not approved. As a result, “adopting remote work” represented not only an arrangement concerning work location but also an implicit judgment by managers about an employee’s reliability. Even if the remote-work policy had no effect at all, employees whom managers considered reliable might still remain with the company longer. In addition, some employees who were already planning to resign looked for new jobs before submitting an application and left before ever appearing on the remote-work list. Others proactively applied for remote work because they were preparing to care for family members and also happened to place greater value on continuity of employment. Although these pathways operated in different directions, all of them could make the remote group appear more stable. The policy’s effect could not be separated from employees’ self-selection merely by comparing the final turnover outcomes of the two groups.

The disagreement became public at the second review meeting. Zhou Ming argued that the company did not need to wait for evidence that was perfect in the academic sense, because management decisions always had to be made with limited information. If remote teams were indeed more stable, the policy should be expanded as soon as possible. Lin Lan countered that whether to expand the policy and whether to claim that causation had been proven were two different questions. A company could act on the basis of employee needs, commuting costs, and competition in recruitment, but it could not package observational findings for which alternative explanations had not yet been ruled out as established facts. She also found that the original report had combined transfers, contract expirations, and voluntary resignations under the heading of “employee attrition” without distinguishing among their causes. Some office-based teams had just completed their projects, and the termination of their contracts was not directly related to work location. Meanwhile, the leaders of remote teams generally had greater budgetary authority and could adjust compensation and positions more quickly. If these managerial differences were not included in the analysis, the supposed remote-work effect was likely to incorporate the combined influence of managerial ability, project stage, and changes in compensation.

To demonstrate the importance of chronological order, Lin Lan reviewed the records of policy changes one by one. Some teams had not been permitted to work remotely until after a series of resignations, because their leaders hoped to reassure the employees who remained. Comparing only those who were still employed after approval would omit employees who had already left before the policy was implemented, creating the illusion that the teams became stable as soon as the remote-work policy began. Some employees were nominally assigned to the office-based group but actually spent much of their time at customer sites or traveling elsewhere for work. Others were registered as remote employees but still attended on-site meetings every week. The crude classifications concealed their actual working conditions. Lin Lan recommended replacing the simple indicator of “whether an employee works remotely” with weekly records of actual work location, modes of collaboration, and policy changes, while also clearly defining the starting point for observation. Only by first establishing that the cause occurred before the outcome and then specifying the rules governing employees’ entry into and exit from the sample could the analysis avoid being skewed by retrospective selection toward an apparently favorable conclusion.

After discussion, management neither canceled the remote-work arrangements nor accepted the overly definitive promotional claim. General Manager Du Heng made three specific decisions. First, the Human Resources Department was to revise the interim report immediately, replacing “remote work reduces employee turnover” with “remote teams are currently observed to coincide with lower turnover rates, but the causal relationship remains to be tested,” and explaining in an appendix potential confounding factors such as position, seniority, managerial authority, and project stage. Second, the company would select several internal support teams with similar types of work that had not yet adopted remote work and open applications to them in phases according to a sequence announced in advance. The timing would not be decided at short notice by managers based on recent performance, thereby reducing selection bias. Third, before the initiative began, the analysts would define turnover, the observation period, and the comparison method, and they would not subsequently be allowed to change the criteria arbitrarily because the results were unfavorable. Employees with caregiving, health, or accessibility needs could still apply directly for special arrangements and would not be treated as instruments in an experiment.

Lin Lan also requested that confidential interviews be added alongside the quantitative records. Turnover was an ultimate outcome, but it could not explain the mechanisms through which the policy operated. Remote work might reduce the fatigue of commuting, but it might also intensify feelings of isolation. It might improve concentration, but it might also make it difficult for new employees to obtain informal guidance. The same policy would not necessarily have the same effects on senior engineers and newly hired consultants. The interviews would be conducted by personnel who were not involved in performance evaluations, with questions focusing on autonomy at work, meeting burdens, expectations for promotion, sense of belonging to the team, and family responsibilities. Information that could identify individuals would be removed when the findings were compiled. The company also established an appeals channel to prevent supervisors from using office-attendance requirements as a punishment and to prevent employees from losing their remote-work eligibility because they declined to participate in the analysis. The purpose was not to find vivid examples supporting a predetermined conclusion, but to examine mechanisms and side effects that were invisible in the data.

One month later, the revised report was published on the company intranet. It did not declare that remote work would inevitably retain employees, but clearly distinguished among known facts, reasonable hypotheses, and questions still awaiting verification. The Recruitment Department withdrew the causal claim it had been preparing to publish, while the Office Management Department retained its flexible workstation plan because that decision could also be supported by independent considerations such as employee convenience and space utilization. Zhou Ming had initially worried that cautious wording would weaken the reform, but he later discovered that clearly defining the limits of the evidence did not amount to refusing to act. Instead, it made the policy’s objective more honest: the company was piloting an arrangement that might improve employees’ experience while continuing to observe whether it affected turnover. The outcome of the review was not proof that remote work was effective or ineffective, but the prevention of a correlation from being prematurely interpreted as causation. Truly reliable conclusions require transparent rules of comparison, stable measures, examination of alternative explanations, and the courage to revise judgments when new evidence emerges.

vocabulary.meaning: 针对某一阶段的工作、研究或调查结果所形成的报告。
员工进入、离开或调动岗位的变化情况。
为了符合某种需要、愿望或倾向而采取相应做法。
按照随机原则把研究对象安排到不同组别，以减少人为选择造成的差异。
将相关资料相互对照，以检查是否准确一致。
在某项制度或措施实施之前，不同群体之间已经存在的差别。
团队在流程、经验、分工和协作等方面的发展完善程度。
决定哪些人能够进入某个群体或获得某种安排的过程和规则。
组织针对工作表现未达到要求的员工进行指导和改进的一段时期。
个人根据自身情况主动选择进入某一群体，由此可能导致样本差异的现象。
通过记录或观察得到的现象或数据，而不一定能证明因果关系。
对预算的分配、调整或使用作出决定的权力。
在结果出现后再选择或排除样本，可能使分析产生偏差。

vocabulary.pinyin: qián zài hùn zá yīn sù
vocabulary.meaning: 同时与研究中的原因和结果有关、可能干扰因果判断的因素。
因研究对象进入不同组别的方式不合理而产生的系统性误差。

vocabulary.pinyin: suí yì gēng huàn kǒu jìng
vocabulary.meaning: 根据需要任意改变定义、统计标准或分析方法。
在保护受访者身份和个人信息的条件下进行的访谈。
现有证据能够支持的结论范围及其限制。
除当前假设之外，也能够解释同一现象的其他原因。
两个变量同时发生变化或彼此存在联系的统计关系，但不等于因果关系。

grammar.explanation: 用于说明同一事物同时具有两个方面的性质、含义或作用。
grammar.example: 于是，“采用远程办公”既代表一种工作地点安排，也暗含了管理者对员工可靠程度的判断。

grammar.explanation: 强调必须先满足前面的条件并完成相应步骤，之后才可能得到后面的结果。
grammar.example: 只有先确定原因发生在结果之前，再处理人员进入和退出样本的规则，分析才不会因事后筛选而偏向一个看似有利的结论。

grammar.explanation: 通过否定一种目的并肯定另一种目的，突出行为的真正意图。
grammar.example: 这样做不是为了给既定结论寻找生动例子，而是为了检查数据中看不见的机制和副作用。

questions.prompt: 林岚为什么认为阶段报告不能证明远程办公减少了离职？
options: 接受远程安排的团队与到岗团队原本可能存在多方面差异
公司没有统计员工对招聘页面的满意程度
远程团队的员工全部在制度实施前离职
到岗团队与远程团队使用了完全相同的管理制度
questions.explanation: 报告比较的不是相同条件下随机分配形成的群体，两组员工在团队成熟度、资历、岗位性质等方面可能早已有差异，因此较低离职率不能直接归因于远程办公。
questions.evidence: 两个群体之间原本就可能存在许多差别，较低的离职率未必是远程办公造成的。

questions.prompt: 管理层对原阶段报告采取了什么处理措施？
options: 删除全部离职数据并停止研究远程制度
修改因果性表述，并补充说明可能影响结果的混杂因素
保留原结论，但把报告限制为管理层内部阅读
立即宣布所有团队永久实行远程办公
questions.explanation: 管理层没有继续使用“远程办公减少离职”这种确定的因果表述，而是改成对相关现象的谨慎描述，并列明岗位、资历、主管权限和项目阶段等混杂因素。
questions.evidence: 第一，人力资源部立即修改阶段报告，把“远程办公减少离职”改为“目前观察到远程团队与较低离职率同时出现，因果关系尚待检验”，并在附录中说明岗位、资历、主管权限和项目阶段等潜在混杂因素。

questions.prompt: 林岚要求加入保密访谈的主要目的是什么？
options: 收集支持远程办公的生动案例，以便用于招聘宣传
识别拒绝远程办公的员工并调整其绩效考核
了解量化数据无法呈现的作用机制和潜在副作用
用员工的个人感受直接代替离职率等量化指标
questions.explanation: 访谈并不是为了给预设结论寻找例子，也不是取代量化分析，而是为了理解远程办公可能通过哪些途径影响员工，并发现孤立感、新人指导困难等数据中不易观察的副作用。

articles.title: 一顿早餐之后：临江中学如何检验课堂进步的真正原因
articles.summary: 海川市临江中学在东校区推行免费早餐后，早课测验平均分有所上升，校方一度准备将这一变化归因于早餐项目。由教师、营养师和家长代表组成的评估小组重新核查实施过程，发现作息调整、测验变化、参加者差异和教师期待等因素都可能干扰判断。学校最终没有仓促宣布因果关系，而是采用分阶段推广、统一测量和持续跟踪的办法继续检验，并据此完善了学生支持政策。
articles.topic: 一顿早餐之后：临江中学如何检验课堂进步的真正原因
paragraphs: 海川市临江中学东校区位于老城区与新建住宅区的交界处，学生中既有住校生，也有每天乘公交车往返的走读生。秋季学期开始后，校方在一楼食堂设置免费早餐窗口，向所有高一学生提供粥、鸡蛋、牛奶和主食。项目实施一个月后，教务处整理早课测验记录，发现年级平均分比项目开始前有所上升。阶段报告据此写道：“免费早餐初步改善了学生的课堂表现。”这句话很快被家长委员会引用，有人建议立即扩大预算，还有教师提出把早餐项目作为学校特色向媒体宣传。然而，负责审核报告的语文教师周岚提出质疑：平均分上升发生在早餐推出之后，并不等于早餐导致了上升。若不能排除其他解释，这个看似合理的结论就可能把时间上的先后关系误当成因果关系。

争论首先集中在“课堂表现”究竟指什么。阶段报告使用的是早课测验平均分，但测验成绩只反映特定时间、特定题目和特定评分方式下的表现，不能自动代表注意力、记忆力、出勤状况或长期学习能力。早餐也不是一个单一变量：学生是否领取、吃了多少、与谁一起吃，以及原来是否空腹上学，都会影响实际作用。假如一名学生每天都在家吃早餐，学校新增的免费餐对他几乎没有改变；而另一名学生过去常因赶车不吃东西，项目对他的意义可能很大。把两类学生放在同一个平均数里，固然便于汇报，却可能掩盖差异。评估小组因此决定先把问题改写为：在其他条件尽可能相近时，获得并实际食用学校早餐，是否使原本容易空腹上学的学生在早课中表现得更稳定？

小组随后来到高一教学楼核对课程表、测验卷和班级日志，发现早餐项目启动时，学校还同时调整了作息。早读比过去推迟，早读与第一节课之间增加了短暂休息；几位教师也减少了纯记忆题，改用课堂讲解后立即作答的练习。与此同时，开学初尚未适应新环境的学生逐渐熟悉教师要求，成绩自然可能回升。天气转凉后，迟到人数的变化也会影响参加早测的人群。更值得注意的是，前后两阶段使用的试卷并不完全相同，题目难度和评分尺度缺乏统一标准。由此看来，平均分上升至少可能来自作息、教学、试卷、季节和适应过程，早餐只是多个同时发生的变化之一。若直接比较项目实施前后的两个平均数，就无法判断各因素分别发挥了多大作用。

参加早餐的学生也不是随机形成的群体。主动领取早餐的人可能更愿意提前到校、更遵守作息，或者本来就得到班主任较多关注；不领取的人则可能已经在家吃过，也可能因迟到而错过供应。倘若直接比较领取者与未领取者，观察到的差距既可能来自食物，也可能来自家庭安排、通勤距离、自律程度和原有成绩。反过来，如果只研究经常空腹的学生，又容易忽略他们所面临的经济压力和照护条件。家长代表担心，过度追问家庭情况会给孩子贴上“困难学生”的标签。营养师则提醒，学校不能为了获得整齐的数据而强迫学生改变饮食。评估必须服从知情、自愿和隐私保护原则，不能把教育支持变成对弱势学生的公开筛选。

另一个冲突来自项目的实际执行。食堂管理员发现，有些学生领取早餐后带到教室，有些只拿牛奶，还有些替同学领取。教师也知道哪些班级正在积极参加项目，可能无意中给予更多鼓励，或者因为期待学生状态改善而改变评分尺度。这种期待效应会让结果看起来比实际作用更强。与此同时，早餐窗口开放后，部分学生提早到校，在食堂与同伴交流，随后结伴进入教室。即使课堂状态确有改善，也未必完全由营养摄入造成，还可能来自稳定的晨间节奏、同伴陪伴和迟到减少。免费早餐其实是一组相互关联的措施，而不是一粒可以与环境分离的药片。要检验因果说法，就必须记录实施细节，而不能只在表格中填上“有早餐”或“无早餐”。

经过两次公开讨论，学校没有取消早餐，也没有把尚未证实的推断写成宣传口号。校务会决定采用分阶段推进的评估方案：由于食堂容量有限，各班原本就需要依次开放早餐预约，因此学校按照预先确定且与成绩无关的次序扩大服务。在等待开放期间，学生仍可使用原有餐饮安排，基本饮食需求仍能得到满足。教务处统一早课任务的范围、时长和评分规则，同时记录出勤、迟到、睡眠自述、是否在家进餐以及实际领取情况。记录只使用编码，班主任看不到个别家庭的敏感信息。评估重点也不再局限于一次测验分数，而是观察注意力是否稳定、缺勤是否减少，以及效果能否持续。这样的设计仍不是毫无缺陷，却比简单的前后比较更有能力排除替代解释。

小组还预先约定分析规则，以免看到结果后再选择最有利的解释。首先比较各阶段服务开放前后的变化，而不是只挑选进步最明显的班级；其次分别观察过去常空腹和原本已有早餐习惯的学生，因为总体平均效果可能掩盖真正受益者；再次检查缺失记录，弄清未参加测验的人是否集中在某些通勤较远或出勤不稳定的群体。若早餐只改善了学生到校后的舒适感，却没有立即提高分数，这仍可能是有价值的结果；若短期分数上升但随后消失，也不能宣称学习能力获得持久改善。因果判断不是寻找一项支持预期的证据，而是主动追问：还有什么情况也会产生同样现象？这些情况是否已经被设计、记录和分析尽量排除？

学期末，学校公布的结论比最初的阶段报告谨慎得多：现有证据表明，免费早餐与部分早晨状态的改善同时出现，但仅凭平均分上升，尚不足以断言早餐本身造成了全部变化。分阶段记录为继续判断提供了更可靠的基础，也揭示出项目的价值不应只用考试成绩衡量。校方据此保留免费早餐，将供应时间与公交到站时间衔接，并取消可能暴露家庭状况的领取方式；同时规定，今后的项目报告必须区分相关关系、可能机制与因果结论。争论最终没有产生一句醒目的宣传语，却带来了更负责任的决定：既不因证据不完美而停止帮助学生，也不因政策目标良善就降低证明标准。一顿早餐或许能够改变一个清晨，但要说明它究竟改变了什么，仍需要耐心、透明和能够接受反面结果的检验。
pinyin: hǎi chuān shì lín jiāng zhōng xué dōng xiào qū wèi yú lǎo chéng qū yǔ xīn jiàn zhù zhái qū de jiāo jiè chù ， xué shēng zhōng jì yǒu zhù xiào shēng ， yě yǒu měi tiān chéng gōng jiāo chē wǎng fǎn de zǒu dú shēng 。 qiū jì xué qī kāi shǐ hòu ， xiào fāng zài yī lóu shí táng shè zhì miǎn fèi zǎo cān chuāng kǒu ， xiàng suǒ yǒu gāo yī xué shēng tí gōng zhōu 、 jī dàn 、 niú nǎi hé zhǔ shí 。 xiàng mù shí shī yí gè yuè hòu ， jiào wù chù zhěng lǐ zǎo kè cè yàn jì lù ， fā xiàn nián jí píng jūn fēn bǐ xiàng mù kāi shǐ qián yǒu suǒ shàng shēng 。 jiē duàn bào gào jù cǐ xiě dào ：“ miǎn fèi zǎo cān chū bù gǎi shàn le xué shēng de kè táng biǎo xiàn 。” zhè jù huà hěn kuài bèi jiā zhǎng wěi yuán huì yǐn yòng ， yǒu rén jiàn yì lì jí kuò dà yù suàn ， hái yǒu jiào shī tí chū bǎ zǎo cān xiàng mù zuò wéi xué xiào tè sè xiàng méi tǐ xuān chuán 。 rán ér ， fù zé shěn hé bào gào de yǔ wén jiào shī zhōu lán tí chū zhì yí ： píng jūn fēn shàng shēng fā shēng zài zǎo cān tuī chū zhī hòu ， bìng bù děng yú zǎo cān dǎo zhì le shàng shēng 。 ruò bù néng pái chú qí tā jiě shì ， zhè ge kàn shì hé lǐ de jié lùn jiù kě néng bǎ shí jiān shàng de xiān hòu guān xì wù dàng chéng yīn guǒ guān xì 。

zhēng lùn shǒu xiān jí zhōng zài “ kè táng biǎo xiàn ” jiū jìng zhǐ shén me 。 jiē duàn bào gào shǐ yòng de shì zǎo kè cè yàn píng jūn fēn ， dàn cè yàn chéng jì zhǐ fǎn yìng tè dìng shí jiān 、 tè dìng tí mù hé tè dìng píng fēn fāng shì xià de biǎo xiàn ， bù néng zì dòng dài biǎo zhù yì lì 、 jì yì lì 、 chū qín zhuàng kuàng huò cháng qī xué xí néng lì 。 zǎo cān yě bú shì yí gè dān yī biàn liàng ： xué shēng shì fǒu lǐng qǔ 、 chī le duō shǎo 、 yǔ shuí yì qǐ chī ， yǐ jí yuán lái shì fǒu kōng fù shàng xué ， dū huì yǐng xiǎng shí jì zuò yòng 。 jiǎ rú yī míng xué shēng měi tiān dōu zài jiā chī zǎo cān ， xué xiào xīn zēng de miǎn fèi cān duì tā jī hū méi yǒu gǎi biàn ； ér lìng yī míng xué shēng guò qù cháng yīn gǎn chē bù chī dōng xī ， xiàng mù duì tā de yì yì kě néng hěn dà 。 bǎ liǎng lèi xué shēng fàng zài tóng yī gè píng jūn shù lǐ ， gù rán biàn yú huì bào ， què kě néng yǎn gài chā yì 。 píng gū xiǎo zǔ yīn cǐ jué dìng xiān bǎ wèn tí gǎi xiě wèi ： zài qí tā tiáo jiàn jǐn kě néng xiāng jìn shí ， huò dé bìng shí jì shí yòng xué xiào zǎo cān ， shì fǒu shǐ yuán běn róng yì kōng fù shàng xué de xué shēng zài zǎo kè zhōng biǎo xiàn dé gèng wěn dìng ？

xiǎo zǔ suí hòu lái dào gāo yī jiào xué lóu hé duì kè chéng biǎo 、 cè yàn juǎn hé bān jí rì zhì ， fā xiàn zǎo cān xiàng mù qǐ dòng shí ， xué xiào hái tóng shí tiáo zhěng le zuò xī 。 zǎo dú bǐ guò qù tuī chí ， zǎo dú yǔ dì yī jié kè zhī jiān zēng jiā le duǎn zàn xiū xī ； jǐ wèi jiào shī yě jiǎn shǎo le chún jì yì tí ， gǎi yòng kè táng jiǎng jiě hòu lì jí zuò dá de liàn xí 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， kāi xué chū shàng wèi shì yìng xīn huán jìng de xué shēng zhú jiàn shú xī jiào shī yāo qiú ， chéng jì zì rán kě néng huí shēng 。 tiān qì zhuǎn liáng hòu ， chí dào rén shù de biàn huà yě huì yǐng xiǎng cān jiā zǎo cè de rén qún 。 gèng zhí de zhù yì de shì ， qián hòu liǎng jiē duàn shǐ yòng de shì juàn bìng bù wán quán xiāng tóng ， tí mù nán dù hé píng fēn chǐ dù quē fá tǒng yī biāo zhǔn 。 yóu cǐ kàn lái ， píng jūn fēn shàng shēng zhì shǎo kě néng lái zì zuò xī 、 jiào xué 、 shì juàn 、 jì jié hé shì yìng guò chéng ， zǎo cān zhǐ shì duō gè tóng shí fā shēng de biàn huà zhī yī 。 ruò zhí jiē bǐ jiào xiàng mù shí shī qián hòu de liǎng gè píng jūn shù ， jiù wú fǎ pàn duàn gè yīn sù fēn bié fā huī le duō dà zuò yòng 。

cān jiā zǎo cān de xué shēng yě bú shì suí jī xíng chéng de qún tǐ 。 zhǔ dòng lǐng qǔ zǎo cān de rén kě néng gèng yuàn yì tí qián dào xiào 、 gèng zūn shǒu zuò xī ， huò zhě běn lái jiù dé dào bān zhǔ rèn jiào duō guān zhù ； bù lǐng qǔ de rén zé kě néng yǐ jīng zài jiā chī guò ， yě kě néng yīn chí dào ér cuò guò gōng yìng 。 tǎng ruò zhí jiē bǐ jiào lǐng qǔ zhě yǔ wèi lǐng qǔ zhě ， guān chá dào de chā jù jì kě néng lái zì shí wù ， yě kě néng lái zì jiā tíng ān pái 、 tōng qín jù lí 、 zì lǜ chéng dù hé yuán yǒu chéng jì 。 fǎn guò lái ， rú guǒ zhǐ yán jiū jīng cháng kōng fù de xué shēng ， yòu róng yì hū lüè tā men suǒ miàn lín de jīng jì yā lì hé zhào hù tiáo jiàn 。 jiā zhǎng dài biǎo dān xīn ， guò dù zhuī wèn jiā tíng qíng kuàng huì gěi hái zi tiē shàng “ kùn nán xué shēng ” de biāo qiān 。 yíng yǎng shī zé tí xǐng ， xué xiào bù néng wèi le huò dé zhěng qí de shù jù ér qiǎng pò xué shēng gǎi biàn yǐn shí 。 píng gū bì xū fú cóng zhī qíng 、 zì yuàn hé yǐn sī bǎo hù yuán zé ， bù néng bǎ jiào yù zhī chí biàn chéng duì ruò shì xué shēng de gōng kāi shāi xuǎn 。

lìng yí gè chōng tū lái zì xiàng mù dì shí jì zhí xíng 。 shí táng guǎn lǐ yuán fā xiàn ， yǒu xiē xué shēng lǐng qǔ zǎo cān hòu dài dào jiào shì ， yǒu xiē zhǐ ná niú nǎi ， hái yǒu xiē tì tóng xué lǐng qǔ 。 jiào shī yě zhī dào nǎ xiē bān jí zhèng zài jī jí cān jiā xiàng mù ， kě néng wú yì zhōng jǐ yǔ gèng duō gǔ lì ， huò zhě yīn wèi qī dài xué shēng zhuàng tài gǎi shàn ér gǎi biàn píng fēn chǐ dù 。 zhè zhǒng qī dài xiào yìng huì ràng jié guǒ kàn qǐ lái bǐ shí jì zuò yòng gèng qiáng 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， zǎo cān chuāng kǒu kāi fàng hòu ， bù fèn xué shēng tí zǎo dào xiào ， zài shí táng yǔ tóng bàn jiāo liú ， suí hòu jié bàn jìn rù jiào shì 。 jí shǐ kè táng zhuàng tài què yǒu gǎi shàn ， yě wèi bì wán quán yóu yíng yǎng shè rù zào chéng ， hái kě néng lái zì wěn dìng de chén jiān jié zòu 、 tóng bàn péi bàn hé chí dào jiǎn shǎo 。 miǎn fèi zǎo cān qí shí shì yī zǔ xiāng hù guān lián de cuò shī ， ér bú shì yī lì kě yǐ yǔ huán jìng fēn lí de yào piàn 。 yào jiǎn yàn yīn guǒ shuō fǎ ， jiù bì xū jì lù shí shī xì jié ， ér bù néng zhǐ zài biǎo gé zhōng tián shàng “ yǒu zǎo cān ” huò “ wú zǎo cān ”。

jīng guò liǎng cì gōng kāi tǎo lùn ， xué xiào méi yǒu qǔ xiāo zǎo cān ， yě méi yǒu bǎ shàng wèi zhèng shí de tuī duàn xiě chéng xuān chuán kǒu hào 。 xiào wù huì jué dìng cǎi yòng fēn jiē duàn tuī jìn de píng gū fāng àn ： yóu yú shí táng róng liàng yǒu xiàn ， gè bān yuán běn jiù xū yào yī cì kāi fàng zǎo cān yù yuē ， yīn cǐ xué xiào àn zhào yù xiān què dìng qiě yǔ chéng jì wú guān de cì xù kuò dà fú wù 。 zài děng dài kāi fàng qī jiān ， xué shēng réng kě shǐ yòng yuán yǒu cān yǐn ān pái ， jī běn yǐn shí xū qiú réng néng dé dào mǎn zú 。 jiào wù chù tǒng yī zǎo kè rèn wù de fàn wéi 、 shí cháng hé píng fēn guī zé ， tóng shí jì lù chū qín 、 chí dào 、 shuì mián zì shù 、 shì fǒu zài jiā jìn cān yǐ jí shí jì lǐng qǔ qíng kuàng 。 jì lù zhǐ shǐ yòng biān mǎ ， bān zhǔ rèn kàn bú dào gè bié jiā tíng de mǐn gǎn xìn xī 。 píng gū zhòng diǎn yě bù zài jú xiàn yú yī cì cè yàn fēn shù ， ér shì guān chá zhù yì lì shì fǒu wěn dìng 、 quē qín shì fǒu jiǎn shǎo ， yǐ jí xiào guǒ néng fǒu chí xù 。 zhè yàng de shè jì réng bú shì háo wú quē xiàn ， què bǐ jiǎn dān de qián hòu bǐ jiào gèng yǒu néng lì pái chú tì dài jiě shì 。

xiǎo zǔ hái yù xiān yuē dìng fēn xī guī zé ， yǐ miǎn kàn dào jié guǒ hòu zài xuǎn zé zuì yǒu lì de jiě shì 。 shǒu xiān bǐ jiào gè jiē duàn fú wù kāi fàng qián hòu de biàn huà ， ér bú shì zhǐ tiāo xuǎn jìn bù zuì míng xiǎn de bān jí ； qí cì fēn bié guān chá guò qù cháng kōng fù hé yuán běn yǐ yǒu zǎo cān xí guàn de xué shēng ， yīn wèi zǒng tǐ píng jūn xiào guǒ kě néng yǎn gài zhēn zhèng shòu yì zhě ； zài cì jiǎn chá quē shī jì lù ， nòng qīng wèi cān jiā cè yàn de rén shì fǒu jí zhōng zài mǒu xiē tōng qín jiào yuǎn huò chū qín bù wěn dìng de qún tǐ 。 ruò zǎo cān zhǐ gǎi shàn le xué shēng dào xiào hòu de shū shì gǎn ， què méi yǒu lì jí tí gāo fēn shù ， zhè réng kě néng shì yǒu jià zhí de jié guǒ ； ruò duǎn qī fēn shù shàng shēng dàn suí hòu xiāo shī ， yě bù néng xuān chēng xué xí néng lì huò dé chí jiǔ gǎi shàn 。 yīn guǒ pàn duàn bú shì xún zhǎo yī xiàng zhī chí yù qī de zhèng jù ， ér shì zhǔ dòng zhuī wèn ： hái yǒu shén me qíng kuàng yě huì chǎn shēng tóng yàng xiàn xiàng ？ zhè xiē qíng kuàng shì fǒu yǐ jīng bèi shè jì 、 jì lù hé fēn xī jǐn liàng pái chú ？

xué qī mò ， xué xiào gōng bù de jié lùn bǐ zuì chū de jiē duàn bào gào jǐn shèn dé duō ： xiàn yǒu zhèng jù biǎo míng ， miǎn fèi zǎo cān yǔ bù fèn zǎo chén zhuàng tài de gǎi shàn tóng shí chū xiàn ， dàn jǐn píng píng jūn fēn shàng shēng ， shàng bù zú yǐ duàn yán zǎo cān běn shēn zào chéng le quán bù biàn huà 。 fēn jiē duàn jì lù wèi jì xù pàn duàn tí gōng le gèng kě kào de jī chǔ ， yě jiē shì chū xiàng mù dì jià zhí bù yīng zhǐ yòng kǎo shì chéng jì héng liáng 。 xiào fāng jù cǐ bǎo liú miǎn fèi zǎo cān ， jiāng gōng yìng shí jiān yǔ gōng jiāo dào zhàn shí jiān xián jiē ， bìng qǔ xiāo kě néng bào lù jiā tíng zhuàng kuàng de lǐng qǔ fāng shì ； tóng shí guī dìng ， jīn hòu de xiàng mù bào gào bì xū qū fēn xiāng guān guān xì 、 kě néng jī zhì yǔ yīn guǒ jié lùn 。 zhēng lùn zuì zhōng méi yǒu chǎn shēng yī jù xǐng mù dì xuān chuán yǔ ， què dài lái le gèng fù zé rèn de jué dìng ： jì bù yīn zhèng jù bù wán měi ér tíng zhǐ bāng zhù xué shēng ， yě bù yīn zhèng cè mù biāo liáng shàn jiù jiàng dī zhèng míng biāo zhǔn 。 yī dùn zǎo cān huò xǔ néng gòu gǎi biàn yí gè qīng chén ， dàn yào shuō míng tā jiū jìng gǎi biàn le shén me ， réng xū yào nài xīn 、 tòu míng hé néng gòu jiē shòu fǎn miàn jié guǒ de jiǎn yàn 。
translation: The East Campus of Linjiang Middle School in Haichuan City lies at the boundary between the old urban district and a newly built residential area. Its students include both boarders and day students who commute by bus every day. After the fall semester began, the school set up a free breakfast counter in the first-floor cafeteria, providing porridge, eggs, milk, and staple foods to all tenth-grade students. One month after the program was introduced, the Office of Academic Affairs compiled the records from early-morning quizzes and found that the grade-wide average score had risen from its level before the program began. On this basis, the interim report stated, “The free breakfast program has initially improved students’ classroom performance.” The statement was soon quoted by the parents’ committee. Some people proposed immediately increasing the budget, while some teachers suggested promoting the breakfast program to the media as a distinctive feature of the school. However, Zhou Lan, the Chinese-language teacher responsible for reviewing the report, raised an objection: the fact that the average score rose after breakfast was introduced did not mean that breakfast caused the increase. Unless other explanations could be ruled out, this seemingly reasonable conclusion might mistake temporal sequence for causation.

The debate first centered on what exactly “classroom performance” meant. The interim report used average scores on early-morning quizzes, but quiz results reflect performance only at a particular time, on particular questions, and under a particular grading method. They do not automatically represent attention, memory, attendance, or long-term learning ability. Breakfast is not a single variable either: whether students collect it, how much they eat, whom they eat with, and whether they previously came to school on an empty stomach can all affect its actual impact. If a student already eats breakfast at home every day, the school’s new free meal changes almost nothing for that student. For another student who used to skip food frequently because of the rush to catch the bus, however, the program may make a major difference. Combining both types of students into a single average is certainly convenient for reporting, but it may conceal their differences. The evaluation team therefore decided to reformulate the question as follows: when other conditions are kept as similar as possible, does receiving and actually eating the school breakfast make the early-morning classroom performance of students who were previously prone to arriving on an empty stomach more consistent?

The team then went to the tenth-grade teaching building to check timetables, quiz papers, and class logs. They discovered that when the breakfast program began, the school had also adjusted its daily schedule. Morning reading started later than before, and a short break had been added between morning reading and the first class. Several teachers had also reduced the number of questions based purely on memorization and replaced them with exercises that students answered immediately after classroom instruction. Meanwhile, students who had not yet adapted to their new environment at the beginning of the school year gradually became familiar with their teachers’ expectations, so their scores might naturally have recovered. As the weather grew cooler, changes in the number of late arrivals could also affect the group taking the morning quizzes. More importantly, the test papers used in the two periods were not entirely the same, and there were no uniform standards for question difficulty or grading scales. The rise in average scores could therefore have resulted from at least the schedule, teaching methods, test papers, seasonal changes, and the adaptation process. Breakfast was only one of several changes occurring at the same time. A direct comparison of the two averages before and after the program could not determine how much of an effect each factor had.

The students who participated in the breakfast program were not a randomly formed group either. Those who voluntarily collected breakfast might have been more willing to arrive early, more likely to follow the school schedule, or already receiving more attention from their homeroom teachers. Those who did not collect it might already have eaten at home, or they might have missed the serving period because they were late. If recipients were compared directly with nonrecipients, any observed difference might result from the food, but it might also result from family arrangements, commuting distance, self-discipline, or prior academic performance. Conversely, studying only students who frequently arrived on an empty stomach could make it easy to overlook the financial pressures and caregiving conditions they faced. Parent representatives worried that excessive questioning about family circumstances would label children as “disadvantaged students.” The nutritionist, meanwhile, cautioned that the school must not force students to change their eating habits merely to obtain tidy data. The evaluation had to comply with the principles of informed consent, voluntary participation, and privacy protection. Educational support must not be turned into a public screening process for vulnerable students.

Another conflict arose from how the program was actually implemented. Cafeteria staff found that some students took their breakfasts to the classroom, some took only milk, and others collected meals for classmates. Teachers also knew which classes were actively participating in the program and might unintentionally offer them more encouragement or alter their grading standards because they expected the students’ condition to improve. This expectation effect could make the results appear stronger than the program’s actual impact. At the same time, after the breakfast counter opened, some students began arriving at school earlier, socializing with their peers in the cafeteria, and then entering the classroom together. Even if their classroom condition genuinely improved, the improvement might not have resulted entirely from nutritional intake. It could also have arisen from a consistent morning routine, peer companionship, and fewer late arrivals. Free breakfast was actually a set of interrelated measures, not a pill that could be separated from its environment. To test a causal claim, the school had to document the details of implementation rather than merely mark “breakfast” or “no breakfast” in a table.

After two public discussions, the school neither canceled breakfast nor turned an unverified inference into a promotional slogan. The school administrative council decided to adopt a phased evaluation plan. Because cafeteria capacity was limited, breakfast reservations already had to be opened to classes in sequence, so the school expanded the service according to a predetermined order unrelated to academic performance. While waiting for access, students could continue using their existing meal arrangements and would still have their basic dietary needs met. The Office of Academic Affairs standardized the scope, duration, and grading rules of early-morning assignments while also recording attendance, late arrivals, self-reported sleep, whether students had eaten at home, and whether they had actually collected breakfast. The records used codes only, and homeroom teachers could not see sensitive information about individual families. The evaluation was also no longer limited to the score from a single quiz. Instead, it examined whether attention became more consistent, whether absences declined, and whether any effects persisted. This design was still not flawless, but it was better able than a simple before-and-after comparison to rule out alternative explanations.

The team also agreed on analytical rules in advance to avoid selecting the most favorable explanation after seeing the results. First, it would compare changes before and after access to the service opened at each stage rather than selecting only the classes that improved the most. Second, it would examine separately students who had often arrived on an empty stomach and those who already habitually ate breakfast, because the overall average effect might obscure those who truly benefited. Third, it would inspect missing records to determine whether students who did not take the quizzes were concentrated in groups with longer commutes or unstable attendance. If breakfast merely made students feel more comfortable after arriving at school without immediately raising their scores, that could still be a valuable outcome. If scores rose in the short term but the increase later disappeared, the school still could not claim that learning ability had improved permanently. Causal judgment is not a search for one piece of evidence that supports an expectation. Instead, it requires actively asking what other circumstances could produce the same phenomenon and whether those circumstances have been excluded as far as possible through the design, records, and analysis.

At the end of the semester, the school announced a conclusion far more cautious than the initial interim report: the available evidence indicated that free breakfast coincided with improvements in some aspects of students’ morning condition, but the rise in average scores alone was not sufficient to conclude that breakfast itself had caused all the changes. The phased records provided a more reliable basis for further assessment and also revealed that the program’s value should not be measured solely by test scores. On this basis, the school retained the free breakfast program, aligned serving times with bus arrival times, and eliminated collection procedures that might expose families’ circumstances. It also stipulated that future program reports must distinguish among correlation, possible mechanisms, and causal conclusions. The debate ultimately produced no striking promotional slogan, but it did lead to a more responsible decision: the school would neither stop helping students because the evidence was imperfect nor lower its standard of proof because the policy’s goal was benevolent. A breakfast may be able to change a morning, but explaining exactly what it changes still requires patience, transparency, and testing that is capable of accepting contrary results.

questions.prompt: 为什么仅凭早餐项目实施前后的平均分变化，不能断定早餐造成了成绩上升？
options: 同期还发生了作息、教学、试卷、季节和适应过程等变化，无法分别判断各因素的作用
免费早餐只向住校生开放，因此走读生的成绩不能纳入比较
项目开始后学校完全取消了早课测验，前后没有可比较的数据
所有领取早餐的学生原本成绩都高于未领取早餐的学生
questions.explanation: 早餐推出时，多项可能影响成绩的因素也在同时变化，因此平均分的前后差异不能单独归因于早餐。
questions.evidence: 由此看来，平均分上升至少可能来自作息、教学、试卷、季节和适应过程，早餐只是多个同时发生的变化之一。

questions.prompt: 评估小组在收集学生家庭和饮食信息时必须遵守什么原则？

遵守知情、自愿和隐私保护原则，避免把支持项目变成对弱势学生的公开筛选
强迫所有学生采用相同饮食，以获得更加整齐的数据
让班主任直接查看每个家庭的敏感信息，以监督学生是否如实填写

questions.prompt: 学期末，学校对早餐项目和今后的项目报告作出了什么决定？
options: 取消免费早餐，并恢复可能显示学生家庭状况的领取方式
把平均分上升直接写成宣传口号，并停止继续收集数据
保留免费早餐、调整供应安排和领取方式，并要求报告区分相关关系、可能机制与因果结论
