questions.prompt: 评估组为什么认为不能仅凭专用袋重量下降就断定按量收费实现了源头减量？
options: 重量下降还可能由分类改善、统计遗漏或违规转移造成
收费后的垃圾重量完全没有下降
居民在试点期间都停止使用专用垃圾袋
卫生局没有公布任何与垃圾重量有关的数据
questions.explanation: 同一项重量下降指标可以由多种不同机制导致，因此它无法排除分类改善、统计遗漏和违规转移等替代解释，也就不足以单独证明源头减量。
questions.evidence: 专用袋重量下降可以是源头减量的结果，也可以是分类改善、统计遗漏或违规转移的结果，因此不能单凭这一项指标作出排他的判断。

questions.prompt: 新的评估方案采取了什么办法来减少其他政策差异对结果的干扰？
options: 停止所有小区的垃圾分类宣传
把尚未收费的小区作为比较对象，同时保持基础服务和分类宣传一致
只比较收费前后相邻两个月的专用袋重量
让每个小区自行决定实施时间且不对外公布
questions.explanation: 方案设置了尚未收费的比较对象，并使这些小区与试点小区的基础服务和分类宣传保持一致，从而尽量控制按量收费之外的政策差异。
questions.evidence: 实施顺序提前公开确定，尚未收费的小区暂时作为比较对象，但基础服务和分类宣传保持一致，以减少其他政策差异造成的干扰。

questions.prompt: 文章最后认为，真正可靠的政策评估应当怎样处理复杂现实和不确定性？
options: 把所有复杂因素压缩成一个便于宣传的结论
等到获得绝对确定的证据后才允许作出任何判断
承认不确定性，区分已有证据支持的判断、仍待证明的问题及后续验证方向
只要政策实施后指标下降，就直接认定政策产生了唯一的因果效果
questions.explanation: 可靠评估既不能把复杂现实简单化，也不必等待绝对确定，而应明确证据目前支持什么、哪些判断仍不确定，以及下一步如何继续检验。
questions.evidence: 真正可靠的政策评估并不追求把复杂现实压缩成单一答案，而是在承认不确定性的同时，指出哪些判断已经得到支持，哪些仍需证据，以及下一步应当如何验证。

articles.title: 一份阶段报告引发的追问：开放实验室真的促进了跨院系合作吗？
articles.summary: 东江大学开放公共实验中心后，跨院系合作项目数量有所增加。校科研委员会没有立即接受“开放实验室提高科研合作”的因果结论，而是重新核对项目口径、开放时间、政策变化和合作质量，并采用分阶段比较、过程记录与反事实分析检验这一说法。调查最终表明，开放措施确实降低了部分合作门槛，但项目增长同时受到经费政策、考核制度和人员流动影响。学校据此决定继续开放实验室，同时完善预约、署名、费用和成果追踪制度，不再用单一项目数量评价开放成效。
articles.topic: 一份阶段报告引发的追问：开放实验室真的促进了跨院系合作吗？
paragraphs: 东江大学公共实验中心位于新校区科研楼，是全校大型仪器最集中的场所。过去，中心设备主要由材料学院管理，其他院系若想使用，往往需要先找到熟悉的教师，再由实验室内部人员代为预约。后来，学校把公共仪器目录、空闲时段和申请条件统一公布，并允许医学、环境、信息等院系直接提交预约。运行一段时间后，科研管理处发布阶段报告，称开放以来跨院系合作项目数量增加，并据此提出“开放实验室提高了科研合作”。这句话很快被写进年度工作简报，也成为扩大开放范围的主要理由。然而，在科研委员会的审议会上，统计学系教授周岚指出，项目数量在开放后上升，只能说明两个现象同时发生，尚不能证明前者导致了后者。若不检查其他同期变化，这个看似直观的结论可能把相关关系误当成因果关系。

争议首先集中在“合作项目”的定义上。阶段报告把申请书中出现两个院系名称的项目都列为跨院系合作，却没有区分实质合作与形式联合。有些项目只是在申报时邀请另一院系教师挂名，实际研究仍由原团队独立完成；有些教师拥有双重聘任，其所在团队虽然被系统识别为跨院系组合，成员却长期在同一实验室工作。与此同时，一项真正需要多学科参与的联合研究，可能被拆成若干内部课题，在统计表里反而只算一个项目。如果指标本身不能稳定反映合作程度，那么数量增加既可能意味着知识、设备与人员之间的联系变得紧密，也可能只是申报方式改变。委员会因此决定返回原始材料，核对项目成员的实际分工、设备使用记录、共同会议纪要和成果署名，而不是仅凭院系标签下结论。

第二个问题是时间顺序背后的混杂因素。实验中心开放的同一学期，学校还调整了科研考核办法：联合申请项目可以在院系考核中获得额外认可，青年教师申报校内启动经费时也被鼓励组成跨学科团队。此外，几家资助机构发布的新指南开始强调医学、工程与数据科学的结合。即使实验室没有开放，这些政策也可能推动合作项目增加。更容易被忽略的是，新校区启用后，原本分散在不同校区的几个院系搬进相邻楼宇，教师在研讨会、食堂和公共平台见面的机会明显增多。空间接近、经费导向、考核激励与实验室开放几乎同时出现，任何一个因素都可能影响结果。若把全部变化归功于开放实验室，不仅会夸大措施的作用，还会使后续资源配置建立在不可靠的解释上。

为了检验因果说法，委员会没有简单地比较开放前后的总数，而是寻找更接近反事实的参照：如果实验室没有开放，合作趋势可能怎样变化？由于不同设备完成公开预约的时间并不一致，他们把先开放的仪器与尚未开放、但用途和服务对象相近的仪器进行分阶段比较，同时观察各院系此前的合作趋势。这个办法仍不等同于随机实验，因为设备开放顺序可能与需求强弱有关；需求旺盛的设备往往更早进入平台，而需求本身就可能促成合作。因此，分析人员又查阅开放决策记录，确认某些开放时间主要受维修、验收和管理系统接入进度影响，并把明显由强烈合作需求推动的设备排除在核心比较之外。委员会还要求报告分别呈现材料分析、医学检测和计算平台的情况，避免用一个平均结果掩盖领域差异。

除了项目数量，调查组还追踪合作形成的具体过程。预约记录能够显示外院系成员何时开始使用设备，却不能证明双方真正交换了知识；共同署名能够反映成果联系，却可能在合作发生很久以后才出现。为此，调查组查看技术咨询、样品制备、数据解释和后续讨论的记录，并访谈平台工程师与项目负责人。他们特别关注合作是否在开放之后首次建立、参与者是否承担了不可替代的工作，以及关系是否延续到新的研究问题。核查发现，开放平台对缺少专用设备的年轻团队帮助较明显：公开目录使他们知道校内有哪些能力，统一预约减少了寻找私人关系的成本，工程师的现场交流也常常把一次检测转化为方法讨论。但对早已有稳定伙伴的资深团队而言，平台开放更多只是把原有使用方式正式化，并未创造新的合作关系。

调查还暴露出一种容易造成反向因果的情形。部分院系原本就准备联合申报项目，为满足样品检测和数据处理需求，他们主动要求学校加快设备开放。表面上看，开放发生在项目正式登记之前，似乎是开放带来了合作；实际上，合作意向早已存在，开放只是对既有需求的回应。如果仅按系统登记日期排列先后，就会错误判断因果方向。委员会于是把项目构思会议、预申请材料和设备咨询邮件纳入时间线，区分“开放促成合作”与“合作推动开放”。这一处理没有完全消除不确定性，却使证据边界更加清楚：开放能够降低资源使用门槛，但并非所有在其后出现的合作都由它产生。因果判断需要说明作用机制，也需要排除至少几种可信的替代解释，不能只依赖一句“开放后增加了”。

在审议阶段，校方还讨论了可能的代价。预约全面开放后，热门仪器的等待时间变长，平台工程师承担了大量基础培训；若只奖励新增项目，管理者可能倾向于接受更多申请，却忽视服务质量、样品安全和长期维护。不同院系对费用分担、数据归属和论文署名的理解也不一致，一次未经充分协商的共享甚至可能破坏合作意愿。因此，开放不是把门锁取消就算完成，而是一套包含准入、培训、收费、责任和争议处理的制度。科研合作也不是越多越好：缺乏共同问题的临时组合会增加协调成本，真正值得鼓励的是双方能力互补、责任清晰并能产生持续知识交流的合作。委员会据此否决了以项目增量作为唯一绩效指标的提案。

最终，科研委员会给出了有限而明确的结论：现有材料支持“开放实验室为一部分跨院系合作提供了必要条件”，也能说明它通过信息公开、直接预约和技术交流降低了合作门槛；但证据不足以支持“项目增长主要由开放造成”这一更强的说法。学校决定继续推进开放，不是因为阶段报告已经证明了单一因果关系，而是因为开放具有资源公平和提高设备利用效率的独立价值。与此同时，科研管理处修改了报告措辞，建立按设备分期追踪的记录制度，并增加实质分工、重复合作、成果共享和使用者负担等指标。一年后的复核将预先确定分析口径，公开排除条件与不确定性。这个结果没有提供一句响亮的宣传口号，却形成了更可靠的决策：承认开放可能有效，说明它在什么条件下有效，也诚实标出仍然无法排除的解释。
pinyin: dōng jiāng dà xué gōng gòng shí yàn zhōng xīn wèi yú xīn xiào qū kē yán lóu ， shì quán xiào dà xíng yí qì zuì jí zhōng de chǎng suǒ 。 guò qù ， zhōng xīn shè bèi zhǔ yào yóu cái liào xué yuàn guǎn lǐ ， qí tā yuàn xì ruò xiǎng shǐ yòng ， wǎng wǎng xū yào xiān zhǎo dào shú xī de jiào shī ， zài yóu shí yàn shì nèi bù rén yuán dài wéi yù yuē 。 hòu lái ， xué xiào bǎ gōng gòng yí qì mù lù 、 kòng xián shí duàn hé shēn qǐng tiáo jiàn tǒng yī gōng bù ， bìng yǔn xǔ yī xué 、 huán jìng 、 xìn xī děng yuàn xì zhí jiē tí jiāo yù yuē 。 yùn xíng yī duàn shí jiān hòu ， kē yán guǎn lǐ chù fā bù jiē duàn bào gào ， chēng kāi fàng yǐ lái kuà yuàn xì hé zuò xiàng mù shù liàng zēng jiā ， bìng jù cǐ tí chū “ kāi fàng shí yàn shì tí gāo le kē yán hé zuò ”。 zhè jù huà hěn kuài bèi xiě jìn nián dù gōng zuò jiǎn bào ， yě chéng wéi kuò dà kāi fàng fàn wéi de zhǔ yào lǐ yóu 。 rán ér ， zài kē yán wěi yuán huì de shěn yì huì shàng ， tǒng jì xué xì jiào shòu zhōu lán zhǐ chū ， xiàng mù shù liàng zài kāi fàng hòu shàng shēng ， zhǐ néng shuō míng liǎng gè xiàn xiàng tóng shí fā shēng ， shàng bù néng zhèng míng qián zhě dǎo zhì le hòu zhě 。 ruò bù jiǎn chá qí tā tóng qī biàn huà ， zhè ge kàn shì zhí guān de jié lùn kě néng bǎ xiāng guān guān xì wù dàng chéng yīn guǒ guān xì 。

zhēng yì shǒu xiān jí zhōng zài “ hé zuò xiàng mù ” de dìng yì shàng 。 jiē duàn bào gào bǎ shēn qǐng shū zhōng chū xiàn liǎng gè yuàn xì míng chēng de xiàng mù dōu liè wèi kuà yuàn xì hé zuò ， què méi yǒu qū fēn shí zhì hé zuò yǔ xíng shì lián hé 。 yǒu xiē xiàng mù zhǐ shì zài shēn bào shí yāo qǐng lìng yī yuàn xì jiào shī guà míng ， shí jì yán jiū réng yóu yuán tuán duì dú lì wán chéng ； yǒu xiē jiào shī yōng yǒu shuāng chóng pìn rèn ， qí suǒ zài tuán duì suī rán bèi xì tǒng shí bié wèi kuà yuàn xì zǔ hé ， chéng yuán què cháng qī zài tóng yī shí yàn shì gōng zuò 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， yī xiàng zhēn zhèng xū yào duō xué kē cān yù de lián hé yán jiū ， kě néng bèi chāi chéng ruò gān nèi bù kè tí ， zài tǒng jì biǎo lǐ fǎn ér zhǐ suàn yí gè xiàng mù 。 rú guǒ zhǐ biāo běn shēn bù néng wěn dìng fǎn yìng hé zuò chéng dù ， nà me shù liàng zēng jiā jì kě néng yì wèi zhe zhī shí 、 shè bèi yǔ rén yuán zhī jiān de lián xì biàn dé jǐn mì ， yě kě néng zhǐ shì shēn bào fāng shì gǎi biàn 。 wěi yuán huì yīn cǐ jué dìng fǎn huí yuán shǐ cái liào ， hé duì xiàng mù chéng yuán de shí jì fēn gōng 、 shè bèi shǐ yòng jì lù 、 gòng tóng huì yì jì yào hé chéng guǒ shǔ míng ， ér bú shì jǐn píng yuàn xì biāo qiān xià jié lùn 。

dì èr gè wèn tí shì shí jiān shùn xù bèi hòu de hùn zá yīn sù 。 shí yàn zhōng xīn kāi fàng de tóng yī xué qī ， xué xiào hái tiáo zhěng le kē yán kǎo hé bàn fǎ ： lián hé shēn qǐng xiàng mù kě yǐ zài yuàn xì kǎo hé zhōng huò dé é wài rèn kě ， qīng nián jiào shī shēn bào xiào nèi qǐ dòng jīng fèi shí yě bèi gǔ lì zǔ chéng kuà xué kē tuán duì 。 cǐ wài ， jǐ jiā zī zhù jī gòu fā bù de xīn zhǐ nán kāi shǐ qiáng diào yī xué 、 gōng chéng yǔ shù jù kē xué de jié hé 。 jí shǐ shí yàn shì méi yǒu kāi fàng ， zhè xiē zhèng cè yě kě néng tuī dòng hé zuò xiàng mù zēng jiā 。 gèng róng yì bèi hū lüè de shì ， xīn xiào qū qǐ yòng hòu ， yuán běn fèn sàn zài bù tóng xiào qū de jǐ gè yuàn xì bān jìn xiāng lín lóu yǔ ， jiào shī zài yán tǎo huì 、 shí táng hé gōng gòng píng tái jiàn miàn de jī huì míng xiǎn zēng duō 。 kōng jiān jiē jìn 、 jīng fèi dǎo xiàng 、 kǎo hé jī lì yǔ shí yàn shì kāi fàng jī hū tóng shí chū xiàn ， rèn hé yí gè yīn sù dōu kě néng yǐng xiǎng jié guǒ 。 ruò bǎ quán bù biàn huà guī gōng yú kāi fàng shí yàn shì ， bù jǐn huì kuā dà cuò shī de zuò yòng ， hái huì shǐ hòu xù zī yuán pèi zhì jiàn lì zài bù kě kào de jiě shì shàng 。

wèi le jiǎn yàn yīn guǒ shuō fǎ ， wěi yuán huì méi yǒu jiǎn dān dì bǐ jiào kāi fàng qián hòu de zǒng shù ， ér shì xún zhǎo gèng jiē jìn fǎn shì shí de cān zhào ： rú guǒ shí yàn shì méi yǒu kāi fàng ， hé zuò qū shì kě néng zěn yàng biàn huà ？ yóu yú bù tóng shè bèi wán chéng gōng kāi yù yuē de shí jiān bìng bù yī zhì ， tā men bǎ xiān kāi fàng de yí qì yǔ shàng wèi kāi fàng 、 dàn yòng tú hé fú wù duì xiàng xiāng jìn de yí qì jìn xíng fēn jiē duàn bǐ jiào ， tóng shí guān chá gè yuàn xì cǐ qián de hé zuò qū shì 。 zhè ge bàn fǎ réng bù děng tóng yú suí jī shí yàn ， yīn wèi shè bèi kāi fàng shùn xù kě néng yǔ xū qiú qiáng ruò yǒu guān ； xū qiú wàng shèng de shè bèi wǎng wǎng gèng zǎo jìn rù píng tái ， ér xū qiú běn shēn jiù kě néng cù chéng hé zuò 。 yīn cǐ ， fēn xī rén yuán yòu chá yuè kāi fàng jué cè jì lù ， què rèn mǒu xiē kāi fàng shí jiān zhǔ yào shòu wéi xiū 、 yàn shōu hé guǎn lǐ xì tǒng jiē rù jìn dù yǐng xiǎng ， bìng bǎ míng xiǎn yóu qiáng liè hé zuò xū qiú tuī dòng de shè bèi pái chú zài hé xīn bǐ jiào zhī wài 。 wěi yuán huì hái yāo qiú bào gào fēn bié chéng xiàn cái liào fēn xī 、 yī xué jiǎn cè hé jì suàn píng tái de qíng kuàng ， bì miǎn yòng yí gè píng jūn jié guǒ yǎn gài lǐng yù chā yì 。

chú le xiàng mù shù liàng ， diào chá zǔ hái zhuī zōng hé zuò xíng chéng de jù tǐ guò chéng 。 yù yuē jì lù néng gòu xiǎn shì wài yuàn xì chéng yuán hé shí kāi shǐ shǐ yòng shè bèi ， què bù néng zhèng míng shuāng fāng zhēn zhèng jiāo huàn le zhī shí ； gòng tóng shǔ míng néng gòu fǎn yìng chéng guǒ lián xì ， què kě néng zài hé zuò fā shēng hěn jiǔ yǐ hòu cái chū xiàn 。 wèi cǐ ， diào chá zǔ chá kàn jì shù zī xún 、 yàng pǐn zhì bèi 、 shù jù jiě shì hé hòu xù tǎo lùn de jì lù ， bìng fǎng tán píng tái gōng chéng shī yǔ xiàng mù fù zé rén 。 tā men tè bié guān zhù hé zuò shì fǒu zài kāi fàng zhī hòu shǒu cì jiàn lì 、 cān yù zhě shì fǒu chéng dān le bù kě tì dài de gōng zuò ， yǐ jí guān xì shì fǒu yán xù dào xīn de yán jiū wèn tí 。 hé chá fā xiàn ， kāi fàng píng tái duì quē shǎo zhuān yòng shè bèi de nián qīng tuán duì bāng zhù jiào míng xiǎn ： gōng kāi mù lù shǐ tā men zhī dào xiào nèi yǒu nǎ xiē néng lì ， tǒng yī yù yuē jiǎn shǎo le xún zhǎo sī rén guān xì de chéng běn ， gōng chéng shī de xiàn chǎng jiāo liú yě cháng cháng bǎ yī cì jiǎn cè zhuǎn huà wèi fāng fǎ tǎo lùn 。 dàn duì zǎo yǐ yǒu wěn dìng huǒ bàn de zī shēn tuán duì ér yán ， píng tái kāi fàng gèng duō zhǐ shì bǎ yuán yǒu shǐ yòng fāng shì zhèng shì huà ， bìng wèi chuàng zào xīn de hé zuò guān xì 。

diào chá hái bào lù chū yī zhǒng róng yì zào chéng fǎn xiàng yīn guǒ de qíng xíng 。 bù fèn yuàn xì yuán běn jiù zhǔn bèi lián hé shēn bào xiàng mù ， wèi mǎn zú yàng pǐn jiǎn cè hé shù jù chǔ lǐ xū qiú ， tā men zhǔ dòng yāo qiú xué xiào jiā kuài shè bèi kāi fàng 。 biǎo miàn shàng kàn ， kāi fàng fā shēng zài xiàng mù zhèng shì dēng jì zhī qián ， sì hū shì kāi fàng dài lái le hé zuò ； shí jì shàng ， hé zuò yì xiàng zǎo yǐ cún zài ， kāi fàng zhǐ shì duì jì yǒu xū qiú de huí yìng 。 rú guǒ jǐn àn xì tǒng dēng jì rì qī pái liè xiān hòu ， jiù huì cuò wù pàn duàn yīn guǒ fāng xiàng 。 wěi yuán huì yú shì bǎ xiàng mù gòu sī huì yì 、 yù shēn qǐng cái liào hé shè bèi zī xún yóu jiàn nà rù shí jiān xiàn ， qū fēn “ kāi fàng cù chéng hé zuò ” yǔ “ hé zuò tuī dòng kāi fàng ”。 zhè yī chǔ lǐ méi yǒu wán quán xiāo chú bù què dìng xìng ， què shǐ zhèng jù biān jiè gèng jiā qīng chǔ ： kāi fàng néng gòu jiàng dī zī yuán shǐ yòng mén kǎn ， dàn bìng fēi suǒ yǒu zài qí hòu chū xiàn de hé zuò dōu yóu tā chǎn shēng 。 yīn guǒ pàn duàn xū yào shuō míng zuò yòng jī zhì ， yě xū yào pái chú zhì shǎo jǐ zhǒng kě xìn de tì dài jiě shì ， bù néng zhǐ yī lài yī jù “ kāi fàng hòu zēng jiā le ”。

zài shěn yì jiē duàn ， xiào fāng hái tǎo lùn le kě néng de dài jià 。 yù yuē quán miàn kāi fàng hòu ， rè mén yí qì de děng dài shí jiān biàn zhǎng ， píng tái gōng chéng shī chéng dān le dà liàng jī chǔ péi xùn ； ruò zhǐ jiǎng lì xīn zēng xiàng mù ， guǎn lǐ zhě kě néng qīng xiàng yú jiē shòu gèng duō shēn qǐng ， què hū shì fú wù zhì liàng 、 yàng pǐn ān quán hé cháng qī wéi hù 。 bù tóng yuàn xì duì fèi yòng fēn dān 、 shù jù guī shǔ hé lùn wén shǔ míng de lǐ jiě yě bù yī zhì ， yī cì wèi jīng chōng fèn xié shāng de gòng xiǎng shèn zhì kě néng pò huài hé zuò yì yuàn 。 yīn cǐ ， kāi fàng bú shì bǎ mén suǒ qǔ xiāo jiù suàn wán chéng ， ér shì yī tào bāo hán zhǔn rù 、 péi xùn 、 shōu fèi 、 zé rèn hé zhēng yì chǔ lǐ de zhì dù 。 kē yán hé zuò yě bú shì yuè duō yuè hǎo ： quē fá gòng tóng wèn tí de lín shí zǔ hé huì zēng jiā xié tiáo chéng běn ， zhēn zhèng zhí de gǔ lì de shì shuāng fāng néng lì hù bǔ 、 zé rèn qīng xī bìng néng chǎn shēng chí xù zhī shí jiāo liú de hé zuò 。 wěi yuán huì jù cǐ fǒu jué le yǐ xiàng mù zēng liàng zuò wéi wéi yī jì xiào zhǐ biāo dì tí àn 。

zuì zhōng ， kē yán wěi yuán huì gěi chū le yǒu xiàn ér míng què de jié lùn ： xiàn yǒu cái liào zhī chí “ kāi fàng shí yàn shì wèi yī bù fèn kuà yuàn xì hé zuò tí gōng le bì yào tiáo jiàn ”， yě néng shuō míng tā tōng guò xìn xī gōng kāi 、 zhí jiē yù yuē hé jì shù jiāo liú jiàng dī le hé zuò mén kǎn ； dàn zhèng jù bù zú yǐ zhī chí “ xiàng mù zēng zhǎng zhǔ yào yóu kāi fàng zào chéng ” zhè yī gèng qiáng de shuō fǎ 。 xué xiào jué dìng jì xù tuī jìn kāi fàng ， bú shì yīn wèi jiē duàn bào gào yǐ jīng zhèng míng liǎo dān yī yīn guǒ guān xì ， ér shì yīn wèi kāi fàng jù yǒu zī yuán gōng píng hé tí gāo shè bèi lì yòng xiào lǜ de dú lì jià zhí 。 yǔ cǐ tóng shí ， kē yán guǎn lǐ chù xiū gǎi le bào gào cuò cí ， jiàn lì àn shè bèi fēn qī zhuī zōng de jì lù zhì dù ， bìng zēng jiā shí zhì fēn gōng 、 chóng fù hé zuò 、 chéng guǒ gòng xiǎng hé shǐ yòng zhě fù dān děng zhǐ biāo 。 yī nián hòu de fù hé jiāng yù xiān què dìng fēn xī kǒu jìng ， gōng kāi pái chú tiáo jiàn yǔ bù què dìng xìng 。 zhè ge jié guǒ méi yǒu tí gōng yī jù xiǎng liàng de xuān chuán kǒu hào ， què xíng chéng le gèng kě kào de jué cè ： chéng rèn kāi fàng kě néng yǒu xiào ， shuō míng tā zài shén me tiáo jiàn xià yǒu xiào ， yě chéng shí biāo chū réng rán wú fǎ pái chú de jiě shì 。
translation: Dongjiang University’s Public Experimental Center is located in the research building on the new campus and houses the university’s largest concentration of major scientific instruments. In the past, the center’s equipment was managed primarily by the School of Materials Science. If researchers from other schools or departments wanted to use it, they often had to first find a faculty member they knew and then ask someone within the laboratory to make a reservation on their behalf. Later, the university published a unified catalog of public instruments, available time slots, and application requirements, and allowed schools and departments such as medicine, environmental studies, and information science to submit reservations directly. After the system had been operating for some time, the Office of Research Administration issued an interim report stating that the number of cross-departmental collaborative projects had increased since the center opened up and, on that basis, concluded that “opening the laboratories increased research collaboration.” This statement was soon included in the annual work report and became a principal justification for expanding the scope of access. At a review meeting of the Research Committee, however, Zhou Lan, a professor in the Department of Statistics, pointed out that the rise in the number of projects after the center opened up showed only that two phenomena had occurred at the same time; it did not yet prove that the former had caused the latter. Unless other changes occurring during the same period were examined, this seemingly intuitive conclusion might mistake correlation for causation.

The dispute first centered on the definition of a “collaborative project.” The interim report classified every project whose application named two schools or departments as cross-departmental collaboration, without distinguishing substantive cooperation from nominal partnership. For some projects, a faculty member from another department had been invited to lend their name only at the application stage, while the original team continued to conduct the actual research independently. Some faculty members held dual appointments, so although the system identified their teams as cross-departmental groups, the members had long worked in the same laboratory. Meanwhile, a joint study that genuinely required multidisciplinary participation might be divided into several internal subprojects yet counted as only one project in the statistics. If the indicator itself could not consistently reflect the degree of collaboration, an increase in the number of projects might mean that connections among knowledge, equipment, and personnel had grown closer, but it might also merely reflect a change in application practices. The committee therefore decided to return to the original materials and verify the actual division of responsibilities among project members, equipment-use records, minutes of joint meetings, and authorship of research outputs, rather than drawing conclusions solely from departmental labels.

The second issue involved confounding factors underlying the sequence of events. During the same semester in which the experimental center opened up, the university also revised its research evaluation rules: jointly submitted projects could receive additional credit in departmental evaluations, and early-career faculty applying for internal start-up funding were encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams. In addition, new guidelines issued by several funding agencies began to emphasize the integration of medicine, engineering, and data science. These policies might have increased the number of collaborative projects even if the laboratories had not opened up. Even more easily overlooked was the fact that, after the new campus began operating, several schools and departments formerly scattered across different campuses moved into adjacent buildings, substantially increasing opportunities for faculty members to meet at seminars, in dining halls, and on shared platforms. Physical proximity, funding priorities, evaluation incentives, and laboratory access emerged at almost the same time, and any of these factors could have affected the outcome. Attributing all the changes to the opening of the laboratories would not only exaggerate the measure’s effect but also cause subsequent resource allocation to be based on an unreliable explanation.

To test the causal claim, the committee did not simply compare the total numbers before and after the laboratories opened up. Instead, it sought a reference point closer to the counterfactual: how might the trend in collaboration have changed if the laboratories had not opened up? Because different instruments became available for public reservation at different times, the committee conducted a phased comparison between instruments that opened earlier and instruments with similar functions and users that had not yet opened, while also examining the departments’ prior collaboration trends. This method was still not equivalent to a randomized experiment, because the order in which equipment opened might have been related to the strength of demand. Equipment in high demand often entered the platform earlier, and demand itself might have encouraged collaboration. The analysts therefore also reviewed the records of decisions on opening access and confirmed that the opening dates of some instruments had been determined mainly by repairs, acceptance inspections, and progress in connecting them to the management system. They excluded from the core comparison equipment whose opening had clearly been driven by strong demand for collaboration. The committee also required the report to present separate findings for materials analysis, medical testing, and computing platforms so that a single average result would not conceal differences among fields.

In addition to project numbers, the investigation team traced the specific processes through which collaboration formed. Reservation records could show when members of outside departments began using equipment, but they could not prove that the two sides had genuinely exchanged knowledge. Joint authorship could indicate a connection between their research outputs, but it might not appear until long after the collaboration began. The team therefore examined records of technical consultations, sample preparation, data interpretation, and follow-up discussions, and interviewed platform engineers and project leaders. It paid particular attention to whether a collaboration had first been established after access opened, whether participants had performed indispensable work, and whether the relationship continued into new research questions. The review found that the open platform provided relatively clear benefits to young teams lacking specialized equipment: the public catalog informed them of the capabilities available within the university, the unified reservation system reduced the cost of seeking personal connections, and on-site exchanges with engineers often turned a single testing request into a discussion of methods. For senior teams that already had stable partners, however, opening the platform mostly formalized their existing patterns of use and did not create new collaborative relationships.

The investigation also revealed a situation that could easily produce reverse causality. Some departments had already been preparing joint project applications and, to meet their needs for sample testing and data processing, had actively urged the university to accelerate the opening of equipment access. On the surface, access opened before the projects were formally registered, making it appear that opening access had produced the collaboration. In reality, the intention to collaborate had existed much earlier, and the opening was merely a response to existing demand. Establishing the sequence solely from system registration dates would therefore lead to an incorrect judgment about the direction of causation. The committee consequently added project-planning meetings, preliminary application materials, and equipment consultation emails to the timeline in order to distinguish between “opening access facilitated collaboration” and “collaboration drove the opening of access.” This approach did not eliminate uncertainty completely, but it clarified the limits of the evidence: opening access could lower barriers to using resources, but it did not generate every collaboration that appeared afterward. A causal judgment must explain the mechanism at work and rule out at least several credible alternative explanations; it cannot rely solely on the statement that “the number increased after access opened.”

During the review, the university administration also discussed potential costs. After reservations were opened to everyone, waiting times for popular instruments grew longer, and platform engineers had to provide a large amount of basic training. If only new projects were rewarded, administrators might be inclined to accept more applications while neglecting service quality, sample safety, and long-term maintenance. Different departments also had differing understandings of cost sharing, data ownership, and authorship of papers, and a single instance of sharing undertaken without adequate consultation could even undermine the willingness to collaborate. Opening access, therefore, was not accomplished merely by removing a lock from the door; it required a system covering admission, training, fees, responsibilities, and dispute resolution. Nor was more research collaboration necessarily better. Temporary groupings without a shared research question would increase coordination costs. What truly deserved encouragement was collaboration in which the two sides had complementary capabilities, clearly defined responsibilities, and the ability to sustain the exchange of knowledge. On this basis, the committee rejected the proposal to use the increase in project numbers as the sole performance indicator.

Ultimately, the Research Committee reached a limited but clear conclusion: the available materials supported the claim that “opening the laboratories provided a necessary condition for some cross-departmental collaboration,” and they also showed that information disclosure, direct reservations, and technical exchanges lowered barriers to collaboration. The evidence was insufficient, however, to support the stronger claim that “the growth in projects was caused primarily by opening the laboratories.” The university decided to continue expanding access, not because the interim report had already demonstrated a single causal relationship, but because open access had independent value in promoting equitable access to resources and improving equipment utilization. At the same time, the Office of Research Administration revised the wording of the report, established a record-keeping system that would track equipment in phases, and added indicators covering substantive divisions of work, repeated collaboration, sharing of research outputs, and burdens on users. The review one year later would define the analytical criteria in advance and disclose the exclusion criteria and uncertainties. This outcome did not provide a catchy promotional slogan, but it produced a more reliable decision: it acknowledged that opening access might be effective, explained the conditions under which it was effective, and honestly identified the explanations that still could not be ruled out.

vocabulary.meaning: 针对某一工作阶段的进展、数据和结果所形成的报告。
涉及两个或多个不同院系。
对重要事项进行审查和讨论，以决定是否通过。
一个因素作为原因引起另一个结果的关系。
参与者在实际研究过程中有明确分工和真实贡献的合作。
同一人员同时受聘于两个单位或拥有两个职位归属。
同时影响研究条件和结果、可能干扰因果判断的其他因素。
与已经发生的事实相对照、假设某种条件没有出现时可能发生的情况。
按照不同时间阶段对研究对象进行对照分析。
通过随机分配研究对象来检验因果关系的实验方法。
分析中最关键、用于支持主要结论的对照比较。
具有独特作用，不能被其他人或事物代替。
误把结果当成原因，或实际因果方向与表面判断相反。
现有证据能够支持的结论范围及其限制。
允许人员、机构或项目进入并使用某种资源的资格规则。
进行统计分析时预先采用的定义、范围、标准和计算方法。

grammar.explanation: 用于提出一个假设条件，并说明在该条件下可能出现的结果。
grammar.example: 如果指标本身不能稳定反映合作程度，那么数量增加既可能意味着知识、设备与人员之间的联系变得紧密，也可能只是申报方式改变。

grammar.explanation: 表示让步关系，强调即便前项条件成立，后项结果仍然可能成立。
grammar.example: 即使实验室没有开放，这些政策也可能推动合作项目增加。

grammar.explanation: 用于否定一种原因，同时指出真正或更重要的原因。
grammar.example: 学校决定继续推进开放，不是因为阶段报告已经证明了单一因果关系，而是因为开放具有资源公平和提高设备利用效率的独立价值。

questions.prompt: 周岚为什么认为项目数量上升不能直接证明开放实验室提高了科研合作？
options: 两个现象同时发生并不能证明开放导致了合作增加，还需检查其他同期变化
阶段报告完全没有统计开放后的项目数量
公共实验中心只允许材料学院使用设备
科研委员会认为跨院系合作没有任何价值
questions.explanation: 周岚强调，时间上的同时出现只能说明相关性，不能直接建立因果关系；还必须考察政策调整、空间变化等同期因素。
questions.evidence: 若不检查其他同期变化，这个看似直观的结论可能把相关关系误当成因果关系。

questions.prompt: 为什么分析人员把部分设备排除在核心比较之外？
options: 这些设备没有留下任何预约和维修记录
这些设备的开放明显受到强烈合作需求推动，可能造成因果判断偏差
这些设备只能由资深团队使用，无法服务年轻团队
这些设备的收费标准与其他设备完全不同
questions.explanation: 如果强烈的合作需求本身推动设备提前开放，那么设备开放与合作之间就存在选择偏差，不能作为可靠的核心对照。
questions.evidence: 因此，分析人员又查阅开放决策记录，确认某些开放时间主要受维修、验收和管理系统接入进度影响，并把明显由强烈合作需求推动的设备排除在核心比较之外。

questions.prompt: 科研委员会最终对开放实验室与项目增长之间的关系作出了什么判断？
options: 现有证据已经证明所有项目增长都由实验室开放造成
实验室开放与科研合作完全没有关系，因此应当停止开放
开放为部分合作提供了条件，但证据不足以证明项目增长主要由开放造成
开放只有宣传价值，并不具有资源公平或设备利用方面的价值
questions.explanation: 委员会认可开放通过信息公开、直接预约和技术交流降低了部分合作的门槛，但没有把项目增长完全或主要归因于开放。
questions.evidence: 最终，科研委员会给出了有限而明确的结论：现有材料支持“开放实验室为一部分跨院系合作提供了必要条件”，也能说明它通过信息公开、直接预约和技术交流降低了合作门槛；但证据不足以支持“项目增长主要由开放造成”这一更强的说法。
